intro: The feature map is the top of the chain that turns intent into working code: feature map > spec > review > tasks > code > result. Each `feature` states a goal and cites the spec items that describe it; the format is `packages/reflect/deus/lang/features.mdl`.

pages.title: Composer
pages.summary: The Composer application: the plugins `packages/apps/composer-app` assembles, and the journeys through the running app that cross plugin boundaries.
pages.content:
The Composer application: the plugins `packages/apps/composer-app` assembles, and the journeys through the running app that cross plugin boundaries. A plugin's own contract lives in its `PLUGIN.mdl`; this document holds what no single plugin owns — for now its `## QA` section, the app-level test suites a Routine runs. The navigation and presentation structure (`node`, `deck`, `plank`, `surface` per `org.dxos.spec.app`) is to follow.

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and one operation the agent invokes (`invoke`); `expect` is the criterion both judge, and `assert` checks it against `$snapshot`, the debug snapshot taken after the step, or against a query operation. Every test owns its fixture (`given` + `before`) and its teardown (`after`), so the suites below are order-independent.

Conventions shared by every test here:

- `$runId` is the run's id and `$start` its start time in milliseconds; every snapshot takes `since: $start`, so `errors` is this run's errors so far. Artifacts carry `QA:` and `$runId`.
- `given` binds `defaultSpace` — the space flagged `default` in the snapshot — for the `after` step that returns the workspace to it: a deleted space stays the workspace until another is chosen, and the app shows "You don't have this workspace" meanwhile.
- The debug plugin must be active (`composer.snapshot` exists). If not: `org.dxos.operation.registry.enablePlugins { ids: ["org.dxos.plugin.debug"] }`, then retry.
- A `QA:` space left by an earlier run means that run's `after` did not finish. Run it (`--stage=after`) or remove the space by hand; never proceed on someone else's artifacts.

- **test** `QA-1` Spaces and documents — The smallest journey through the app — a space, three documents, one deletion, and what survives.

- **test** `QA-2` Rename, undo and a second space — Rename through the update operation, delete and undo from the toast, and switch between two spaces.

- **test** `QA-3` Comments — Create, reply to, resolve, reopen and delete a comment thread on a document; the agent reads the threads off `planks[].comments`.

- **test** `QA-4` The assistant edits the document — Ask the document's assistant to translate one paragraph in place; needs an AI provider the app can reach (the assistant settings' provider, EDGE by default).

- **test** `QA-5` First run and logout — What a brand new identity lands on, and what survives logging out — the journey every other test starts from.

- **test** `QA-6` Collections — nest, reorder, delete and undo — The navtree's containment model: a collection holds objects, drag changes containment and order, and a delete is undoable with its contents.

- **test** `QA-7` A second device on one identity — Joining a device to an existing identity, and what replicates to it afterwards — settings and space membership.

- **test** `QA-8` Two peers in one space — Sharing a space by invitation and editing one document from both sides — the collaboration path, as opposed to QA-7's one-identity replication.

- **test** `QA-9` The guided tours — The help tours, including the steps other plugins contribute to a document's tour.

- **test** `QA-10` Invite a known contact to a second space — A host who already shares a space with someone (and so has them as a contact) invites that same person into a DIFFERENT space directly from the contact picker, skipping the invitation-code exchange — as opposed to QA-8'…

- **test** `QA-11` Composer basics tour — A single walk through the default space that touches the core surfaces: comment on the README, write a linked document, enable plugins, draw a diagram, fill a table with the assistant while editing a sheet, then plot th…

- **test** `QA-13` Plugin showcase — One short, wordless beat per visually distinct plugin, recorded for the Grid montage (tools/autocue/showcase SHOWCASE.md): each plugin creates its object off camera, then performs one characteristic gesture.

## Suites

- **test** `QA-12` Two people collaborate, then one invites the other from the notifications inbox — The messenger demo.
- **test** `QA-15` Showcase clip — The 20s showcase clip: Walk the Bramble Coffee Roasters space: a project, its tasks, and the roastery handbook.

- **suite** `smoke` Boots, one space, three documents, one deletion — The five-minute check — QA-1 alone.

- **suite** `basics` The app-level journeys — Spaces, documents, rename, undo and comments.

- **suite** `multi-peer` Journeys that need a second browser profile — A second device on one identity, and a second identity in one space.

- **suite** `onboarding` First run, logout and the guided tours — What a new identity sees, and the help surface that explains it.

- **suite** `assistant` Journeys that need an AI provider — Runs only where the assistant settings name a reachable provider; otherwise reports blocked.

- **suite** `editor` The markdown plugin's own contract, run at app level — The plugin tests already verified through the port, so the nightly run covers a plugin as well as the app.

- **test** `QA-14` Bramble — Kai locks the Spring Blend — A story demo of the Bramble template: Kai Chen, head roaster, is six weeks from launching a new espresso blend, and every step answers one question, whether the Spring Blend is ready.
- **test** `QA-16` Hot-reload a plugin capability — Dev-server demo of plugin hot replacement: edits to plugin-space's app-graph builder (a capability with no React in it), made from a terminal floated over the app, re-run that module in place and the navtree follows; ed…

pages.title: Composer Performance
pages.summary: Performance flows: journeys measured rather than asserted.
pages.content:
Performance flows: journeys measured rather than asserted. Each `test` here is the top-level description of a flow whose stages a Playwright spec drives and instruments — this document says what the flow is and what "too slow" would mean, and [`src/playwright/perf-projects.spec.ts`](https://github.com/dxos/dxos/blob/main/packages/apps/composer-app/src/playwright/perf-projects.spec.ts) is the same flow as executable stages. A step's `id` IS the stage id the harness records, so the description and the numbers join without a second mapping to keep in sync.

Functional QA lives in [`APP.mdl`](https://github.com/dxos/dxos/blob/main/packages/apps/composer-app/spec/APP.mdl). Nothing here gates a merge: the flows run nightly from `main` and trend into PostHog.

## Measurement contract

What the harness (`@dxos/perf-harness`) records per stage, and the rules that make two runs comparable at all:

- **Two modes, never mixed.** `measure` reads counters at stage boundaries and runs the V8 sampling profiler, writing no profiles, so that per-realm CPU is trended; it is the sole mode trended. `diagnose` adds a screencast and keeps the profiles. The line between them is the SCREENCAST: measured on one flow, profiler-only costs +2.6% against `measure` — below the run-to-run noise — while adding the screencast costs +47%, because it encodes a JPEG per frame and waits on an ack before the next. Note also that Playwright's own Network domain makes Blink retain response bodies in EVERY mode (the finding behind `scripts/memory/plain-soak.mjs`), so the absolute footprint is inflated by an unmeasured constant while a trend across runs stays valid.
- **Per stage:** wall ms; total CPU ms across every Chrome process (`SystemInfo.getProcessInfo`); CPU per REALM from the profiler, the only instrument that reaches a worker — process CPU folds a dedicated worker into its renderer, and the `Performance` domain does not exist on a worker target at all; the page main thread's `script`/`layout`/`recalcStyle` split; JS heap per target after a forced GC; the renderers' private footprint, with Chrome's own processes reported separately; DOM node and listener counts; network bytes split code-load vs API; long tasks and TBT for the page, and timer-drift lag per realm.
- **Recorded on every row, or the trend is noise:** serving mode (`vite preview` over a production bundle — `vite serve` costs ~2.5x on the main thread), plugin set, profile state (first-run performs onboarding and loads a different module set), settle time, and which instruments were attached. Per `scripts/memory/README.md` §"Comparing runs".
- **Memory means four different things** that differ by 3-5x. The trended one is the renderers' private footprint: it counts wasm linear memory, where automerge documents live outside every JS-heap reading, and unlike RSS it is disjoint per process, so the renderers can be added. A peak of RSS summed over the whole process tree, which this replaced, multi-counted the shared pages every process maps and buried the app under ~218 MB of Chrome's own.

## QA

- **test** `QA-1` A project with a large task set and long documents — One journey across TWO different cost engines, because a project is not a task list and anything in the app can tank performance.

## Suites

- **suite** `perf-nightly` The measured flows, from main — Runs both modes of every flow.

pages.title: ECHO queries
pages.summary: How a live ECHO query gets its answer: from the `Query` builder in `@dxos/echo`, through the client's `LocalQueryEngine`, to the host index and EDGE and back.
pages.content:
How a live ECHO query gets its answer: from the `Query` builder in `@dxos/echo`, through the client's `LocalQueryEngine`, to the host index and EDGE and back.

Two properties define the subsystem and outrank everything else:

- **A local write is visible before the writing call returns.** For any branch with an in-process contribution, an object added, edited or removed through this database is in `results` and has notified subscribers by the time `db.add`, `Obj.update` or `db.remove` returns [F-2].
- **A remote answer is evidence, not truth.** The index and EDGE answer from copies that can be behind this tab. Each remote entry is checked against what the tab holds and is dropped when local state contradicts it [F-5].

The packages involved:

| Package              | Role                                                                                    |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@dxos/echo`         | `Query`, `Filter`, `Order`, `Aggregate` builders; the public `QueryResult` type.        |
| `@dxos/echo-protocol`| `QueryAST`; `Query.characteristics`, the static classification of a query.             |
| `@dxos/echo-client`  | `QueryResultImpl`, `LocalQueryEngine`, `WorkingSetView`, `RegistryView`, the merge.     |
| `@dxos/protocols`    | The `QueryService` wire schema shared by the host and EDGE.                             |
| `@dxos/echo-host`    | `QueryExecutor` (memory and SQL), `SqlPlanCompiler`.                                    |
| `@dxos/index-core`   | The object snapshot index: each object's JSON copy, its heads and its version.         |

The long-form design, with the reasoning and the rejected alternatives, is `packages/core/echo/echo-client/docs/SYNC_QUERIES.md`. Tests map to the acceptance scenarios: `echo-client-e2e/src/sync-query.test.ts` (T-1 to T-9), `echo-client/src/query/local-query-engine.test.ts` (T-10, T-11) and the executor-evidence suite in `echo-host/src/db-host/echo-host.test.ts` (T-12, T-13).

## Diagrams

Diagrams are plugin-illustrator renders. The `diagram` block is the source; regenerate the image with `moon run plugin-illustrator:render-diagrams -- <abs path>/spec/diagrams/<name>.dx`.

### Pipeline

![QueryResultImpl reads the LocalQueryEngine, which owns a WorkingSetView per database and the RegistryView, takes verdicts from merge-plan, and reads RemoteQuerySources; IndexQuerySource implements RemoteQuerySource over QueryService to the host's QueryExecutor, which compiles SQL and answers from the object snapshot index.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dxos/dxos/main/packages/core/echo/echo-client/spec/diagrams/pipeline.dx.svg)

```diagram
diagram flow=down
group client "@dxos/echo-client" {
  node Result "QueryResultImpl" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-client/src/query/query-result.ts"
  node Engine "LocalQueryEngine" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-client/src/query/local-query-engine.ts"
  node WorkingSet "WorkingSetView" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-client/src/query/working-set-view.ts"
  node Registry "RegistryView" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-client/src/query/registry-view.ts"
  node Plan "merge-plan" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-client/src/query/merge-plan.ts"
  node Remote "RemoteQuerySource" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-client/src/query/remote-query-source.ts"
  node Index "IndexQuerySource" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-client/src/client/index-query-source-provider.ts"
}
group host "@dxos/echo-host" {
  node Service "QueryServiceImpl" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-host/src/db-host/query-service.ts"
  node Executor "QueryExecutor" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-host/src/query/query-executor.ts"
  node Sql "SqlPlanCompiler" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-host/src/query/sql/compile.ts"
}
group core "@dxos/index-core" {
  node Snapshots "ObjectSnapshotIndex" ref="packages/core/echo/index-core/src/indexes/object-snapshot-index.ts"
}
edge Result -> Engine
edge Engine owns WorkingSet
edge Engine owns Registry
edge Engine -> Plan "verdicts"
edge Engine -> Remote
edge Index implements Remote
edge Index -> Service "QueryService"
edge Service -> Executor
edge Executor -> Sql
edge Executor -> Snapshots "index copies"
```

### Remote entry verdicts

![A remote entry for a feed item is checked against the local feed write; a flat-query entry is verified when held at its version, and otherwise its filter is re-checked; a traversal entry has its paths checked. Each check ends in verified, drop or trusted.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dxos/dxos/main/packages/core/echo/echo-client/spec/diagrams/verdicts.dx.svg)

```diagram
diagram flow=right
node Entry "remote entry" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-client/src/query/merge-plan.ts"
node Paths "check paths" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-client/src/query/path-revalidation.ts"
node Version "held at version?" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-client/src/query/merge-plan.ts"
node Filter "re-check filter" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-client/src/query/merge-plan.ts"
node Tail "feed local write" ref="packages/core/echo/echo-client/src/query/working-set-view.ts"
node Verified "verified"
node Drop "drop"
node Trusted "trusted"
edge Entry -> Paths "traversal"
edge Entry -> Version "flat query"
edge Entry -> Tail "feed item"
edge Version -> Verified "equal heads"
edge Version -> Filter "differ"
edge Filter -> Verified "matches"
edge Filter -> Drop "no match"
edge Filter -> Trusted "not loaded"
edge Paths -> Verified "a path holds"
edge Paths -> Drop "all broken"
edge Paths -> Trusted "unknown"
edge Tail -> Verified "matches"
edge Tail -> Drop "no match"
```

## Types

- **type** `Completeness` How much of the answer a live query holds right now.

| Value        | Meaning                                                                                   |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `complete`   | Nothing outstanding.                                                                      |
| `local-only` | In-process results are shown; no remote has answered yet.                                 |
| `merged`     | Some remotes answered and some have not, or an answer withheld paths or a manifest.       |
| `stale`      | A remote answer predates a local write inside its scope; the re-run has not arrived.      |
| `failed`     | A remote source errored or timed out; `sources` names it.                                 |
| `pending`    | Nothing in-process contributes and no remote has answered.                                |

- **type** `Version` The state a remote evaluated an entry at.

- **type** `PathEdge` One hop of a traversal the index took to reach a hit.

- **type** `ManifestEntry` One member's share of a collapsed group's scalar aggregates.

- **type** `Verdict` What the engine does with one remote entry.

- **type** `BranchCharacteristics` The static classification `Query.characteristics(ast)` returns per branch: one record per union member, with wrappers above a union applied to each member.

## Services

- **service** `LocalQueryEngine` The client side of every live query.

- **service** `RemoteQuerySource` An out-of-process answerer: the host index, or EDGE through the same QueryService.

- **service** `QueryService` The streamed RPC the host and EDGE both serve (`@dxos/protocols`).

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` One engine, local views, remote sources
  - `F-1.1` a live query is created → its QueryResultImpl reads one LocalQueryEngine, which owns a WorkingSetView per database and
  - `F-1.2` the engine needs an answer from outside the tab → it reads RemoteQuerySources only — the host index and EDGE, both through QueryService
  - `F-1.3` the engine stops and starts again → stop closes the views and the remote streams, and start re-applies the current query, so a

- **feat** `F-2` Local writes are synchronous
  - `F-2.1` an object is added, edited or removed through this database inside the scope of a branch with → the result reflects it and subscribers are notified before the writing call returns
  - `F-2.2` a subscriber writes from inside a notification → that write is a separate commit with its own notification, after the first commit's
  - `F-2.3` a recompute leaves the result's ids and order unchanged → no subscriber is notified; a completeness transition alone is silent
  - `F-2.4` a query has no order of its own → entries appear in natural order (by id), wherever each object is held

- **feat** `F-3` Characteristics and completeness
  - `F-3.1` Query.characteristics(ast) is called → it returns one BranchCharacteristics per branch, derived from the AST alone
  - `F-3.2` a text, timestamp, feed-cursor, changes or in-query node appears anywhere in a branch's filter → the branch's revalidation is none and nothing is dropped locally
  - `F-3.3` a live query is read → completeness is computed from the plan and the remote sources' states, per [Completeness]

- **feat** `F-4` Versions
  - `F-4.1` a remote row is sent → it carries a Version — the document's id and the heads it was read at, or the feed block's
  - `F-4.2` the indexer stores an object's copy → objectSnapshot.version records the heads the copy was read at, and objectSnapshot.heads marks a
  - `F-4.3` a remote entry's object is held here at exactly the entry's version → the entry is verified without re-evaluating the filter

- **feat** `F-5` Remote entries are revalidated
  - `F-5.1` a remote entry of a flat query names an object loaded here with a body → the filter and the deleted option are re-evaluated against the local document; a match is
  - `F-5.2` a remote entry names an object not loaded here, or the branch's revalidation is none → the entry is trusted and shown on the remote's word, with resolution.verified false
  - `F-5.3` a remote entry is verified → resolution.verified is true and resolution.version is the version the remote sent

- **feat** `F-6` By-id queries
  - `F-6.1` every id of a live by-id query is loaded with a body in a space the query covers → the engine answers from the working set alone and no remote stream is open — neither the index
  - `F-6.2` a by-id query names an id that is not loaded → the remote streams open, and the ids no remote answered are loaded through their documents
  - `F-6.3` run() is called on a by-id query → it answers the loaded ids first, then takes the remote answer, then loads only the ids no

- **feat** `F-7` Traversal paths
  - `F-7.1` a traversal reaches a hit → the hit carries one path per derivation, each a list of PathEdge; both executors produce them
  - `F-7.2` the engine checks a hit's paths → each edge is checked against its holder's document and each level's filter against each loaded
  - `F-7.3` a hit has more than 16 paths or a compiled row more than 512 edges → the hit ships no paths and is trusted
  - `F-7.4` one answer's paths exceed 256 KiB → the response sets truncated: paths and completeness reads merged
  - `F-7.5` a traversal sits inside a union branch or a subquery → its hits ship no paths and are trusted

- **feat** `F-8` Aggregate manifests
  - `F-8.1` a remote collapses a group of scalar aggregates (no items aggregate) → the group carries a manifest: each member's id, version and share of count, sum, min and max
  - `F-8.2` the engine adjusts a group → it subtracts the share of each member it holds, adds the value of each local member, and lists
  - `F-8.3` a local value would narrow min or max → the extreme only widens, and removing a held extreme marks the group unverified
  - `F-8.4` one answer's manifests exceed 256 KiB → the response sets truncated: manifest and completeness reads merged

- **feat** `F-9` Local ordering and windows
  - `F-9.1` a query has a property or natural order and no limit or skip → the engine applies the order over the merged local and remote entries, and characteristics does
  - `F-9.2` a property-ordered window has a limit and no skip → loaded local matches that sort at or before the last entry of a full remote window are admitted,
  - `F-9.3` any other window is merged → local evidence can only drop entries from it, never re-page it

- **feat** `F-10` Feeds
  - `F-10.1` an object is appended to or edited in a feed through its handle → a simple selection over that feed, or over all feeds of the space, shows it before the write
  - `F-10.2` a feed is first opened after a query over all feeds starts → its writes join that query
  - `F-10.3` a remote feed entry has a local write of the same id that no longer matches → the entry is dropped
  - `F-10.4` a write appends, edits or deletes feed objects → only the objects it names are re-evaluated, so a turn of n appends costs O(n), not O(n²)
  - `F-10.5` a feed query is a window (a limit or a skip) → it is remote-only

- **feat** `F-11` The host answers from index copies
  - `F-11.1` the memory executor matches an object whose index copy is at the document's current heads → it answers from the copy and does not load the document; it counts echo.querySnapshotHits and
  - `F-11.2` the SQL executor answers → it never loads a document
  - `F-11.3` a client subscription already holds a hit's document → the row ships without its JSON copy or stored changes

## Current limits

- EDGE's executor sends no versions, paths or manifests, so every EDGE entry is trusted.
- The working set keeps no typename map: window admission and shapes without a delta scan every loaded object.
- A re-run already in flight when a local write lands can clear `stale` early.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` An add notifies once, before it returns

- **scenario** `T-2` An edit that disqualifies an object removes it at once

- **scenario** `T-3` An edit to an unread property notifies nobody

- **scenario** `T-4` A write from a notification is its own commit

- **scenario** `T-5` A traversal hit leaves when its holder drops the edge

- **scenario** `T-6` A count follows a local write

- **scenario** `T-7` A property order spans local and index entries

- **scenario** `T-8` Feed writes appear at once

- **scenario** `T-9` Completeness follows the sources

- **scenario** `T-10` A by-id query over loaded ids opens no remote stream

- **scenario** `T-11` A by-id run loads only what the index lacks

- **scenario** `T-12` Rows ship their versions

- **scenario** `T-13` Traversal hits and groups ship their evidence

pages.title: EchoSqlite
pages.summary: `@dxos/echo-sqlite` is the smallest backend that implements the ECHO `Database` interface from `@dxos/echo` without `@dxos/echo-client` / `@dxos/echo-host`: no Automerge, no feeds, no replication, no client/host split.
pages.content:
`@dxos/echo-sqlite` is the smallest backend that implements the ECHO `Database` interface from `@dxos/echo` without `@dxos/echo-client` / `@dxos/echo-host`: no Automerge, no feeds, no replication, no client/host split. Entities are stored as JSON rows in SQLite and surface to callers as ordinary in-memory live objects (`Obj.make` proxies).

Two properties define it and outrank simplicity:

- **SQLite is the source of truth and the space is never resident.** Opening a database, querying it, or resolving a ref materializes only the rows that call needs. Memory is bounded by what callers hold, not by the size of the space [F-3].
- **Queries run in SQLite.** A query AST compiles to one read-only SQL statement, following the design in `packages/core/echo/echo-host/docs/SQL_QUERY_EXECUTION.md` and its compiler `packages/core/echo/echo-host/src/query/sql/compile.ts`. Only the result rows are hydrated; nothing is filtered, traversed or ordered in JavaScript [F-4].

Tests map to the acceptance scenarios: `src/memory.test.ts` (T-1, T-2), `src/differential.test.ts` (T-3), `src/sql/explain.test.ts` (T-4, T-5), `src/database.test.ts` (T-6 to T-9). Benchmarks are in `src/testing/database.bench.ts` and `src/memory.report.test.ts`; results are recorded in `BENCHMARKS.md`.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Database interface
  - `F-1.1` SqliteDatabase is constructed → it satisfies Database.Database, Database.isDatabase(db) is true, and db.graph is a
  - `F-1.2` the database is opened with an Effect SqlClient in scope → it runs on every SqlClient the repo supports — node (@effect/sql-sqlite-node), browser
  - `F-1.3` code runs in Effect → SqliteDatabase.layer(options) provides Database.Service, and closing its scope flushes
  - `F-1.4` a caller uses feeds, branches, history (getVersion, getChanges), a non-inline blob backend, or → the call fails with UnsupportedOperationError; nothing silently no-ops or returns a

- **feat** `F-2` Storage layout
  - `F-2.1` an entity is stored → it is one row of the entity table, keyed by (spaceId, id), holding the full ECHO JSON
  - `F-2.2` the compiler needs a field to select, join or order on → that field is a denormalized, indexed column written in the same transaction as the body —
  - `F-2.3` an entity holding references or text is written → its outgoing references (target id, normalized property path) and its extracted string
  - `F-2.4` the schema changes → the change is a new numbered, immutable .sql migration in src/migrations with its own
  - `F-2.5` several spaces share one SQLite file → every statement is constrained to its spaceId and no space can read or write another's rows

- **feat** `F-3` Bounded memory — the space is never loaded whole — The non-negotiable requirement.
  - `F-3.1` a database is opened → it runs migrations and reads at most the persisted type rows (kind = type); no object or
  - `F-3.2` a query runs → only the rows in its final result are read from SQLite and hydrated; a LIMIT bounds the
  - `F-3.3` a ref is loaded (ref.load(), Database.load, db.makeRef(uri).load()) → the single target row is read by (spaceId, id) and hydrated; ref.target / ref.peek()
  - `F-3.4` a row is hydrated → it enters a working set keyed by id; while any caller still holds that live object, every
  - `F-3.5` no caller holds a hydrated object any longer and it has no unflushed changes → the working set releases it (weakly held); the working set never pins objects for the
  - `F-3.6` relations, parents or references are added or resolved → endpoints and targets are resolved one row at a time on demand; no traversal preloads a
  - `F-3.7` db.diagnostics() is read → it reports resident objects, rows hydrated, compiled statements and single-row loads, so

- **feat** `F-4` Queries compile to SQL — Follows packages/core/echo/echo-host/docs/SQL_QUERY_EXECUTION.md with the package's own compiler (src/sql/compile.ts), so the package does not depend on echo-host.
  - `F-4.1` a query (Query or Filter) is executed → it compiles to exactly one read-only statement, WITH RECURSIVE with one CTE per plan step
  - `F-4.2` the compiler builds SQL → compilation is pure (plan in, SQL out, no store reads); every value is a bound parameter,
  - `F-4.3` a property filter is compiled → it reads json_extract(body, '$."k1"."k2"') with typed comparison — gt/gte/lt/lte match
  - `F-4.4` a query selects by type, id, timestamp, tag, foreign key, meta key or text → type/id/timestamp read the denormalized columns through their indexes (a typed select is
  - `F-4.5` a query traverses references, incoming references, relations or the hierarchy → the traversal is a join on the normalized id columns or the reverse-reference table, and
  - `F-4.6` deleted objects are in scope → an object is deleted if its own row is deleted or any parent (up to depth 10) or relation
  - `F-4.7` a query orders, limits or skips → order, LIMIT and OFFSET run in SQL; natural order is by id in BINARY (code-unit)
  - `F-4.8` a clause cannot be expressed as SQL without first reading the store (e.g.
  - `F-4.9` a query runs while the database has unflushed changes → pending writes are committed before the statement executes, so run() always reflects
  - `F-4.10` a query is executed against the registry scope (Scope.registry()) → it is answered from the in-process registry, which is small and code-shipped, and is the

- **feat** `F-5` Query results and reactivity
  - `F-5.1` QueryResult.run() / runEntries() / first() is called → the compiled statement executes and the hydrated results are returned
  - `F-5.2` QueryResult.runSync() / .results / .entries is read → it returns the results of the most recent execution of that query (empty before the first
  - `F-5.3` a query has a subscriber (subscribe or atom) → it executes once on subscribe and re-executes after each committed write batch that could
  - `F-5.4` a re-execution returns the same rows in the same order → subscribers are not notified; they are notified only when membership or order changes

- **feat** `F-6` Writes and durability
  - `F-6.1` an entity is added, mutated (Obj.update, nested or meta changes) or removed → only that entity's row (and its side-table rows) is rewritten, batched per microtask into
  - `F-6.2` an object added to the database references (Ref.make) or relates to entities not yet stored → those entities are stored with it in the same batch
  - `F-6.3` db.remove(obj) is called → the row is soft-deleted (deleted = 1), re-adding the object restores it, and
  - `F-6.4` a write batch fails → the batch stays pending and the next flush retries it and rejects if it fails again;
  - `F-6.5` the process restarts and the database is reopened → every flushed entity — body, meta, parent, relation endpoints, references, deletion state,

- **feat** `F-7` Types
  - `F-7.1` static types are passed to open({ types }) → rows of those types hydrate as typed live objects
  - `F-7.2` db.addType(type) is called → a Type entity with the type's JSON Schema is stored (idempotent on typename + version) and
  - `F-7.3` a row's type is unknown → it hydrates as a read-only snapshot instead of failing the query that returned it

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Opening a large space reads nothing

- **scenario** `T-2` The working set releases unheld objects

- **scenario** `T-3` Differential against the in-memory matcher

- **scenario** `T-4` Compiled SQL uses the indexes

- **scenario** `T-5` One statement per query

- **scenario** `T-6` Read-your-writes

- **scenario** `T-7` Subscriptions fire only on change

- **scenario** `T-8` Persistence across reopen

- **scenario** `T-9` A failed write is retried, not dropped

## Rules

- **rule** `echo-sqlite-no-whole-space-read` Never read or hydrate a whole space

- **rule** `echo-sqlite-no-js-query-evaluation` Queries are answered by SQL, not by JavaScript matching

- **rule** `echo-sqlite-bound-parameters` SQL values are bound, never interpolated

- **rule** `echo-sqlite-ddl-in-migrations` Schema lives only in numbered migrations
