pages.title: ChessPlugin
pages.summary: A two-player chess game plugin for `DXOS` Composer.
pages.content:
A two-player chess game plugin for `DXOS` Composer.

## Types

- **type** `Color`

- **type** `PieceKind`

- **type** `Piece`

- **type** `Square`

- **type** `Move`

- **type** `Board`

- **type** `Player`

- **type** `GameStatus`

- **type** `Game`

## Components

- **component** `Lobby` Entry point where players create or join a game.

- **component** `Gameboard` Interactive chess board for an active game.

## Services

- **service** `ChessEngine` Validates moves and computes game state.

- **service** `GameStore` Persists and replicates Game state via ECHO.

## Operations

Pure operations (no effects, no service dependencies) — safe to call anywhere.

- **op** `getLegalMoves` Returns legal target squares for the piece on the given square.

- **op** `validateMove` Checks a move against chess rules without mutating state.

- **op** `applyMove` Applies a validated move and returns the next board state.

Effectful operations — mutate persistent state.

- **op** `startGame` Creates a new Game with two players and an initial Board.

- **op** `playEngineMove` Uses the chess engine to play the next move for a side.

- **op** `submitMove` Validates and applies a move, then persists the updated Game.

- **op** `resignGame` Player forfeits; opponent wins.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Start Game
  - `F-1.1` New Board created with pieces in standard starting positions.
  - `F-1.2` White moves first.

- **feat** `F-2` Make Move
  - `F-2.1` player submits a Move on their turn → Move validated against chess rules
  - `F-2.2` Move is valid → Board updated; turn advances to opponent
  - `F-2.3` resulting position leaves opponent's king in check → Board.status set to check
  - `F-2.4` no legal moves remain for the side to move → Board.status set to checkmate (if in check) or stalemate

- **feat** `F-3` Lobby
  - `F-3.1` Player sees list of open games on entering the Lobby.
  - `F-3.2` player creates a game → new Game created with status waiting; player assigned white
  - `F-3.3` second player joins an open game → Game.status transitions to active; joining player assigned black
  - `F-3.4` Game.status becomes active → both players navigated to Gameboard

- **feat** `F-4` Gameboard
  - `F-4.1` player selects a square containing their piece → legal move targets highlighted on board
  - `F-4.2` player selects a highlighted target square → Move submitted via submitMove(); board updated on success
  - `F-4.3` pawn reaches the back rank → promotion dialog shown via overlay slot; player selects piece kind
  - `F-4.4` Game.status is finished → result overlay shown (winner or draw); further moves disabled

- **feat** `F-5` Move Validation
  - `F-5.1` Gameboard calls submitMove → op:validateMove runs before any state change
  - `F-5.2` validation fails → error returned to caller; Game state unchanged
  - `F-5.3` square is selected on Gameboard → op:getLegalMoves called; results drive component:Gameboard.highlights

- **feat** `F-6` Game Persistence
  - `F-6.1` op:startGame completes → Game written to ECHO and visible in component:Lobby game list
  - `F-6.2` op:submitMove completes → updated Game replicated to all peers via ECHO
  - `F-6.3` peer receives a Game update → component:Gameboard re-renders with new Board state

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` New game starting position

- **scenario** `T-2` Illegal move rejected

- **scenario** `T-3` Create and join game

- **scenario** `T-4` Legal move highlight

- **scenario** `T-5` Pawn promotion

- **scenario** `T-6` Submit valid move

- **scenario** `T-7` Submit invalid move rejected atomically

- **scenario** `T-8` Legal moves highlighted

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Start a game and play the opening — The core chess round-trip — create a game, play the first few moves, read the position back.
- **test** `QA-2` Showcase clip — The 10s showcase clip: Replay Morphy's Opera Game move by move.

pages.title: ClaudePlugin
pages.summary: Models Anthropic Claude managed agents — agents Anthropic hosts and runs on your behalf — as objects in the space.
pages.content:
Models Anthropic Claude managed agents — agents Anthropic hosts and runs on your behalf — as objects in the space. A `ClaudeManagedAgent` holds the configuration (model, system prompt, toolsets, skills, MCP servers) and, once deployed, the server-assigned agent id. A `ClaudeAgentSession` records one run of that agent.

Configuration and execution are deliberately separate: the object is edited locally and pushed to Anthropic by an explicit deploy step, so a half-configured agent never reaches the API. Session events are not mirrored into the space; the transcript is fetched on demand from the session id.

The plugin also offers Claude Code on this computer as an agent a project's tasks can be assigned to. An `AgentHelper` host runs it through the Claude Code ACP adapter this plugin ships, against the user's own `claude`, and the chat holds its session. The plugin owns that host's interface and the agent server behind it; its Tauri-only module runs the server as the desktop app's `dx-agent` sidecar, and plugin-dev-shell runs the same server inside a Vite dev server.

## Types

pages.title: CloudflarePlugin
pages.summary: A **headless** Composer plugin that connects a Cloudflare account.
pages.content:
A **headless** Composer plugin that connects a Cloudflare account. It has no React surfaces and syncs nothing into ECHO. It contributes one thing: a **Connector** entry (`source: "cloudflare.com"`) that runs Cloudflare's OAuth flow through `kms-service` and leaves the grant behind as an `AccessToken` plus a `Connection`.

Everything downstream — an operation, an assistant tool, another plugin — resolves that token through `CredentialsService` keyed on the source, the same seam `plugin-ideogram` uses for its API key. Nothing here knows what the token will be used for.

The grant is sized for that downstream work rather than for this plugin: a coding agent that names the resources it needs should be able to deploy a Worker and bind its storage without the user touching the dashboard.

## Connector

- **feat** `CloudflareConnector` Contributes a ConnectorEntry via Capability.contribute(Connector, [entry]) on the ConnectorEvents.Start activation event.

## Dependencies

- `@dxos/plugin-connector` (workspace:\*) — `ConnectorSpec.Connector` capability key and `ConnectionTestError`.
- `@dxos/compute` — `Credential.getApiKeyValue` for the stored token.
- `@dxos/protocols` — `OAuthProvider.CLOUDFLARE`, whose provider spec lives in `kms-service`.
- `@dxos/app-framework`, `@dxos/app-toolkit`, `@dxos/echo`, `@dxos/link`, `effect`.
- No `react` / `@dxos/react-ui*`.

## Acceptance

- **test** `T-1` Label from the user endpoint

- **test** `T-2` Label falls back to the account name

- **test** `T-3` A rejected token fails the connection test

## Out of scope (v1)

- Syncing any Cloudflare resource (Workers, zones, R2, D1) into ECHO. The connector declares no `sync`, so `plugin-connector` offers no bindings for it.
- Operations or assistant tools over the v4 API. This plugin holds the credential; calling the API is somebody else's job.
- Cloudflare API tokens as an alternative to OAuth (no `credentialForm`).
- Narrowing the grant per use. Every scope is requested at connect time; there is no path for an agent to ask for `d1:write` only when it first needs D1.

## QA

- **flow** `QA-1` Connect a Cloudflare account — Headless — the whole plugin is one Connector entry, so the flow is the generic connector UI end to end.

pages.title: CodeGraphPlugin
pages.summary: A canvas of the codebase, built from code-index.
pages.content:
A canvas of the codebase, built from code-index. Boxes are resources in the index (packages, files, symbols); arrows are facts between them (imports, package dependencies). The assistant fills and reshapes a graph by querying the index. The canvas lays the same graph out with the illustrator's semantic engine, a force-directed layout, or by dependency rank, and can show the illustrator's full drawing.

Dev only: the page reaches the index through a `vite dev` route that runs `code-index mcp` beside the app (`tauri dev` loads the same dev server). See `docs/DESIGN.md`.

## Types

- **type** `CodeGraph` A curated view of the code index.
- **type** `Node` One box.
- **type** `Edge` One arrow, from the subject to the object of a triple.
- **type** `NodeKind`
- **type** `Layout`

## Operations

- **op** `query` Runs a SPARQL SELECT over the index and returns the rows; draws nothing.
- **op** `inspect` Returns one resource's outgoing facts and incoming counts.
- **op** `read` Returns a graph's boxes, arrows and layout.
- **op** `addFromQuery` Runs a SELECT and draws its rows; ?from/?to rows are arrows, ?node rows are boxes.
- **op** `addNodes` Adds boxes for resources and connects every box pair the index links by imports or usesPackage.
- **op** `addNeighbors` Adds the neighbours of boxes along one predicate, outward, inward or both.
- **op** `remove` Removes boxes and their arrows, or everything.
- **op** `setLayout` Chooses the layout, optionally forgets dragged positions, and optionally turns grouping by package on or off.
- **op** `runCommand` Carries out one short command with its own fast model, which may only add SPARQL results or remove boxes by a text filter; a decision model ends the loop.

## Components

- **component** `CodeGraphArticle` The article surface.
- **component** `CodeGraphCanvas` react-ui-canvas's dynamic projection with one box per resource, as plugin-projects' FeatureCanvas uses it.
- **component** `CodeGraphDiagram` plugin-illustrator's SceneSvg drawing of the semantic layout, read-only, with package frames and routed arrows.
- **component** `NodeDetails` The selected resource's facts, with expand and remove actions.
- **component** `CommandBar` A floating button (or `/`) that opens a one-line command field over the canvas, with a microphone toggle for spoken commands and a line for the outcome and the trailer.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Read the index from the app
  - `F-1.1` A same-origin dev-server route answers read-only code-index tools by running `code-index mcp` as a child process.
  - `F-1.2` The route accepts only loopback callers and JSON requests, so other pages and machines cannot read the source tree.
  - `F-1.3` Without the route (a deployed build), every operation fails with an error that names the missing route.
- **feat** `F-2` The assistant shapes the graph
  - `F-2.1` The Code Graph skill offers query, inspect, read, addFromQuery, addNodes, addNeighbors, remove and setLayout, and the space's addObject to create a graph.
  - `F-2.2` A chat about a CodeGraph object carries the skill (SkillsAnnotation).
  - `F-2.3` Adding never duplicates a box or an arrow, and a box an arrow needs is added with it.
  - `F-2.4` An addition that would take a graph past 300 boxes fails whole with `LimitError`.
- **feat** `F-3` Two layouts on one canvas
  - `F-3.1` The illustrator layout solves the graph as semantic DSL and places canvas boxes at the solved centres; when the graph is grouped it frames each package's boxes, the package box included, in a tinted frame titled with th…
  - `F-3.2` The force layout uses the canvas's own force arrangement; rank uses its fewest-crossings arrangement.
  - `F-3.3` Dragging a box saves only its position; boxes the user did not move stay under the layout.
  - `F-3.4` The diagram layout renders the illustrator's full drawing with SceneSvg.
- **feat** `F-4` Inspect a box
  - `F-4.1` Double-clicking a box opens its facts from the index.
  - `F-4.2` The details panel expands the box's dependencies or dependents, or removes it.

feat F-5: Single commands req F-5.1: A command bar, apart from the chat assistant, takes one typed or spoken command and runs it with RunCommand. req F-5.2: The command model sees the graph as it is and may only add the rows of a SPARQL SELECT or remove boxes matching a text filter (`*`, `kind:<kind>`, `/regex/`, or text). req F-5.3: Between turns a decision model (the space's default, Clef on Workers AI unless configured) judges whether the command is done; a failed or empty action earns another turn without asking, and a turn that only removed boxes ends the command; at most 3 turns. req F-5.4: A command adds at most 40 boxes; the rest are left out and summarised in a trailer (counts by kind and package, and a few names) shown to the user and the model. req F-5.5: Speaking uses Whistle on the device: with the microphone on, each pause ends a command. req F-5.6: Before the first model call, the packages and exported symbols the command names are looked up in the index and given to the model as exact IRIs; the lookup is skipped after 1.5 s. req F-5.7: A verbose toggle in the bar, remembered per browser, lists every step of the last command (lookup, model call, add, remove, judge) with its time, its token counts or row counts, and the SPARQL or filter it ran.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Draw package dependencies

pages.title: CodePlugin
pages.summary: - **plugin** `CodePlugin` Authors, reviews and syncs DEUS specs, and scaffolds the code they describe.
pages.content:
- **plugin** `CodePlugin` Authors, reviews and syncs DEUS specs, and scaffolds the code they describe.

A plugin for AI-assisted Composer plugin development. Hosts authored DEUS specs (`.mdl` files), couples them to a `CodeProject`, and provides a Coder skill that lets the assistant verify a spec, write source files into the project, and (eventually) dispatch a build agent. The build/sandbox itself is a separate EDGE service (out of scope until phase 2).

Phase 1 shipped: rename, schema, skill scaffold, settings, credential wiring, and stub `verifySpec` / `runBuildAgent` operations.

Phase 1.5 (this PR) adds an in-memory CRUD surface for source files. The agent can scaffold a project, list/read/write/delete files, and call the `introspect-mcp` server to look up DXOS / Composer APIs. All file state is ECHO-canonical — there is no sandbox or build runtime yet. The CodeArticle renders a file tree alongside a CodeMirror editor (via `react-ui-editor`'s `Editor.Root`) so a human can see what the agent is producing.

The plugin reuses `react-ui-editor`'s `Editor.Root` / `Editor.Toolbar` / `Editor.Content` together with the existing `mdl()` CodeMirror extensions instead of a bespoke editor implementation.

## Types

- **type** `Spec` A DEUS spec document.

- **type** `CodeProject` A coding project.

- **type** `SourceFile` A single file in a CodeProject.

- **type** `Settings` Plugin settings (plugin-scoped, not per-space).

## Components

- **component** `CodeArticle` Article surface for a CodeProject.

- **component** `FileTree` Renders a flat list of SourceFile-style entries as a hierarchical tree.

- **component** `SpecArticle` Article surface for a Spec, laid out as an IDE page: the MDL editor beside a panel of views (definitions graph, review, code, decisions, data model, API).

- **component** `CodeSettings` Settings surface contributed via `AppPlugin.addSettingsModule`.

## Services

- **service** `Credentials` Composer credentials API (`@dxos/functions/services/CredentialsService`).

- **service** `BuildAgent` The remote EDGE service that runs the Claude Agent SDK to generate Composer plugins from a Spec.

- **op** `verifySpec` Static verification of a DEUS spec — lint + structural checks.

- **op** `runBuildAgent` Dispatches a build of the project via the EDGE BuildAgent.

- **op** `listFiles` List the source files in a CodeProject (path + size).

- **op** `readFile` Read the content of a single file in a CodeProject.

- **op** `writeFile` Create or overwrite a file in a CodeProject.

- **op** `deleteFile` Remove a file from a CodeProject by path.

- **op** `scaffoldProject` Seed a CodeProject with a minimal Composer plugin scaffold (package.json, src/plugin.ts, README.md).

- **op** `helloWorld` Sanity-check operation.

- **op** `resetProject` Delete every source file in a CodeProject.

- **op** `buildProject` Compile the project's TypeScript sources in-browser.

- **op** `runBuild` Build the project and, on a clean build, execute the entry source on the main thread inside a `console`-capturing wrapper.

- **op** `importSpec` Links a spec file in a local checkout to a Spec, keyed by its source key; returns the existing Spec when one already carries the key (F-14.6).

- **op** `importSpecFile` The import of the `.mdl` FileMapping: creates a Spec for a new file, or applies the remote change to Spec.content with TextMerge.applyAt as of the heads of the last sync.

- **op** `exportSpecFile` The export of the `.mdl` FileMapping: Spec.content as it stands, with the heads it was read at.

- **op** `listLocalSpecs` Lists the `.mdl` specs in every known checkout as source keys, reviews excluded.

## Skills

- **type** `CoderSkill` Skill key `org.dxos.skill.coder`.

pages.title: CommercePlugin
pages.summary: A Composer plugin for structured product search across configurable vendor sites.
pages.content:
A Composer plugin for structured product search across configurable vendor sites. Users configure **Providers** (search site templates), compose a **Search** across one or more of them, and get back a list of **Results**. Providers are authored once — either by the user or via an LLM skill that derives the template by inspecting the vendor site — and reused across many searches.

Supported verticals include retail (products), automotive listings, real estate, or any site whose results can be reached by HTTP GET/POST and parsed from HTML or JSON.

## Types

- **type** `Provider` A configured search site.

- **type** `RequestMapping` Describes how to build the HTTP request from criteria values.

- **type** `FieldBinding` Maps one criteria field to one request parameter with an optional transform hint.

- **type** `ResultMapping` Describes how to extract listing rows from the HTTP response.

- **type** `FieldExtractor` Extracts one field value relative to a located item.

- **type** `Search` A saved search configuration.

- **type** `Result` A single product listing returned by a provider search.

## Components

- **component** `SearchArticle` Master/detail article surface for a Search object.

- **component** `ResultCard` Masonry tile for a single Result.

- **component** `ProviderArticle` Article surface for editing a Provider.

## Services

- **service** `AnalyzeProviderSkill` LLM skill that derives a Provider's template from the live vendor site.

## Operations

- **op** `AnalyzeProvider` Fetches the provider's vendor site via the edge proxy and returns the page HTML/JSON source.

- **op** `SetProviderTemplate` Persists a derived template onto a Provider: sets searchSchema, request mapping, and result mapping in one atomic write.

- **op** `RunProviderSearch` Executes one provider template against a Search's criteria.

- **op** `RunSearch` Fan-out orchestrator.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Provider Templates — Users configure Provider objects with typed search fields and HTTP mappings.
  - `F-1.1` User can create a Provider object via the plugin's create menu.
  - `F-1.2` Provider.kind is 'api' or 'scrape'.
  - `F-1.3` Provider.searchSchema is a JSONSchema describing criteria fields; drives the form.
  - `F-1.4` Provider.request maps criteria values to HTTP request parameters.
  - `F-1.5` Provider.result maps the HTTP response to a list of result rows.
  - `F-1.6` Provider.enabled defaults to true; disabled providers are skipped by RunSearch.

- **feat** `F-2` Skill-Derived Templates — LLM agent derives Provider template from the live site.
  - `F-2.1` AnalyzeProvider fetches the vendor site and returns page source.
  - `F-2.2` SetProviderTemplate persists searchSchema + request + result in one write.
  - `F-2.3` ProviderArticle Analyze button triggers the skill flow.
  - `F-2.4` After SetProviderTemplate, the provider is ready for RunProviderSearch.

- **feat** `F-3` Search Execution — RunSearch fans out to all enabled providers and links results.
  - `F-3.1` SearchArticle toolbar includes a Run Search button.
  - `F-3.2` Clicking Run Search sets Search.status to 'running' and disables the button.
  - `F-3.3` RunSearch invokes RunProviderSearch for each enabled provider in the Search.
  - `F-3.4` Results from all providers are merged into Search.results (refs).
  - `F-3.5` After completion Search.status returns to 'idle' and Search.lastRunAt is set.
  - `F-3.6` Provider failures are non-fatal; the search continues with remaining providers.
  - `F-3.7` Empty Search.providers disables the Run Search button.

- **feat** `F-4` Criteria Form — Dynamic form built from the union of selected providers' search schemas.
  - `F-4.1` SearchArticle computes the union of searchSchema fields from selected providers.
  - `F-4.2` The criteria form renders one input per union field using the field type from JSONSchema.
  - `F-4.3` Range fields (min/max) render as a RangeField component.
  - `F-4.4` Criteria values are stored in Search.criteria keyed by field name.
  - `F-4.5` Changing provider selection recomputes the union; orphaned criteria values are preserved.

- **feat** `F-5` Results Display — Masonry grid of ResultCard tiles; detail pane for selected result.
  - `F-5.1` SearchArticle renders Search.results as a Masonry grid of ResultCard tiles.
  - `F-5.2` Each tile shows the first image (if any), title, price, and key properties.
  - `F-5.3` Clicking a tile opens ResultDetail in a companion/detail pane.
  - `F-5.4` Empty state shown when Search.results is empty.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Create Provider

- **scenario** `T-2` SetProviderTemplate persists template

- **scenario** `T-3` RunProviderSearch skips untemplate'd provider

- **scenario** `T-4` RunSearch fans out and links results

- **scenario** `T-5` RunSearch is non-fatal on provider error

- **scenario** `T-6` Criteria form union

- **scenario** `T-7` Run Search button disabled without providers

---

## Design Notes

### Template Authoring

Provider templates are the central configuration artifact. Two authoring paths exist:

- **Skill path (agent-assisted).** The `AnalyzeProvider` skill fetches the vendor site and derives `searchSchema`, `request`, and `result` mappings via an LLM. The agent uses two tools (`AnalyzeProvider` for fetch, then `SetProviderTemplate` to persist). Triggered from ProviderArticle's Analyze button or via chat.
- **Manual path.** The user edits the raw mappings directly in ProviderArticle. Useful when the vendor site is behind auth or when the user knows the API structure precisely.

### Request Binding

`bindRequest` compiles `RequestMapping` against `Search.criteria` to produce a concrete `{ method, url, headers, body }` request descriptor. Field tokens are resolved from criteria; transforms (`min`, `max`, format templates) are applied at binding time. Unknown criteria keys that don't appear in the mapping are silently ignored.

### Result Extraction

`extractResults` accepts the raw HTTP response body and a `ResultMapping`. For `html` responses, CSS selectors locate items and fields; for `json` responses, JSONPath expressions are used. The result is an array of `ResultData` objects with well-known fields (`title`, `url`, `price`, `currency`, `images`) plus a `properties` bag for extras. Extraction errors for individual items are silently skipped (partial results are better than no results).

### Edge Proxy

All outbound HTTP requests are routed through the DXOS edge proxy via `fetchViaProxy`. This avoids CORS restrictions when searches run client-side and provides a uniform path for rate-limiting or credential injection in a future revision.

### Criteria Union

`buildUnionSchema` computes the union of `searchSchema` fields from the selected providers. Fields with matching names are merged (first-seen type wins). This is how a cross-provider criteria form is possible: providers covering the same vertical tend to share field names (`make`, `model`, `minPrice`, `maxPrice`).

### Scheduleable Searches

`RunSearch` is a pure operation (no UI dependency). It can be invoked by an agent on a schedule — the user creates a Search, configures providers and criteria, and asks the agent to run it periodically. Results accumulate across runs (dedup by URL is an optional future extension).

### Out of Scope

- Result deduplication across providers or runs.
- Authenticated vendor requests (would require credential storage in Provider).
- Pagination — first page only per provider per run.
- Saved result snapshots / history (results are replaced on each run).

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Configure a provider by hand and run a search — The core round-trip without the LLM-derivation path (F-2) — a manually authored 'api' Provider, a Search against it, and a run that produces Results.

pages.title: ConductorPlugin
pages.summary: Visual node-based compute graph plugin for `DXOS` Composer — wire data sources, AI models, logic, and transformations into reactive pipelines that execute in the local-first runtime.
pages.content:
Visual node-based compute graph plugin for `DXOS` Composer — wire data sources, AI models, logic, and transformations into reactive pipelines that execute in the local-first runtime.

## Types

- **type** `ComputeValueType`

- **type** `NodeType`

- **type** `ComputeNode` A node in the compute graph persisted via ECHO.

- **type** `ComputeEdge` A directed edge connecting an output port on one node to an input port on another.

- **type** `ComputeGraph` Persistent ECHO object holding the full node-edge graph plus special I/O reference nodes.

- **type** `ValueBag` A set of named asynchronous value effects passed between nodes.

## Components

- **component** `CanvasArticle` Full-screen canvas editor for a ComputeGraph; renders as an article or a section embed.

## Operations

Pure operations — no effects, no service dependencies.

- **op** `evalConstant` Returns the scalar value stored on a constant node.

- **op** `jsonTransform` Evaluates a JSONPath expression over an input value.

- **op** `boolAnd` Logical AND of two boolean inputs.

- **op** `boolOr` Logical OR of two boolean inputs.

- **op** `boolNot` Logical NOT of a boolean input.

- **op** `ifRoute` Routes a value to the true or false output port based on a condition.

- **op** `ifElseSelect` Ternary — returns trueValue or falseValue depending on condition.

Effectful operations — mutate persistent state or call external services.

- **op** `appendToQueue` Appends items to an ECHO queue or collection identified by DXN.

- **op** `createQueue` Allocates a new append-only Feed and returns a Ref to it.

- **op** `invokeGpt` Sends the current conversation thread to the configured AI model and streams the reply.

- **op** `invokeFunction` Deserialises a PersistentOperation from ECHO and invokes it with the provided input bag.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Canvas Editor
  - `F-1.1` User can create a new compute graph via the "Create object" entry.
  - `F-1.2` Canvas renders nodes as draggable, resizable shapes on an infinite panning surface.
  - `F-1.3` user drags from an output port to an input port → a ComputeEdge is created connecting the two ports
  - `F-1.4` a ComputeEdge is deleted → downstream nodes stop receiving values from the disconnected output

- **feat** `F-2` Node Palette
  - `F-2.1` Toolbar exposes all built-in NodeTypes; user can drag them onto the canvas.
  - `F-2.2` Constant nodes display an inline editor for their scalar value and valueType.
  - `F-2.3` Template nodes render a text input with {{variable}} interpolation.
  - `F-2.4` Function nodes allow selecting a PersistentOperation from the space.

- **feat** `F-3` Reactive Execution
  - `F-3.1` any upstream node value changes → ComputeGraphController re-evaluates dependent nodes in topological order
  - `F-3.2` Node execution is lazy; nodes only run when their outputs are consumed.
  - `F-3.3` a node fails with ConductorError → downstream nodes receive a NotExecuted marker and do not throw
  - `F-3.4` a node emits a ValueBag → individual output ports can resolve at different times (async bag semantics)

- **feat** `F-4` AI Integration
  - `F-4.1` GPT node connects to AiService; configuration includes model, system prompt, and tools.
  - `F-4.2` GPT node executes → op:invokeGpt streams the model response back to the output port
  - `F-4.3` Function node can reference any PersistentOperation registered in the space.

- **feat** `F-5` Data Sources and Sinks
  - `F-5.1` Queue node reads messages from a Feed referenced by DXN.
  - `F-5.2` Append node writes items to a Feed or ECHO collection referenced by DXN.
  - `F-5.3` Database node exposes ECHO space contents as a query tool for AI nodes.
  - `F-5.4` Thread node surfaces a conversation thread with its message history.

- **feat** `F-6` Logic and Control Flow
  - `F-6.1` If node routes a value to true or false output port based on a boolean condition.
  - `F-6.2` IfElse node selects one of two values using a ternary condition.
  - `F-6.3` Reducer node collects an array of values from multiple upstream ports.
  - `F-6.4` And / Or / Not nodes implement standard boolean combinators.

- **feat** `F-7` Persistence and Collaboration
  - `F-7.1` ComputeGraph is stored as an ECHO object; graph topology is replicated to peers.
  - `F-7.2` a peer modifies a node value or edge → all collaborators see the change reflected on the canvas in real time
  - `F-7.3` a CanvasBoard is embedded as a section in another document → the graph renders in the section aspect-square container and remains interactive

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Create empty graph

- **scenario** `T-2` Add constant node and read value

- **scenario** `T-3` Boolean AND gate

- **scenario** `T-4` JSONPath transform

- **scenario** `T-5` GPT node invocation

- **scenario** `T-6` Append to queue

- **scenario** `T-7` Collaborative edit

- **scenario** `T-8` NotExecuted propagation

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Build and run a small compute graph — The core canvas round-trip — create a graph, wire a constant into a JSON transform, and read the reactive result.
- **test** `QA-2` Showcase clip — The 10s showcase clip: Open a new compute circuit.

pages.title: ConnectorPlugin
pages.summary: A Composer plugin that manages connections to external services.
pages.content:
A Composer plugin that manages connections to external services. It stores OAuth credentials and API tokens as `AccessToken` objects in ECHO, organises them into `Integration` records that carry one or more sync targets, and orchestrates the full lifecycle: provider registration, credential acquisition (OAuth popup, redirect-flow, or custom token form), target selection, and incremental sync. Other plugins register themselves as `IntegrationProvider` capability entries; the plugin renders a generic UI that adapts automatically to however many providers are currently loaded.

## Types

- **type** `IntegrationTarget` One sync target row on an Integration.

- **type** `Integration` ECHO-persisted record binding an AccessToken to one or more sync targets.

- **type** `RemoteTarget` Wire shape returned by a provider's getSyncTargets operation.

- **type** `IntegrationOAuthSpec` OAuth flow descriptor contributed on an IntegrationProvider entry.

- **type** `CredentialFormResult` Discriminated result from a provider's credential-form submission.

- **type** `IntegrationProviderEntry` One row contributed to the IntegrationProvider capability registry.

## Components

- **component** `IntegrationArticle` Main surface for a persisted Integration.

- **component** `IntegrationAuthButton` Inline auth trigger contributed via role "integration--auth".

- **component** `SyncTargetsChecklist` Dialog opened after OAuth completes (or on demand) that lists available remote targets returned by the provider's getSyncTargets operation.

- **component** `CustomTokenDialog` Generic provider-form dialog.

## Operations

- **op** `CreateIntegration` Creates a new Integration bound to an existing AccessToken.

- **op** `SetIntegrationTargets` Reconciles an Integration's targets array to match a user-chosen selection.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Provider Registration
  - `F-1.1` Any plugin may contribute one or more IntegrationProviderEntry rows via the IntegrationProvider capability.
  - `F-1.2` The integration UI queries IntegrationProvider at render time; adding or removing a provider plugin updates the list without a build step.
  - `F-1.3` a provider declares oauth → the coordinator routes through the Edge OAuth service using provider.oauth.provider and provider.oauth.scopes
  - `F-1.4` a provider declares credentialForm → the coordinator opens CustomTokenDialog before starting any OAuth flow
  - `F-1.5` a provider declares getSyncTargets → the coordinator opens SyncTargetsChecklist after OAuth completes

- **feat** `F-2` OAuth Popup Flow
  - `F-2.1` user triggers auth for an OAuth provider (no credentialForm or loginHint already supplied) → coordinator calls Edge /oauth/initiate and opens a popup window to the returned authUrl
  - `F-2.2` Edge posts a success message to window.opener → coordinator finalizes the pending entry (persists AccessToken + Integration, runs onTokenCreated)
  - `F-2.3` Edge posts a failure message → pending entry is discarded; no ECHO writes occur
  - `F-2.4` In-memory pending entries are keyed by AccessToken.id; a localStorage snapshot is written for redirect-flow recovery.

- **feat** `F-3` OAuth Redirect Flow
  - `F-3.1` provider declares oauth.useRedirectFlow = true → authUrl is opened in a new browser tab instead of a popup
  - `F-3.2` A PendingSnapshot keyed by accessTokenId is written to localStorage before opening the new tab.
  - `F-3.3` Edge redirects the new tab to /redirect/oauth with accessToken params → the NavigationHandler calls IntegrationCoordinator.finalizeRedirectFlow
  - `F-3.4` finalizeRedirectFlow runs → PendingSnapshot is read from localStorage, AccessToken + Integration are rebuilt, standard finalize path runs
  - `F-3.5` After finalize the PendingSnapshot is deleted from localStorage.

- **feat** `F-4` Custom / Non-OAuth Credentials
  - `F-4.1` provider has no oauth field → coordinator opens CustomTokenDialog (generic raw-token form or provider's credentialForm)
  - `F-4.2` credentialForm.onSubmit returns kind=complete → AccessToken + Integration from the result are persisted directly via createCustomIntegration
  - `F-4.3` credentialForm.onSubmit returns kind=oauth with a loginHint → coordinator re-enters createIntegration with the supplied loginHint and starts the OAuth popup

- **feat** `F-5` Target Selection
  - `F-5.1` a provider has getSyncTargets and OAuth just completed → coordinator invokes getSyncTargets and opens SyncTargetsChecklist with the result
  - `F-5.2` user confirms a selection in SyncTargetsChecklist → op:SetIntegrationTargets is called; added and removed counts are returned
  - `F-5.3` Targets whose remoteId is already present in Integration.targets are preserved with their existing cursor and options.
  - `F-5.4` existingTarget is supplied and at least one new target is added → the first new target's object ref is set to existingTarget

- **feat** `F-6` Integration Persistence and Navigation
  - `F-6.1` finalize completes → AccessToken and Integration are written to ECHO; AccessToken.parent is set to the Integration
  - `F-6.2` Integration is persisted → Composer navigates to the Integration article in the active Deck
  - `F-6.3` onTokenCreated is declared by the provider → it is called once after AccessToken + Integration are persisted, before navigation
  - `F-6.4` onTokenCreated failures are caught and logged; they do not abort the finalize flow.

- **feat** `F-7` Integration Article UI
  - `F-7.1` IntegrationArticle is rendered for any ECHO object of type org.dxos.type.integration via the AppSurface.Article role.
  - `F-7.2` The article lists all Integration.targets with their name, lastSyncAt, and lastError fields.
  - `F-7.3` user clicks "Add targets" → SyncTargetsChecklist opens using the provider's getSyncTargets operation
  - `F-7.4` user clicks "Delete" → the Integration and its AccessToken are removed from ECHO

- **feat** `F-8` Provider Picker in Create Form
  - `F-8.1` The Integration create-object form schema carries IntegrationProviderAnnotationId on its providerId field.
  - `F-8.2` a form-input Surface encounters IntegrationProviderAnnotationId → it renders a SelectField populated from registered IntegrationProvider entries
  - `F-8.3` The dropdown updates live when provider plugins are loaded or unloaded.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` OAuth popup flow creates Integration

- **scenario** `T-2` OAuth callback finalizes Integration

- **scenario** `T-3` OAuth failure discards pending entry

- **scenario** `T-4` Redirect flow recovery

- **scenario** `T-5` Custom token flow

- **scenario** `T-6` SetIntegrationTargets adds and removes

- **scenario** `T-7` Auto-created target preserved by SetIntegrationTargets

- **scenario** `T-8` existingTarget wired to first new target

- **scenario** `T-9` Provider picker reflects live registry

- **scenario** `T-10` onTokenCreated failure does not abort finalize

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Bind an access token to a new Integration and configure targets — plugin-connector is core infrastructure (`getCorePlugins` in composer-app), always active — there is no "enable it first" precondition, unlike a content plugin.

---

pages.title: CrmPlugin
pages.summary: A Composer plugin that contributes a **CRM skill** for researching people and organizations and producing structured Profile documents in the user's space.
pages.content:
A Composer plugin that contributes a **CRM skill** for researching people and organizations and producing structured Profile documents in the user's space. v1 is a library-layer plugin only — no UI surfaces. It is deliberately thin: the heavy lifting (web research, database CRUD, markdown document creation) is reused from existing `@dxos/assistant-toolkit` skills (`research`, `database`, `markdown`). plugin-crm contributes CRM-specific instructions, one relation schema, one image-attachment operation, and a pluggable research-source contract for future extensions (e.g., a LinkedIn browser-extension integration).

Given a reference to a `Person`, `Organization`, or an email `Message`, the skill drives an agent to (a) locate or create the corresponding Person and Organization ECHO objects, (b) produce a markdown Profile document following an editable section template, (c) link the Profile to its subject via a typed `ProfileOf` relation, and (d) attach a best-effort avatar / company-logo image uploaded to the DXOS image service.

## Types

- **type** `ContactExtract` Structured output of the email-signature extractor utility.

- **type** `ProfileOf` ECHO relation linking a Profile Document to its subject (Person or Organization).

- **type** `ResearchSource` Pluggable contract for augmenting the CRM skill with additional research tools.

## Skill

- **skill** `CrmSkill` Composes the CRM operations with the web-search, database, and markdown skills so an agent can maintain Person/Organization records and enrich their Profile documents with researched content.

## Operations

- **op** `attachImage` Downloads an external image URL, re-uploads it to the DXOS image service (POST /thumbnail), and stores the returned canonical URL on the subject's `image` field.

- **op** `processMailbox` Cursored CRM pipeline over a mailbox's message feed.

- **op** `researchPerson` Deterministic profile scaffolding for a Person: creates a markdown Profile skeleton pre-filled from known ECHO data (emails, role, organization link), parents it to the subject, and links it via a ProfileOf relation.

- **op** `researchOrganization` Deterministic profile scaffolding for an Organization; mirrors researchPerson and additionally lists the space's known people at the organization.

## Services

- **service** `ImageService` DXOS EDGE image service.

- **service** `AssistantToolkit` Reused skills and operations from @dxos/assistant-toolkit.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Polymorphic Subject Resolution — The skill accepts a Ref<Person | Organization | Message> and branches deterministically based on the loaded object's typename.
  - `F-1.1` Skill instructions describe how to load the subject via database.load.
  - `F-1.2` Instructions describe the three branches (Person, Organization, Message).
  - `F-1.3` subject is a Message → agent extracts { fullName, email, phone?, orgName?, orgDomain?, locations?
  - `F-1.4` subject is a Person → agent seeds research from Person.fullName, Person.emails, and Person.organization (if set)
  - `F-1.5` subject is an Organization → agent seeds research from Organization.name and Organization.website

- **feat** `F-2` Deterministic Contact Extraction — Contact-extraction semantics are owned by @dxos/extractor-lib (shared with mail sync and plugin-inbox's extractor operations), not by plugin-crm: buildContactFromActor builds the Person, the IdentitySpecs dedupe by norm…
  - `F-2.1` processMailbox delegates to buildContactFromActor with a run-scoped overlay of the space's identity index.
  - `F-2.2` A repeat sender never yields a second Person, whether processed by this operation or by mail sync.
  - `F-2.3` Extraction provenance for feed messages is recorded via Mailbox.recordExtraction (feed items cannot be relation endpoints).
  - `F-2.4` plugin-crm ships no parallel extraction heuristics of its own.

- **feat** `F-3` Person & Organization Upsert — The skill's instructions guide the agent to deduplicate by email and by organization domain/name before creating new objects.
  - `F-3.1` an email address is known → agent queries existing Person objects for emails containing that address
  - `F-3.2` no matching Person exists → agent creates a new Person with extracted fields via database.objectCreate
  - `F-3.3` a matching Person exists → agent updates it via database.objectUpdate with newly discovered fields (non-destructive)
  - `F-3.4` orgDomain or orgName is known → agent queries existing Organization objects by website or name
  - `F-3.5` no matching Organization exists AND domain is not free-mail → agent creates a new Organization
  - `F-3.6` a Person has an Organization → agent ensures Person.organization references the Organization

- **feat** `F-4` Research & Profile Composition — Profile structure is deterministic; profile content is agentic.
  - `F-4.1` The section template is rendered by the research operations, not prose; the agent extends sections rather than creating parallel documents.
  - `F-4.2` Re-running a research operation refreshes ProfileOf.lastResearchedAt and never regenerates the document body.
  - `F-4.3` The "Notes" section records disambiguation hints and uncertainty (e.g., free-mail sender, ambiguous name).
  - `F-4.4` The "Sources" section lists URLs that contributed to the profile, mirrored into ProfileOf.sources.

- **feat** `F-5` ProfileOf Relation — A typed relation links the Profile Document to its subject.
  - `F-5.1` ProfileOf schema is registered into the space's schema registry at plugin init.
  - `F-5.2` a Profile Document is created for a Person → a ProfileOf relation is created with source=Document, target=Person
  - `F-5.3` a Profile Document also covers an Organization → an additional ProfileOf relation is created with target=Organization
  - `F-5.4` Relation carries sources[], lastResearchedAt, and summary.

- **feat** `F-6` Image Attachment — Best-effort avatar / logo retrieval.
  - `F-6.1` attachImage operation uploads via POST /thumbnail and writes the result URL to subject.image.
  - `F-6.2` imageServiceUrl is read from @dxos/config at invocation time.
  - `F-6.3` imageServiceUrl is not configured → operation returns ConfigMissing error; agent continues without image
  - `F-6.4` image upload fails → operation returns a structured error; subject.image is not modified
  - `F-6.5` No fallback search path inside attachImage — the agent is responsible for supplying the URL.

- **feat** `F-7` Pluggable Research Sources — Future sources (notably LinkedIn via browser extension) will register additional tools into the CRM skill.
  - `F-7.1` ResearchSource TypeScript interface is exported from src/sources.
  - `F-7.2` The CRM skill picks up registered sources' tools at skill.make() time.
  - `F-7.3` Skill instructions enumerate the currently-registered sources by id + description so the agent knows what is available.
  - `F-7.4` No ResearchSource is bundled in v1; composer-crx will ship the first one in a later PR.

- **feat** `F-8` Configuration Surface (deferred) — Per-space CrmSettings ECHO type is planned but not implemented in v1.
  - `F-8.1` v1 does NOT ship a CrmSettings schema.
  - `F-8.2` Design allows adding CrmSettings later without breaking API — the attachImage operation reads from Config for now.
  - `F-8.3` No API keys are required to run v1.

- **feat** `F-9` CRM Navigation Section — A top-level "CRM" group in the nav tree surfaces the space's Organizations and People as plain nodes.
  - `F-9.1` A CRM group node (GraphPath.GroupTypes.crm) is contributed per space and hidden when it has no children.
  - `F-9.2` Organizations and People nodes appear under the group only when the space contains objects of that type, mirroring the Database section's natural type folders.
  - `F-9.3` Selecting a node opens plugin-space's generic TypeArticle for the type; CRM contributes no article surface of its own.
  - `F-9.4` TypeArticle offers a Cards (masonry) and Table (DynamicTable) layout switch; selecting an item opens it as a sibling plank.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` ProcessMailbox — gated extraction over the fixture mailbox

- **scenario** `T-2` ProcessMailbox — idempotent and incremental

- **scenario** `T-3` ProcessMailbox — research chain

- **scenario** `T-4` Full-loop playground — corporate short signature (tuning)

- **scenario** `T-5` Full-loop playground — free-mail personal contact

- **scenario** `T-6` Full-loop playground — corporate rich signature

- **scenario** `T-7` attachImage — success path

- **scenario** `T-8` attachImage — config missing

- **scenario** `T-9` Graduation — assistant-e2e suite

---

## Design Notes

### Composition over duplication

plugin-crm is a thin composition layer with a deterministic core. Structural work — contact extraction, dedup, cursoring, profile scaffolding — is done by typed operations that compose existing machinery (`@dxos/extractor-lib` for gate/identity/contact building, `@dxos/link` for the durable feed cursor) rather than reimplementing it or describing it in prose. Content work — web research, dossier writing — remains agent-orchestrated through the `web-search`, `database`, and `markdown` skills from `@dxos/assistant-toolkit`. This means:

- No `search_web` / `fetch_url` tools of plugin-crm's own; enrichment composes existing skills.
- The trigger loop is deterministic: routines bind `process-mailbox` directly, so no model sits between trigger and operation.
- Tuning structural behaviour is a code change with deterministic tests; tuning content behaviour is a prompt change on the (thin) skill instructions.

### LinkedIn / browser extension seam

LinkedIn is out of scope for v1 code. The `ResearchSource` TypeScript interface is defined in `src/sources/research-source.ts`, and the skill's `make()` function iterates over any registered sources and includes their tools in the skill's tool list. No sources are registered by default. The planned future implementation will live in `composer-crx` and communicate with the user's authenticated LinkedIn session via the browser.

### Image attachment — no fallback search

`attach-image` does not itself search for candidate images. The agent finds them (favicon, OG image, public Gravatar, company-website logo) via the web-search skill's `Fetch` operation and `AnthropicWebSearch` tool, then passes the URL to `attach-image`. This keeps the operation small, single-purpose, and mockable in tests.

### Extraction gate

Sender gating is owned by `shouldExtractContact` in `@dxos/extractor-lib` — an allow-list (outbound sender, or domain matches a known Organization; never no-reply/bulk/role mail), shared verbatim with mail sync. This both prevents a "Gmail" Organization from a free-mail sender and prevents automated senders from filling the space with contacts nobody will look at. Deterministic Organization creation from unknown domains is deliberately withheld pending the allow-list rework (sent-mail recipients; tracked in the mailbox-research project).

### Profile section template

The section template is rendered by `renderProfile` in `src/operations/research.ts` (Overview, Details, Organization|People, Key Links, Notes, Sources). The document body is user/agent-owned after creation: re-running a research operation refreshes provenance, never content.

### Testing strategy

Three layers:

1. **Operation tests** (`src/operations/{research,process-mailbox}.test.ts`) — deterministic, CI-on-by-default: the fixture-driven feed → cursor → contact → profile chain, idempotency, and the extraction gate.
2. **Template tests** (`src/templates/*.test.ts`) — scaffold shape of the project/automation templates, including the runnable + feed-trigger wiring.
3. **Graded eval** (`packages/core/compute/assistant-evals/src/evals/crm-mailbox.eval.ts`) — the agentic enrichment path, scored with deterministic DB-effect assertions plus an LLM accuracy judge.

### Out of scope for v1

- Settings panel (no CrmSettings surface).
- `CrmSettings` ECHO type (planned; see F-8).
- Any ResearchSource implementation, including LinkedIn.
- API-keyed search providers (Tavily, Brave, Google CSE, Clearbit, etc.).
- Deduping of multiple Person matches by fuzzy-name — v1 updates the best match or asks the user.
- Image-quality heuristics — v1 accepts whatever candidate URL the agent supplies.

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

plugin-crm is a library-layer plugin with no UI surfaces (see the document intro) — every step is driven through the skill's operations, so a "human" run means a person asking the assistant to do these things in chat, not a navtree gesture. `actors: agent` below reflects that every step has a real `invoke`.

- **test** `QA-1` Research a Person end to end — The core CRM round-trip — create a Person, scaffold and link its Profile, read it back.

- **test** `QA-2` Attach an image to a Person — The image-attachment path — a candidate URL is downloaded, re-hosted, and written to `image`.

---

pages.title: CrxPlugin
pages.summary: Coordinates with the `@dxos/composer-crx` browser extension.
pages.content:
Coordinates with the `@dxos/composer-crx` browser extension. Owns the Composer side of the page-actions bridge: plugins contribute page actions (serializable descriptor + target operation) under a plugin-scoped capability; the extension caches the descriptors in its registry and invokes them over same-origin `window` `CustomEvent`s. This plugin answers registry-list requests, validates invoke requests, resolves the active space, executes the target operation, and surfaces outcomes as toasts. It also contributes three picker actions (Person, Organization, Note) whose operations map a page snapshot to an ECHO object, and owns the user-facing settings surface — including the render-proxy settings (absorbed from the retired plugin-extension) for the extension's page-rendering facility.

The extension owns the DOM picker, popup toolbar, extractors, and bridge sender; this plugin owns envelope validation, snapshot → ECHO object mapping, and user feedback (toast). The extension keeps a hand-validated mirror of the wire types at `packages/apps/composer-crx/src/page-actions/types.ts` which must be updated in lockstep.

## Types

- **type** `Settings` User preferences for extension ↔ Composer coordination, persisted via the app-framework settings store.

- **type** `Source`

- **type** `Selection`

- **type** `Hints` Cheap signals harvested from the whole page at capture time.

- **type** `Snapshot` Generic page capture produced by the extension's `snapshot` extractor.

- **type** `PageActionDescriptor` Serializable descriptor for a plugin-contributed page action, synced to the extension's registry cache.

- **type** `PageAction` A live page-action contribution: the descriptor fields plus the actual operation definition (serialized to its key string when listed).

- **type** `ListRequest` Sent by the extension as `composer:page-actions:list`; acked as `composer:page-actions:list:ack`.

- **type** `ListAck`

- **type** `InvokeRequest` Sent by the extension as `composer:page-action:invoke`; acked as `composer:page-action:invoke:ack`.

- **type** `InvokeAck`

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Settings Capability
  - `F-1.1` plugin is activated → a single `Settings` atom is registered under a plugin-scoped capability
  - `F-1.2` another plugin reads the capability → it receives the current Settings with defaults applied

- **feat** `F-2` Settings Surface
  - `F-2.1` the app-framework settings panel renders the CRX section → a schema-driven form is shown covering all Settings fields, wired to
  - `F-2.2` the user presses the Test connection button → a ping round-trips over the page → content-script → background path and

- **feat** `F-2c` Settings Enforcement
  - `F-2c.1` `enabled` is false and a page-action invoke arrives → no object is created; the request is still acked (so the extension does
  - `F-2c.2` `autoOpenAfterClip` is true and a page action succeeds → the created object is opened via LayoutOperation.Open
  - `F-2c.3` `autoOpenAfterClip` is false (default) → focus is not moved; only the success toast is shown

- **feat** `F-3` Page Action Contributions — Plugins contribute `PageAction[]` under the plugin-scoped `CrxCapabilities.PageAction` capability.
  - `F-3.1` plugin is activated → three picker-only actions are contributed — Person, Organization, and
  - `F-3.2` the extension lists actions → contributions are resolved per-request, so actions from

- **feat** `F-4` Registry Listing
  - `F-4.1` plugin is activated → window event listeners for `composer:page-actions:list` and
  - `F-4.2` a valid list request arrives → the ack carries the currently contributed actions as serializable
  - `F-4.3` a list request fails schema decoding → the ack is { ok: false, error: 'invalidPayload' } with a best-effort

- **feat** `F-5` Invoke Validation & Dispatch
  - `F-5.1` an invoke request's envelope fails decoding → ack is { ok: false, error: 'invalidPayload' } and nothing is invoked
  - `F-5.2` the envelope has a version other than 1 → ack is { ok: false, error: 'unsupportedVersion' } with the request id
  - `F-5.3` the strict payload fails decoding → ack is { ok: false, error: 'invalidPayload' }
  - `F-5.4` `actionId` matches no registered action → ack is { ok: false, error: 'unknownAction' }
  - `F-5.5` the active space cannot be determined → nothing is invoked; ack is { ok: false, error: 'noSpace' }
  - `F-5.6` the request resolves to an action and an active space → the action's operation is invoked with
  - `F-5.7` the operation returns an error or throws → ack is { ok: false, error: 'operationFailed' }

- **feat** `F-6` Snapshot → Object Mapping — Each contributed operation maps a Snapshot to an ECHO object and adds it to the target database via SpaceOperation.AddObject.
  - `F-6.1` AddPersonFromSnapshot is invoked → a Person is created with best-effort fields:
  - `F-6.2` AddOrganizationFromSnapshot is invoked → an Organization is created with best-effort fields:
  - `F-6.3` AddNoteFromSnapshot is invoked → a Markdown document is created with a small prelude (title, source
  - `F-6.4` there is no name/title candidate → the object is still created; empty name is acceptable

- **feat** `F-7` User Feedback
  - `F-7.1` an invoke ack is produced with ok = true → a success toast is shown
  - `F-7.2` an invoke ack is produced with ok = false → an error toast is shown naming the stable error code

- **feat** `F-8` Page Actions Registry & Invocation — Plugins contribute page actions (serializable descriptor + target operation) under a plugin-scoped capability.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Settings atom registered

- **scenario** `T-2` Toggling enabled persists

- **scenario** `T-3` List request returns descriptors

- **scenario** `T-4` Invalid list request is rejected

- **scenario** `T-5` Valid person invoke creates Person

- **scenario** `T-6` Organization mapping falls back to og:title

- **scenario** `T-7` Missing name is allowed

- **scenario** `T-8` Unsupported envelope version

- **scenario** `T-9` Invalid invoke payload is rejected

- **scenario** `T-10` Unknown action

- **scenario** `T-11` No active space

- **scenario** `T-12` Operation failure

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

Note: this document declares no `op` blocks, so the operations below are referenced by their full runtime key rather than `[op:...]` — see `src/types/CrxOperation.ts`.

- **test** `QA-1` Add a Person from a page snapshot — The core snapshot → object mapping (F-6.1), standing in for the browser extension's picker, which an agent cannot drive — the extension is a separate, unautomatable browser process.

- **test** `QA-2` Accept-extension-actions toggle gates invocation — The settings enforcement path (F-2c.1) — no operation exists for the settings atom itself (it is a plain app-framework settings store), so this step is human-only.

---

pages.title: DebugPlugin
pages.summary: Developer debugging utilities for `DXOS` Composer — a debug panel (console, log viewer, and every developer tool as a navtree) docked as the deck's bottom drawer or floated as a window, synthetic-object generation, a per-object Debug companion, a space-objects browser, a wirefra…
pages.content:
Developer debugging utilities for `DXOS` Composer — a debug panel (console, log viewer, and every developer tool as a navtree) docked as the deck's bottom drawer or floated as a window, synthetic-object generation, a per-object Debug companion, a space-objects browser, a wireframe overlay, and a transient-stats panel. The panel is a navtree over a hidden `root/debug` app-graph category that this plugin contributes; the Devtools inspector (`org.dxos.plugin.devtools`) attaches its tree there too. Nothing under `root/debug` appears in the main navtree, opens in the deck, or has a URL.

## Types

- **type** `Settings`

- **type** `DebugPluginOptions`

- **type** `DebugPanelMode`

- **type** `DebugPanelViewState` Persisted (localStorage) so a debugging session survives the reloads it provokes; the floating window's open/closed state is not part of it (the drawer's is deck state).

## App graph

- **feat** `DebugCategory` A hidden `debug` category on the app-graph root: node `root/debug`, type `GraphPath.GroupTypes.debug`, `data: null`, `disposition: hidden`, not draggable or droppable.

| Node                        | Type                | Article                    |
|-----------------------------|---------------------|----------------------------|
| `root/debug/debug`          | `DebugNodes.id`     | branch (no article); open with the console selected on a pristine panel |
| `root/debug/debug/console`  | `DebugNodes.Console`| Console (agent debug shell)|
| `root/debug/debug/logs`     | `DebugNodes.Logs`   | Log viewer                 |
| `root/debug/debug/space`    | `DebugNodes.SpaceType` | Generate objects (active space) |
| `root/debug/devtools/...`   | contributed by `org.dxos.plugin.devtools` | Client / HALO / ECHO / MESH / EDGE inspectors, App Graph, SDK Explorer, CLI |

## Components

- **component** `DebugPanel` The debug surface in parts (`DebugPanel.Root` / `Body` / `Sidebar` / `Main`) with two hosts that share one `Root` context, so selection and open branches carry over when the panel moves: `DebugPanelDrawer` renders it in…

## Features

- **feat** `DebugPanel` A status-bar button shows the debug panel: docked (the default) it toggles the deck's bottom drawer via `LayoutOperation.UpdateDrawer`, so the planks reflow above it, its height is dragged from the top edge and persists…

- **feat** `GenerateObjects` Create configurable batches of synthetic ECHO objects into the active workspace's space, from the Debug → Generate objects page of the panel.

- **feat** `ObjectDebugCompanion` A Debug companion tab on every ECHO object exposing raw field values and DXNs.

- **feat** `SpaceObjectsBrowser` A deck companion listing all objects in the active space with live reactive updates.

- **feat** `Wireframe` Overlay labelled borders around every article and section surface.

- **feat** `StatsPanel` The shared telemetry store (`AppCapabilities.StatsPanel`) as one `StatCard` per plugin compartment.

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

plugin-debug is a dev-only utility plugin: it defaults on in `isDev` builds (see `packages/apps/composer-app/src/plugin-defs.tsx`), off otherwise.

- **test** `QA-1` Insert Lorem ipsum from the slash menu — The one debug feature with a real operation behind it — the MenuExtension contribution used as the worked example in plugin-markdown's QA-3.

- **test** `QA-2` Generate synthetic objects into a collection — The SpaceGenerator UI (GenerateObjects) — no operation exists behind it, so this is a human-only sanity check that the debug tooling itself works.

- **test** `QA-3` Walk the review-queue demo space — The demo script for the Review template (`samples/review`): seed a space holding one project whose finished tasks carry merged dxos/dxos pull requests with their screenshots and demo recordings, and whose tasks in revie…

- **test** `QA-4` Alien Labs — a customer asks for one more thing — The first Alien Labs vignette, a working moment for Astrid Holm, engineering manager.

- **test** `QA-5` Alien Labs — what the agents did this week — The second Alien Labs vignette.

- **test** `QA-6` Alien Labs — the customer pipeline — The third Alien Labs vignette, Alien Labs' accounts as structured data: the CRM section's organizations and people, the pricing sheet behind a quote, and a customer note whose links lead to its contacts.

- **test** `QA-7` Alien Labs — after the incident — The fourth Alien Labs vignette, the documents an incident leaves behind: the postmortem with its timeline sheet embedded, the runbook with its escalation drawing, and the decision log the fix fed.

- **test** `QA-8` Alien Labs — how Cairn plugs into DXOS — The fifth Alien Labs vignette.

- **test** `QA-9` Hello Worker — the agent finishes the spec, plans the work and ships the Worker — The Hello Worker template run on camera.

pages.title: Timeline
pages.summary: A chart of a sheet range with one event per row (date, category, title, description, image), drawn along a vertical spine, kept as its own object so documents can embed it as a section or a slide.
pages.content:
A chart of a sheet range with one event per row (date, category, title, description, image), drawn along a vertical spine, kept as its own object so documents can embed it as a section or a slide.

## Types

- **type** `Chart` A chart of a range of a sheet, owned by the sheet.

- **type** `TimelineSettings` How a timeline chart is drawn.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Chart objects — Each chart is its own object, so a document can embed it.
  - `F-1.1` A sheet holds its charts as refs; each `type:Chart` refs its sheet back and is deleted with it.
  - `F-1.2` Sheets stored with inline charts are migrated to chart objects when their space opens.
  - `F-1.3` A chart renders as an article, a section in a document, and a slide.

- **feat** `F-2` Timeline chart — Events from a sheet range along a vertical spine.
  - `F-2.1` Each row is one event: date, category, title, and an optional description and image URL.
  - `F-2.2` The spine sits left, center or right; spacing is log, linear or compact, animated when it changes.
  - `F-2.3` Categories nest by path (`Tech/AI`) and toggle from tags; ⌘-click shows only one.
  - `F-2.4` Clicking or the arrow keys select an event and show its card; Escape unselects.
  - `F-2.5` A text filter narrows the events and reports how many match.

- **feat** `F-3` Slide embeds — A presented markdown deck shows an embedded object full-viewport.
  - `F-3.1` `![label](echo:…)` in a deck renders the object's slide surface over the whole viewport.
  - `F-3.2` While an embed shows, the deck acts on no key but Escape.

- **feat** `F-4` Presenter space — A space template with an events sheet, its timeline chart, and a deck built from a markdown template.
  - `F-4.1` The deck's `{{timeline}}` placeholder is replaced with the created chart's EID.

F-5, the timeline research skill, is named on the project's feature map and is not written yet: it researches the events for a range of years and a set of categories and fills a sheet with them.

## Phases

- Phase 1: F-1 and F-2, checked against the test fixture (the Presenter space's events sheet).
- Phase 2: F-3 and F-4.
- Phase 3: F-5.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` A timeline chart of the fixture

- **scenario** `T-2` A chart in a slide

One Cloudflare Worker that answers every request with a greeting and the current time, deployed from a sandbox with no Cloudflare account and handed to its reader to claim.

## Types

## Features

pages.title: DeckPlugin
pages.summary: The Deck plugin is the core layout engine for DXOS Composer.
pages.content:
The Deck plugin is the core layout engine for DXOS Composer. It manages the multi-plank workspace ("deck"), the sidebar, the complementary sidebar, the bottom drawer, dialogs, popovers, and toast notifications. It owns the persisted and ephemeral layout state, handles URL routing, and implements every `LayoutOperation` that changes what is visible on screen.

## Types

There is a single deck mode: presentation is derived from plank count and breakpoint rather than stored. On desktop a singleton `active` renders `fullbleed`, exactly two planks render `tiling` (flush proportional split), and three or more render `sliding`; below the `md` breakpoint the deck is always `sliding` with full-viewport-width scroll-snapped planks. Fullscreen is a transient overlay (`EphemeralDeckState.fullscreen`), not a mode.

- **type** `DeckPresentation`

- **type** `PartAdjustment`

- **type** `DeckState`

- **type** `StoredDeckState` Persisted plugin state stored in KVS/localStorage.

- **type** `EphemeralDeckState` Transient plugin state that is NOT persisted across sessions.

- **type** `DeckSettings`

## Components

- **component** `Matrix` The primary workspace canvas.

- **component** `DeckContent` The `Main.Root` host for the whole layout: the navigation and complementary sidebars, the `Main.Content` the deck renders into, and the bottom drawer — a `Main.Drawer` (`@dxos/react-ui`) fixed to the block-end edge betw…

- **component** `DeckSettings` Settings panel rendered in the Composer settings surface.

## Operations

- **op** `Open` Opens one or more subjects (item IDs or navigation paths) in the deck.

- **op** `Close` Removes one or more subjects from the active deck.

- **op** `UpdateSidebar` Update the sidebar visibility state (closed / collapsed / expanded).

- **op** `UpdateDrawer` Open, close, toggle or resize the bottom drawer.

- **op** `UpdateComplementary` Update the complementary-sidebar visibility state and optional panel selection.

- **op** `UpdateDialog` Show or hide the global dialog overlay.

- **op** `UpdatePopover` Show or hide the global popover.

- **op** `UpdateCompanion` Update the companion-pane open state and active variant.

- **op** `AdjustPlank` Apply a PartAdjustment to a specific plank (close, fullscreen, move, companion).

- **op** `UpdatePlankSize` Persist the width of a plank in rem.

- **op** `UpdateTilingSize` Persist the tiling split as the start pane's width in rem (the end pane fills the remainder).

- **op** `AddToast` Push a toast notification into the ephemeral queue.

- **op** `ScrollIntoView` Schedule a subject to be scrolled into view when its plank mounts.

- **op** `SwitchWorkspace` Switch the active workspace deck, persisting the previous workspace ID.

- **op** `RevertWorkspace` Revert to the previously active workspace.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Deck Presentations
  - `F-1.1` the active deck changes length or the breakpoint changes → presentation is derived, never stored — desktop renders fullbleed (1 plank), tiling (2),
  - `F-1.2` presentation is sliding on desktop → planks render side by side in a horizontally scrollable row, separated by a fixed
  - `F-1.3` a sliding plank's width would exceed the viewport minus the space reserved for the other → its width is capped so its controls are never hidden behind pinned spines
  - `F-1.4` a sliding plank is scrolled past a viewport edge → it pins there as a sliver; once the visible sliver narrows below the fold threshold (one
  - `F-1.5` a folded spine is clicked → the plank scrolls smoothly back into view and unfolds
  - `F-1.6` presentation is tiling → planks split the viewport width proportionally with no horizontal overflow or inter-plank
  - `F-1.7` the breakpoint is below `md` (mobile) → planks are fixed full-viewport-width scroll-snap points, not user-resizable; the deck
  - `F-1.8` subject is already present in the active deck → deck is unchanged and the existing plank scrolls into view
  - `F-1.9` viewing plank controls → the reordering controls (increment-start / increment-end) are hidden pending a

- **feat** `F-2` Fullscreen
  - `F-2.1` user triggers AdjustPlank with type=fullscreen for a plank → EphemeralDeckState.fullscreen is set to that plank's id; it fills the viewport headless
  - `F-2.2` user triggers AdjustPlank with type=fullscreen for the currently-fullscreen plank → EphemeralDeckState.fullscreen is cleared and the deck returns to its normal presentation
  - `F-2.3` the app reloads → fullscreen is not restored — it is transient and never persisted or reflected in the URL

- **feat** `F-3` Sidebar & Complementary Sidebar
  - `F-3.1` UpdateSidebar is dispatched with a new state → sidebar transitions between closed / collapsed / expanded and state is persisted
  - `F-3.2` UpdateComplementary is dispatched with a panel → complementary sidebar opens to the specified panel
  - `F-3.3` UpdateDrawer is dispatched with a state or height → the bottom drawer opens, closes, toggles or resizes; `drawerState` and `drawerHeight` are
  - `F-3.4` the drawer is open and the navigation or complementary sidebar changes state → the drawer's inline edges follow the sidebars (it spans the content area between them)
  - `F-3.5` the drawer is open and a plank enters fullscreen → the drawer is hidden for the duration and reappears, at the same height, when fullscreen ends

- **feat** `F-4` Dialog & Popover Overlay
  - `F-4.1` UpdateDialog is dispatched with a subject component → the matching surface is rendered inside the global dialog overlay
  - `F-4.2` UpdatePopover is dispatched with an anchorId → popover is positioned relative to that DOM element
  - `F-4.3` dialog or popover state is set to false → overlay is closed and content is unmounted

- **feat** `F-5` URL Navigation & Deep Linking — The URL is a pair chain (`/w/<workspace>/<key>/<id>/…`) with one pair per plank path segment; id-less keys (singletons like `settings`, `members`) consume no id segment.
  - `F-5.1` app loads with a URL referencing items → DeckPlugin resolves each pair against the declared url mappings and opens the items in
  - `F-5.2` the active deck, attention, or companion selection changes → browser URL is re-serialized from deck.active, appending the attended plank's open
  - `F-5.3` an active plank's node declares no url mapping → it is omitted from the URL and a warning is logged; no fallback representation is
  - `F-5.4` a navigation target cannot be resolved (unknown key, failed resolver, or missing node) → Open operation redirects to a 404 node

- **feat** `F-6` Toast Notifications
  - `F-6.1` AddToast is dispatched → a toast is appended to the queue and displayed for its configured duration
  - `F-6.2` ShowUndo is dispatched → a toast with an undo action is shown; invoking it executes the linked undo operation

- **feat** `F-7` Navigation Model — Interaction model replacing the former `navigationDefault` setting and replace-the-attended-plank behavior.
  - `F-7.1` desktop — user plain-clicks an item in the nav tree → the deck becomes just that plank (fullbleed), unless the item is already open — then the
  - `F-7.2` desktop — user modifier-clicks (or drags) an item from the nav tree → the item is appended to the deck (or inserted at the drop position), scrolled into view,
  - `F-7.3` desktop — user follows an inline reference inside a plank (e.g.
  - `F-7.3a` desktop — user opens an object from a card (a hover card, an object card's title, or its → navigation always adds a new plank beside the card's own plank (Open with disposition 'add'
  - `F-7.4` desktop — user closes a plank → only that plank closes (no cascade); closing the last plank shows the empty state
  - `F-7.5` mobile (PROPOSED, unimplemented) — user navigates from any plank (nav drawer or in-plank link) → the target is pushed after the current plank and slid into view; navigating from
  - `F-7.6` mobile (PROPOSED, unimplemented) — user closes a plank → the plank and every plank after it are popped (the journey stack unwinds)
  - `F-7.7` the attended plank folds to a spine (or leaves the viewport entirely, in the mobile snap → attention moves to the unfolded plank nearest the viewport center; while the attended

- **feat** `F-8` Flat Navigation (breadcrumbs) — The `flatten` setting (on by default) collapses the scrolling deck into a single-plank view whose navigation history is a breadcrumb trail in the heading.
  - `F-8.1` the flatten setting is on → only the current (last) active plank renders — plus its companion — so the deck presents as
  - `F-8.2` the flatten setting is on and the active stack has more than one plank → the earlier entries render as breadcrumbs in the current plank's heading, in stack order,
  - `F-8.3` the flatten setting is on and a breadcrumb is clicked → the deck goes back to that entry, dropping every plank after it (Close on the trailing
  - `F-8.4` the flatten setting is off → the deck renders the full active stack as the scrolling/tiling/fullbleed presentation (F-1),

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Open subject beside an active plank

- **scenario** `T-2` Open with pivot insertion

- **scenario** `T-3` Open already-visible subject

- **scenario** `T-4` Enter fullscreen

- **scenario** `T-5` Exit fullscreen

- **scenario** `T-5a` Toggle and resize the bottom drawer

- **scenario** `T-6` Close plank

- **scenario** `T-7` Toast is shown and dismissed

- **scenario** `T-8` Two planks render tiling with a persisted split ratio

- **scenario** `T-9` Sliding plank folds to a spine

- **scenario** `T-10` Desktop nav-tree click navigates solo

- **scenario** `T-11` Desktop modifier-click appends
- **scenario** `T-11a` Card navigation always adds beside the card's plank (add)
- **scenario** `T-11b` In-plank inline reference follows the deck (auto)

- **scenario** `T-12` Mobile branch from mid-stack pops forward

- **scenario** `T-13` Attention follows scroll with hysteresis

- **scenario** `T-14` Flatten renders the current plank with breadcrumbs

- **scenario** `T-15` Breadcrumb click goes back

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

plugin-deck is core layout infrastructure — it ships with every profile and is never toggled off.

- **test** `QA-1` Open, resize, and close a second plank — The core deck round-trip — open a document beside an existing plank, resize the tiling split, close it.

- **test** `QA-2` Sidebar and companion toggles — The chrome operations outside the deck itself — sidebar visibility and the companion pane.
