pages.title: DeepSeekPlugin
pages.summary: A **headless** Composer plugin that makes [DeepSeek](https://platform.deepseek.com) connectable and runnable.
pages.content:
A **headless** Composer plugin that makes [DeepSeek](https://platform.deepseek.com) connectable and runnable. It has no React/UI surfaces and contributes two things:

1. A **Connector** entry (`source: "deepseek.com"`) with an API-key credential form, so the user connects DeepSeek through the generic `plugin-connector` UI. On submit the key is stored as an `AccessToken` (source `deepseek.com`) plus a `Connection` in ECHO.
2. A **Skill** (`org.dxos.skill.deepseek`, `agentCanEnable: true`) that runs the DeepSeek harness — DeepSeek's own coding agent — inside a `plugin-sandbox` container, with that credential bound to the container by reference.

## Connector

- **feat** `DeepSeekConnector` Contributes a ConnectorEntry via Capability.contribute(Connector, [entry]) on the connector Start activation event (mirrors plugin-ideogram's non-OAuth credentialForm connector).

## Harness skill

- **feat** `DeepSeekSkill` Contributes an AppCapabilities.SkillDefinition.

- **op** `installHarness` Creates a sandbox via op:createSandbox, binds the space's deepseek.com AccessToken to it as the DEEPSEEK_API_KEY credential (by REFERENCE — the sandbox resolves it per exec, so the key never enters an operation result o…

- **op** `runHarness` Runs the harness on a prompt in a provisioned sandbox via op:exec.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Connector builds AccessToken + Connection

- **scenario** `T-2` Empty token rejected

- **scenario** `T-3` Install fails cleanly with no credential

- **scenario** `T-4` The prompt is shell-quoted

## QA

Executable tests against the running app. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Connect DeepSeek with an API key — The whole plugin, end to end — enable it, create a Connection choosing DeepSeek, paste a key, and see the connection listed under the space's Connections.

- **test** `QA-2` Run the harness in a sandbox — The skill end to end — provision a sandbox against a connected DeepSeek account and run the harness on a trivial prompt.

## Out of scope (v1)

- Any in-browser DeepSeek API client / model provider; the harness runs in the sandbox.
- OAuth (DeepSeek uses a static API key).
- Multi-account configuration.
- Streaming harness output; a run returns once, when the command exits.
- Pinning the harness CLI's distribution. The npm package and binary names are constants with per-call overrides (`harnessPackage`, `harnessBin`) precisely because DeepSeek's CLI release channel is not something this plugin can guarantee.

pages.title: DevShellPlugin
pages.summary: Proof-of-concept, dev-only coding harness for Composer ("Dev Shell"): a bash tool and a multi-string-replace edit tool, carried by a single vite server route (`vite dev` or `vite preview`) that runs a shell script under a configured root.
pages.content:
Proof-of-concept, dev-only coding harness for Composer ("Dev Shell"): a bash tool and a multi-string-replace edit tool, carried by a single vite server route (`vite dev` or `vite preview`) that runs a shell script under a configured root. Nothing is mounted outside a vite server.

In a browser it also contributes the browser version of plugin-projects' **Composer Plugin** project template: a project whose agent uses these tools to build a TypeScript Composer plugin on this machine and offer it back to load (QA-2). The desktop app has no vite server, so it offers plugin-projects' own version instead.

## Operations

- **op** `bash` Runs a shell script under the harness root and returns its output.

- **op** `edits` Applies a batch of exact find/replace edits to files; all-or-nothing.

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Run a shell command and apply an edit — The plugin has no ECHO types and no navtree/article surface — it is two raw tools (`bash`, `edits`) exposed to the assistant.

- **test** `QA-2` Build a plugin with an agent from the Composer Plugin project template — The demo script for the Composer Plugin project template (`src/templates/composer-plugin.ts`): an agent works one parent task and its four subtasks on this machine — read the guide, write a TypeScript plugin, typecheck…

pages.title: DevtoolsPlugin
pages.summary: Developer inspector plugin for `DXOS` Composer — structured devtools panels for Client/HALO/ECHO/Mesh/EDGE subsystems, an app-graph inspector, and a tools explorer.
pages.content:
Developer inspector plugin for `DXOS` Composer — structured devtools panels for Client/HALO/ECHO/Mesh/EDGE subsystems, an app-graph inspector, and a tools explorer. The tree attaches to the hidden `root/debug` app-graph category (`AppNodeMatcher.whenDebugGroup`) and is reached only through the floating debug panel that `@dxos/plugin-debug` renders from the status bar — never the main navtree, the deck, or a URL. Debugging utilities (object generation, wireframe overlays, per-object inspection, stats) live in the sibling `@dxos/plugin-debug`.

## Types

- **type** `Settings`

- **type** `DebugPluginOptions`

- **type** `DebugContextType`

## Components

- **component** `DebugSettings` Settings panel rendered in the plugin-settings article slot; controls wireframe and traceAll toggles and exposes log download.

- **component** `DebugStatus` Status-indicator surface shown in the main toolbar; reflects the generator timer running state.

- **component** `DevtoolsOverviewContainer` The "Stats" deck companion: polls the client's stats once (`useStats`) and renders `StatsPanel` (`@dxos/devtools`) — a toolbar with refresh and live toggle over a scrolling stack of cards — with one `AppSurface.Devtools…

- **component** `DebugObjectPanel` Companion panel for any ECHO object that shows raw field values, type info, and DXN.

- **component** `DebugSpaceObjectsPanel` Deck-companion panel listing all objects in the active space with their type, ID, and field count.

- **component** `DebugGraph` Visual representation of the Composer app-graph as a collapsible JSON tree.

- **component** `SpaceGenerator` Article view for generating synthetic ECHO objects into a space; controls count, type mix, and relation density.

- **component** `Wireframe` Transparent overlay that wraps any article or section surface and renders a labelled border for layout debugging.

- **component** `SchemaTable` Tabular display of all registered ECHO schemas with typename, fields, and version.

- **component** `GithubPanel` Developer panel linking to open GitHub issues and CI run status for the current build.
```

## Components (Devtools Panels)

The following components are thin wrappers around `@dxos/devtools` panel components, each bound to a specific `Devtools.*` node:

| Component              | Devtools node              | Displays                                |
|------------------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| ConfigArticle            | Client.Config              | Vault config JSON viewer                |
| StorageArticle           | Client.Storage             | Local storage browser                   |
| LoggingArticle           | Client.Logs                | Live log stream; download via logStore  |
| DiagnosticsArticle       | Client.Diagnostics         | Client health / metric charts           |
| IdentityArticle          | Halo.Identity              | Local identity key + device list        |
| DeviceListArticle        | Halo.Devices               | All devices paired with this identity   |
| KeyringArticle           | Halo.Keyring               | Raw keyring entries                     |
| CredentialsArticle       | Halo.Credentials           | Credentials held in the active space    |
| SpaceListArticle         | Echo.Spaces                | All spaces with state + select action   |
| SpaceInfoArticle         | Echo.Space                 | Selected space feeds / pipelines        |
| FeedsArticle             | Echo.Feeds                 | Feed entries for the active space       |
| ObjectsArticle           | Echo.Objects               | All objects in the active space         |
| SchemaArticle            | Echo.Schema                | Schemas registered in the active space  |
| AutomergeArticle         | Echo.Automerge             | Automerge document internals            |
| QueuesArticle            | Echo.Queues                | Pending queue items                     |
| MembersArticle           | Echo.Members               | Space members with last-seen            |
| MetadataArticle          | Echo.Metadata              | Space/feed metadata blobs               |
| SignalArticle            | Mesh.Signal                | Signal-server connection state          |
| SwarmArticle             | Mesh.Swarm                 | Active swarm peers                      |
| NetworkArticle           | Mesh.Network               | Full network topology for active space  |
| AgentHaloArticle         | Agent.Halo                 | An agent's HALO, read from EDGE         |
| EdgeDashboardArticle     | Edge.Dashboard             | EDGE node health / worker stats         |
| WorkflowArticle          | Edge.Workflows             | Workflow definitions in active space    |
| InvocationTraceContainer | Edge.Traces              | Invocation trace timeline from feed     |
| TestingArticle           | Edge.Testing               | Integration test harness for EDGE       |
| ToolsExplorer          | ToolsExplorer              | MCP-backed tools explorer               |

## Operations

No first-party operations are defined by DebugPlugin. The plugin invokes `SpaceOperation.AddObject`, `SpaceOperation.Migrate`, `LayoutOperation.Open`, and `ScriptOperation.CreateScript` from other plugins via `useOperationInvoker` inside its surfaces.

## Features

```mdl
feat F-1: Devtools Graph Node

  req F-1.1:
    when: DevtoolsPlugin is loaded
    then: a "DevTools" branch (`root/debug/devtools`) appears under the hidden `root/debug` category, listed in the floating debug panel's sidebar after Console and Logs

  req F-1.2: The DevTools branch contains sub-trees for Client, HALO, ECHO, MESH, Agent, and EDGE categories, plus App Graph, SDK Explorer, and CLI pages.
  req F-1.3: An app-graph sub-node renders DebugGraph rooted at the graph root.

  req F-1.7: Agent › HALO (AgentHaloArticle) lists the agents the viewer administers: those whose default space (`AppSpace.AGENT_SPACE_TAG`) the client holds with the viewer as an ADMIN or EDITOR member. For the one picked it reads the agent's HALO from EDGE through the client's `client.edge.http` (`GET /compute/brain/:did/halo`), since no client replicates an agent's HALO: its identity, admins and spaces as JSON, or every credential in the HALO in the table HALO › Credentials uses. EDGE answers the agent's admins only, and its refusal shows as `error`.
```

- **feat** `F-2` Object Debug Companion

pages.title: DiscordPlugin
pages.summary: A Composer plugin that connects a Discord bot to a workspace so that server channels stream alongside everything else the user is working on.
pages.content:
A Composer plugin that connects a Discord bot to a workspace so that server channels stream alongside everything else the user is working on. Messages from every guild the bot belongs to are synced into ECHO as `@dxos/types` `Message` objects inside `Channel` feeds — fully local-first and replicated to all peers.

## Types

- **type** `RemoteTarget` Wire shape returned by GetDiscordChannels representing one Discord text channel.

- **type** `DiscordTargetOptions` Per-target sync options stored under IntegrationTarget.options and edited from the Integration UI.

- **type** `PullResult` Summary of a completed incremental sync for one target channel.

- **type** `DiscordChannel` Config of a Discord-backed Channel (`Channel.backend.config`, backend kind `org.dxos.channel.backend.discord`): the bot that posts and the Discord channels it listens in.

- **type** `ShowAndTellEntry` One link shared in a show-and-tell channel; a row of the space's show-and-tell table.

## Services

- **service** `DiscordREST` dfx DiscordREST service layer.

## Operations

- **op** `GetDiscordChannels` Discovery only.

- **op** `MaterializeDiscordTarget` Find-or-create the empty local feed-backed Channel for a selected Discord channel, keyed by the Discord channel id, so a sync cursor can reference it.

- **op** `SyncDiscordChannel` Pull-only incremental sync for every Discord target bound to a Connection.

- **op** `FileLinks` Files every link of one shared message as a ShowAndTellEntry: each link in the message text, in order, then the links the model lists that the text does not hold (attachments).

- **op** `ListLinks` The entries shared in a period (this-week by default, last-week, this-month or all; weeks start Monday, UTC), optionally of one author or category, oldest first, with a Markdown digest: one section per author, the most…

- **op** `EnableShowAndTell` Makes an agent the show-and-tell curator of one Discord channel: adds the channel id to the config's channels and curate lists, creates the agent's Show-and-tell mode (binding the curator skill) when it has none, and sw…

## Channel backend

- **service** `DiscordChannelBackend` plugin-thread `ChannelBackendProvider` for Discord channels, so agents and other callers reach Discord through plugin-thread's generic channel operations rather than Discord-specific ones.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Bot Identity and Credential Setup
  - `F-1.1` User provides a bot token from the Discord developer portal via the credential form.
  - `F-1.2` user submits the credential form → token is validated against GET /users/@me before any Integration is persisted
  - `F-1.3` token is valid → bot's display name (global_name ??
  - `F-1.4` AccessToken is stored in ECHO and referenced by the Integration; the raw token is never re-exposed after setup.

- **feat** `F-2` Channel Discovery
  - `F-2.1` user opens the Integration target picker → op:GetDiscordChannels is invoked and returns one entry per reachable text/announcement channel
  - `F-2.2` Entries are labeled "#channel — Guild" to disambiguate channels with identical names across guilds.
  - `F-2.3` a guild's channel list cannot be fetched (bot removed, network error) → that guild's channels are omitted from results; other guilds are unaffected
  - `F-2.4` User selects one or more channels as Integration targets; unselected channels leave no trace in the space.

- **feat** `F-3` Incremental Message Sync
  - `F-3.1` op:SyncDiscordChannel is invoked for an Integration → for each selected target channel, messages newer than target.cursor are fetched and appended
  - `F-3.2` a target has no cursor (first sync) → lookback window is determined by DiscordTargetOptions.maxDays (default 30, max ~3 years)
  - `F-3.3` sync succeeds for a target → target.cursor advances to the newest message snowflake id seen; subsequent runs are incremental
  - `F-3.4` sync fails for a target → target.lastError is set with a human-readable description; other targets continue unaffected
  - `F-3.5` System messages (joins, pins, calls) are filtered out; only DEFAULT (type 0) and REPLY (type 19) messages are stored.
  - `F-3.6` Discord bot replies carry the referenced message id in Message.threadId to enable reply-chain reconstruction.

- **feat** `F-4` Channel Materialization
  - `F-4.1` a target channel is synced for the first time → a local ECHO Channel keyed by the Discord channel snowflake id is created in the space
  - `F-4.2` Channel keying uses Obj.Meta foreign-key [{source: 'discord.com', id: channelSnowflakeId}]; re-running sync on the same channel is idempotent.
  - `F-4.3` the channel's name changes on Discord → the local Channel.name is updated to the "#channel — Guild" label on the next sync
  - `F-4.4` a target ref exists from a legacy integration (remoteId not set) → the Discord channel id is recovered from the Channel's foreign-key metadata rather than the target entry

- **feat** `F-5` ECHO Persistence and Replication
  - `F-5.1` Each synced Message is appended to the Channel's ECHO Feed via Feed.append.
  - `F-5.2` a peer receives a Message-feed update → the channel's message list reflects the new messages without additional sync
  - `F-5.3` All ECHO mutations (Channel creation, Message append, cursor update) are transacted per-target so a mid-sync crash cannot leave the space in a partially-updated state.

- **feat** `F-6` Show-and-tell Curator
  - `F-6.1` A team commits one Discord channel to demos and links; an agent bound to it files each shared demo or link and summarizes what everybody shared.
  - `F-6.2` a top-level message in a channel listed in DiscordChannel.curate has a link or an attachment and does not address the agent → EDGE submits it to the agent with `addressed: curate` in its header, and the agent calls op:F…
  - `F-6.3` Each shared link becomes one ShowAndTellEntry (date, author, link, title, category, summary); the same link in the same message is filed once.
  - `F-6.4` someone asks the agent what was shared or done in a period ("what did we do this week?") → the agent calls op:ListLinks and replies with a summary drawn only from the entries returned
  - `F-6.5` op:EnableShowAndTell switches the curator on for one channel; removing the channel from DiscordChannel.curate switches it off.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Valid bot token accepted

- **scenario** `T-2` Invalid token rejected

- **scenario** `T-3` Channel discovery lists all guilds

- **scenario** `T-4` Channel discovery skips failed guild

- **scenario** `T-5` First sync materializes channel and appends messages

- **scenario** `T-6` Incremental sync fetches only new messages

- **scenario** `T-7` System messages filtered out

- **scenario** `T-8` Sync failure recorded per target

- **scenario** `T-9` Channel re-sync is idempotent

- **scenario** `T-10` maxDays controls initial lookback

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

plugin-discord is not in `getDefaults` or the dev-only default set (see `packages/apps/composer-app/src/plugin-defs.tsx`) — it is OFF by default. Its whole surface depends on a real Discord bot token, which no agent session holds, so the credential and discovery steps are `blocked` per Execution Rule 9; only the sync step, given a pre-existing Integration, can run unattended.

- **test** `QA-1` Connect a bot and sync a channel — The core Discord round-trip — add the credential, discover channels, select one, sync messages.

- **test** `QA-2` Re-sync is idempotent — The incremental-sync guarantee (F-3.3, F-4.2) against an Integration that already exists — still requires a live bot token, so this is also blocked absent one, but is written separately since it exercises different requ…

pages.title: DoctorPlugin
pages.summary: Self-introspection skill for Composer.
pages.content:
Self-introspection skill for Composer. Contributes one AI tool, `queryComposerLogs`, that reads the browser tab's own NDJSON log store (populated by `@dxos/log-store-idb`) and lets the assistant filter, project, aggregate, and count entries.

## Operations

- **op** `queryComposerLogs` Query the local browser tab's own NDJSON log store.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Self-introspection from skill
  - `F-1.1` assistant has the Doctor skill loaded → queryComposerLogs is offered as a tool
  - `F-1.2` filters are passed → tokens are normalized (`!foo` → `-foo:trace`) and grouped via
  - `F-1.3` messageRegex is passed alongside grep → messageRegex matches against record.m; grep matches against the
  - `F-1.4` since / until are passed → bounds are inclusive; both ISO strings and epoch ms are accepted
  - `F-1.5` select is passed → emitted entries (and aggregate=sample buckets) include only the
  - `F-1.6` groupBy is set → output contains `groups`, sorted by count desc, capped at topK;
  - `F-1.7` aggregate=firstLast → each bucket carries `first` and `last` ISO timestamps drawn from
  - `F-1.8` format=pretty → entries are space-separated strings matching scripts/query-logs.mjs
  - `F-1.9` limit, topK, or sampleSize exceed hard caps (1000/1000/25) → values are clamped and `truncated` is set if the source had more

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-2` Top messages by frequency

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

plugin-doctor is not in `getDefaults` or the dev-only default set (see `packages/apps/composer-app/src/plugin-defs.tsx`) — it is OFF by default. It contributes no UI surface at all, only the `queryComposerLogs` tool, so the test is a single agent-invoked query.

- **test** `QA-1` Query the browser tab's own log store — The plugin's entire surface — ask the assistant a question that requires reading its own NDJSON log store back.

pages.title: ExplorerPlugin
pages.summary: An interactive hypergraph visualization plugin for `DXOS` Composer that reveals relationships between objects in a workspace.
pages.content:
An interactive hypergraph visualization plugin for `DXOS` Composer that reveals relationships between objects in a workspace. The plugin renders a live `Graph` object — backed by a `View` and a `QueryAST` query — through four switchable layout variants: force-directed, radial cluster, edge bundling, and lattice. Node colours are derived from ECHO object types; hovering a node triggers an anchor-card preview.

## Types

- **type** `QueryInput`

- **type** `GraphObject` ECHO-persistent object that describes a hypergraph visualisation session.

- **type** `ExplorerVariant`

## Components

- **component** `ExplorerArticle` Top-level article / section surface for a Graph object.

- **component** `Visualization` Internal component that owns a single persistent SVG.Graph mount.

## Operations

- **op** `createGraph` Creates a new Graph object scoped to a target space or collection.

- **op** `buildFilter` Compiles a raw query string into a Filter via QueryBuilder.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Graph Object
  - `F-1.1` A Graph object stores a name, a View ref, and a compiled QueryAST.
  - `F-1.2` user creates a new graph → op:createGraph derives a ViewModel from the chosen typename and writes the Graph to ECHO
  - `F-1.3` Graph is persisted → it appears in the space object list and can be opened as an article

- **feat** `F-2` Live Graph Model
  - `F-2.1` ExplorerArticle mounts with a valid Graph subject → SpaceGraphModel is opened against the subject's database
  - `F-2.2` user types a query in the toolbar → op:buildFilter compiles the raw string; model.setFilter applied; SVG re-renders
  - `F-2.3` Graph is unmounted → SpaceGraphModel is closed and all subscriptions released
  - `F-2.4` an ECHO object in the database changes → SpaceGraphModel emits an update and SVG.Graph re-renders without full remount

- **feat** `F-3` Visualization Variants
  - `F-3.1` variant tab is selected → Visualization swaps projector; previous node x/y seed the new projector so positions tween
  - `F-3.2` variant is force → SVG.Zoom wrapper is mounted enabling pan/zoom drag interaction
  - `F-3.3` variant is cluster or bundle → no SVG.Zoom wrapper; leaves grouped by typename; radial labels fade in after tween
  - `F-3.4` variant is lattice → nodes rendered as small rounded rectangles sorted by typename then label
  - `F-3.5` variant is cluster and user clicks a root or group node → subtree toggles collapsed/expanded via GraphClusterProjector.toggleCollapsed

- **feat** `F-4` Node Interaction
  - `F-4.1` pointer enters a node → DxAnchorActivate event dispatched with the object's DXN and label, kind: card
  - `F-4.2` pointer leaves a node → DxAnchorActivate cleared (onNodeHover called with null)
  - `F-4.3` node has no underlying ECHO object (synthetic root / group) → no preview dispatched; node rendered in neutral colour

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Graph creation

- **scenario** `T-2` Article mounts model

- **scenario** `T-3` Variant switch preserves positions

- **scenario** `T-4` Query filter updates graph

- **scenario** `T-5` Node hover preview

- **scenario** `T-6` Lattice sort order

- **scenario** `T-7` Model closed on unmount

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

plugin-explorer is not in `getDefaults` or the dev-only default set (see `packages/apps/composer-app/src/plugin-defs.tsx`) — it is OFF by default. Neither `createGraph` nor `buildFilter` is a registered runtime `Operation` (no `DXN.make` key exists in `src/`) — creation goes through the generic `CreateObjectEntry` capability (`src/capabilities/create-object.ts`), a UI-driven path with no operation key to invoke, and the query editor calls `buildFilter` as a plain in-process function. Both steps are human-only.

- **test** `QA-1` Create a Graph and switch layout variants — The core explorer round-trip — create a Graph object, watch it render, switch between layout variants.
- **test** `QA-2` Showcase clip — The 10s showcase clip: Pan a graph of the space.

pages.title: FileSystemPlugin
pages.summary: - **plugin** `FileSystemPlugin` Opens local directories as workspaces and gives every plugin local file access.
pages.content:
- **plugin** `FileSystemPlugin` Opens local directories as workspaces and gives every plugin local file access.

A native filesystem plugin for `DXOS` Composer that lets users open local directories as workspaces on the desktop. Markdown files and images inside the directory are surfaced in the app graph alongside ECHO objects. Changes to files on disk are reflected in real time; edits made in Composer are persisted back to disk. Requires the Electron-based Composer desktop app — the plugin is not available in browser builds.

## Types

- **type** `FileSystemFile` A single file tracked by the plugin.

- **type** `FileSystemDirectory` A directory node.

- **type** `FileSystemEntry` Union of file and directory nodes.

- **type** `FileSystemWorkspace` A top-level directory opened by the user.

- **type** `FileSystemState` Plugin-level reactive atom that tracks all open workspaces.

## Components

- **component** `WorkspaceSettings` Settings surface for a FileSystemWorkspace.

## Services

- **service** `FileSystem` Local files by absolute path, for any plugin: workspaces opened here, spec sync in plugin-code, and general dev work on a checkout.

## Operations

- **op** `openDirectory` Presents the OS directory-picker dialog, reads the selected directory tree, and registers a new FileSystemWorkspace in the plugin state atom.

- **op** `closeDirectory` Removes the workspace from the plugin state atom and persists the change.

- **op** `refreshDirectory` Re-scans the directory at the workspace's stored path and updates the children tree in the state atom.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Open Workspace
  - `F-1.1` An "Open Folder" action is registered as a primary app graph action.
  - `F-1.2` user activates the action → OS directory picker is presented
  - `F-1.3` user selects a directory → directory tree is scanned (markdown + image files); workspace added to state
  - `F-1.4` the directory path was already open → the existing workspace entry is replaced (idempotent)
  - `F-1.5` op:openDirectory succeeds → layout navigates to the workspace root node

- **feat** `F-2` Close Workspace
  - `F-2.1` user invokes Close Folder → workspace is removed from plugin state and from the navtree
  - `F-2.2` The underlying directory on disk is not modified.
  - `F-2.3` State is persisted after removal so the workspace does not reappear on reload.

- **feat** `F-3` Refresh Workspace
  - `F-3.1` user invokes Refresh Folder on a workspace node → directory is re-scanned; children tree updated
  - `F-3.2` Files open in the editor are not force-closed during refresh.

- **feat** `F-4` App Graph Integration
  - `F-4.1` Each FileSystemWorkspace appears as a root navtree node.
  - `F-4.2` Each subdirectory appears as a branch node under its parent.
  - `F-4.3` Each markdown file appears as a Text-typed leaf node backed by an ECHO Text object.
  - `F-4.4` a markdown file is modified via the Composer editor → the edit is written back to disk
  - `F-4.5` Image files are ignored in the current implementation.
  - `F-4.6` Workspace ordering is persisted via the ECHO personal-space shared order array.

- **feat** `F-5` Markdown Integration
  - `F-5.1` The plugin registers a Markdown extension so files opened from a workspace
  - `F-5.2` a markdown file node is activated → the file content is loaded into an ECHO Text object and displayed in the editor
  - `F-5.3` a markdown file is not yet bound to a Text object (pending state) → a placeholder node is shown with the file name and icon

- **feat** `F-6` Workspace Settings
  - `F-6.1` Each workspace exposes a "General" settings sub-node in the navtree.
  - `F-6.2` The settings article renders a WorkspaceSettings form.
  - `F-6.3` user renames the workspace → the navtree label updates immediately

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Open a directory

- **scenario** `T-2` Idempotent open

- **scenario** `T-3` Close workspace

- **scenario** `T-4` Refresh workspace

- **scenario** `T-5` Markdown file editing

- **scenario** `T-6` Workspace ordering persisted

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Open, refresh and close a workspace — The core filesystem round-trip — open a local directory, see it reflected in the navtree, close it.

pages.title: FilePlugin
pages.summary: FilePlugin enables DXOS Composer to store and preview binary files — images, videos, and PDFs — as first-class ECHO objects.
pages.content:
FilePlugin enables DXOS Composer to store and preview binary files — images, videos, and PDFs — as first-class ECHO objects. A File object's `data` field is a reference to a `Blob` ECHO object (defined in `@dxos/echo`), which abstracts where the bytes actually live and how they're read. Uploads are routed through a pluggable storage system: the built-in `inline` storage embeds bytes on the Blob object itself, while external storage (e.g. WNFS, edge) can be contributed by other plugins by registering a `BlobBackend` on the ECHO Hypergraph. `Blob.url`/`Blob.read` resolve a renderable URL or raw bytes uniformly regardless of backend, so the File schema and preview surfaces stay backend-agnostic without a dedicated URL-resolver capability.

## Types

- **type** `File` ECHO object (typename org.dxos.type.file, version 0.2.0) representing an uploaded binary asset.

- **type** `BackendDescriptor` UI-facing descriptor for a registered storage option.

- **type** `Settings` Per-user plugin settings stored in the ECHO space.

## Components

- **component** `Preview` Composite preview of a file's content, in Radix parts.

- **component** `FileInput` Drag-and-drop / browse file picker used inside the Create Object form.

- **component** `FileSettings` Plugin settings panel rendered in the Composer settings surface.

- **component** `FileArticle` Full-viewport article container rendered for article, section, and slide roles.

## Operations

- **op** `Create` Resolves the MIME type to store (FileLimits.toStoredMimeType), resolves the active BackendDescriptor, and composes File.fromBytes (which hashes/uploads the bytes via the Blob API and adds the resulting Blob to the datab…

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` File upload
  - `F-1.1` Every MIME type MUST be accepted, including an absent one.
  - `F-1.2` Maximum upload size MUST be 4 MB when the resolved backend's storage
  - `F-1.3` user submits the Create Object form with a valid file → - op:Create is invoked with the selected file and active database
  - `F-1.4` file MIME type is unrecognized or empty (e.g.
  - `F-1.5` file size exceeds the limit and the resolved backend's storage is 'inline' → FileTooLargeError returned; no ECHO write occurs

- **feat** `F-2` Backend capability system
  - `F-2.1` Any plugin may contribute a BackendDescriptor capability.
  - `F-2.2` The inline BackendDescriptor MUST always be registered by FilePlugin
  - `F-2.3` The active backend is determined by Settings.backend.
  - `F-2.4` A BackendDescriptor's `storage` names the Blob storage used by

- **feat** `F-3` File preview
  - `F-3.1` FileArticle MUST resolve a renderable URL via Blob.url before
  - `F-3.2` Preview.Content MUST render the appropriate element for each MIME
  - `F-3.4` A PDF MUST render every page, not one at a time.
  - `F-3.5` Rendering MUST be cancelled before the document is torn down.
  - `F-3.3` FileArticle surfaces are registered for article, section,

- **feat** `F-4` Markdown integration
  - `F-4.1` A Markdown extension contributed at MarkdownEvents.SetupExtensions

- **feat** `F-5` Settings
  - `F-5.1` The Settings panel MUST list all registered BackendDescriptor
  - `F-5.2` Selecting a backend MUST persist the choice to Settings.backend

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Upload image inline

- **scenario** `T-2` Reject oversized file

- **scenario** `T-3` Store an unrecognized MIME type

- **scenario** `T-4` Preview inline image

- **scenario** `T-5` Preview PDF

- **scenario** `T-6` Backend fallback to the default storage

- **scenario** `T-7` External blob resolved via a registered BlobBackend's getUrl

- **scenario** `T-8` External blob without getUrl falls back to reading bytes

- **scenario** `T-9` No backend error

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

plugin-file is on by default (`FilePlugin.meta.profile.key` is in `getDefaults`; see `packages/apps/composer-app/src/plugin-defs.tsx`).

- **test** `QA-1` Upload an image and preview it — The core file round-trip — upload an inline image via the Create Object form, place it, and read the preview back.

- **test** `QA-2` Reject an oversized upload — The rejection path (F-1.5) — a validation round-trip that must leave no ECHO write behind.

pages.title: FreeqPlugin
pages.summary: A Composer plugin that integrates freeq — an IRCv3-over-WebSocket chat service that authenticates users via AT Protocol / Bluesky identities — as a live channel backend for the DXOS Composer thread plugin.
pages.content:
A Composer plugin that integrates freeq — an IRCv3-over-WebSocket chat service that authenticates users via AT Protocol / Bluesky identities — as a live channel backend for the DXOS Composer thread plugin. The plugin connects to a freeq server over WebSocket, authenticates using the ATPROTO-CHALLENGE SASL mechanism, joins an IRC channel, streams inbound messages in real time, and sends outbound messages from the Composer composer. Messages are transient: live messages are held in memory for the session and channel history is backfilled from freeq's read-only REST API on join. A single WebSocket is shared across every Composer channel that targets the same server and identity.

The `FreeqChannel` schema, the shared `ConnectionManager` capability, and the live `ChannelBackend` capability are implemented. Authenticated send is validated against the freeq reference client but not yet confirmed against a server that accepts app-password `pds-session` SASL tokens; v1 ships read-capable, with guest (unauthenticated) channels supported end-to-end.

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Join a guest channel and read backfilled history — The plugin's only user-visible surface — plugin-thread renders a Channel whose `backend.config` is a FreeqChannel; freeq itself contributes no app graph action, no create operation, and no runtime operation of any kind…

pages.title: GamePlugin
pages.summary: A generic game host plugin for `DXOS` Composer that provides shared infrastructure for multi-player, local-first turn-based games.
pages.content:
A generic game host plugin for `DXOS` Composer that provides shared infrastructure for multi-player, local-first turn-based games. Variant plugins (e.g. plugin-chess, plugin-tictactoe) contribute a `GameVariant` capability and game-specific surfaces; plugin-game supplies the `Game` ECHO type, create flow, and dispatch scaffolding.

## Types

- **type** `Player`

- **type** `Game`

- **type** `GameVariant` Contribution interface from a variant plugin.

## Components

- **component** `CreateGamePanel` Two-stage creation panel.

- **component** `GameArticle` Article / Section surface for Game objects.

- **component** `GameCard` Card surface for Game objects.

## Operations

- **op** `createGame` Creates a variant state object via `variant.createVariant`, adds it to the space as a hidden object, then wraps it in a top-level Game.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Variant Registration
  - `F-1.1` a variant plugin loads → it contributes a GameVariant via `Capability.contributes(GameCapabilities.VariantProvider, …)`
  - `F-1.2` GameCapabilities.VariantProvider contributions are queried → all registered variants are returned as an ordered list

- **feat** `F-2` Game Creation
  - `F-2.1` user opens the create-object flow for type `org.dxos.type.game` → CreateGamePanel is shown with a searchable list of available variants
  - `F-2.2` user selects a variant with no inputSchema → op:createGame is invoked immediately with empty input
  - `F-2.3` user selects a variant that has an inputSchema → a form rendered from the schema is shown; op:createGame is invoked on submit
  - `F-2.4` op:createGame completes → a Game object appears in the space graph; variant state is hidden

- **feat** `F-3` Game Article / Card Rendering
  - `F-3.1` Composer navigates to a Game object → GameArticle resolves `game.variant` and delegates to the matching `variant.article`
  - `F-3.2` a Game object is shown in a Card layout → GameCard resolves `game.variant` and delegates to `variant.card`
  - `F-3.3` no matching variant is found for the loaded state object → GameArticle renders an "Unsupported game variant" fallback message
  - `F-3.4` the variant ref is not yet loaded → neither GameArticle nor GameCard renders (returns null)

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Variant picker shows all contributions

- **scenario** `T-2` Create game without form

- **scenario** `T-3` Create game with form

- **scenario** `T-4` Atomic game creation

- **scenario** `T-5` Rollback on second write failure

- **scenario** `T-6` Unknown variant rejected

- **scenario** `T-7` Unsupported variant fallback

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Create a game through the variant picker and render it — The generic host round-trip — pick a registered variant, create the Game wrapper plus its hidden variant state, and confirm dispatch renders the variant's article.

---

pages.title: GitHubPlugin
pages.summary: Bidirectional GitHub integration for DXOS Composer.
pages.content:
Bidirectional GitHub integration for DXOS Composer.

Connects one or more GitHub OAuth integrations to a space and keeps organizations, people, repositories, issues, and pull requests synchronized with ECHO.  Users select repositories as sync targets; owning organizations and their members are pulled automatically.  Local edits to issue title, description, and open/closed status are pushed back to GitHub via snapshot-diff reconciliation.

## Types

- **type** `SyncTargetDescriptor` Lightweight descriptor returned by GetGitHubRepositories; never stored in ECHO directly.

- **type** `SyncOptions` Per-target sync tuning knobs stored on Integration.targets[i].options.

- **type** `GitHubUser` Subset of the GitHub REST user object consumed by the sync service.

- **type** `GitHubOrg` Subset of the GitHub REST org object.

- **type** `GitHubRepo` Subset of the GitHub REST repo object.

- **type** `GitHubIssue` Subset of the GitHub REST issue object; PRs appear here with a non-null pull_request field.

- **type** `GitHubLabel`

- **type** `GitHubPullRef` Minimal PR marker stored inline on a GitHubIssue.

- **type** `GitHubComment`

- **type** `RepoSnapshot` Fields recorded on the binding's snapshots after each repository read; used to detect local divergence on push.

- **type** `TaskSnapshot` Fields recorded on Integration.snapshots after each pull; used to detect local divergence on push.

- **type** `SyncResult` Counters returned by SyncGitHubRepositories.

## Operations

Discovery operations — read-only, no local writes.

- **op** `GetGitHubRepositories` List GitHub repositories reachable from an integration token.

- **op** `MaterializeGitHubTarget` Find-or-create the Repo bound to a selected GitHub repo, and the TaskSet that mirrors its issues, both keyed by the repo's foreign id, so a Cursor can reference the Repo as its `spec.target`.

Effectful sync operations — pull from GitHub, push diverged fields back.

- **op** `SyncGitHubRepositories` Poll every bound GitHub repository as [SYNC.mdl](https://github.com/dxos/dxos/blob/main/packages/plugins/plugin-github/spec/SYNC.mdl) describes.

- **op** `ImportPullRequest` Add one pull request to the space, named by a github.com URL or `owner/repo#number`, so a reviewer with a link in hand need not sync the whole repository first.

- **op** `ImportPullRequestFromSnapshot` The browser extension's page action: import the pull request the open page shows.

- **op** `SubmitPullRequestApproval` Approve a pull request as the space's GitHub connection.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` OAuth Integration
  - `F-1.1` user connects a GitHub integration → plugin-connector OAuth flow redirects to GitHub for authorization
  - `F-1.2` OAuth callback completes → accessToken stored in ECHO; fetchUser called to set accessToken.account to user login
  - `F-1.3` Integration source is "github.com"; provider id is "github".
  - `F-1.4` user connects the GitHub App ("github-app", kind app) → EDGE authorizes them, offers the installations on accounts they administer, and stores a
  - `F-1.5` An app connection is named after the installation's account, read from

- **feat** `F-2` Repository Discovery
  - `F-2.1` user opens the integration target picker → GetGitHubRepositories returns all repos visible to the token sorted by full_name (case-insensitive)
  - `F-2.2` No local ECHO objects are created during discovery.
  - `F-2.3` Owner, collaborator, and org-member repo affiliations are included.
  - `F-2.4` For an App installation token (`ghs_`), discovery and sync list the installation's

- **feat** `F-3` Pull — Organizations and People
  - `F-3.1` a selected repo is owned by a GitHub organization → that org is upserted as an Organization in ECHO (name, description, website, image)
  - `F-3.2` org is synced → org members are upserted as Person objects linked to the Organization
  - `F-3.3` Personal-account repos (owner is not an org) skip org/member pull without error.
  - `F-3.4` A single org is pulled at most once per sync pass regardless of how many repos it owns.

- **feat** `F-4` Pull — Repositories as Repos
  - `F-4.1` a selected repo does not yet have a local mirror → a Repo is created in ECHO with foreign key [source: "github.com", id: String(repo.id)], with a TaskSet carrying the same key for its issues
  - `F-4.2` a selected repo already has a local mirror → Repo name and description are updated via three-way merge against the stored snapshot, at most once an hour ([SYNC.mdl](https://github.com/dxos/dxos/blob/main/packages/plugins/plugin-github/spec/SYNC.mdl) F-2.6)
  - `F-4.3` a binding targets the issue TaskSet (bound before bindings targeted a Repo) → the binding is rewired to the repo's Repo

- **feat** `F-5` Pull — Issues as Tasks, pull requests as PullRequests
  - `F-5.1` an issue does not yet have a local mirror → Task created with fields title, description, status (open→todo, closed→done), assignee and milestone, listed by the repo's issue TaskSet
  - `F-5.2` an issue already has a local mirror → Task fields updated via three-way merge against stored snapshot
  - `F-5.3` A pull request is a PullRequest with `repository` set, pull-only; the polling delta and its GraphQL batch are specified in [SYNC.mdl](https://github.com/dxos/dxos/blob/main/packages/plugins/plugin-github/spec/SYNC.mdl).
  - `F-5.4` maxDaysBack is set on a target → the first poll reads only issues and pull requests updated within that window; later polls read from the binding's watermark

- **feat** `F-6` Push — Local Edits Back to GitHub
  - `F-6.1` Repo.description diverges from the last pulled snapshot → PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo} sends the new description
  - `F-6.2` Task.title or Task.description diverges from snapshot → PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number} sends the updated fields
  - `F-6.3` Task.status diverges from snapshot and the issue is not a PR → PATCH sends state: open or closed accordingly
  - `F-6.4` PR status diverges locally → divergence is logged; push is skipped (PRs are pull-only for status)
  - `F-6.5` Repo.name (repo rename) divergence is logged but never pushed.

- **feat** `F-7` Error Handling and Resilience
  - `F-7.1` a per-target sync fails → lastError is set on that target; other targets continue
  - `F-7.2` a repo is inaccessible to the integration token → lastError is set to "Repository not accessible to integration token"
  - `F-7.3` an HTTP request returns 429 or 5xx → request is retried with exponential backoff + jitter (max 3 retries, 500 ms base)
  - `F-7.4` sync succeeds → LayoutOperation.AddToast fires a success notification
  - `F-7.5` sync fails → LayoutOperation.AddToast fires an error notification with a human-readable message

- **feat** `F-8` Link Previews
  - `F-8.1` a document contains a repository, pull-request or issue URL → githubLinks (contributed via MarkdownCapabilities.ExtensionProvider) renders it as an anchor chip
  - `F-8.2` the chip is activated → the plugin's PreviewCapabilities.LinkResolver answers with an in-memory Repo, PullRequest or Issue (@dxos/types), never stored
  - `F-8.3` The object comes from a contributed GitHubCapabilities.LinkSource when a host provides one; otherwise it is fetched from the GitHub API with the space's connection token, or anonymously when the space has none.
  - `F-8.4` GitHubCard is the CardContent surface for Repo, Issue and PullRequest, so the popover shows reference, state, author, diff size (or default branch) and a link out.

- **feat** `F-9` Pull Request Review
  - `F-9.1` the user runs the "Import pull request" command and names a pull request → ImportPullRequest files it in the active space and the deck opens it
  - `F-9.2` The article's subject is the PullRequest, not its walkthrough — so a pull request with no narration yet opens, showing its state, CI outcome and a "Generate walkthrough" action.
  - `F-9.3` the space holds a walkthrough of the open pull request → the article's Walkthrough tab renders its prose and diff chunks, and the toolbar action regenerates rather than generates
  - `F-9.4` A Walkthrough opened by id resolves to the same article, through the pull request it narrates.
  - `F-9.5` the user clicks "Open PR in Composer" in the browser extension on a github.com pull → ImportPullRequestFromSnapshot files that pull request in the active space, and the
  - `F-9.6` The article opens on an Overview tab showing the pull request's live description as markdown, with the harness's Claude Code footer and CI's Composer preview block taken out of the prose.
  - `F-9.7` A link into the agent-artifacts R2 bucket renders as a pill that previews its image or video in place, and each such artifact, the Composer preview and the Claude Code session are listed as related cards in a masonry gr…
  - `F-9.8` The Overview lists every check run on the head commit, failures first, with its outcome, duration and a link to the provider's logs.
  - `F-9.9` The Overview shows the pull request's reference, state, CI outcome and branches as a read-only form in a details card.
  - `F-9.10` A Files tab shows one changed file at a time as the walkthrough's own diff chunk, beside a tree of every changed file with its change counts; the toolbar steps to the previous or next file.
  - `F-9.11` the reader checks a file off, in the tree or with the toolbar's Reviewed action → the file counts as reviewed in that browser until a push changes it, and the toolbar action moves on to the next file
  - `F-9.12` the user types a pull request URL or `owner/repo#123` into the search dialog (Cmd+K) → an "Import owner/repo#123 from GitHub" row appears above the results without a request to

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Token account populated on connect

- **scenario** `T-2` Repository discovery is read-only

- **scenario** `T-3` First sync — create Repo, Tasks and PullRequests

- **scenario** `T-4` Incremental pull — remote-wins merge

- **scenario** `T-5` Push issue edit

- **scenario** `T-6` PR status not pushed

- **scenario** `T-7` Inaccessible repo error surfaced

- **scenario** `T-8` Org deduplication

- **scenario** `T-9` Personal-account owner skips org pull

- **scenario** `T-10` maxDaysBack filters issue window

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Connect, select a repository, and sync — The core round-trip — authorize a GitHub connection, discover repos, materialize and sync one as a Repo with its issues as Tasks.

- **test** `QA-2` Local edit pushes back to GitHub — A push-direction check — editing a synced Task's title round-trips to the GitHub issue via PATCH.

- **test** `QA-3` Open a pull request from the browser extension — The plugin-crx page action, end to end through the operation it names.

- **test** `QA-4` Import a pull request from the search dialog — Cmd+K offers to import a pull request the moment its URL is pasted, then imports and opens it.

pages.title: HandpanPlugin
pages.summary: Handpan music notation and real-time note detection for `DXOS` Composer.
pages.content:
Handpan music notation and real-time note detection for `DXOS` Composer. Phase 1 (this document) is the audio-analysis layer and a `Tuner` that calibrates the detector to an instrument and shows notes — and chords — as they are played. Notation, built on `plugin-sequencer`'s `Score`, is Phase 2; see `docs/DESIGN.md` for the roadmap and the analysis techniques considered.

## Notes (Phase 2)

- Notation on `plugin-sequencer`'s `Score` / `Sequence` / `Note` (key, per-sequence overrides and `Note.articulation` added there); `strikesToNotes` converts detected strikes
- Notation grid editor and article surface; register with `composer-app`
- Record mode: strikes and tempo quantized into bars

## Types

- **type** `Scale` A set of playable pitches; the ding is the handpan's central note.

- **type** `NoteEvent` A resolved strike: an onset followed by its pitch, measured from a long window after the onset minus an equal window before it, so notes still ringing do not bias it.

- **type** `NoteTemplate` A calibrated note — the reference Live mode and chord detection match against.

## Components

- **component** `Tuner` Calibrates the detector to an instrument and displays notes as they are played.

- **component** `HandpanLayout` Top-down pan; ding centre, fields zig-zag ascending from the bottom.

- **component** `NoteDisplay` Current note (or chord, or Tak) with a ±50 cent meter; dimmed once nothing sounds.

- **component** `LevelMeter` Input level on a dB scale with the "sounding" threshold marked.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Note detection
  - `F-1.1` Onsets are detected by spectral flux on a peak-normalized spectrum, independent of
  - `F-1.2` A strike's attack and tone bloom within 100 ms of each other are one strike.
  - `F-1.3` Each strike's pitch is measured from 8192-sample windows either side of the onset; a
  - `F-1.4` Strikes without a clear pitch are reported as percussive (tak).

- **feat** `F-2` Calibration
  - `F-2.1` The user strikes each note of the scale in turn (ding first); the target advances
  - `F-2.2` Each strike is logged with its outcome: accepted (with cents), a different note, no
  - `F-2.3` Octave and twelfth readings are folded back onto the target.
  - `F-2.4` Calibrated notes are drawn in the success colour; calibration can be reset or a
  - `F-2.5` With persist, the scale and calibration survive a reload.
  - `F-2.6` Bound to an instrument (`calibration` / `onCalibrationChange`), calibration is read from

- **feat** `F-3` Live
  - `F-3.1` The displayed note switches only after several consistent frames and is released
  - `F-3.2` Gain and sensitivity are adjustable while listening, with tooltips.
  - `F-3.3` Input level is shown against the sounding threshold.

- **feat** `F-4` Chords
  - `F-4.1` With chords on, a strike is decomposed against the note templates (NNLS); notes
  - `F-4.2` Learned templates attribute sympathetic resonance to the struck note.
  - `F-4.3` Known limit — an octave pair (e.g.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Overlapping notes are measured precisely

- **scenario** `T-2` Calibration advances

- **scenario** `T-3` Resonance is not a chord

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`). The plugin has no app surface yet (Phase 2), so the flow runs in storybook; there are no operations to bind.

- **test** `QA-1` Calibrate and play in the simulated session — The primary journey with synthesized audio, so it needs no instrument: calibrate every note, then play notes, a tak and a chord in Live mode.
- **test** `QA-2` Showcase clip — The 10s showcase clip: Play a melody around the handpan.

pages.title: IbkrPlugin
pages.summary: An Interactive Brokers plugin for `DXOS` Composer: a once-a-day background sync captures a Flex Web Service report into a per-space feed (or the user imports a Flex XML file manually from the toolbar), the assistant answers portfolio, cash, and trade questions from the latest st…
pages.content:
An Interactive Brokers plugin for `DXOS` Composer: a once-a-day background sync captures a Flex Web Service report into a per-space feed (or the user imports a Flex XML file manually from the toolbar), the assistant answers portfolio, cash, and trade questions from the latest stored snapshot, and `Instrument` objects provide navigable, deduplicated references to tradable securities with static identity metadata plus research surfaces (TradingView chart embed, SEC EDGAR fundamentals fetched at view time via operations).

## Architecture

- **feat** `A-1` External access via operations — Components and surfaces never call external services (IBKR Flex, SEC EDGAR, or any other HTTP/API client) directly.
  - `A-1.1`
  - `A-1.2` a surface needs dynamic data from an external provider → it invokes the appropriate op via `OperationInvoker` (e.g.
  - `A-1.3`
  - `A-1.4`

## Types

The two persistent types are ECHO objects, identified by their DXN typename. `Portfolio` is the navigable owner that appears in the navtree; `PortfolioReport` is an append-only snapshot of the raw Flex XML. The `Position`, `Cash`, and `Trade` structs are not stored — they are parsed from `PortfolioReport.xml` on read and form the shape of the operation outputs.

- **type** `Portfolio` DXN typename: org.dxos.type.ibkr.Portfolio@0.1.0.

- **type** `PortfolioReport` DXN typename: org.dxos.type.ibkr.PortfolioReport@0.1.0.

- **type** `Position` An open position parsed from a report's OpenPosition rows.

- **type** `Cash` An ending cash balance for a single currency (the BASE_SUMMARY rollup row is dropped).

- **type** `Trade` A single executed trade parsed from a report's Trade rows.

- **type** `Lot` A single tax lot (one acquisition).

- **type** `AssetClass` Kind of tradable security represented by an Instrument.

- **type** `Instrument` DXN typename: org.dxos.type.ibkr.Instrument@0.1.0.

## Components

- **component** `PortfolioArticle` Article view for a Portfolio: lists the stored daily PortfolioReport snapshots (newest first) from the Portfolio's backing feed.

- **component** `PortfolioSyncAction` Toolbar action mirroring the Gmail mailbox connect/sync switch.

- **component** `PortfolioProperties` Companion properties panel for a Portfolio: a single toggle that creates the daily sync trigger on first enable and enables/disables it thereafter.

- **component** `PortfolioReportDetail` Companion plank showing one PortfolioReport parsed into sections: aggregated open positions, trades, and cash balances, plus the per-lot breakdown (open tax lots) and realized closed lots when the query emits them.

- **component** `InstrumentArticle` Article surface for an Instrument: static header (name, symbol, sector) from the ECHO object, a TradingView Advanced Chart embed (presentation widget only — no plugin HTTP from this component), and a fundamentals panel…

- **component** `InstrumentCard` Card surface (`AppSurface.CardContent`) for an Instrument: compact identity (symbol, name, exchange, assetClass) suitable for masonry, search results, and popovers.

## Services

- **service** `FlexWebService` Client for the Interactive Brokers Flex Web Service.

- **service** `SecEdgar` Client for the SEC EDGAR public data API (`data.sec.gov`, `www.sec.gov`).

## Operations

Portfolio read operations parse stored XML and never call IBKR. Network I/O reaches external services only through operation handlers (`SyncPortfolioReport` → `FlexWebService`; instrument research → `SecEdgar`). Components invoke ops via `OperationInvoker`; they never import `service:*` clients.

- **op** `SyncPortfolioReport` Fetches a fresh Flex report from IBKR and appends it to the Portfolio feed as a PortfolioReport.

- **op** `ImportPortfolioReport` Appends a manually supplied raw Flex report XML to the Portfolio feed as a PortfolioReport.

- **op** `GetPortfolio` Reads the open positions and cash balances from the most recent stored report.

- **op** `GetTrades` Reads the trade history from the most recent stored report, limited to the last 7 days.

- **type** `FundamentalsValuation` Valuation metrics (market data, price multiples).
- **type** `FundamentalsPerformance` Income-statement metrics from SEC EDGAR XBRL.
- **type** `FundamentalsRatios` Balance-sheet and profitability ratios.
- **type** `FundamentalsAdditional` Remaining us-gaap concepts from SEC EDGAR, keyed by XBRL concept name.
- **type** `FundamentalsSnapshot` Transient output of op:GetInstrumentFundamentals.

- **op** `MaterializeInstrument` Find-or-create an Instrument in the space, keyed by foreign id.

- **op** `GetInstrumentFundamentals` Fetches a compact fundamentals snapshot for an Instrument's primary `symbol` via service:SecEdgar.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Connection — The user connects Interactive Brokers via the Flex Web Service by supplying a Flex token and a Flex query id through a Composer Connection.
  - `F-1.1`
  - `F-1.2` the credential form is submitted → an AccessToken is created with the Flex token in token (the secret) and the
  - `F-1.3` a connection already exists in the space
  - `F-1.4` a connection already exists in the space → component:PortfolioSyncAction shows the Sync button instead of Connect
