pages.title: IdeogramPlugin
pages.summary: A **headless** Composer plugin that makes [ideogram.ai](https://ideogram.ai) available as an image-generation provider.
pages.content:
A **headless** Composer plugin that makes [ideogram.ai](https://ideogram.ai) available as an image-generation provider. It has no React/UI surfaces. It contributes two things:

1. A **Connector** entry (`source: "ideogram.ai"`) with an API-key credential form, so the user connects Ideogram through the generic `plugin-connector` UI. On submit the key is stored as an `AccessToken` (source `ideogram.ai`) plus a `Connection` in ECHO.
2. An **`GenerationService`** implementation (the abstraction owned by `plugin-studio`) whose `generate()` calls the Ideogram HTTP API and maps the response to `VariantData[]`.

The credential set up by the Connector is resolved back at generation time by `plugin-studio`'s `generateImage` operation through `CredentialsService`, keyed by the provider's `source`. This plugin never reads the prompt UI and `plugin-studio` never reads Ideogram credentials — the Connector + `CredentialsService` are the seam.

## Connector

- **feat** `IdeogramConnector` Contributes a ConnectorEntry via Capability.contributes(Connector, [entry]) on the SetupConnectors activation event (mirrors plugin-ibkr's non-OAuth credentialForm connector).

## Provider

- **feat** `IdeogramImageGenerationService` Contributes an GenerationService via Capability.contributes(StudioCapabilities.GenerationService, [service]) on Startup.

## File layout (mirrors plugin-osrm)

```text
packages/plugins/plugin-ideogram/
  PLUGIN.mdl                         # this file
  README.md
  package.json                       # "private": true
  moon.yml                           # --entryPoint per export subpath; platform=neutral
  src/
    index.ts                         # exports meta + IdeogramPlugin
    meta.ts                          # Plugin.getMetaFromConfig (id org.dxos.plugin.ideogram)
    plugin.ts                        # Plugin.lazy
    IdeogramPlugin.tsx               # Plugin.define(meta).pipe(addModule Connector on SetupConnectors, addModule Provider on Startup, Plugin.make)
    dx.config.ts
    capabilities/
      index.ts                       # Capability.lazy(Connector, GenerationService)
      connector.ts                   # Capability.contributes(Connector, [entry])
      generation-service.ts    # Capability.contributes(StudioCapabilities.GenerationService, [service])
    services/
      index.ts
      IdeogramClient.ts              # generate(request, { apiKey }) → VariantData[]
      ideogram-mapping.ts            # response → VariantData[]
      ideogram-mapping.test.ts       # fixture-based unit test
```

## Dependencies

- `@dxos/plugin-studio` (workspace:\*) — `/types` subpath for the `GenerationService` capability key + request/result schemas.
- `@dxos/plugin-connector` (workspace:\*) — `Connector` capability key + `Connection` type; `@dxos/types` for `AccessToken`.
- `@dxos/app-framework`, `@dxos/app-toolkit`, `@dxos/echo`, `effect`.
- No `react` / `@dxos/react-ui*`.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Connector builds AccessToken + Connection

- **scenario** `T-2` Empty token rejected

- **scenario** `T-3` Response mapping (mocked fetch)

- **scenario** `T-4` Missing key

## Out of scope (v1)

- OAuth (Ideogram uses a static API key).
- Edit / upscale / remix / describe endpoints; only `/generate`.
- Multi-account and per-artifact provider configuration.
- A server-side (edge function) transport that keeps the API key off the client entirely; v1 resolves the key client-side and proxies the call.

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Connect an Ideogram key and generate an image — Headless like plugin-heygen — Ideogram contributes only a Connector credential form and a GenerationService; generation runs through plugin-studio's generic `Generate` operation with `provider: "ideogram"`.

pages.title: IllustratorPlugin
pages.summary: A headless diagramming host plugin for `DXOS` Composer.
pages.content:
A headless diagramming host plugin for `DXOS` Composer. Owns the `Drawing` ECHO type and the agent-facing drawing skill and operations; the scene model, the `.dx` DSL and its layout engines live in `@dxos/diagram`, whose [SPEC.mdl](https://github.com/dxos/dxos/blob/main/packages/common/diagram/SPEC.mdl) covers the stack as a whole. Canvas renderers (plugin-canvas, plugin-tldraw, plugin-excalidraw) contribute a `VariantProvider` capability supplying their canvas schema, a builder that maps the scene DSL onto their records, and surface components; plugin-illustrator resolves the variant at runtime and delegates.

## Types

- **type** `Drawing` Named handle around a renderer-specific canvas object.

- **type** `Canvas` The renderer's records, opaque to ECHO.

## Capabilities

- **component** `VariantProvider` Contributed by renderer plugins; supplies the canvas type, a scene-DSL builder

## Operations

- **op** `create` Creates a Drawing with an empty canvas for the requested (or default) variant.
- **op** `convert` Moves a sketch onto another variant by replaying its scene onto a fresh canvas of that variant
- **op** `read` Returns the current scene of a drawing as world objects with object-local coordinates.
- **op** `edit` Applies scene commands to a drawing via the variant's builder; returns the resulting scene.
- **op** `draw` Applies a `.dx` document: semantic statements of any diagram kind (structure, sequence,
- **op** `score` Grades the drawing as laid out on one 0–1 scale, per layout constraint and cost term, with
- **op** `generate` DEPRECATED, superseded by `draw`.

## Commands

`dx drawing` (contributed through `AppCapability.commands`; React-free, so it loads in the CLI):

| Command                         | Effect                                                                         |
|---------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `render <file.dx> [-o] [--plain]` | Lays out a semantic-DSL file and writes a `.dx.svg` (or bare `.svg`); prints the layout report. |
| `import <file.dx.svg>`          | Adds the drawing a `.dx.svg` carries to a space under fresh ids.               |
| `list`                          | Lists the drawings in a space.                                                 |
| `export <id> [-o]`              | Writes an SVG-variant drawing, edits included, back out to a `.dx.svg`.        |

## Dialects

Higher-level diagram languages compile to scene commands (see `@dxos/diagram`, `packages/common/diagram/src/dialect.ts`); each dialect owns its layout, so its output lands as ordinary world objects that stay editable by id. The `.dx` DSL is the authoring language; the mermaid dialects below are deprecated and kept working.

- **component** `MermaidFlowchart` DEPRECATED.
- **component** `UmlClass` DEPRECATED.
- **component** `UmlGrid` Grid variant — equal-size cells on the document grid (GRID=32), barycenter column
- **component** `UmlEngine` Engine-backed placement (dagre | ELK layered) over the grid cells and routing — proper

## Variants

- **component** `SvgVariant` SVG renderer variant owned by this plugin (peer of tldraw/excalidraw): the scene DSL is

## Skills

- **component** `DrawingSkill` Drawing via the `.dx` DSL.

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Create, edit, and read back a drawing — The scene-DSL round-trip through the SVG variant (owned by this plugin, so no renderer plugin dependency is needed).

- **test** `QA-2` Generate a UML class diagram from mermaid source — The UML skill's path (the skill is plugin-uml's) — replace a drawing's contents with a class diagram compiled from mermaid source, with layout owned by the dialect.

- **test** `QA-3` Render a diagram from the terminal and import it into a space — The `dx drawing` commands: a semantic-DSL file is laid out headlessly into a `.dx.svg`, re-laid out after an edit, and imported into a space as an editable drawing.
- **test** `QA-4` Showcase clip — The 10s showcase clip: Draw shapes on an SVG drawing.

pages.title: InboxPlugin
pages.summary: Unified inbox plugin for `DXOS` Composer — email, calendar, and contacts in one place, surfaced alongside workspace content.
pages.content:
Unified inbox plugin for `DXOS` Composer — email, calendar, and contacts in one place, surfaced alongside workspace content. Mail syncs from multiple providers (Google/Gmail and JMAP, e.g. Fastmail) into an append-only feed; calendar and contacts sync from Google. AI extractors, a cursored processing pipeline, and an enrichment cascade derive structured objects, summaries, classifications, and RDF facts from message content.

Entry points: `plugin.tsx` (browser), `plugin.node.ts` (skills/ops/schema only), and `plugin.workerd.ts` (ops + schema — lets EDGE run sync remotely).

## External types

- `Message`, `DraftMessage`, `Event`, `Person`, `Organization` — `@dxos/types`. Messages/events live in feeds; people/organizations in the space. A `DraftMessage` is an unsent `Message`, distinguished by its own instance check rather than by a field.
- `Feed`, `Tag`, `TagIndex` — `@dxos/echo` / `@dxos/schema`. Feed members are immutable; mutable tag membership lives in the mailbox's `TagIndex` sidecar.
- `Cursor` (`@dxos/link`) — the sync **binding**: an external cursor whose `spec.target` is the Mailbox/Calendar and whose `spec.source` is the provider access token. Carries sync options and durable window/delta state.
- `Connection`, `ConnectorSpec` — `@dxos/plugin-connector`. Provider credentials and the connector registry (materialize/sync/trigger declarations live in plugin-google / plugin-jmap).
- `Instructions`, `Project` — `@dxos/compute`. Reply guidance; extracted project objects.
- `Fact` / `FactStore` — `@dxos/pipeline-rdf`.

## Types

- **type** `Mailbox` The mail container: a named handle onto an append-only message feed plus its mutable sidecars.

- **type** `SavedFilter` A saved, named query string surfacing as a folder node under the mailbox.

- **type** `MessageFilter` An exclusion rule dropped messages must match (currently a `from` regex).

- **type** `SystemTags` Canonical, provider-agnostic tag registry: starred | inbox | important | sent | draft | personal | social | promotions | updates | forums | spam.

- **type** `Calendar` Calendar container — same feed + tags shape as Mailbox; no deck chain.

- **type** `DraftEvent` Not a schema — a convention with helpers: a space-db Event parented to its Calendar with no provider foreign key is a draft; saving it creates the remote event and the next sync reconciles it.

- **type** `ExtractedFrom` Provenance relation extracted-object → source Message.

- **type** `SentTag` Foreign key of the tag the provider's own copy of a sent message will carry (Gmail's SENT label, or the JMAP account's Sent folder resolved by role).

- **type** `MailSend` Provider-agnostic send contract, routed via the MailSendOperation capability by connector id.

- **type** `Settings` KVS-backed plugin settings.

- **type** `SyncOptions` Per-binding sync options stored on the Cursor spec.

- **type** `SyncStreamConfig` Per-provider pipeline tuning (page sizes, fetch concurrency, run caps, date chunking).

Capability tags (`InboxCapabilities`): `Settings` (writable atom), `ObjectExtractor` (multi — contact + summarize extractors contributed here; other plugins may add more), `MailboxAction` (injected toolbar actions, e.g. plugin-brain's Analyze), `MailSendOperation` (provider send op keyed by connector id).

## App graph

Node paths: space → `communications` group → `mailboxes` section → mailbox → child segments. System-tag views are pre-seeded, non-removable filter nodes — the same mechanism as saved user filters.

- **node** `MailboxesSection` Nav-tree section shown when any Mailbox exists in the space.

- **node** `MailboxNode` One node per Mailbox.

- **node** `MessageNodes` Every feed message (and mailbox-scoped draft) as a hidden child of its mailbox — deep-link resolution only, never shown in the nav tree.

- **node** `CalendarNode` Standard type section for Calendar; events (and draft events) as hidden children.

The sync action appears only when an external `Cursor` targets the mailbox/calendar and a matching `Connection` exists; its spinner/disabled state reads the `#sync` progress monitor.

## Deck

- **deck** `MailboxDeck` Reading a mailbox is a chain of details: a message opens as the mailbox plank's detail, and an attachment as the message's.

- **plank** `MailboxPlank`

- **plank** `MessagePlank`

## Companions

This plugin contributes **no companion nodes of its own** — message/event children are ordinary hidden nodes, not companions. Companions appearing on inbox objects come from generic every-object contributors: plugin-space (properties/info), plugin-assistant (chat), plugin-routine (automations — consuming this plugin's Routine templates), plugin-debug. The mailbox's create-topic action reveals a `topic` companion contributed externally.

The message or event shown beside a mailbox or calendar is the deck's detail tab, not a companion this plugin contributes: rows open with `LayoutOperation.Open` and `disposition: 'detail'`.

## Surfaces

- **surface** `MailboxSurface`

- **surface** `SubscriptionsSurface`

- **surface** `MessageSurface`

- **surface** `DraftMessageSurface`

- **surface** `CalendarSurface`

- **surface** `EventSurface`

- **surface** `MessageCardSurface`

- **surface** `EventCardSurface`

- **surface** `PropertiesSurfaces`

- **surface** `SaveFilterPopoverSurface`

- **surface** `RelatedSurfaces`

## Menus

- **menu** `MailboxToolbar`

- **menu** `MailboxContextMenu`

- **menu** `SavedFilterMenu`

## Components

Containers (surface-bound, lazy). Presentation state (selection, tags, stars) rides atoms; feed reads are paginated.

- **component** `MailboxArticle` Paged, thread-grouped message list over the feed (whole-thread semi-join), with filter editor (tag/text grammar, save-as-filter), per-tile tag chips + star toggle, toolbar (menu:MailboxToolbar), and a statusbar Progress…

- **component** `MessageArticle` Conversation (thread) detail: message tiles over a combined space+feed query by threadId, summaries from the annotations feed, AI reply, delete, open-as-plank.

- **component** `EditMessageArticle` Draft composer — subject/to/body editor, send via contributed MailSendOperation, AI generate-reply.

- **component** `CalendarArticle` Calendar grid + event list with range selection; InitializeCalendar empty state.

- **component** `EventArticle` Event detail/editor; draft events are editable and savable (creates the remote event).

- **component** `SubscriptionsArticle` Bulk-mail subscription list (sender, count); select + unsubscribe.

Supporting: `MessageCard` / `EventCard` (card bodies), `MailboxProperties` / `CalendarProperties` (object-properties panels: sync toggle/trigger), `SaveFilterPopover` (names a filter into `mailbox.filters`), `RelatedToContact` / `RelatedToOrganization` (related messages/events/people), `InitializeMailbox` / `InitializeCalendar` (connect flows).

## Services

- **service** `MailSyncProvider` Effect service each mail provider implements (gmail in plugin-google, jmap in plugin-jmap): name, SyncStreamConfig, foreignKeySource, and prepare(preparation) → source stream.

- **service** `FactStore` Space-level RDF fact store (from @dxos/pipeline-rdf); AnalyzeMailbox writes extracted facts here.

## Operations

Keys `org.dxos.operation.inbox.<name>`. Provider-facing ops are defined here but handled in plugin-google / plugin-jmap; `GenerateReply` is handled in plugin-brain. Long-running mailbox pipelines report through progress monitors keyed `<mailbox uri>#<suffix>` (`sync`, `process`, `enrich`, `classify`, `summarize`, `analyze`, `correspondents`, `subscriptions`) and serialize on a per-mailbox lock.

### Sync (provider-handled)

- **op** `GoogleMailSync` Sync Gmail into the mailbox feed via the shared harness.

- **op** `JmapSync` Same contract for JMAP (Fastmail).

- **op** `GoogleCalendarSync` Sync Google Calendar events into the calendar feed (windowed; separate from the mail harness).

- **op** `GoogleContactsSync` Sync a Google contact group into space Person objects (upserts).

`MaterializeGmailTarget` / `MaterializeJmapTarget` / `MaterializeCalendarTarget` create the local Mailbox/Calendar before a cursor exists; `GetGoogleCalendars` / `GetGoogleContactGroups` discover remote targets. All are ConnectorSpec plumbing.

### Compose & send

- **op** `DraftEmail` Agent-facing draft creation (subject/to/body/replyTo).

- **op** `DraftEmailAndOpen` Create a draft (compose | reply | reply-all | forward) and open it as a plank.

- **op** `GmailSend` Send a draft via Gmail; JmapSend is the JMAP counterpart.

- **op** `CreateGoogleCalendarEvent` Write counterpart of calendar sync — creates the remote event for a saved draft event.

### Extract, classify, enrich

- **op** `ExtractMessage` Dispatch one message to the best-matching ObjectExtractor; persist results + ExtractedFrom provenance.

- **op** `EnrichMailbox` Cascade orchestrator over tiers deterministic → classify → summarize → analyze (default: first three).

- **op** `ProcessMailbox` Cursored processing pipeline over the feed (durable consumer cursor); ResetFeedCursor rewinds it.

Constituents (each idempotent, capped, individually invocable): `ClassifyEmail` / `ClassifyMailbox` (AI tagging, spam + category, known-Person short-circuit), `SummarizeMailbox` (per-contact summaries into the annotations feed), `AnalyzeMailbox` (RDF facts into FactStore), `ExtractCorrespondents` (Person/Organization for people the user wrote to), `ExtractSubscriptions` (List-Unsubscribe scan → mailbox.subscriptions), `ExtractContactFromMessage` / `ExtractSummaryFromMessage` (pure extract, no writes), `CreateProjectFromMessage` (thread → Project with LLM summary), `GenerateReply` (grounded reply draft; handled in plugin-brain). `ExtractContact` and `ExtractMailbox` are deprecated.

### Misc & navigation

- **op** `ReadEmail` Agent tool — read mailbox content as text (skip/limit).

`AddMailbox` (create-object flow), `RenameFilter` (saved-filter node action), `ResetFeedCursor` (rewinds a named consumer's durable cursor over the feed), `UnsubscribeSender` (adds a skip-sender filter and fires the RFC 8058 one-click endpoint).

## Sync

`runMailSync` (subpath export `@dxos/plugin-inbox/sync`, no React) is the provider-agnostic harness: it loads binding → mailbox → feed → tag index, resolves date windows and delta tokens from the durable `Cursor`, streams provider pages through dedup → cap → decode, merges provider reconciles (retag/delete by foreign id), runs the shared email tail (attachments → contacts → draft reconciliation → stats → commit units), commits in groups, reports progress (`#sync` monitor), and schedules itself again (`runAgain`) while capped or behind delta. Scheduling policy is domain-owned: 10-minute cron, auto-sync on, remote (EDGE) on. Provider `MailSyncProvider` layers live in plugin-google and plugin-jmap; calendar/contacts sync are separate plugin-google handlers.

Routine templates (`automation-templates.ts`): hourly `processMailbox` and daily `enrichMailbox` runnables, disabled by default, surfaced in the automations companion.

## Skills

- **Inbox** (`org.dxos.skill.inbox`, agent-enableable; attached to Mailbox via SkillsAnnotation) — mailbox management: ClassifyEmail, DraftEmail, ReadEmail, GoogleMailSync, ExtractMessage.
- **Inbox Send** (`org.dxos.skill.inboxSend`) — send-only companion: GmailSend.
- **Calendar** (`org.dxos.skill.calendar`; attached to Calendar) — GoogleCalendarSync.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Mailbox
  - `F-1.1` Messages sync into an append-only feed; the article lists them paged and
  - `F-1.2` Tags, stars, and read state live in the TagIndex sidecar keyed by canonical
  - `F-1.3` System-tag folders (inbox, all-mail, sent, drafts) and saved user filters are

  - `F-2.1` Opening a message from the mailbox reuses the message-level plank (deck chain);
  - `F-2.2` Message and event nodes resolve deep links but stay hidden in the nav tree.

- **feat** `F-3` Provider sync
  - `F-3.1` Sync is idempotent, resumable, capped per run, and cancellable; progress reports
  - `F-3.2` A provider is a MailSyncProvider layer; adding one requires no harness changes.
  - `F-3.3` Sync runs on EDGE (workerd entry) on a 10-minute cron when enabled.

- **feat** `F-4` Compose & send

  - `F-5.1` Events sync into the calendar feed; draft events are local Events parented to the

  - `F-6.1` Extractors are contributed capabilities; extraction records ExtractedFrom provenance.
  - `F-6.2` The enrich cascade (deterministic → classify → summarize → analyze) is idempotent

  - `F-6.4` A conversation summary links the people and organizations it mentions to their objects,
  - `F-6.5` The "Analyze New Mail" routine template runs the cascade from the mailbox feed, so mail
  - `F-6.6` Analyze is offered on a mailbox with no connection, since its content was imported and

- **feat** `F-8` Related content
  - `F-8.1` People and organizations surface their related messages, events, and contacts via

pages.content:
Visual project management plugin for `DXOS` Composer — organise any ECHO type into drag-and-drop columns driven by a single-select field, with full local-first persistence and real-time peer replication.

pages.title: LabelerPlugin
pages.summary: Triages a mailbox: labels each message with the space's own tags and a priority band by asking a decision model three questions per message, applying only the answers it is confident about, and extracts what a message asks of the reader as tasks with an extraction model.
pages.content:
Triages a mailbox: labels each message with the space's own tags and a priority band by asking a decision model three questions per message, applying only the answers it is confident about, and extracts what a message asks of the reader as tasks with an extraction model.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Ask about a message
  - `F-1.1` Each message is asked three questions in one call: needs-reply (probability), label (classify), urgency (rate).
  - `F-1.2` The label options are the space's own user tags plus "none of these"; canonical and provider tags are excluded.
  - `F-1.3` With no user tags in the space the label question is omitted and the other two still run.
  - `F-1.4` The state sent is the sender, subject and a snippet — never the full message body.
- **feat** `F-2` Apply only what it is confident about
  - `F-2.1` A label is applied only when its confidence reaches the threshold (default 0.5).
  - `F-2.2` `Needs reply` is applied at a probability of 0.6 or above.
  - `F-2.3` Every message is placed in exactly one priority band — Urgent, High priority, Normal or Low priority — applied as the inbox's priority system tags; Urgent needs the top of the scale and a confident answer.
  - `F-2.4` Nothing but tags is written; the message itself is not modified.
- **feat** `F-3` Run it over the inbox
  - `F-3.1` A toolbar action, "Triage inbox", runs the labeller over the whole mailbox.
  - `F-3.2` A cascade pass (`label`, after `contacts`) runs it as part of Analyze.
  - `F-3.3` A message already carrying a priority band is skipped, so a re-run is cheap.
  - `F-3.4` A run is capped (default 50, max 200 messages) since each message costs one call.
- **feat** `F-4` Extract what a message asks for as tasks
  - `F-4.1` A message that needs a reply is read by an extraction model (Cloudflare's Clairic) for up to three requests and the due date of the first.
  - `F-4.2` The first request becomes a task at a low confidence bar; further ones only when clear-cut, so what the sender will do themselves is not filed as the reader's work.
  - `F-4.3` Tasks are filed in one project per mailbox, created on first use, whose instructions tell an agent how to answer the email a task came from.
  - `F-4.4` A task carries its message's priority, names the email it came from, references the message, and is recorded as extracted from it so it shows under the email.
  - `F-4.5` A message already extracted is not read again; a failed or unavailable extraction leaves the message labelled.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` An urgent request is tagged
- **scenario** `T-2` A receipt is labelled with the user's own tag
- **scenario** `T-4` A request becomes a task in the inbox project
- **scenario** `T-3` Re-running changes nothing

## QA

- **test** `QA-1` Label an inbox from the toolbar — The plugin's whole journey — a mailbox of mixed mail, one click, tags that match.

test QA-2: Triage an inbox, then let the agent answer the most urgent email desc: The demo journey — one click sorts an unread inbox into priority bands and turns requests into tasks; the top task goes to the agent, which drafts the reply and asks before it sends. actors: human covers: [F-2.3, F-3.1, F-4.1, F-4.3, F-4.4] status: unverified given:
    - an identity exists
    - space: a space created from the "Inbox triage" template (plugin-debug), whose sample mailbox sends locally
    - plugin-labeler, plugin-typesafe and plugin-debug are enabled steps:
    - name: Start with an unsorted inbox do: Open the Inbox mailbox. expect: nine unread messages in date order, none grouped or tagged
    - name: Triage the inbox do: Choose "Triage inbox" from the toolbar's magic-wand menu. invoke: org.dxos.operation.labeler.labelMailbox expect: the list regroups under Urgent, High priority, Normal and Low priority, with the renewal alone under Urgent
    - name: Every request becomes a task do: Open the "Inbox tasks" project from the navtree and its Tasks tab. expect: one task per request, each with its email's priority
    - name: Open the most urgent email do: Back in the inbox, open the message under Urgent. expect: the task extracted from it is listed under its body
    - name: Assign the task to the agent do: Open the task's "…" menu and choose "Assign to agent". expect: the Assistant companion opens on a new chat that starts working on the task
    - name: The agent asks before it sends expect: the chat shows a permission card asking to send an email reply note: sending is the inbox's send-email permission; the agent cannot send without the person's answer
    - name: Allow it to send do: Choose "Allow" on the card. expect: the card shows the answer and the agent finishes the task
    - name: See the reply under the email do: Open the renewal email again. expect: the reply ("Re: …") is threaded under the original message, tagged Sent
```

## Changelog

```mdl
decision D-1: Triage applies a priority band to every message with the decision model, extracts tasks from each message with an extraction model served by Cloudflare, and the mailbox list groups messages by priority.
  date: 2026-10-27
  by: user:dmaretskyi
  affects: [F-2.3, F-4.1]
```

- **decision** `D-2` Extracted tasks are shown under the email they came from, and a task assigned to the agent from there opens the Assistant, which drafts the reply and asks for the send-email permission before sending it.

- **decision** `D-3` Four bands (Urgent, High priority, Normal, Low priority) as inbox system tags; urgency at or above 0.9, or a reply needed at 0.5, is High; a reply needed or urgency at 0.5 is Normal. Fills in [D-1]. — Every message must sit in one band for the list to group the whole inbox; the tags live in the inbox so the list can group without depending on this plugin.

- **decision** `D-4` Clairic is asked for three request slots and a due date; the first slot is kept from confidence 0.15, later slots from 0.6, and only messages that need a reply are read. Fills in [D-1]. — A Clairic list field answers with short fragments, while separate text fields answer with whole requests; later slots are where it picks up the sender's own next steps.

- **decision** `D-5` Tasks file into one project per mailbox, keyed to the mailbox, whose instructions bind the inbox skills and name the send-reply operation. Fills in [D-2]. — A delegated chat takes its skills and system prompt from its task's project, so the project is where the agent learns how to answer an email.

- **decision** `D-6` The urgency and needs-reply questions name marketing and automated mail as never urgent and never asking for a reply. Fills in [D-3]. — Asked plainly, Jev rated a conference promotion ending tonight as urgent and needing a reply.

- **decision** `D-7` QA-1 runs the labeller through "Triage inbox", the toolbar action's current name. Fills in [D-1]. — The action was renamed from "Label messages" when it took on priority and extraction, so the old step named a menu item that no longer exists.

pages.title: LaMetricPlugin
pages.summary: Shows a Composer space on a LaMetric TIME: a progress bar while a task is running, the space's statistics otherwise, cycled through the device's frames.
pages.content:
Shows a Composer space on a LaMetric TIME: a progress bar while a task is running, the space's statistics otherwise, cycled through the device's frames.

Unlike the Stream Deck, no companion application is needed: the device is an HTTP server on the LAN, so this plugin pushes to it directly. Local push goes through LaMetric's stock "My Data (DIY)" app, because a custom indicator app cannot be pushed to locally; cloud push, for use off the device's network, is a separate mechanism against a published app. Requests go through Tauri's HTTP client because neither endpoint is reachable from a web view. Design: `agents/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-lametric-design.md`.

## Types

- **type** `GoalData` A determinate progress bar the device draws itself.

- **type** `Frame` One screen in the device's cycle.

- **type** `Payload` The whole body of a widget update; the device replaces its cycle with these frames.

- **type** `TransportConfig` Where and how to push.

- **type** `PushStatus` What the last push did, published so a surface can show a failure only the user can fix.

## Components

- **component** `VirtualLaMetric` On-screen replica of the 37x8 matrix, rasterised by the same pure function as the tests, so

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` What the device shows
  - `F-1.1` While any task is pending or running, a determinate task renders as a goal frame and the
  - `F-1.2` A task reporting no total renders as a text frame, because `goalData` requires an end.
  - `F-1.3` With nothing running, the frames show the space's object, feed, type and plugin counts.
  - `F-1.4` At most four frames are pushed; the device cycles at a fixed rate, so a longer list
  - `F-1.5` Statistic labels are abbreviated at the source.
  - `F-1.6` Favorites are not rendered: with no bindable input a favorite is a name scrolling past.
  - `F-1.7` Every frame carries an explicit `index`.

- **feat** `F-2` Transport
  - `F-2.1` A configured device address is preferred over the cloud — it avoids a round-trip through
  - `F-2.6` Local and cloud are different requests, not one request at two hosts.
  - `F-2.7` The DIY widget UUID is discovered from the device's app list, since it identifies one
  - `F-2.2` Both paths issue their request through Tauri's HTTP client.
  - `F-2.3` The permission is scoped to the LaMetric hosts, not granted globally.
  - `F-2.4` Incomplete configuration builds no transport and issues no request, which is the common
  - `F-2.5` A rejected push is reported through `PushStatus` and logged, never thrown at the caller.
  - `F-2.8` A 2xx is not evidence that anything rendered.

- **feat** `F-3` Push rate
  - `F-3.1` A payload identical to the last one is not sent.
  - `F-3.2` Changes inside the minimum interval are coalesced and the last one is sent on the
  - `F-3.3` The driver runs with no surface rendered, so the display stays live with no panel open.

- **feat** `F-4` Source of the projection
  - `F-4.1` The space is projected by `plugin-space`'s dashboard capability, so one set of queries
  - `F-4.2` This plugin applies its own geometry — the frame count — to those facts.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` A running task takes over the display

- **scenario** `T-2` An indeterminate task still says something

- **scenario** `T-3` Statistics fit without scrolling

- **scenario** `T-4` The device is only addressed when it is configured

- **scenario** `T-7` The DIY widget is found on the device

- **scenario** `T-5` A burst of space changes becomes one push

- **scenario** `T-6` The request is what the device expects

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

This plugin has no `op` extension and ships no registered operations — the driver is a settings config plus a background push loop, not something a user object-model action drives. It is dev-only in `getDefaults` (`isDev`), so OFF for a normal user; enabling it is a Settings action, same caveat as plugin-chess's own enable step.

- **test** `QA-1` Configure a local device and see the display take over — The one user-visible surface — entering transport settings and watching the driver push.

pages.content:

pages.title: LinearPlugin
pages.summary: Integrates Linear into DXOS Composer, mirroring teams, projects, and issues as local-first objects that stay available alongside everything else in the workspace.
pages.content:
Integrates Linear into DXOS Composer, mirroring teams, projects, and issues as local-first objects that stay available alongside everything else in the workspace.

The plugin bridges the Linear GraphQL API with ECHO's object graph using a snapshot-driven three-way merge: remote edits to untouched fields flow in, local edits to untouched fields are preserved, and on conflict the remote wins. The user selects Linear teams; the plugin then pulls all projects for each team as `Project` objects and all issues as `Task` objects keyed by their Linear ids.

Sync is bidirectional (pull then push) per team. The pull phase upserts projects and tasks, refreshing a snapshot for each object. The push phase walks every locally-mirrored object and sends only the fields that diverged from the snapshot, so read-only syncs produce no network traffic. Workflow states are fetched lazily and only when a status-change push is needed. Creating new local issues on Linear is not supported in v1 — push covers edits to already-synced objects only.

Credentials are stored as a Bearer token in an `AccessToken` object inside the user's `Integration`. Linear OAuth produces a single opaque token; no API-key pairing is required. Priority and workflow-state mappings use Linear's stable numeric codes and category constants, not workspace-customisable display names.

## Types

- **type** `Viewer`

- **type** `Team`

- **type** `Project`

- **type** `StateType`

- **type** `IssueState`

- **type** `Issue`

- **type** `WorkflowState`

- **type** `SyncTarget`

- **type** `SyncOptions`

- **type** `PullResult`

## Operations

- **op** `GetLinearTeams` Discovery only — list Linear teams reachable from the integration's token.

- **op** `SyncLinearTeams` Reconcile Linear data for currently-selected team targets in an Integration.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Discover Teams
  - `F-1.1` user opens the integration target picker → op:GetLinearTeams returns one SyncTarget per reachable team, sorted by key; no local object is created

- **feat** `F-2` Pull Projects
  - `F-2.1` SyncLinearTeams runs and a remote project has no matching local Project → a Project is created in ECHO keyed by the remote project id; name and description populated
  - `F-2.2` SyncLinearTeams runs and a remote project has a matching local Project → three-way merge applied per field (name, description);

- **feat** `F-3` Pull Issues
  - `F-3.1` SyncLinearTeams runs and a remote issue has no matching local Task → a Task is created in ECHO keyed by the remote issue id; title, description, status, priority, estimate, project populated
  - `F-3.2` SyncLinearTeams runs and a remote issue has a matching local Task → three-way merge applied per field (title, description, status, priority, estimate);
  - `F-3.3` SyncOptions.maxDaysBack is set → only issues with updatedAt >= (now − maxDaysBack days) are fetched
  - `F-3.4` a remote issue belongs to a project → Task.project ref is set to the corresponding local Project

- **feat** `F-4` Push Projects
  - `F-4.1` a local Project has name or description diverged from its snapshot → Linear.projectUpdate called with only the diverged fields; snapshot refreshed
  - `F-4.2` a local Project is soft-deleted → push skipped for that object

- **feat** `F-5` Push Issues
  - `F-5.1` a local Task has title or description diverged from its snapshot → Linear.issueUpdate called with only the diverged fields
  - `F-5.2` a local Task has status diverged from its snapshot → workflow states fetched (lazy, once per team);
  - `F-5.3` a local Task has priority diverged from its snapshot → Linear.issueUpdate called with the numeric priority (1–4); null sent to clear
  - `F-5.4` a local Task has estimate diverged from its snapshot → Linear.issueUpdate called with estimate; null sent to clear

- **feat** `F-6` Priority Mapping
  - `F-6.1` Linear priority 1 (Urgent) maps to Task.priority 'urgent'.
  - `F-6.2` Linear priority 2 (High) maps to Task.priority 'high'.
  - `F-6.3` Linear priority 3 (Medium) maps to Task.priority 'medium'.
  - `F-6.4` Linear priority 4 (Low) maps to Task.priority 'low'.
  - `F-6.5` Linear priority 0 (None) maps to Task.priority undefined.

- **feat** `F-7` Status Mapping
  - `F-7.1` StateType started maps to Task.status 'in-progress'.
  - `F-7.2` StateType completed or canceled maps to Task.status 'done'.
  - `F-7.3` StateType triage, backlog, or unstarted maps to Task.status 'todo'.
  - `F-7.4` On push, Task.status 'todo' resolves to StateType 'unstarted'.
  - `F-7.5` On push, Task.status 'in-progress' resolves to StateType 'started'.
  - `F-7.6` On push, Task.status 'done' resolves to StateType 'completed'.

- **feat** `F-8` Resilience
  - `F-8.1` an HTTP request or GraphQL transport fails with a 429 or 5xx status → exponential back-off retry with jitter, up to 3 attempts
  - `F-8.2` a request fails with a 4xx status (excluding 429) or returns GraphQL errors → no retry; error propagated immediately
  - `F-8.3` a sync target fails → lastError recorded on that target; remaining targets continue

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Discover teams — no local side effects

- **scenario** `T-2` Pull creates new project

- **scenario** `T-3` Pull creates new task

- **scenario** `T-4` Pull applies three-way merge

- **scenario** `T-5` Push updates diverged project name

- **scenario** `T-6` Push updates diverged task status

- **scenario** `T-7` maxDaysBack limits issue fetch

- **scenario** `T-8` Push skips soft-deleted objects

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

plugin-linear is registered only in the `experimental` array in `plugin-defs.tsx` — it is not in `getDefaults` under any environment, so it is OFF by default even in dev builds, and enabling it is a Settings action. The whole test additionally requires a real Linear OAuth `Integration` with a Bearer token — there is no local fixture for the Linear GraphQL API in this repo's QA harness.

pages.title: LingoPlugin
pages.summary: A Composer plugin for reading in a language you are learning.
pages.content:
A Composer plugin for reading in a language you are learning. Vocabulary lives in the space as ECHO objects, collected into **word lists** and drilled with flashcards on a Leitner schedule. The plugin's centre of gravity is the **reading companion**: a read-only pane beside any document, email or transcript that holds a whole-passage translation and a structural analysis of the source, so hovering a word reveals its meaning and clicking a clause highlights the same clause in the translation.

Analysis is a single cheap-model call that returns nested regions quoted verbatim; character offsets are computed deterministically from those quotes, because a model cannot count characters but can copy a phrase exactly. The result is cached on an `Analysis` object keyed by subject and language, so reopening a document costs a query rather than a model call.

## Types

- **type** `Level` CEFR proficiency band.

- **type** `Language` A language the user is studying.

- **type** `Vocabulary` A word list, scoped to one language.

- **type** `Progress` One word's Leitner schedule state.

- **type** `Word` A single vocabulary entry.

- **type** `Range` Half-open character range `[start, end)` within one text.

- **type** `SegmentKind` Coarse to fine; a smaller index is a larger region.

- **type** `Segment` One analyzed region, carrying its extent in the source and — when the analysis ran over a language pair — the corresponding extent in the translation.

- **type** `Analysis` A cached structural analysis of one object's text.

- **type** `Settings` Plugin settings, persisted per profile.

## Components

- **component** `ReaderArticle` The reading companion, offered beside any object whose text this plugin can reach.

- **component** `ReaderPane` One read-only editor pane with the analysis revealed.

- **component** `VocabularyArticle` A word list, ordered by term or by due date.

- **component** `FlashcardsArticle` Companion drill over a deck's due words.

## Operations

- **op** `AddWord` Adds a word to a deck, deduplicating on the term.

- **op** `RecordReview` Records one flashcard answer and advances the word's Leitner schedule.

- **op** `TranslateTerm` Translates a single term in context.

- **op** `TranslatePassage` Translates a whole passage into the base language, preserving its markdown so the two panes line up paragraph for paragraph.

- **op** `AnalyzeText` Analyzes a passage into nested paragraph / sentence / clause / vocabulary regions and caches the result on an Analysis object.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Vocabulary — Word lists as ECHO objects, scoped to a language.
  - `F-1.1` User can create a Language and a Vocabulary via the plugin's create menu.
  - `F-1.2` Deck membership is the Word's `vocabulary` ref; a deck holds no array of words.
  - `F-1.3` Word.language is denormalized so a term resolves across every deck for that language.
  - `F-1.4` AddWord deduplicates on the term and returns the existing Word rather than failing.

- **feat** `F-2` Flashcards — Leitner drill over a deck's due words.
  - `F-2.1` A word with no `progress` is treated as box 0 and is due immediately.
  - `F-2.2` A correct answer advances one box; a miss resets to box 0 and zeroes the streak.
  - `F-2.3` Box intervals are 0, 1, 3, 7 and 21 days.
  - `F-2.4` Each answer is persisted as it is given, not batched at the end of a session.

- **feat** `F-3` Reading companion — A read-only pane beside any object whose text the plugin can reach.
  - `F-3.1` Offered on Markdown documents, Text objects, and any type registered under
  - `F-3.2` The companion never writes to the object it reads.
  - `F-3.3` The language selector defaults to `Settings.language`, then to English — never to
  - `F-3.4` Translating and analyzing is one explicit action; neither runs on open.
  - `F-3.5` The translation and its Analysis can be deleted, returning the pane to its initial state.

- **feat** `F-4` Structural selection — Hover and click select the most specific analyzed region under the pointer.
  - `F-4.1` Hovering outlines the most specific region covering the position; clicking commits it.
  - `F-4.2` The committed selection is distinct from the editor's own text selection.
  - `F-4.3` A committed segment drives the popover, the other pane, and the toolbar actions.
  - `F-4.4` Ranges are NOT mapped through document changes.
  - `F-4.5` Deck vocabulary produces `vocab` segments too, so the editor has one selection

- **feat** `F-5` Analysis caching — One Analysis per subject and language, reused until the text diverges.
  - `F-5.1` Analysis is matched by filtering on the subject AND language refs.
  - `F-5.2` A same-space Ref stores an unqualified URI, so matching compares refs rather than
  - `F-5.3` A cached analysis whose `sourceHash` and `targetHash` both match is returned without
  - `F-5.4` `refresh` forces a fresh analysis regardless.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Create a word list

- **scenario** `T-2` Leitner schedule

- **scenario** `T-3` Leitner reset

- **scenario** `T-4` Most specific region wins

- **scenario** `T-5` Cross-pane selection

- **scenario** `T-6` Analysis is reused

- **scenario** `T-7` Stale analysis dims

- **scenario** `T-8` Harvesting from the analysis

## Design Notes

**The model quotes; deterministic code counts.** `segmentText` asks for regions quoted verbatim and never for offsets. A model cannot count characters reliably but can copy a phrase exactly, so `alignSegments` locates each quote in the source and computes the range itself. Children are aligned within their parent's extent, and a quote that cannot be located is dropped along with its children rather than guessed at.

**Two hashes, not one.** A paired analysis is only valid against the exact translation its target ranges point into. Re-translating the same source moves those offsets, so `targetHash` is checked alongside `sourceHash`.

**Segmentation is shared, not plugin-local.** `Segment`, `Segmentation` and the aligner live in `@dxos/nlp` beside the POS parser, so an extraction pipeline can reuse them without depending on a UI plugin.

**Tokenization uses `Intl.Segmenter`.** A `\p{L}+` regex returns a whole Japanese sentence as one token, so no deck term ever matched. The segmenter is paired with a longest-match over up to four adjacent segments, so compounds ICU splits ("パン屋" → "パン" + "屋") still resolve.

**Reading is requested only where it helps.** The analysis prompt asks for a `reading` on every vocab region when the script needs one — furigana for Japanese, pinyin for Mandarin — and explicitly suppresses it otherwise, since a pronunciation guide for a script the learner already reads is noise.

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

plugin-lingo is dev-only in `getDefaults` (`isDev`), so OFF by default for a normal user.

- **test** `QA-1` Add a word to a deck and drill it to box 3 — The core vocabulary round-trip — create a Language and Vocabulary, add a Word,

- **test** `QA-2` Translate and analyze a passage in the reading companion — The reading-companion round-trip — open a document, run translate + analyze, and confirm

pages.title: MagazinePlugin
pages.summary: A Composer plugin for syndicated content.
pages.content: A Composer plugin for syndicated content. Today it supports RSS and ATproto Feeds whose Posts are synced into the space as ECHO objects. This revision adds **Magazines** — agent-curated collections of articles drawn from one or more Feeds and displayed as a Masonry grid. The user describes in natural language what content a Magazine should gather; pressing *Curate* triggers feed sync followed by an agent that selects matching articles, fetches their text and hero images, and appends them to the Magazine. The design also scaffolds (schema-only) a future tagging feature in which the agent assigns tags to curated Posts to enable navigation, filtering, and feed-discovery flows. ## Types - **type** `FeedType` - **type** `Feed` A subscription source. - **type** `Post` An individual syndicated article. - **type** `Magazine` An agent-curated collection of articles drawn from one or more Feeds. ## Components - **component** `MagazineArticle` Article surface bound to a Magazine object. - **component** `MagazineTile` Single masonry cell rendering a curated Post. - **component** `PostArticle` Independent article surface for a single Post. ## Services - **service** `MagazineSkill` Agent skill referenced by each Magazine's Routine. ## Operations - **op** `SyncFeed` Existing operation. - **op** `ListCandidatePosts` Returns lightweight summaries of Posts from the Magazine's referenced feeds that have NOT yet been added to the Magazine. - **op** `FetchArticleContent` Fetches post.link over HTTP and returns extracted plain text plus any image URLs found (og:image and tags). - **op** `AddPostToMagazine` Writes snippet and imageUrl onto the Post and appends the Post's ref to magazine.posts. - **op** `CurateMagazine` Deterministic one-shot curation invoked by the Curate button. ## Features - **feat** `F-1` Magazine Type — Introduce the Magazine ECHO type with feeds, instructions, and curated posts. - `F-1.1` User can create a Magazine object via the plugin's create menu. - `F-1.2` Magazine.name is optional; magazine is labeled by name when set. - `F-1.3` Magazine.feeds is an array of Ref; empty by default. - `F-1.4` Magazine.routine is an optional Ref, created lazily on first curate; hidden from the standard form input. - `F-1.5` Magazine.posts is an array of Ref; empty by default; insertion order preserved. - **feat** `F-2` Post Extensions — Add optional snippet, imageUrl, readAt, and tags to existing Post type. - `F-2.1` All new fields are optional; existing Post objects load unchanged. - `F-2.2` snippet is a plain string; no max length enforced at schema level. - `F-2.3` imageUrl is a plain string URL. - `F-2.4` readAt is an ISO 8601 timestamp; presence = read, absence = unread. - `F-2.5` tags is a string array; defaults to empty; not populated in this revision. - **feat** `F-3` Magazine Curate Flow — Sync referenced feeds then invoke the agent to curate articles. - `F-3.1` MagazineArticle toolbar includes a Curate button. - `F-3.2` user clicks Curate → button shows spinner, is disabled, tooltip shows phase ('Syncing feeds...' / 'Curating articles...') - `F-3.3` Curate runs → SyncFeed invoked in parallel for each Ref in magazine.feeds; per-feed failures are collected but do not abort the flow - `F-3.4` all feed syncs resolve (success or failure) → CurateMagazine operation is invoked with the Magazine ref - `F-3.5` CurateMagazine completes → button returns to idle; reactive UI renders the new tiles - `F-3.6` magazine.feeds is empty → Curate button is disabled with tooltip 'Add at least one feed first' - `F-3.7` Re-clicking Curate while running is a no-op (button disabled; in-memory running flag). - **feat** `F-4` Agent Curation Behavior — Agent uses tools to select, fetch, and add Posts. - `F-4.1` Agent reads magazine.instructions Text and magazine.feeds refs from context. - `F-4.2` Agent calls ListCandidatePosts(magazineId) to receive unenriched candidates. - `F-4.3` Agent filters candidates against the instructions and skips low-relevance posts. - `F-4.4` For each selected Post, agent calls FetchArticleContent(postId) to obtain text and images. - `F-4.5` Agent produces a concise snippet (target ~200 chars) and selects the best image URL. - `F-4.6` Agent calls AddPostToMagazine(magazineId, postId, snippet, imageUrl). - `F-4.7` AddPostToMagazine is idempotent; re-invocation with the same postId is a no-op append. - **feat** `F-5` Masonry Display — Render curated Posts in a Masonry grid with rich tiles. - `F-5.1` MagazineArticle renders magazine.posts in reverse insertion order (newest first) in a Masonry grid. - `F-5.2` Each tile shows imageUrl (if present), title, snippet, feed name, author, published date. - `F-5.3` Tile tags row renders only when post.tags.length > 0. - `F-5.4` Tiles where post.readAt is set are visually dimmed. - `F-5.5` Clicking a tile opens the ArticleReader for that Post. - `F-5.6` Opening the reader sets post.readAt to the current ISO timestamp if not already set. - `F-5.7` Empty state — when magazine.posts is empty — shows: 'No articles yet. - `F-5.8` Grid uses the @dxos/react-ui-masonry Masonry component. - **feat** `F-6` Post Article Detail (master-detail via layout dispatch) — Post detail is rendered by a standalone PostArticle surface. - `F-6.1` PostArticle is registered as a React surface matching - `F-6.2` PostArticle is a Panel with a Toolbar. - `F-6.3` user clicks a tile in MagazineArticle → - post.readAt is set to the current ISO timestamp if unset - `F-6.4` useShowItem is invoked in 'mobile' layout mode → the complementary sidebar opens on linkedSegment('post') - `F-6.5` useShowItem is invoked in 'multi' layout mode → a sibling plank opens for the post's path, pivoted on the magazine - `F-6.6` useShowItem is invoked in the default ('deck') layout mode → the current plank's companion changes to linkedSegment('post') - `F-6.7` An app-graph extension under each Magazine node exposes a - **feat** `F-7` Future Tagging (schema scaffolding only) — Schema fields in place so the tagging feature composes without migration. - `F-7.1` Post.tags exists as Schema.Array(Schema.String).pipe(Schema.optional). - `F-7.2` MagazineTile renders a tags row conditionally on tags.length > 0. - `F-7.3` FetchArticleContent is reusable as the input stage for a future TagPosts operation. ## Acceptance - **scenario** `T-1` Create Magazine - **scenario** `T-2` Post schema backward compatibility - **scenario** `T-3` Curate button disabled without feeds - **scenario** `T-4` Curate flow runs sync then deterministic curation - **scenario** `T-4a` Agent curation via skill — The skill path is distinct from the Curate button (T-4). - **scenario** `T-5` Partial feed sync failure is non-fatal - **scenario** `T-6` ListCandidatePosts excludes curated - **scenario** `T-7` AddPostToMagazine is idempotent - **scenario** `T-8` FetchArticleContent surfaces images - **scenario** `T-9` Tile dimming on read - **scenario** `T-10` Tile metadata ## QA Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number. plugin-magazine is dev-only in `getDefaults` (`isDev`), so OFF by default for a normal user. - **test** `QA-1` Create a Magazine, add a feed, curate deterministically — The button-path round-trip — create a Magazine, attach a Feed, sync it, and run the - **test** `QA-2` Open a curated tile and confirm read state — The master-detail path — clicking a tile opens PostArticle and marks the post read. - **test** `QA-3` Showcase clip — The 10s showcase clip: Browse the Weekend Reading magazine and open an article. --- ## Design Notes ### Curation via Routine (this revision) Curation runs a persisted **Routine** rather than an ephemeral one. The Magazine no longer carries an `instructions` Template; it carries an optional `routine: Ref` plus a `topic` seed string. - **Eager creation.** `Magazine.make()` creates the `Routine` at magazine instantiation time. The Routine's `instructions` Text is seeded with the default editorial methodology and an optional topic woven into a `## Topic` section; it references the MagazineSkill and is parented to the magazine (cascade-delete). The magazine is added to the Routine's `objects` (context). - **Run.** The curate op invokes `AgentPrompt` (Run Routine) with `prompt: magazine.routine` and the candidate JSON `input`; it decodes the `completeJob` structured output and applies selections mechanically (keep-bound, per-post snippet/imageUrl). No ephemeral routine is constructed. - **Instruction split.** Skill = HOW (FetchArticleContent + completeJob contract). Routine = editorial (selection criteria, dedup, snippet style, hero-image choice) + topic. This removes the prior overlap where the skill held both. - **Properties editing.** The `routine` field carries `FormInlineAnnotation`, so the Routine's own fields (name, description, instructions) render inline in the generic `DefaultProperties` companion — no custom surface needed. - **Template.** `Template` is retained (it is the type of `Skill.instructions` and is used across the codebase). The Magazine simply stops using it; the Routine's `instructions` is a plain `Ref`. ### Content Flow Two curation paths exist side-by-side: - **Button path (deterministic).** The Curate toolbar button runs `SyncFeed` per referenced feed, then invokes `CurateMagazine`. Snippets and images are derived from each Post's existing `description` field (no HTTP, no LLM). Chosen for the user-initiated button because it is fast, reliable, and does not depend on an LLM runtime being present. - **Agent path (skill).** The `MagazineSkill` exposes three fine-grained tools (`ListCandidatePosts`, `FetchArticleContent`, `AddPostToMagazine`) and an instruction template that tells an agent to consult `Magazine.instructions` when selecting Posts. Triggered when an agent chat references the Magazine — not when the button is clicked. Delivers higher-quality curation (full-article fetch + LLM-driven selection) at the cost of latency and LLM availability. `SyncFeed` is always run deterministically (either by the button or outside the scope of this feature). Neither curation path fetches feed indices on its own — that is `SyncFeed`'s job. ### Tool Granularity Three tools rather than one combined `curateMagazine` tool: - `ListCandidatePosts` returns lightweight summaries so the agent can triage cheaply without loading article bodies. - `FetchArticleContent` is a read-only HTTP fetch + extract; it is reusable by the future `TagPosts` operation which will need the same inputs. - `AddPostToMagazine` is the sole mutation. Idempotence lives in this tool (by ref-set membership check) rather than in the prompt. Quality of selection is the agent's job; the tools deliberately don't try to rank or filter on the agent's behalf. ### Snippet Storage `Post.snippet` is a plain inline string, not a `Ref`. Snippets are short (~200 chars target) and read-only to the user; the `Ref` indirection used for `Agent.instructions` and `Magazine.instructions` is appropriate for long-form, user-editable content and is not needed here. ### Read State Represented as an optional ISO timestamp `readAt`, not a boolean or enum. Absence = unread; presence = read (at that time). This leaves room to show "read 2 days ago" or to expire reads without a schema change. ### Image Extraction `FetchArticleContent` returns a list of candidate image URLs; the agent picks the "best" one for the Post's `imageUrl`. The prompt should prefer `og:image` when present. If no suitable image exists the Post is still added with `imageUrl` undefined — `MagazineTile` renders without the image region. HTML parsing uses whatever parser the existing codebase already uses for similar tasks. If no parser is in use, `linkedom` is the proposed addition — small, no-DOM-globals footprint, works in Node and browser. Addition of a parser dependency is a decision point flagged during implementation planning. ### Deduplication Policy Deduplication is keyed on Post ref identity, not on URL or guid. If a Post is removed from the Magazine and later re-curated, the agent will re-add it. Dedup across a Feed's historical sync is out of scope — `Feed` already deduplicates on `guid` when syncing. ### Relationship to Future Tagging The tagging feature is strictly additive to this design: - `Post.tags` already exists as an optional string array. - `FetchArticleContent` is the reusable read-stage for tagging. - `MagazineTile` renders a tags row when non-empty — no UI change needed. - A `TagPosts` operation and either an extended prompt in `MagazineSkill` or a second `MagazineTagger` skill will complete the feature in a later revision. Further future work enabled by tags (all out of scope here): tag-filter chips in the Magazine toolbar; a "Find more like this" action prompting the agent to curate Posts with overlapping tags; a "Suggest feeds" action proposing new Feed URLs based on accumulated tag distribution. ### Out of Scope - Rendering the full original article body inside the reader (would require storing full extracted text; current design stores only the snippet). - Scheduled / background Curate runs — this revision only supports the explicit toolbar-triggered flow. - Cross-Magazine deduplication — two Magazines may both curate the same Post. - Editing or regenerating a snippet after curation — re-curation is the path to different content.

pages.title: MapSolidPlugin
pages.summary: A SolidJS-native map surface plugin for `DXOS` Composer.
pages.content:
A SolidJS-native map surface plugin for `DXOS` Composer. Provides an alternative rendering path for `Map` objects using SolidJS Web Components, delivering fine-grained reactivity for high-frequency geospatial updates without a React reconciler.

## Types

- **type** `MapViewType` Rendering mode for the map surface.

- **type** `GeoMarker` A resolved geographic pin derived from a dataset row.

- **type** `MapSurfaceData` Data payload injected into the dx-map-surface Web Component.

## Components

- **component** `MapSurface` SolidJS Web Component (custom element dx-map-surface) that renders a Map object.

- **component** `MapControl` Leaflet-based 2-D tile map rendered with SolidJS reactive primitives.

- **component** `GlobeControl` 3-D interactive globe rendered with SolidJS reactive primitives.

## Operations

- **op** `resolveSurfaceMarkers` Derives a reactive GeoMarker list from a Map object's linked View.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` SolidJS Surface Registration
  - `F-1.1` MapSolidPlugin registers the dx-map-surface custom element on plugin activation.
  - `F-1.2` a Map object is opened with role article or section → the ReactSurface capability routes rendering to dx-map-surface at position first
  - `F-1.3` The surface filter uses Obj.instanceOf(Map.Map) so only genuine Map ECHO objects match.

- **feat** `F-2` Reactive Marker Derivation
  - `F-2.1` the Map's linked View changes → the typename and schema signals update; the ECHO query re-runs automatically
  - `F-2.2` a row is added to the dataset → a new GeoMarker appears on the surface without a full component remount
  - `F-2.3` a row's GeoPoint field is absent or malformed → that row is excluded from the marker list silently

- **feat** `F-3` View Toggle
  - `F-3.1` the user triggers onToggle on MapControl → local type signal switches to globe; GlobeControl is shown
  - `F-3.2` the user triggers onToggle on GlobeControl → local type signal switches to map; MapControl is shown
  - `F-3.3` Toggle state is local to each dx-map-surface instance.

- **feat** `F-4` No Shadow DOM
  - `F-4.1` The custom element calls noShadowDOM() so Tailwind utility classes from the host apply inside the component.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Surface renders for Map object

- **scenario** `T-2` Markers appear from linked view

- **scenario** `T-3` Malformed coordinate filtered

- **scenario** `T-4` Toggle to globe

- **scenario** `T-5` Filter rejects non-Map object

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Create a Map and view it through the SolidJS surface — The plugin contributes no operations of its own — `resolveSurfaceMarkers` is a reactive derivation, not an invocable op, and creating a Map goes through the generic CreateObjectEntry factory like plugin-chess's `startGa…

---

pages.title: MapPlugin
pages.summary: An interactive geospatial mapping plugin for `DXOS` Composer.
pages.content:
An interactive geospatial mapping plugin for `DXOS` Composer. Renders table records that contain latitude/longitude coordinates as pins on a zoomable map or 3-D globe. Supports creating map objects backed by a view over any ECHO dataset, with a geolocation field selector for automatic marker placement.

The map surface is generic: any plugin can contribute a `MarkerProvider` capability that plots its own object type (e.g. plugin-trip plots a `Trip`'s segments). When a provider matches an object the plugin also offers a map **companion** for it. A configured MapTiler API key (plugin settings) selects the tile provider; otherwise OpenStreetMap is used.

## Types

- **type** `GeoPoint` A geographic coordinate pair stored in GeoJSON [lng, lat] order.

- **type** `MapViewType`

- **type** `Map` An ECHO object representing a named geospatial map, optionally linked to a view over a dataset.

- **type** `CreateMap` Input schema for the create-object dialog.

- **type** `MapState` Transient viewport state held in a plugin-scoped Atom.

- **type** `APIKey` A named API key scoped to a service domain (defined in @dxos/schema).

- **type** `MapSettings` Plugin-scoped settings surfaced as a form via AppCapabilities.Settings.

- **type** `GeoLine` Origin → destination arc, rendered as a great-circle line on the globe.

- **type** `MarkerSet` Reactive marker data a MarkerProvider resolves for a subject.

- **type** `MarkerProvider` Capability (array) contributed by any plugin that can plot a subject.

## Components

- **component** `MapArticle` Generic map surface (article / section / inline 'map' role / companion).

- **component** `MapViewEditor` Object-properties panel for picking the dataset view and geolocation field.

## Operations

- **op** `createMap` Creates a new Map ECHO object, optionally with a view derived from a dataset.

- **op** `toggleMapView` Toggles the active MapState between map and globe rendering modes.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Map Creation
  - `F-1.1` User can create a Map object from the space or collection create menu.
  - `F-1.2` typename is provided in the creation form → a ViewModel is created for that schema; Map.view references it
  - `F-1.3` locationFieldName is provided → the View's pivotFieldId is set to the corresponding field id
  - `F-1.4` A Map with no view can still display static coordinates from Map.coordinates.

- **feat** `F-2` Geospatial Rendering
  - `F-2.1` a Map object is opened as article or section → MapArticle renders in the current MapState.type mode (map or globe)
  - `F-2.2` Map.view is set → the plugin queries the linked dataset and converts rows to GeoMarker pins
  - `F-2.3` a row's GeoPoint field is absent or malformed → that row is silently omitted from the marker list
  - `F-2.4` MapState.type === globe → GlobeControl is rendered instead of MapControl

- **feat** `F-3` View Toggle
  - `F-3.1` the toggle operation is invoked → MapState.type flips between map and globe
  - `F-3.2` Toggle state is plugin-scoped; all open map surfaces reflect the change.

- **feat** `F-4` Object Properties
  - `F-4.1` Map object properties are opened → MapViewEditor is rendered in the properties panel
  - `F-4.2` User can change the source typename and geolocation field from the editor.

- **feat** `F-5` Skill
  - `F-5.1` MapPlugin contributes a Skill that enables AI to create and update maps.
  - `F-5.2` The skill instructions describe the plugin's geospatial capabilities.

- **feat** `F-6` Pluggable marker providers & companion — Gating the companion on a matching provider lives in the app-graph-builder connector (capability-aware).
  - `F-6.1` MapPlugin registers a built-in MarkerProvider for Map objects (view rows → pins).
  - `F-6.2` Other plugins can contribute a MarkerProvider for their own object types.
  - `F-6.3` a MarkerProvider matches an object (other than a Map itself) → a 'map' companion is offered for that object via the app graph
  - `F-6.4` Selecting a marker (map click or nearest-marker globe click) dispatches LayoutOperation.Select.

- **feat** `F-7` Tile providers via API keys
  - `F-7.1` Plugin settings expose an `apiKeys` list of { name, domain, apiKey }.
  - `F-7.2` The apiKeys property is annotated with recognized domains (e.g.
  - `F-7.3` an API key for 'maptiler.com' is configured → the map renders MapTiler tiles; otherwise OpenStreetMap is used

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Create map without view

- **scenario** `T-2` Create map with view

- **scenario** `T-3` Toggle map/globe

- **scenario** `T-4` Malformed GeoPoint omitted

- **scenario** `T-5` Object properties editor shown

- **scenario** `T-6` Companion offered for a provided object

- **scenario** `T-7` MapTiler tiles when key configured

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

plugin-map is NOT in `getDefaults` under any environment (not even `isDev`) — it is OFF by default in every build. Enabling is a UI action (Settings -> plugin registry).

- **test** `QA-1` Create a map over a dataset, see markers, toggle to globe — The core map round-trip — create a Map from an existing GeoPoint-bearing dataset, confirm
- **test** `QA-2` Showcase clip — The 10s showcase clip: Fly into London to street level, on to Tokyo, then spin the globe.

---

pages.title: MarkdownPlugin
pages.summary: Collaborative markdown editor plugin for `DXOS` Composer.
pages.content:
Collaborative markdown editor plugin for `DXOS` Composer. Beyond editing, it hosts the document **review model**: checkpoints, branches and merge (`@dxos/versioning`), the version toolbar/banner UI, and the ambient Google-Docs-style review surface (Editing / Suggesting / Viewing) that overlays every author's suggestions and comments on the live editor.

## External types & capabilities

The review model composes primitives owned elsewhere:

- `Version`, `Branch`, `History`, `BranchBinding` (`@dxos/versioning`) — named checkpoints, per-object branches (`kind: 'draft' | 'suggestion'`), CRDT merge, and the writable per-surface branch binding.
- `VersioningCapabilities.VersioningState` / `ReviewMode` / `ReviewRenderPolicy` / `HistoryProvider` (`@dxos/plugin-versioning`) — the per-user selection + review-mode state, the mode→visibility policy, and the generic history-companion gate. This plugin contributes a `HistoryProvider` and consumes the rest.
- `trackChanges`, `suggestions({ base })`, `suggestionsOverlay`, `rebaseHunks`, `diffView`, `mergeConflicts` (`@dxos/ui-editor`) — the inline tracked-change / diff / overlay extensions.
- `MarkdownCapabilities.SuggestionSourcesProvider` — the slot plugin-comments contributes to; this plugin consumes it to overlay other authors' suggestions without a dependency cycle.
- `CollaborationOperation.AcceptChange` / `RejectChange` (`@dxos/app-toolkit`) — the durable cherry-pick/revert ops the ambient accept/reject controls route through.

## Types

- **type** `ViewMode`

- **type** `DiffView` How a selected branch is compared against its parent (default `suggest`).

- **type** `Document`

- **type** `Settings`

## Services

- **service** `HistoryProvider` Contributes VersioningCapabilities.HistoryProvider for Markdown.Document, so plugin-versioning renders the generic version-history companion (timeline of checkpoints/branches/merges) for markdown docs.

- **service** `SuggestionSourcesConsumer` MarkdownArticle consumes MarkdownCapabilities.SuggestionSourcesProvider (contributed by plugin-comments) to enumerate every active suggestion branch and overlay them, diffed against main, on the ambient editor.

## Components

- **component** `MarkdownArticle` Full-surface markdown editor for a Document or Text subject.
- **component** `VersionToolbar` The version-review banner row shown above the editor while off "main @ now": a slim strip for the active checkpoint / branch / fork (at most one selected).
- **component** `VersionBanner` A single banner (checkpoint | branch | fork).
- **component** `MarkdownCard` Read-only preview card for embedding a Document in other surfaces.
- **component** `EditableMarkdownCard` Inline-editable card variant used when data.editable is true.

## Operations

- **op** `create` Creates a new markdown Document and adds it to the active space.
- **op** `createDraft` UI-facing factory invoked by the navtree create action.
- **op** `open` Reads the current contents of a markdown Document.
- **op** `update` Applies a set of find/replace edits to a markdown Document (optionally on a branch).
- **op** `CreateBranch` Fork a core branch off main (or a checkpoint), returning the branch's canonical content DXN.
- **op** `MergeBranch` CRDT-merge a branch back into main and archive its registry entry.
- **op** `CreateCheckpoint` Record a named checkpoint (Version) of main or the selected branch's heads.
- **op** `SuggestEdit` Find-or-create the caller's per-author `kind:'suggestion'` branch and apply edits to it, so the proposal accrues for review rather than mutating main.
- **op** `scrollToAnchor` Scrolls the editor for the attendable surface to a cursor position.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Edit Document
  - `F-1.1` Editor opens Document.content as a collaborative CodeMirror surface.
  - `F-1.2` Edits replicate to all peers via ECHO Text.
  - `F-1.3` Document.name renders as the surface title; fallbackName used when name is empty.
- **feat** `F-2` View Modes
  - `F-2.1` Document opens in settings.defaultViewMode (source | preview | readonly).
  - `F-2.2` user toggles view mode → editor switches between source and preview; state persists per Document
  - `F-2.3` viewMode is readonly → editor is non-editable; toolbar hidden
- **feat** `F-3` Formatting Toolbar
  - `F-3.1` settings.toolbar is true → formatting toolbar shown above editor with bold, italic, headings, lists, links
  - `F-3.2` Toolbar surfaces toolbar-disposition actions from the app graph for the current attendable.
- **feat** `F-4` Inline References
  - `F-4.1` user types `@` in the editor → link query opens with objects from the active space
