pages.title: MeetingRecorderPlugin
pages.summary: Granola-style meeting notes for calls held in other apps.
pages.content:
Granola-style meeting notes for calls held in other apps. On Composer Desktop the plugin notices when another app (Zoom, Meet in a browser, Teams, FaceTime, Slack, …) starts using the microphone, offers to take notes, and records the call into a `Meeting` (plugin-meeting) with a live transcript — the microphone as the local user, the system audio as the other participants. When the app releases the microphone the recording stops and the meeting is summarized.

The native half is the `tauri-plugin-meeting-capture` crate (`packages/apps/composer-app/src-tauri/plugins/meeting-capture`), modelled on anarlog's `detect` and `audio` crates: CoreAudio process objects (`kAudioProcessPropertyIsRunningInput`) for detection and a global process tap for system audio. A browser build records the microphone only, started by hand.

## Types

- **type** `MicApp` An app holding the microphone, as the native side reports it.

- **type** `RecorderState` The recorder's lifecycle; held in MeetingRecorderCapabilities.State.

- **type** `Settings`

## Components

- **component** `RecorderStatus` Status-bar item standing in for Granola's menu-bar control.

## Operations

- **op** `Start` Creates a Meeting in the given (or active) space, opens it, and starts transcribing the microphone and, on desktop, the system audio.

- **op** `Stop` Stops capture after the buffered audio is transcribed, then summarizes the meeting when autoSummarize is on.

- **op** `HandleDetection` Applies the settings and ignore list to a change in the apps using the microphone; prompts, starts or stops accordingly.

- **op** `ClearDetection` Returns a detected-but-unanswered meeting to idle without recording it.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Meeting Detection
  - `F-1.1` On desktop, the native side reports every change in the set of apps holding the microphone, excluding Composer and the WebKit helpers that record on its behalf.
  - `F-1.2` a non-ignored app starts using the microphone and the recorder is idle → the recorder enters `detected` and shows a "Take notes" prompt naming the app
  - `F-1.3` Apps in the ignore list (dictation, IDEs, screen recorders, AI assistants) never prompt.
  - `F-1.4` With autoStart, detection starts recording without a prompt.
  - `F-1.5` A detected app releasing the microphone before the prompt is answered returns the recorder to idle.

- **feat** `F-2` Recording
  - `F-2.1` Starting creates a Meeting (with transcript, notes and summary) in the active space and opens it.
  - `F-2.2` The microphone is transcribed with the local identity as sender.
  - `F-2.3` On desktop, the system audio is transcribed with sender "<App> participants".
  - `F-2.4` Each source is segmented at speech pauses (SpeakingMonitor), not at a fixed interval.
  - `F-2.5` Without system-audio permission the recording continues from the microphone alone.

- **feat** `F-3` Stopping
  - `F-3.1` Stopping transcribes the audio still buffered before closing the pipeline.
  - `F-3.2` With autoStop, the meeting app releasing the microphone stops the recording.
  - `F-3.3` With autoSummarize, stopping runs MeetingOperation.Summarize on the meeting.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Detect, prompt and record

- **scenario** `T-2` Ignored app

- **scenario** `T-3` Meeting ends

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Detect a meeting in another app and record it into a Meeting — The Granola round-trip — a meeting app takes the microphone, the user takes notes, speech is transcribed, the meeting ends and is summarized.

---

pages.title: MeetingPlugin
pages.summary: A meeting management plugin for DXOS Composer that captures notes, transcribes audio in real time, and generates AI-powered summaries of meetings held inside a call or video session.
pages.content:
A meeting management plugin for DXOS Composer that captures notes, transcribes audio in real time, and generates AI-powered summaries of meetings held inside a call or video session.

## Types

- **type** `Meeting`

- **type** `MeetingState`

## Components

- **component** `MeetingArticle` Detail view for a single Meeting object; shows notes and AI summary side-by-side.

- **component** `MeetingsList` Companion panel shown alongside a call channel; lists all meetings in the space.

## Operations

- **op** `Create` Creates a new Meeting object in the given space, including linked Transcript, notes, and summary Text objects.

- **op** `SetActive` Sets the currently active meeting in plugin state and broadcasts the meeting DXN to the call layer as an activity payload.

- **op** `HandlePayload` Processes an incoming call-layer meeting payload; resolves the Meeting and Transcript feed objects from ECHO and updates transcription state.

- **op** `Summarize` Reads transcript and notes content from the active Meeting, sends them to the AI model, and writes the resulting markdown back to meeting.summary.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Meeting Creation
  - `F-1.1` A new Meeting is created with an ISO timestamp and empty participants list.
  - `F-1.2` The meeting is linked to a freshly created Transcript feed object.
  - `F-1.3` Empty notes and summary Text objects are created and linked.
  - `F-1.4` meeting is created from the MeetingsList panel → meeting is immediately set as the active meeting

- **feat** `F-2` Active Meeting
  - `F-2.1` op:SetActive is invoked with a meeting → plugin state activeMeeting is updated
  - `F-2.2` op:SetActive is invoked with a meeting → call layer is updated with meeting DXN as activity payload
  - `F-2.3` op:SetActive is invoked with undefined → active meeting is cleared and call layer activity is reset

- **feat** `F-3` Real-Time Transcription
  - `F-3.1` user joins a call → TranscriptionManager is opened and stored in plugin state
  - `F-3.2` HandlePayload is received with transcriptionEnabled: true → transcription starts writing to the linked Transcript feed
  - `F-3.3` user's speaking state changes → TranscriptionManager.setRecording is called with the current value
  - `F-3.4` user leaves the call → TranscriptionManager is closed and plugin state is reset

- **feat** `F-4` AI Summary
  - `F-4.1` user requests a summary → op:Summarize combines transcript text and notes content as input
  - `F-4.2` AI model returns a result → markdown is written to meeting.summary and persisted via ECHO
  - `F-4.3` summary already exists → MeetingArticle shows a regenerate button instead of the initial generate button
  - `F-4.4` no tasks are found in the transcript → tasks section is omitted from the summary

- **feat** `F-5` Notes
  - `F-5.1` Notes section always rendered in MeetingArticle regardless of summary state.
  - `F-5.2` Notes are persisted as a linked Text object in ECHO and replicated to all peers.

- **feat** `F-6` Entity Extraction
  - `F-6.1` entityExtraction setting is true and a transcript message arrives → Assistant annotates mentions of known objects (people, organisations) in the message
  - `F-6.2` entityExtraction setting is false → messages are stored without annotation enrichment

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Create meeting

- **scenario** `T-2` Set active meeting

- **scenario** `T-3` Clear active meeting

- **scenario** `T-4` Handle incoming payload

- **scenario** `T-5` Generate summary

- **scenario** `T-6` Regenerate summary

- **scenario** `T-7` Transcription lifecycle

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Create a meeting, set it active, and generate a summary — The core meeting round-trip — create against a call channel, make it the active meeting, generate an AI summary.

- **test** `QA-2` A four-person meeting call, with notes taken during it — The local user joins a Meeting's call after three colleagues have started, is greeted, they talk, and the local user writes the action items into the meeting's notes.

pages.title: MessengerPlugin
pages.summary: Cross-space notifications for Composer.
pages.content:
Cross-space notifications for Composer. Contacts and bots send short messages through the HALO inbox (signed envelopes relayed by EDGE); each recipient device stores them once in a feed in the user's default space and lists them in a deck companion panel with an unread badge. Space invitations are messages too: they render plugin-client's Join/Open surface and raise a toast on the device that stored them. A message is an alert that points elsewhere — a short text and a link to the object where the work lives — not a chat channel.

Design: `agents/superpowers/specs/2026-10-04-plugin-messenger-design.md`.

## Types

- **type** `Notifications` Not a user type, so it never appears in the navtree.

- **type** `StoredMessage`

## Capabilities

- **component** `MessengerCapabilities.Sender` `send(recipientDid, message): Effect<void, InboxSendError>`.

- **component** `MessengerCapabilities.NotificationsContainers` Atom of the default space's Notifications containers, the one every device writes to first; empty until one exists, and more than one only until the materializer converges them.

- **component** `InboxMaterializer` Startup module (ClientEvents.SpacesAvailable).

## Components

- **component** `NotificationTile` Mosaic tile (in the NotificationsPanel folder) — unread dot, subject, time; invitation surface or sender + text + links; menu.

- **component** `NotificationsPanel` Panel with a toggle-group filter (all / unread / invitations) and "Mark all as read", over a Mosaic.VirtualStack of NotificationTile, newest first.

- **component** `MessengerCompanion` Deck companion `messenger` (icon ph--envelope--regular).

## Operations

- **op** `send` Sends a notification to a contact through MessengerCapabilities.Sender.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Materialization
  - `F-1.1` a contact's message arrives in the HALO inbox → it is stored once in the default space's notifications feed and then acked
  - `F-1.2` a message arrives from a non-contact → it stays pending and is shown if the sender later becomes a contact
  - `F-1.3` two devices of one identity receive the same envelope → one copy is stored; both ack
  - `F-1.4` a space invitation is stored → the storing device shows a toast with Join; other devices do not

- **feat** `F-2` Panel
  - `F-2.1` there are unread notifications → the envelope tab in R0 shows the unread count
  - `F-2.2` the user clicks a notification → it is marked read and its first linked object is opened
  - `F-2.3` the user picks a filter → only all / unread / invitation notifications are listed
  - `F-2.4` the user chooses Mark as unread or Delete from a tile's menu → the read state changes, or the message leaves the feed

- **feat** `F-3` Sending
  - `F-3.1` a plugin or agent sends to a contact's DID → the message is relayed; non-contacts and oversized messages fail with typed errors

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Two users

---

## QA

- **test** `QA-1` A contact's notification reaches the panel — Send from one identity, receive and read on another, through the storybook harness.

pages.title: NativePlugin
pages.summary: A Tauri-based native platform integration plugin for DXOS Composer that enables desktop-specific capabilities on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
pages.content:
A Tauri-based native platform integration plugin for DXOS Composer that enables desktop-specific capabilities on macOS, Linux, and Windows. It manages Spotlight window integration, over-the-air application updates, and an Ollama sidecar process for local AI model inference.

## Types

- **type** `Settings`

- **type** `UpdateStatus`

- **type** `UpdateState`

## Components

- **component** `NativeSettings` Settings panel section rendered inside the global Settings dialog under the App (native) plugin entry.

## Operations

- **op** `CheckForUpdate` Initiates an OTA update check via the Tauri updater plugin.

- **op** `InstallUpdate` Downloads and installs a pending update, streaming progress events to the UpdateManager status atom.

- **op** `RelaunchApp` Relaunches the Tauri app process to apply the installed update.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Spotlight Window Integration
  - `F-1.1` the main Composer window receives a spotlight:invoke Tauri event with operation = 'open' → the LayoutOperation.Open intent is dispatched with the payload, decoded against its input schema
  - `F-1.2` the main Composer window receives a spotlight:invoke event with operation = 'switch-workspace' → the LayoutOperation.SwitchWorkspace intent is dispatched with the payload, decoded against its input schema
  - `F-1.3` a spotlight:invoke event is handled successfully → the main Composer window is shown and brought to focus
  - `F-1.4` a spotlight:invoke event carries an unrecognised operation → a warning is logged and no intent is dispatched
  - `F-1.5` a spotlight:invoke payload does not decode against the operation's input schema → the error is logged and no intent is dispatched

- **feat** `F-2` Over-the-Air Updates
  - `F-2.1` the Updater module activates on a supported platform (macOS, Linux, Windows) in production → a background Effect fiber is started that checks for updates immediately and repeats hourly
  - `F-2.2` an update is available and successfully downloaded → a toast notification is shown with a Relaunch action; the status atom transitions to ready
  - `F-2.3` the Tauri updater check throws → the status atom transitions to failed with a human-readable error string
  - `F-2.4` the app is running in a dev-server build (port not in TAURI_LOCALHOST_PORTS) → the updater is disabled and status remains unsupported
  - `F-2.5` the Updater module is torn down → the background update-check fiber is interrupted cleanly

- **feat** `F-3` Ollama Sidecar
  - `F-3.1` the AssistantEvents.SetupAiServiceProviders event fires → the Ollama sidecar binary is spawned via Tauri shell on localhost port 21434
  - `F-3.2` the Ollama sidecar is running → it is registered as an AiModelResolver under AppCapabilities.AiModelResolver
  - `F-3.3` the Ollama capability is torn down → the sidecar process is killed and the managed runtime is disposed

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Spotlight open dispatches LayoutOperation.Open

- **scenario** `T-2` Unknown spotlight operation is silently dropped

- **scenario** `T-3` Update check transitions status atom

- **scenario** `T-4` Failed update check transitions to failed status

- **scenario** `T-5` Dev-server build disables updater

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Check for an OTA update — The plugin contributes no runtime operation — `CheckForUpdate`, `InstallUpdate`, and `RelaunchApp` are direct calls into the Tauri updater/shell plugins from native-only code (`Updater` module, `SpotlightListener`), not…

pages.title: NavTreePlugin
pages.summary: Hierarchical navigation sidebar for `DXOS` Composer — renders the application graph as a collapsible tree, manages workspace tabs, exposes keyboard-driven command search, and handles drag-and-drop rearrangement of spaces, folders, and objects.
pages.content:
Hierarchical navigation sidebar for `DXOS` Composer — renders the application graph as a collapsible tree, manages workspace tabs, exposes keyboard-driven command search, and handles drag-and-drop rearrangement of spaces, folders, and objects.

## Types

- **type** `NavTreeItemState`

- **type** `KeyBinding`

- **type** `NodeProperties`

## Components

- **component** `NavTree` Root navigation tree that renders workspace tabs at the top level and a collapsible subtree for the active workspace.

- **component** `NavTreeContainer` Smart container that wires the NavTree to the app graph, layout state, and drag-and-drop monitor.

- **component** `CommandsDialogContent` Full-screen command palette dialog — surfaces all graph actions, searchable by label.

- **component** `CommandsTrigger` Search-input surface slot component — opens the commands dialog on click or ⇧⌘K / Ctrl+Shift+K.

## Operations

- **op** `expose` Expands tree nodes along the path to a subject and marks each as open so the item becomes visible in the NavTree.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Sidebar Navigation
  - `F-1.1` NavTree renders all root-level graph connections as workspace tabs.
  - `F-1.2` user selects a workspace tab → LayoutOperation.SwitchWorkspace is invoked; subtree for that workspace is expanded
  - `F-1.3` sidebar is closed and user selects a workspace tab → sidebar opens (state transitions to expanded)
  - `F-1.4` same active tab is clicked while sidebar is expanded → sidebar collapses (state transitions to collapsed or closed on mobile)

- **feat** `F-2` Tree Expand / Collapse
  - `F-2.1` Tree items with children show an expand/collapse toggle.
  - `F-2.2` user expands a node → open state persisted to localStorage keyed by path; Graph.expand called for the node
  - `F-2.3` plugin initialises after layout is ready → all paths previously marked open are re-expanded from localStorage
  - `F-2.4` op:expose is called → all ancestors of the subject are expanded and marked open

- **feat** `F-3` Item Selection
  - `F-3.1` user selects a non-current item → LayoutOperation.Open is invoked with disposition 'solo' and the shift modifier forwarded
  - `F-3.2` user option-clicks a currently active item → LayoutOperation.Close is invoked for that item
  - `F-3.3` user clicks a currently active item without option key → LayoutOperation.ScrollIntoView is invoked
  - `F-3.4` item has a default disposition action → that action is run after navigation
  - `F-3.5` navigation succeeds on mobile → sidebar is closed automatically

- **feat** `F-4` Drag and Drop
  - `F-4.1` NavTree items can be dragged to rearrange within the same parent.
  - `F-4.2` NavTree items can be dragged to a different parent, moving within a shared move scope and linking elsewhere when the target accepts links.
  - `F-4.3` drop instruction is rearrange → onRearrange callback on the parent node is called with the new order
  - `F-4.4` the source's parent and the target share a move scope → onMoveOut is called on the source's parent, then onMoveIn on the target
  - `F-4.5` the drop crosses a move scope and the target accepts links → onLink callback on the target is called and the source's parent is left alone
  - `F-4.6` target node's blockInstruction returns true for an instruction → that instruction is blocked and the drop is not applied
  - `F-4.7` the dropped item would only be listed at the target, its parent elsewhere → the drop indicator is dashed

- **feat** `F-5` Keyboard Shortcuts
  - `F-5.1` NavTree plugin registers keyboard shortcuts for all graph actions that declare a keyBinding property.
  - `F-5.2` Graph is traversed on change (debounced 500 ms) to bind newly added shortcuts.
  - `F-5.3` The commands dialog is opened via ⇧⌘K (macOS) / Ctrl+Shift+K (Windows/Linux).
  - `F-5.4` plugin deactivates → Keyboard.singleton is destroyed and all shortcuts are unregistered

- **feat** `F-6` State Persistence
  - `F-6.1` Per-path open/current state is stored in an atom family keyed by path string.
  - `F-6.2` Open state (not current) is persisted to localStorage on every change.
  - `F-6.3` Current state reflects active layout items and is never persisted.
  - `F-6.4` layout.active changes → removed items are marked not-current; newly active items are marked current

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Workspace tab switch

- **scenario** `T-2` Tree node expand persists

- **scenario** `T-3` Expose navigates to nested item

- **scenario** `T-4` Select item

- **scenario** `T-5` Command palette opens on keyboard shortcut

- **scenario** `T-6` Drag-and-drop rearrange

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Expose a nested document and select it — NavTree itself is system-tagged and force-enabled (never a user-facing toggle — see `getCorePlugins` in `plugin-defs.core.tsx`).

pages.title: OsrmPlugin
pages.summary: A Composer plugin that contributes a **driving-route provider** to plugin-trip.
pages.content:
A Composer plugin that contributes a **driving-route provider** to plugin-trip. It implements the (new) plugin-trip `RoutingService` capability by combining two free, no-key OpenStreetMap services:

- **Nominatim** (`nominatim.openstreetmap.org`) — geocodes city names → `[lon, lat]`.
- **OSRM** (`router.project-osrm.org`) — the public Open Source Routing Machine demo; computes the `driving` route through an ordered list of coordinates and returns per-leg distance, duration, and geometry.

The plugin is the first concrete `RoutingService`, mirroring how `plugin-duffel` is the first concrete `BookingService`. plugin-trip's new `PlanRoute` operation resolves the registered routing service and uses it to turn an ordered list of cities into a connected chain of road `Segment`s, each carrying real driving distance, drive time, and a map polyline. plugin-trip stays provider-agnostic; this plugin (or a future keyed provider such as OpenRouteService) plugs in behind the same contract.

This is a **prototype** provider: both upstream services are free, require no API key, and permit browser CORS — so the plugin works immediately with zero setup. Their public-instance usage policies (Nominatim ≤ 1 req/s + a descriptive `User-Agent`; OSRM demo "not for heavy/production use") make this suitable for development and demos, not production traffic.

## Scope of this milestone

This milestone spans **three** packages. Per the agreed plan, the authoritative spec is written here in `plugin-osrm/PLUGIN.mdl` now; the `plugin-trip` and `plugin-map` additions described below are captured here as cross-package sections and will be folded into each plugin's own `PLUGIN.mdl` once implemented.

| Package       | Additions                                                                                          |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `plugin-trip` | `RoutingService` capability + DTOs; `RoadDetails` route fields; `PlanRoute` op; Route section UI; map polyline. |
| `plugin-osrm` | New private plugin: the Nominatim + OSRM `RoutingService` implementation (this spec's home).        |
| `plugin-map`  | Bespoke settings surface with a named tile-provider picker; provider registry; `buildTileUrl` generalization. |

## Cross-package additions

### plugin-trip — `RoutingService` capability

A new capability, parallel to `BookingService`, declared in `plugin-trip/src/types/TripCapabilities.ts`:

- **type** `RoutingService` Pluggable driving-route provider.

DTOs live in `plugin-trip/src/types/Routing.ts`, defined as Effect Schema with derived interfaces — matching how `BookingSearch.SearchQuery` / `Offer` are defined.

- **type** `RouteProfile`
- **type** `Waypoint` A stop on the route.
- **type** `RouteQuery`
- **type** `RouteStep` A turn / segment within a leg.
- **type** `RouteLeg` A leg between two consecutive route waypoints.
- **type** `Route` A computed route.
- **type** `RouteResult` Service result — geocoded stops plus the route alternatives.
- **type** `MissingApiKeyError` Reused convention from BookingSearch — a RoutingService throws this (or a similar Error) when it requires credentials that are not configured.

### plugin-trip — `RoadDetails.routes`

The existing `RoadDetails` variant (`plugin-trip/src/types/Segment.ts`) gains one optional `routes` field. Optional, so existing road segments, the `makeDefault('road')` factory, and the extractor paths stay valid.

### plugin-trip — `PlanRoute` operation

- **op** `PlanRoute` Computes driving routes for a trip's existing road Segments.

### plugin-trip — "Plan route" toolbar action (UI)

- **feat** `PlanRouteAction` There is no dedicated route-planning panel.

### plugin-trip — map polyline

- **feat** `TripRoutePolyline` Extends the existing tripMarkerProvider (plugin-trip/src/capabilities/marker-provider.tsx).

### plugin-map — tile-provider settings surface

plugin-map already has: a `Settings` schema with `apiKeys: APIKey[]`, a `RECOGNIZED_API_KEY_DOMAINS = ['maptiler.com']` list, a `buildTileUrl()` that hardcodes a MapTiler `streets-v2` URL when a `maptiler.com` key is present, and the auto-generated `DefaultSettings` form. This milestone replaces the auto-form with a bespoke surface offering a **named provider picker**, and generalizes tile-URL construction via a registry.

- **type** `TileProvider` Registry entry for a known tile service.

- **feat** `MapTileSettingsSurface` Bespoke settings surface for plugin-map (replaces the auto-generated DefaultSettings form for this plugin id).

## This plugin — `OsrmRoutingService`

- **feat** `OsrmRoutingService` plugin-osrm's RoutingService impl.

### File layout (mirrors plugin-duffel)

```text
packages/plugins/plugin-osrm/
  PLUGIN.mdl                         # this file
  README.md
  package.json                       # "private": true; deps incl. @dxos/plugin-trip workspace:*
  moon.yml                           # --entryPoint per export subpath
  src/
    index.ts                         # exports meta + plugin only
    meta.ts                          # Plugin.makeMeta (id org.dxos.plugin.osrm)
    plugin.ts                        # Plugin.lazy
    OsrmPlugin.tsx                   # Plugin.define(meta).pipe(...)
    translations.ts
    capabilities/
      index.ts                       # Osrm LazyCapability
      osrm.ts                        # Capability.contributes(TripCapabilities.RoutingService, service)
    services/
      index.ts
      OsrmRoutingService.ts          # makeOsrmRoutingService() factory
      NominatimClient.ts             # geocode(name) → Place
      OsrmClient.ts                  # route(coords) → raw OSRM response
      osrm-mapping.ts                # response → Route[] (parseRoutes)
      osrm-mapping.test.ts           # fixture-based unit tests
```

## Acceptance

## Out of scope (v1)

- Keyed routing providers (OpenRouteService, Mapbox Directions, GraphHopper). They drop in as additional `RoutingService` contributions with no plugin-trip changes; documented as the upgrade path, not built here.
- Profiles other than `driving` (walking, cycling). The `profiles` field reserves room.
- Route optimization / reordering cities (TSP). PlanRoute routes the list in the given order; the user orders cities manually.
- Persisting the city list on `Trip` (Approach B). Initial list is derived from planner-owned road segments; revisit if draft persistence is needed.
- Turn-by-turn directions, alternative routes, traffic, tolls, ETAs at time-of-day.
- Production hardening of the public OSRM/Nominatim usage (self-hosting, rate-limit backoff, caching). Prototype uses the public demo instances.
- A map "tile preview" thumbnail in the provider picker; labels + hints only in v1.

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Plan a driving route across two road segments — plugin-osrm contributes no operation of its own — it registers a `RoutingService` capability that `plugin-trip`'s `PlanRoute` operation resolves and calls.

pages.title: PipelinePlugin
pages.summary: A multi-column Kanban-style pipeline plugin for DXOS Composer.
pages.content:
A multi-column Kanban-style pipeline plugin for DXOS Composer. Each Pipeline holds an ordered list of Columns; each Column is backed by a ViewModel whose query selects any ECHO object type from the space. Objects can be dragged between columns and the pipeline state persists collaboratively via ECHO.

## Types

- **type** `Pipeline` Root ECHO object (typename org.dxos.type.pipeline).

- **type** `Column` One lane of the pipeline.

- **type** `ViewModel` Runtime ECHO object that holds a QueryAST and JSON schema projection for a Column.

## Components

- **component** `PipelineArticle` Full-canvas article surface rendered for a Pipeline object.

- **component** `PipelineComponent` Composable component set that renders the Kanban board.

- **component** `PipelineProperties` Settings companion panel for managing pipeline columns.

## Operations

- **op** `createPipeline` Creates a new Pipeline ECHO object and adds it to the target space.

- **op** `createResearchProject` Built-in template that scaffolds a Research pipeline with Mailbox, Contacts, Organizations, and Notes columns.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Create Pipeline
  - `F-1.1` A new Pipeline is created with an empty columns array.
  - `F-1.2` The Pipeline is added to the active space via SpaceOperation.AddObject (hidden=true).
  - `F-1.3` The Pipeline appears as an article in Composer.
  - `F-1.4` Graph companions "Invocations" and "Automation" are added to the pipeline node.

- **feat** `F-2` Manage Columns
  - `F-2.1` user clicks "+" in the pipeline toolbar → Settings companion panel opens
  - `F-2.2` user clicks "+" in PipelineProperties → a new Column is appended with an empty ViewModel and a Filter.nothing() query
  - `F-2.3` user renames a column → column.name updated immediately via Obj.update
  - `F-2.4` user deletes a column → Column removed from pipeline.columns; associated ViewModel ECHO object removed from db
  - `F-2.5` user drags a column to a new position → pipeline.columns reordered via arrayMove

- **feat** `F-3` Column Query
  - `F-3.1` user changes the query in ViewEditor → column.view.query.ast updated; column.view.projection updated to match new schema
  - `F-3.2` query targets a feed (queue DXN) → Query.from({ feeds: [queue] }) applied; items ordered newest-first
  - `F-3.3` query targets the space directly → items ordered by ECHO insertion order

- **feat** `F-4` Drag and Drop — The item itself is not moved to a different ECHO location; only the order array changes.
  - `F-4.1` user drags a Column tile → pipeline.columns reordered; change persisted via Obj.update
  - `F-4.2` user drags an item between columns → column.order updated to reflect new position
  - `F-4.3` Only Pipeline.Column objects are accepted as column drop targets (isColumn guard).

- **feat** `F-5` Research Template
  - `F-5.1` user creates a pipeline from the "org-research" template → Research pipeline created with Mailbox, Contacts, Organizations, and Notes columns
  - `F-5.2` Template creation fails gracefully when no Mailbox exists in the database.

- **feat** `F-6` Invocation Companion
  - `F-6.1` Pipeline article is open → "Invocations" companion tab shows InvocationTraceContainer for the pipeline's database
  - `F-6.2` Pipeline article is open → "Automation" companion tab is available for wiring pipeline automation

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` New pipeline is empty

- **scenario** `T-2` Add column

- **scenario** `T-3` Rename column

- **scenario** `T-4` Delete column

- **scenario** `T-5` Research template

- **scenario** `T-6` Research template missing mailbox

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Create a Pipeline and add a column — Pipeline creation delegates to `SpaceOperation.AddObject` behind the generic `CreateObjectEntry` factory (same pattern as plugin-chess's `startGame`), and column management (`addColumn`/`renameColumn`/`deleteColumn`/`se…

---

pages.title: PresenterPlugin
pages.summary: A presentation plugin for DXOS Composer.
pages.content:
A presentation plugin for DXOS Composer. A Presentation is an ordered deck of sections, each an owned markdown slide or a link to any workspace object, shown in the navtree as a folder of slides and presented with fullscreen mode and keyboard navigation. A markdown document can still be previewed as a deck through its Presenter companion. Slides are written in a strict Slidev subset (layouts, slots, click steps, notes) with DXOS extensions (video backgrounds, embedded object surfaces).

## Types

- **type** `Presentation` An ordered deck of slides.

- **type** `Slide` One slide of a Presentation, owned by it.

- **type** `SlideViewState` Per-user, per-deck view state (`presenter-slide`, local backend) in `@dxos/react-ui-attention`, keyed by the Presentation's (or previewed document's) URI.

- **type** `PresenterSettings` The plugin's settings (`PresenterSettings.Settings`, persisted per device).

- **type** `SlideTheme` A deck's theme settings (`SlideTheme.Settings`): a built-in theme name and optional overrides.

- **type** `SlideSource` One slide of a deck: `text` is an owned Text rendered as markdown; `object` is any linked object (a Markdown.Document included) rendered through the slide surface fallback; `markdown` is one `---`-separated slide of a p…

## Components

- **component** `Deck` A composite (`Deck.Root`, headless, holding the state and keys; `Deck.Content`, the focus scope that handles keys and prints; `Deck.Viewport`, the current slide; `Deck.Grid`, every slide as a thumbnail; `Deck.Pager`, `D…

- **component** `PresentationArticle` A Presentation's article is a grid of its slides (`Deck.Grid`); presenting shows one slide at a time (`Deck.Viewport`).

- **component** `SlideEditorArticle` Article for an owned slide, opened by clicking the slide's child node in the navtree.

- **component** `SectionPicker` Toolbar picker ("Add to presentation") over the space's objects that links the chosen object into the presentation as a section.

- **component** `Slide` A composite: `Slide.Root` (headless) holds one SlideSource and its options; `Slide.Frame` is a fixed 16:9 logical canvas scaled to its container (inset in a solid void with `inset`, unscaled for print), so every slide c…

- **component** `MarkdownSlide` Renders one slide of the Slidev markdown subset on the 2560x1440 canvas: per-slide frontmatter (`layout`, `image`, `background`, `class`, `backgroundVideo`, `backgroundOpacity`, `backgroundPosition`, `bleed`, and `theme…

- **component** `SlideLayouts` The layouts a slide's `layout` names: default, cover, center, section, intro, end, fact, statement, quote, two-cols, two-cols-header, three-cols, two-by-two, image, image-left, image-right, full, none.

- **component** `SlideBackground` The slide's background: a colour, an `image`, or a looping, muted, autoplaying `backgroundVideo`, with `backgroundOpacity` and `backgroundPosition`.

- **component** `EmbeddedSurface` Renders the object a slide's `<Surface ref="echo:///<id>" role="slide|section|card" />` names, through ObjectSurface (fallback `slide`, `section`, `card`, then a title slide).

- **component** `DocumentArticle` Presenter companion of a Markdown document: the shared Deck over the document content, split into slides on horizontal `---` separators outside fenced code, honouring leading headmatter and per-slide frontmatter (markdo…

- **component** `SlideArticle` The AppSurface.Slide surface for Markdown.Document objects: renders the document as a slide, without a frame (Slide.Frame owns it).

- **component** `SpeakerNotes` A composite: `SpeakerNotes.Subtitles` shows the current slide's notes over the bottom of a presented slide; `SpeakerNotes.Prompter` is the speaker's view: the slide's notes large (one line per bullet or sentence), its p…

- **component** `PresentedOverlay` Drawn over a presented Presentation (inside `Deck.Viewport`): the speaker notes as the `notes` setting asks — subtitles, or a second browser window (a portal, so it shares the app's state; keys pressed there move the de…

Extension points: `PresenterSurface.Toolbar` (data `{ subject: Presentation }`) adds items to a Presentation's toolbar before the play button; `PresenterSurface.Overlay` draws over the presented deck; the `PresentationEventHandler` capability (`onStart`, `onSlide({ presentation, slide?, id, title?, index, step })`, `onStop`) follows a presentation. Another plugin (the recorder) uses them; presenter depends on none of them.

## Operations

- **op** `TogglePresentation` Enters or exits presentation for a Markdown document or Presentation by toggling the deck's fullscreen overlay (EphemeralDeckState.fullscreen).

- **op** `GenerateSlideImage` Generates an image for a slide from a prompt with plugin-studio's `StudioOperation.Generate` (image kind, the space's configured provider), stores it as a `MediaArtifact`, and sets it as the slide's `image`.

- **op** `ImportDeck` Creates a Presentation from one Slidev markdown deck: one owned markdown slide per `---`-separated part (F-6.7's splitting rule), each keeping its own frontmatter and trailing notes comment, filed like a created present…

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Presentation Mode
  - `F-1.1` Every Markdown document in the workspace has a companion "Presenter" node in the app graph.
  - `F-1.2` user activates TogglePresentation on a document → the presenter companion fills the screen in the deck's fullscreen overlay, without the companion tab strip, and the URL does not change
  - `F-1.3` user presses Shift+Cmd+P (macOS) or Shift+Alt+P (Windows) → TogglePresentation is invoked for the focused object
  - `F-1.4` user activates TogglePresentation on a Presentation → the Presentation's own plank fills the screen in the fullscreen overlay and the URL does not change

- **feat** `F-2` Document Preview
  - `F-2.1` DocumentArticle mounts with a Markdown.Document → the Deck renders the document content as slides
  - `F-2.2` Slides are separated by horizontal `---`; vertical slides are not configured.
  - `F-2.3` user presses Escape or the exit action is triggered → fullscreen exits for that document, leaving it and its companion as they were

- **feat** `F-3` Presentation Object
  - `F-3.1` A Presentation is created from the space's create-object menu, is filed into the space's Collections, and holds an ordered `sections` array.
  - `F-3.2` One section is exactly one slide; `---` inside a section is a horizontal rule, not a slide break.
  - `F-3.3` A section is an owned markdown Text (parented to the presentation) or a link to any object.
  - `F-3.4` user adds a slide from the toolbar → a new owned Text section is appended
  - `F-3.5` user links an object through SectionPicker → the object becomes a section and keeps its own parent
  - `F-3.6` an owned slide is deleted with the space's Delete → it leaves the deck and the navtree, and the delete can be undone
  - `F-3.7` a linked section is removed from the presentation → only the link is removed; the object remains
  - `F-3.8` Presentation deletion does not cascade to linked objects.

- **feat** `F-4` Presentation Deck
  - `F-4.1` PresentationArticle mounts → the slide at the viewer's stored index is shown, clamped to the deck
  - `F-4.2` The pager shows the current slide and total count; an empty deck shows none.
  - `F-4.3` Keys bind to the deck's focus scope, never `window`.
  - `F-4.4` user presses `f` → the deck toggles fullscreen in place
  - `F-4.5` the deck is fullscreen and the pointer is idle → the overlay pager hides, and shows again on pointer movement
  - `F-4.6` user presses Escape in fullscreen → the deck exits fullscreen
  - `F-4.7` The current slide index is per-user view state, kept across navigation and reloads, and never shared with collaborators.
  - `F-4.8` Only an attended deck takes focus on mount.
  - `F-4.9` A linked object with no slide surface renders as a title slide rather than failing.
  - `F-4.10` A section whose target was deleted is omitted from the deck; one whose target has not loaded shows a pending slide.
  - `F-4.11` Inline, a Presentation shows every slide as a fully revealed thumbnail in a vertically scrolling grid with no pager; the current slide is selected, and arrow keys or a click move it.
  - `F-4.12` user drags a thumbnail before or after another → the section moves there, and the moved slide stays current
  - `F-4.13` user double-clicks a thumbnail → the deck presents fullscreen from that slide

- **feat** `F-6` Markdown Slides
  - `F-6.1` A slide is written in a strict Slidev subset: per-slide frontmatter `layout`, `image`, `background`, `class`, `title` (and the DXOS keys of F-8.1 and F-8.5 and the `theme` headmatter of F-6.8); slots `::left::`, `::righ…
  - `F-6.2` The layouts are default, cover, center, section, intro, end, fact, statement, quote, two-cols, two-cols-header, three-cols, two-by-two, image, image-left, image-right, full and none.
  - `F-6.3` a slide names an unknown layout → it renders with default, no error is shown, and a validation issue is reported
  - `F-6.4` a slide's frontmatter YAML is malformed → the body still renders, the frontmatter is ignored and a validation issue is reported
  - `F-6.5` Raw HTML other than `v-click`, `v-clicks`, `v-after`, `Surface` and `br` is escaped, never rendered or executed; URLs with unsafe schemes are not followed.
  - `F-6.6` A fenced code block renders highlighted; a `{2,4-5}` meta marks the lines that stay emphasised, and Slidev's `{lines:true}` option numbers the lines.
  - `F-6.7` In the preview companion `---` splits slides except inside a fenced code block, and a leading frontmatter block is slide metadata.
  - `F-6.8` A deck has one theme, `default`, `light`, `dark` or `serif`, named by the first slide's `theme:` headmatter; `default` follows the app's light/dark mode and `light`/`dark` force one, code highlighting included.
  - `F-6.9` A Presentation's `theme` setting names the theme and may override its accent, background and text colors, its text font (`mono`, `sans`, `rounded`, `serif`, `display`, `space-grotesk`, `mali`, `geist`, `orbitron`, `unbo…
  - `F-6.10` a slide names an unknown theme, or an override is not a plain color or font list → the default theme or value applies and, for an unknown name, a validation issue is reported

- **feat** `F-7` Click Steps
  - `F-7.1` `<v-click>`, `<v-clicks>` (`depth`, `every`) and `<v-after>` reveal their content one click at a time; a hidden element keeps its layout.
  - `F-7.2` user presses Space or right with steps remaining → the next step reveals, and only after the last step does the deck advance
  - `F-7.3` user presses left with steps revealed → the last step hides; at step 0 the previous slide shows fully revealed
  - `F-7.4` Click steps reset on any slide change and are never persisted; only the slide index is view state.
  - `F-7.5` Space on a focused button or link activates it and does not advance.

- **feat** `F-8` Backgrounds and Embedded Surfaces
  - `F-8.1` Frontmatter `backgroundVideo` plays as a looping, muted, autoplaying background, with `backgroundOpacity` and `backgroundPosition`.
  - `F-8.2` a slide contains `<Surface ref="echo:///<id>" role="slide|section|card" />` in any slot → the referenced object renders there through its slide surface, falling back to section, card and a title slide
  - `F-8.3` the ref is malformed, never existed, or its target is deleted → a "Missing object" placeholder shows in its place, with no spinner left
  - `F-8.4` An image whose URL is an object URI (`![label](echo:///<id>)`) embeds that object as `<Surface ref>` with the `slide` role; alone in its paragraph it fills its slot, and the label is ignored.
  - `F-8.5` Frontmatter `bleed: left` or `bleed: right` takes the outer column of a `two-cols` or `three-cols` slide to the slide's edges on that side, top and bottom, with no padding, for an embedded object to fill.

- **feat** `F-9` Printing
  - `F-9.1` the focused or fullscreen deck is printed → every slide of the deck prints, one per 16:9 page at full size, with every click step shown and the app chrome, overlay and other decks left out
  - `F-9.2` Print rules apply only while a deck is printing, so printing anything else in the app is unaffected.

- **feat** `F-10` Slide Editor
  - `F-10.1` The slide editor has a toolbar with markdown formatting, slide tools (layout, click step, column break, object, background, notes) and view controls (preview mode, previous/next slide, present from here).
  - `F-10.2` Picking a layout writes the slide's `layout:` frontmatter, keeping its other keys; each toolbar edit is one undo step.
  - `F-10.3` The preview shows below the editor in a resizable vertical split, or in the plank's companion; the mode and split position are kept per user.
  - `F-10.4` the cursor is inside a `<v-click>` or `<v-clicks>` group → the preview reveals up to that group's step, and in a slotted layout the cursor's slot is outlined
  - `F-10.5` user clicks an element in the preview → the editor's caret moves to the start of that element's source (no range is selected) and scrolls into view
  - `F-10.6` "Present from here" opens the deck fullscreen at this slide.

- **feat** `F-5` Navtree Folder
  - `F-5.1` A Presentation node lists its sections as children.
  - `F-5.2` An owned slide is labelled by its name, else its first markdown heading, else "Slide N".
  - `F-5.3` user drags a child to a new position → `sections` is reordered to match
  - `F-5.4` user clicks a slide child → the slide's own article opens (SlideEditorArticle for an owned slide)
  - `F-5.5` An owned slide offers no remove action, only the space's Delete; a linked section's remove action is labelled "Remove from presentation".
  - `F-5.6` The children are the deck's slides in deck order, so a deleted section leaves both.

- **feat** `F-11` Slides as Objects
  - `F-11.1` A Presentation's slides are `Slide` objects, each holding its content (an owned Text or a linked object) and the slide's own metadata (title, hidden, notes, image).
  - `F-11.2` A Presentation has an optional description.
  - `F-11.3` Opening a slide opens its `Slide`; the assistant companion beside it has the Slide, its content and its presentation as context, with the presenter skill enabled.
  - `F-11.4` the assistant is asked for an image on the slide it is beside → it calls `GenerateSlideImage`, and the slide shows the generated image in its layout
  - `F-11.5` An image is held as a ref to a plugin-studio `MediaArtifact`, which the slide background resolves to its image.
  - `F-11.6` Presentations of version 0.1.0 migrate in place: each section becomes a `Slide`, and a markdown slide's `hide: true` becomes `hidden`.

- **feat** `F-12` Speaker Notes
  - `F-12.1` A slide's speaker notes are its `notes` text, else the markdown slide's trailing notes comment; they are read one line per bullet or paragraph, split again after each sentence.
  - `F-12.2` the `notes` setting is `subtitles` and a Presentation is presented → the current slide's notes show over the bottom of the slide
  - `F-12.3` the `notes` setting is `window` and a Presentation is presented → a second window shows the current slide's notes, the time on the slide against its desired length, and the next slide's notes; it closes when the present…
  - `F-12.4` Arrow keys and Space pressed in the notes window move the deck as they do in the deck.
  - `F-12.5` When the browser refuses the notes window, the deck shows a button that opens it.
  - `F-12.6` A slide has an optional desired length (`duration`, seconds), edited with its other properties.
  - `F-12.7` Other plugins add toolbar items and overlays through `PresenterSurface.Toolbar` and `PresenterSurface.Overlay`, and follow a presentation through `PresentationEventHandler`.

- **feat** `F-13` Showcase Decks
  - `F-13.1` A showcase, the account of what a body of work such as a pull request changed, is a Presentation: an ordered array of slides, each a markdown slide or a reference to an ECHO object, with at least one markdown slide.
  - `F-13.2` A showcase is written as one Slidev markdown deck: a summary slide first, then one slide per demo artifact, a video as a `backgroundVideo` slide and a screenshot as an image slide, with the demo's narration as that slid…
  - `F-13.3` the ImportDeck operation is invoked with a showcase deck → a Presentation is created with one owned slide per part of the deck, each keeping its frontmatter and notes
  - `F-13.4` The presenter skill imports a deck it is given whole with ImportDeck rather than rewriting its slides.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Document presenter opens in fullscreen

- **scenario** `T-2` Document slides split on separators

- **scenario** `T-3` Exit returns to document view

- **scenario** `T-4` Presentation renders one slide per section

- **scenario** `T-5` Slide advance

- **scenario** `T-6` Slide index survives reload

- **scenario** `T-7` Keyboard shortcut registered

- **scenario** `T-8` Presentation presents fullscreen on its own plank

- **scenario** `T-9` Reorder in the navtree

- **scenario** `T-10` Removing a linked section keeps the object

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-4` Slidev subset and click steps — Preview a document that uses layouts, click steps, a video background and an embedded surface, then step through it.

- **test** `QA-1` Preview a document in the companion, then present it — The core presenter round-trip — create a document with slide separators, preview it in the presenter companion, present it fullscreen, then exit.
- **test** `QA-2` Showcase clip — The 10s showcase clip: Present a document as slides and page through them.
- **test** `QA-3` Build and present a Presentation — Create a Presentation, add a slide, link a markdown document, reorder in the navtree, present it fullscreen, step, exit and reload.

pages.title: ProjectsPlugin
pages.summary: Projects: long-running work composed of instructions, skills, tasks, routines, artifacts and chats in the project's context.
pages.content:
Projects: long-running work composed of instructions, skills, tasks, routines, artifacts and chats in the project's context. A project starts from a template (`src/templates/`); this document covers the templates whose run is a demo worth walking end to end.

The **Composer Plugin** template (`src/templates/composer-plugin.ts`) is offered in the desktop app: an agent builds a TypeScript Composer plugin in a local sandbox and offers it back to load. The sandbox holds nothing but the bun runtime the app ships; the guide comes from GitHub and the packages from pkg.pr.new and npm, pinned to the commit and library versions the app was built from (`VITE_DX_PLUGIN_TOOLCHAIN`, stamped by composer-app's vite config). The browser has no local sandbox, so there plugin-dev-shell contributes its own version of the template, which builds with the dev shell of a vite server.

Every variant builds World Clock from one spec, `src/templates/world-clock.mdl`: the project files it as its artifact, and the plugin bundles it as its `PLUGIN.mdl` and contributes it as a plugin asset, so once installed its page in Plugins → Registry opens the spec it was built from. The **World Clock** space template (`src/samples/world-clock/`) seeds that project with a feature per `feat` block of the spec, and is offered wherever the Composer Plugin template is.

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Build a plugin with an agent in the desktop app — An agent works the Composer Plugin template's parent task and four subtasks in a local sandbox — fetch the guide, write a TypeScript plugin, install and build it, publish and offer it — and the reader loads the result.
- **test** `QA-2` Build a plugin with an agent in the browser and install it from the private registry — The browser variant of QA-1.
- **test** `QA-3` Read a project's tasks as details — A project's task list opens each task as the project plank's detail.
- **test** `QA-4` Plan a project and hand its tasks to an agent — The demo path — create a project from the Default template, brief its agent, break the work into tasks, fill one in, and select tasks for the agent.
- **test** `QA-5` Showcase clip — The 20s showcase clip: Open a task of the Chess MCP on Workers project, then tick it and send it to the agent.
- **test** `QA-6` World Clock round trip — build from the space template, install from the registry, open the spec — The investor-demo walk of QA-2, started from the World Clock space template instead of an empty space and ending on the spec.

pages.title: Feature links
pages.summary: Tests and analytics in the code link to the features on a project's feature map.
pages.content:
Tests and analytics in the code link to the features on a project's feature map. A feature is named by a DXN: its `meta.key`, then `#` and its mnemonic, for example `dxn:network.dxos.team.features.mcp.codeMode#ABC123`. Code cites that DXN in a `@feature` JSDoc tag; analytics events carry it in a `feature` property. A scanner collects the tags, and the feature map shows each feature's DXN and the code that cites it.

There is no global resolver. A DXN resolves against the spaces the reader is a member of.

It spans three places: the DXN grammar in `@dxos/keys` (`DXN`), the mnemonic in `@dxos/echo` (`Obj.getMnemonic`, `Filter.mnemonic`, `Filter.key`), and plugin-projects (`Feature`, the feature map).

## Diagram

```diagram
diagram flow=right
group repo "repository" {
  node Test "test file"
  node Event "analytics event"
  node Scanner "feature-link scanner"
}
group keys "@dxos/keys" {
  node Dxn "DXN"
}
group projects "plugin-projects" {
  node Import "importFeatureLinks"
  node Resolve "resolveFeatureLink"
  node Feature "Feature"
  node Map "feature map"
}
node PostHog "PostHog"
edge Test -> Scanner "@feature dxn:…#ABC123"
edge Scanner -> Import "links"
edge Import -> Resolve "each DXN"
edge Resolve depends-on Dxn "parse"
edge Resolve -> Feature "meta.key + mnemonic"
edge Import -> Feature "write code links"
edge Feature -> Map "DXN, code links"
edge Event -> PostHog "feature: dxn:…"
```

## Naming a feature

A DXN with a mnemonic is `dxn:<nsid>[:<version>][#<mnemonic>]`. The NSID is the object's `meta.key`. The mnemonic is `Obj.getMnemonic`: the last six characters of the object id, uppercased. They are the random part of the ULID, so they stay the same for the life of the object.

- **feat** `F-1` DXN mnemonic suffix
  - `F-1.1` `DXN.tryMake` accepts an optional `#<mnemonic>` after the NSID and the optional version, where the mnemonic is six Crockford base32 characters (`EntityId.isValidMnemonic`), in either case.
  - `F-1.2` `DXN.getName` and `DXN.getVersion` ignore the suffix; `DXN.getMnemonic` returns it uppercased, or undefined when there is none.
  - `F-1.3` `DXN.withMnemonic(dxn, mnemonic)` sets or replaces the suffix and `DXN.withoutMnemonic(dxn)` removes it.
  - `F-1.4` `DXN.make` builds DXNs without a suffix only, so a type, plugin or operation key never carries one.

- **feat** `F-2` Feature key
  - `F-2.1` A feature's NSID is its `meta.key`.
  - `F-2.2` `Feature.getLink(feature)` returns `dxn:<meta.key>#<mnemonic>`, or undefined when the feature has no `meta.key`.
  - `F-2.3` Two features in one space with the same `meta.key` are allowed; the mnemonic tells them apart.

## Resolving a link

- **feat** `F-3` Resolution
  - `F-3.1` a DXN is resolved against a database → the resolver queries features by `Filter.key` on the NSID; with a mnemonic, the match whose mnemonic is equal wins
  - `F-3.2` the key matches no feature but the mnemonic matches one → that feature is the result, with status `renamed`, so a link survives a change of `meta.key`
  - `F-3.3` the key matches features and none has the mnemonic → the result is `stale` when exactly one feature has the key, and `ambiguous` when several do
  - `F-3.4` The result is one of `exact`, `renamed`, `stale`, `ambiguous` or `missing`, and names the feature for every status except `missing` and `ambiguous`.
  - `F-3.5` A reader resolves a link against each space they are a member of; a link resolves only where the feature's space is open to the reader.

## Citing a feature in code

- **feat** `F-4` The `@feature` tag
  - `F-4.1` Code cites a feature with a JSDoc block tag `@feature <dxn>`, one DXN per tag; a block can have several tags.
  - `F-4.2` A tag on a `describe` applies to every test inside it; a tag on a `test`, a function, a class or a constant applies to that symbol.
  - `F-4.3` The DXN in a tag carries a mnemonic, so it resolves when two spaces hold a feature with the same key.
  - `F-4.4` An analytics event that measures a feature carries the same DXN in a `feature` property, because a JSDoc tag does not exist at runtime.

- **feat** `F-5` Scanner
  - `F-5.1` `scanFeatureLinks(path, text)` returns one link per tag: the DXN, the file path, the 1-based line of the tag, the symbol the comment documents, and its kind (`test`, `suite` or `code`).
  - `F-5.2` The kind is `suite` for a `describe`, `test` for a `test` or `it`, and `code` for anything else.
  - `F-5.3` A tag whose value is not a valid DXN is reported as an error with its path and line, not dropped.
  - `F-5.4` The `scan-feature-links` script runs the scanner over the TypeScript files git tracks and prints the links as JSON, so the output can be passed to `op:ImportFeatureLinks` without editing.

## On the feature map

- **feat** `F-6` Code links on features
  - `F-6.1` A feature holds the code that cites it in `code`, a list of links (path, line, symbol, kind), so the feature map reads them without the repository.
  - `F-6.2` `op:ImportFeatureLinks` resolves each link's DXN in the space, replaces the `code` list of every feature it resolved, and returns the links it could not resolve with their status.
  - `F-6.3` The feature card shows how many tests cite the feature; a feature that no test cites shows nothing.
  - `F-6.4` The feature article shows the feature's DXN with a copy button, and lists its code links, each opening the file at its line on GitHub.
  - `F-6.5` A feature without a `meta.key` shows no DXN, and its article offers to set the key.

- **scenario** `T-1` A test links to its feature

- **scenario** `T-2` A renamed key keeps its links

## QA

- **test** `QA-1` Cite a feature from code — A feature on the map shows the DXN that code cites it by and the tests and code that cite it; a feature with no key offers to set one.

## Out of scope

- Showing analytics on the feature map (event counts per feature). Events carry the DXN now ([F-4.4]), so a later change can read them from PostHog.
- A global resolver, or resolving in spaces the reader is not a member of.

pages.title: QaPlugin
pages.summary: A store for QA results.
pages.content:
A store for QA results. A `TestPlan` declares a set of `TestCase`s; each execution of the plan appends a `TestRun` to the plan's feed, carrying one `TestResult` per case together with the documents, screenshots and recordings that evidence it. Plans are authored and results are pushed by an agent over the DXOS MCP surface, so the same plan a human reads in Composer is the one a `test QA-n` run reports against.

## Ontology

Three ECHO objects and three inline structs. The split is deliberate:

- **`TestCase` is an object** because a case outlives any one plan revision — results across months of runs point at the same case, and coverage questions ("has QA-3 ever passed on main?") are queries over that identity.
- **`TestRun` is an object** because it is the feed entry: the plan owns a `Feed<TestRun>`, so a run is appended, never mutated in place by a later run.
- **`TestResult` is a struct nested in its run**, not an object. A result has no life outside the run that produced it and is never referenced from elsewhere; making it an object would double the object count per run for no query anyone asks.
- **There is no artifact type.** An artifact is a `Ref` to whatever the artifact already is — a `Document`, a `File`, a recording — plus a caption at the reference site.

```
TestPlan ──cases[]──▶ TestCase
    └── feed ─▶ Feed<TestRun>
                    TestRun ──plan──▶ TestPlan
                        └── results[]  (TestResult)  ──case──▶ TestCase
                                └── steps[] (TestStepResult)
                                └── artifacts[] ──▶ Ref<Document | File | …>
```

## Types

- **type** `TestResultStatus` A terminal outcome — the only thing a case or a step can be reported as.

- **type** `TestStatus` A run's status: any terminal outcome, or `running` while it is open.

- **type** `TestStep` One move in a case — the authored instruction and its criterion.

- **type** `TestCase` The definition of one test.

- **type** `TestPlan` Root ECHO object and the container the UI opens.

- **type** `Actor` Not defined here — `Actor` from @dxos/types (name / email / identityDid / contact / role), the same type a Message sender uses.

- **type** `TestTarget` What a run was executed against.

- **type** `TestArtifactRef` A reference to evidence.

- **type** `CapturedCase` A case the run set out to cover, captured at `startRun`.

- **type** `TestStepResult` Per-step outcome within a TestResult.

- **type** `TestResult` The outcome of one TestCase within one TestRun.

- **type** `TestRun` One execution of a plan, appended to TestPlan.feed.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Author and maintain plans
  - `F-1.1` A TestPlan can be created empty, or generated from the `## QA` section of a
  - `F-1.2` Cases are added, updated, reordered and removed through operations, so an agent over
  - `F-1.3` Re-generating a plan from an updated spec matches existing cases by `key` and updates
- **feat** `F-2` Record runs
  - `F-2.1` Starting a run appends a TestRun with status `running` to the plan's feed and returns
  - `F-2.2` A result is pushed per case, incrementally, so a long run is observable while it is
  - `F-2.3` Finishing a run computes `status` as a rollup over the case keys captured at
  - `F-2.4` A run is immutable once finished; a correction is a new run, not an edit.
- **feat** `F-3` Evidence
  - `F-3.1` An artifact is attached by reference to an existing object; the plugin never copies
  - `F-3.2` Artifacts attach at step granularity as well as case granularity.
- **feat** `F-4` Read the history
  - `F-4.1` The plan surface shows the feed newest-first, one row per run, with its target and
  - `F-4.2` A case surface shows that case's outcome across every run, so a flaky or long-broken
- **feat** `F-5` Agent access over MCP
  - `F-5.1` A `QaSkill` names the plan-editing and result-pushing operations in its `tools`, which
  - `F-5.2` Every operation takes refs and plain values only.
  - `F-5.3` Mutation hints are declared per operation so a host can distinguish reading history

## Operations

- **op** `createPlan` Creates a TestPlan with its feed.

- **op** `setCase` Creates or updates a case by `key` within a plan, appending it to `cases` when new.

- **op** `removeCase` Removes a case from the plan's `cases`.

- **op** `setCaseOrder` Sets the plan's case ordering.

- **op** `startRun` Appends a `running` TestRun to the plan's feed and returns a ref to it.

- **op** `pushResult` Appends (or replaces, by case key) one TestResult on a running run.

- **op** `completeRun` Rolls up `status` over the run's captured `cases`, stamps `finishedAt`, and seals the run.

- **op** `queryRuns` Reads the plan's feed, newest-first, with optional filters.

- **op** `getCaseHistory` One case's status across runs, newest-first — the query behind F-4.2.

## Skill

- **skill** `QaSkill` Makes the QA store reachable over the DXOS MCP surface: an agent generates a plan from a spec's `## QA` section, runs the tests, and pushes a run back as it goes.

## Components

- **component** `TestPlanArticle` Main surface for a plan — the case list above the run feed.

- **component** `TestRunArticle` One run — the per-case result table, each row expanding to steps and artifacts.

- **component** `TestCaseArticle` One case — its authored steps, and its outcome across every run (F-4.2).

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` A run rolls up to the worst outcome
- **scenario** `T-2` A failure dominates a block
- **scenario** `T-3` A run covering nothing seals as skipped — the same holds for startRun called with cases: [] on a plan that has cases
- **scenario** `T-4` An unreported case cannot seal as passed
- **scenario** `T-5` A finished run is immutable
- **scenario** `T-6` Re-generation preserves case identity
- **scenario** `T-7` Artifacts are references, not copies
- **scenario** `T-8` A mid-run plan edit does not reject a captured case

## QA

- **test** `QA-1` Record a run against a plan — createPlan is a factory — it creates the plan in the target database but places nothing, so the placement below is a separate step even though the navtree does both in one gesture.

## Open questions

1. **Does a plan pin its cases by revision?** Today `TestCase` is mutable and a past result points at its current text, so a re-worded case silently re-writes what an old run appears to have tested. The alternative — snapshotting the case's steps into the `TestResult` — costs bytes per run but makes history honest. Deferred, not decided.
2. **Where do plans come from in CI?** The MCP path covers an agent at a desk. A CI job pushing runs needs either the same operations behind an EDGE-hosted MCP server or a thin ingest endpoint; the ontology is the same either way.
3. **Suites.** `TestPlan.cases` is flat. Grouping arrives as either nested plans or a `group` field on the case; flat is correct until a real plan is large enough to hurt.

---

pages.title: RecorderPlugin
pages.summary: Records the voice-over of a plugin-presenter deck while it is presented, slide by slide.
pages.content:
Records the voice-over of a plugin-presenter deck while it is presented, slide by slide. Each slide has its own takes, listed in the slide's Recordings companion, where a new take is recorded, played, selected as the slide's main take, or deleted. The presentation's Recordings companion records across every slide (the recording is split into a take per slide) and plays or downloads the voice-over assembled from each slide's main take. Every recording starts with a 3-2-1 count-in; the presenter shows each slide's speaker notes (subtitles or a notes window, a presenter setting) while it is read.

## Types

- **type** `Slide.takes` Fields plugin-presenter's `Slide` holds for the recorder.

- **type** `Take.Log` How a take was recorded, held in its Variant's `config`.

- **type** `RecorderSettings`

## Operations

- **op** `DeleteTake` Deletes a take of a slide (and its file); the newest remaining take becomes main if it was.
- **op** `RestoreTake` Re-adds a deleted take and its file at its place among the slide's takes, and its main mark.
- **op** `SelectTake` Marks a take as its slide's main take.

## Components

- **component** `RecordButton` The presenter toolbar item (PresenterSurface.Toolbar): records the whole presentation.
- **component** `RecordingOverlay` Over a deck being recorded (PresenterSurface.Overlay): the 3-2-1 count-in, then, centered at the top, REC, the recording's length, the time left on the slide when it has a desired length (red once over), and a compact l…
- **component** `LevelMeter` Peak meter over -60..0 dBFS: the target band -12..-3 marked, a peak-hold marker for 1.5s, CLIP above -1 dBFS, and NO SIGNAL after 2s of digital silence.
- **component** `RecordingsPanel` The layout both Recordings companions share: the toolbar, a full-width RecordingList (a react-ui-list Listbox with shared column tracks, its leading check and trailing buttons under the toolbar's icons; the current row…
- **component** `SlideRecordingsArticle` The Recordings companion of a Slide, on RecordingsPanel.
- **component** `PresentationRecordingsArticle` The Recordings companion of a Presentation, on RecordingsPanel.
- **component** `RecorderSettings` The plugin settings: microphone and camera pickers, the video source, and Test microphone with the meter.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Record
  - `F-1.1` A Presentation's toolbar, and its Recordings companion's toolbar, record every slide, presenting the deck from its first slide.
  - `F-1.2` A Slide's Recordings companion toolbar records that slide alone; the deck presents from it and the recording and presentation end when the reader leaves it.
  - `F-1.3` Every recording starts with a 3-2-1 count-in shown over the deck; nothing is recorded during it.
  - `F-1.4` The microphone is opened with echo cancellation, noise suppression and auto gain off.
  - `F-1.5` A recording is split by slide: each slide read becomes a take of that slide, named by its start time; no take is overwritten.
  - `F-1.6` A new take becomes its slide's main take.
  - `F-1.7` A take that cannot be saved stays listed with Save again and Discard.
  - `F-1.8` While recording, the deck shows REC, the recording's length and a level meter with NO SIGNAL and CLIP warnings, but no level readout, centered at the top.
  - `F-1.9` While recording a slide with a desired length, the overlay shows the time left on it, and how far over once past.
- **feat** `F-2` Slide takes
  - `F-2.1` A Slide has a Recordings companion listing its takes, newest first, with the main take marked.
  - `F-2.2` A take's row has a check that makes it the main take, Play, and Delete; a delete can be undone.
  - `F-2.4` Both Recordings companions share one layout: a toolbar, a keyboard-navigable list, and the current row's player in the status bar.
  - `F-2.3` Each take shows its length against the slide's desired length, flagged when over.
- **feat** `F-3` Presentation voice-over
  - `F-3.1` A Presentation has a Recordings companion listing each presented slide with its main take's length against its desired length.
  - `F-3.2` A slide's row has Play (its main take) and a double-click opens the slide; Play all plays every main take in slide order.
  - `F-3.3` Download saves the main takes, in slide order, as one WAV file.
- **feat** `F-4` Settings
  - `F-4.1` The settings choose the microphone, the video source (none, screen, camera) and the camera.
  - `F-4.2` Test microphone opens the chosen microphone on the level meter without recording.
  - `F-4.3` With no microphone chosen, a device whose label matches /shure/i is preferred.

## QA

- **test** `QA-1` Record a presentation's voice-over, then re-record one slide — The primary journey — record every slide, re-record one, pick its main take, and download the voice-over.

pages.title: ReviewPlugin
pages.summary: ReviewPlugin is the **review layer** over ECHO objects (primarily Markdown documents) — the merge of the former comments and versioning plugins into one surface.
pages.content:
ReviewPlugin is the **review layer** over ECHO objects (primarily Markdown documents) — the merge of the former comments and versioning plugins into one surface. It contributes three anchored, attributed review mechanisms and the surfaces that operate them:

- **Comment threads** — anchored discussions, with an optional per-thread AI agent that answers and may propose document edits.
- **Suggestions** — Google-Docs-style proposed changes authored on per-user `kind:'suggestion'` branches, rendered inline (tracked changes / multi-author overlay) and as reviewable change-block cards (accept/reject), with per-author colours and per-author visibility toggles.
- **Version history** — named checkpoints, draft branches, time travel, compare/merge, and the git-graph Timeline companion.

The editor integration is inverted: `@dxos/plugin-markdown` owns neutral sockets (`EditorBindingHook`, `ExtensionProvider`, `ViewModeExtension`) and this plugin contributes the behaviour — the version-aware editor binding, the comment-sync extension, and the "Suggesting" view mode. It depends on no other plugin: message/thread UI comes from `@dxos/react-ui-thread`, review/diff primitives from `@dxos/ui-editor`, branch machinery from `@dxos/versioning`, and the `Thread`/`Message`/`AnchoredTo` schema from `@dxos/types`.

Companion documents: [DESIGN.md](https://github.com/dxos/dxos/blob/main/packages/plugins/plugin-review/DESIGN.md) (three-layer spec, invariants I-1..I-9 each naming its enforcing test, known risks) and [TEST-PLAN.md](https://github.com/dxos/dxos/blob/main/packages/plugins/plugin-review/TEST-PLAN.md) (test tiers, shared scenarios, F1–F6 walkthrough scripts).

## External types & capabilities

The review layer composes primitives owned elsewhere; the plugin binds to them rather than redefining them:

- `Thread`, `Message`, `AnchoredTo` (`@dxos/types`) — the anchored-annotation schema. `AnchoredTo` carries an optional `branch` tag scoping an annotation to a review branch (undefined = main).
- `Branch`, `Version`, `History` (`@dxos/versioning`) — branches (core CRDT branches keyed in the database registry; a per-user suggestion branch is `kind:'suggestion'` keyed by author `creator` DID), checkpoints, fork anchors, `contentAt` snapshots. Find-or-create of the suggestion branch is identity-stable and serialized per (doc, creator); a stale branch is reconciled by folding main IN (`db.syncBranch`, CRDT merge), never by re-forking.
- `SuggestionSource`, `trackChanges`, `suggestions({ sources, base })`, `suggestionsOverlay`, `changeBarGutter`, `diffHunks`/`groupHunks`/`pairMarkupHunks`/`rebaseHunks`, `cherryPickHunk`/ `revertHunk`, `automerge` (`@dxos/ui-editor`) — the inline diff/overlay/sync primitives. Word-level hunks are minimized (an insert adjacent to identical text never strikes it), markdown delimiter pairs coalesce into one atomic hunk, and accept/reject merge every hunk a range spans.
- `MarkdownCapabilities.EditorBindingHook` / `ExtensionProvider` / `ViewModeExtension` (`@dxos/plugin-markdown`) — the sockets this plugin contributes to.
- `CollaborationOperation.AcceptChange` / `RejectChange` / `AcceptProposal` (`@dxos/app-toolkit`) — the durable cherry-pick/revert ops every review surface routes accept/reject through.
- `ViewState` (`@dxos/react-ui-attention`) — the per-session, per-object state backend for the `viewAspect` (version selection, review mode, current change, hidden authors) and the comments companion view state.

## Types

- **type** `ReviewMode` Per-user editing posture for a document (Google-Docs-style).

- **type** `VersionSelection` Which version of an object the local user is viewing: the current tip, a branch (editable tip), a branch's fork point (read-only parent snapshot), or a checkpoint.

- **type** `VersioningView` Per-object version view state, stored in the ViewState `viewAspect` (in-memory, per session).

- **type** `ReviewRenderConfig` What the editor renders for a review mode: `defaultReviewRenderPolicy` gives GDocs parity — editing/suggesting show suggestions+comments and are editable; viewing is read-only, comments only.

- **type** `ViewModeSelection` One dropdown gesture: a built-in editor view mode, or a contributed review mode.

- **type** `BindingDescriptor` Output of the pure `deriveBinding(inputs)` lifecycle derivation (invariant I-8): which document backs the editor (main, own suggestion branch, selected branch, or a detached snapshot), keyed how, rendered how.

- **type** `ResolvedSuggestionBranch` A resolved `kind:'suggestion'` branch: its author (identity DID), current content read live from the bound branch doc, and the parent text at the branch's fork anchor (`base`) — proposals are diffed against the revision…

- **type** `SuggestionGroup` One reviewable suggestion card: a grouped DiffHunk from a single author, anchored in the base (main) text, tinted with the author's colour.

- **type** `AgentMode` Per-thread agent firing policy.

- **type** `AgentConfig` Per-thread agent configuration.

- **type** `AgentIdentity` Effect/Capability identity of the comment-thread agent, resolved at runtime (not stored on threads).

- **type** `CommentsState` In-memory comment UI state (atom).

## Services

- **service** `EditorBindingHook` Implements MarkdownCapabilities.EditorBindingHook (`useMarkdownEditorBinding`): the version-aware editor binding.

- **service** `ExtensionProvider` Implements MarkdownCapabilities.ExtensionProvider (commentSync): syncs anchored comment threads with editor ranges, scopes visible comments to the active review branch (AnchoredTo.branch), tracks selection/comment overl…

- **service** `ViewModeExtension` Contributes the "Suggesting" entry to the markdown editor's view-mode dropdown (MarkdownCapabilities.ViewModeExtension, reviewMode 'suggesting').

- **service** `ReviewRenderPolicy` Maps a ReviewMode to its ReviewRenderConfig.

- **service** `HistoryProvider` Per-type opt-in to the generic History companion (checkpoints/branches timeline): `id` is the gating typename, `getTarget` resolves the versioned Text root.

- **service** `CommentAgentRunner` `AppCapabilities.CommentAgentRunner` (@dxos/app-toolkit): executes one agent turn for a thread + subject after the triggering message is in the thread's feed.

## Operations

Comment-thread operations (keys `org.dxos.plugin.review.operation.<name>`):

- **op** `Create` Create a (staged) comment thread anchored to a subject; seeds CommentsState.drafts.
- **op** `AddMessage` Append a user message to a thread (promoting a staged draft to active).
- **op** `Delete` Delete a thread + its anchor.
- **op** `Restore` Inverse of Delete.
- **op** `DeleteMessage` Delete a single message from a thread.
- **op** `RestoreMessage` Inverse of DeleteMessage.
- **op** `SetResolved` Set thread.status to active or resolved.
