pages.title: AutomationPlugin
pages.summary: A workflow automation engine plugin for DXOS Composer that enables event-driven pipelines connecting ECHO objects to persistent compute functions.
pages.content:
A workflow automation engine plugin for DXOS Composer that enables event-driven pipelines connecting ECHO objects to persistent compute functions.

Triggers listen for ECHO mutations, timer schedules, incoming feeds (email, webhook), or data subscriptions and invoke `PersistentOperation` handlers when their conditions fire. Each trigger carries optional structured input and is dispatched by a per-space `TriggerDispatcher` that runs locally in the browser, or is delegated to the DXOS edge when the trigger's `remote` flag is set. A space-wide `triggersDisabled` flag acts as a kill-switch that stops local dispatch entirely.

The plugin integrates with the `@dxos/compute` operation registry and the `@dxos/functions-runtime` execution layer. Skill, operation-handler, and toolkit contributions from other plugins are gathered at application scope and merged before being offered to space-level operation registries, so any plugin that contributes a `Capabilities.OperationHandler` automatically becomes invocable from an automation trigger.

Users interact with automations through the `AutomationPanel` settings surface, which lists active triggers for a space (or for a specific ECHO object) and opens the `TriggerEditor` form to create, configure, and enable/disable individual triggers.

## Types

Existing types used by this plugin (defined in `@dxos/compute` and `@dxos/functions-runtime`):

| Type                 | Source                    | Role in AutomationPlugin                                           |
|----------------------|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `Trigger`            | `@dxos/compute`           | Persistent trigger configuration (spec, function ref, input, enabled) |
| `PersistentOperation`| `@dxos/compute`           | Registered compute function callable from a trigger               |
| `Trace.Message`      | `@dxos/compute`           | Execution trace record appended after each trigger run            |
| `Script`             | `@dxos/compute`           | Source script that produces one or more `PersistentOperation`s    |
| `Feed`               | `@dxos/echo`              | Feed object that a `feed`-spec trigger listens to                 |
| `ComputeGraph`       | `@dxos/conductor`         | Visual workflow graph selectable as a trigger function            |

New types defined by this plugin:

- **type** `TriggerTemplate` Lightweight description of a trigger's spec used when creating a trigger from a pre-defined template (e.g.

## Components

- **component** `AutomationPanel` Settings surface that lists all triggers for a space (or filtered to a specific ECHO object) and provides inline create / edit / delete via the TriggerEditor form.

- **component** `TriggerEditor` Form-driven editor for a single Trigger.

- **component** `FunctionsPanel` Settings surface listing all PersistentOperation objects in a space.

- **component** `TemplateEditor` Markdown + Handlebars source editor backed by a Ref<Text>.

- **component** `RoutineProperties` Object-properties form for a Routine, rendered via ObjectProperties.

## Surfaces

## Operations

- **op** `CreateTriggerFromTemplate` Creates a new Trigger from a lightweight template, optionally wiring it to a named Script's PersistentOperation, and navigates to the automations settings panel for the target space.

- **op** `RunPromptInNewChat` Creates a new chat, binds context objects and skills, then runs a prompt.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Trigger Management
  - `F-1.1` User can create a Trigger in any space via AutomationPanel.
  - `F-1.2` User can edit an existing Trigger's function, spec, and input.
  - `F-1.3` User can delete a Trigger; it is removed from space.db.
  - `F-1.4` User can enable or disable a Trigger via an inline toggle.
  - `F-1.5` object context provided to AutomationPanel → only triggers matching that object's type or query are shown

- **feat** `F-2` Trigger Dispatch
  - `F-2.1` space.properties.triggersDisabled is unset or false → TriggerDispatcher starts for that space
  - `F-2.2` space.properties.triggersDisabled === true → TriggerDispatcher stops for that space
  - `F-2.3` triggersDisabled changes → any in-flight dispatcher transition is cancelled before the new one starts
  - `F-2.3a` trigger.remote === true → the local TriggerDispatcher skips the trigger (it runs on the edge instead)
  - `F-2.4` trigger spec.kind === "timer" and enabled === true → TriggerDispatcher fires trigger according to cron expression
  - `F-2.5` trigger spec.kind === "feed" → TriggerDispatcher processes new messages from the linked Feed
  - `F-2.6` trigger spec.kind === "subscription" → TriggerDispatcher invokes trigger on matching ECHO object mutations

- **feat** `F-3` Force Run and Cursor Reset
  - `F-3.1` timer trigger is enabled and space.properties.triggersDisabled !== true → user can force-run the trigger immediately from AutomationPanel
  - `F-3.2` trigger.remote !== true → force-run invokes TriggerDispatcher.invokeTrigger directly in-process
  - `F-3.3` trigger.remote === true → force-run calls FunctionsServiceClient.forceRunCronTrigger via HTTP
  - `F-3.4` trigger spec.kind === "feed" and a cursor is stored → user can reset the cursor to reprocess the feed from the beginning

- **feat** `F-4` Operation Registry
  - `F-4.1` plugin activates → all Capabilities.OperationHandler contributions are merged into a single OperationHandlerProvider
  - `F-4.2` OperationRegistry per space resolves operations from the merged OperationHandlerProvider.
  - `F-4.3` Skill registry is populated from AppCapabilities.SkillDefinition contributions.
  - `F-4.4` OpaqueToolkit aggregates AppCapabilities.Toolkit contributions for agent invocation.

- **feat** `F-5` Trace Sink
  - `F-5.1` a trigger executes → execution trace messages are written to the space Feed via FeedTraceSink
  - `F-5.2` FeedTraceSink is contributed to Capabilities.TraceSink and routed via makeRoutingSink.

- **feat** `F-6` Create Trigger From Template
  - `F-6.1` op:CreateTriggerFromTemplate is invoked → a Trigger is created and added as a hidden ECHO object in the target space
  - `F-6.2` scriptName is provided → the Trigger.function is wired to the PersistentOperation linked to that Script
  - `F-6.3` template.type === "timer" → Trigger.spec is set via Trigger.specTimer(template.cron)
  - `F-6.4` template.type === "feed" → Trigger.spec is set via Trigger.specFeed(template.feed)
  - `F-6.5` trigger is created → layout navigates to the automations settings panel for the space

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Create trigger via AutomationPanel

- **scenario** `T-2` Save new trigger

- **scenario** `T-3` Edit existing trigger

- **scenario** `T-4` Enable/disable toggle

- **scenario** `T-5` Force run timer trigger (local)

- **scenario** `T-6` Dispatcher lifecycle on kill-switch change

- **scenario** `T-7` CreateTriggerFromTemplate with timer

- **scenario** `T-8` CreateTriggerFromTemplate with feed

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Create a routine and run it — The core automation round-trip — create a Routine from a template, then run it on demand.

- **test** `QA-2` Timer trigger from a template — Wire a timer-spec Trigger from a lightweight template — the entrypoint used by Skill actions.

---

pages.title: S3Plugin
pages.summary: A **headless** Composer plugin that stores file blobs in an S3-compatible bucket — Cloudflare R2, AWS S3 or MinIO.
pages.content:
A **headless** Composer plugin that stores file blobs in an S3-compatible bucket — Cloudflare R2, AWS S3 or MinIO. It has no React/UI surfaces. It contributes two things:

1. A **Connector** entry with a credential form capturing the bucket endpoint and an access key pair. On submit the pair is stored as an `AccessToken` (`source` = the bucket host, `account` = the access key id, `token` = the secret) plus a `Connection` in ECHO.
2. A **`BlobBackend`** registered on the Hypergraph under the storage name `s3`, plus the matching `FileCapabilities.Backend` descriptor so it is selectable in the file plugin's settings.

The seam is the same one `plugin-wnfs` uses: `plugin-file` owns the storage-selection UI and `@dxos/echo-client` owns the backend registry, so neither has to know S3 exists. The credential seam is `CredentialsService`, so a server-custodied token resolves through EDGE unchanged.

## Addressing

- **type** `S3Uri` A stored blob is addressed `s3://<host>/<key>`, where host is the virtual-hosted bucket endpoint and key is `<spaceId>/<contentHash>`.

## Connector

- **feat** `S3Connector` Contributes a ConnectorEntry on the ConnectorEvents.Start activation event.

## Storage backend

- **feat** `S3BlobBackend` Contributes FileCapabilities.Backend and registers a BlobBackend under the storage name `s3` on FileEvents.Start (the file plugin's start — this plugin has no surface of its own to gate on).

## Signing

- **feat** `SigV4` AWS Signature Version 4 over WebCrypto, hand-rolled rather than taken from @aws-sdk: the SDK signer pulls a credential-provider chain, a region resolver and a Node crypto shim that a browser holding one static key pair…

- **scenario** `SigV4AwsVectors` The signer is checked against AWS's own published example signatures for both the header-auth and presigned-URL forms, so the tests are evidence of correctness rather than of self-consistency.

## Operator requirements

- **feat** `BucketConfiguration` Two things must be true of the bucket or nothing works.

pages.title: SandboxPlugin
pages.summary: Sandbox plugin for DXOS Composer providing isolated shell environments, and the git repositories that keep what they build.
pages.content:
Sandbox plugin for DXOS Composer providing isolated shell environments, and the git repositories that keep what they build.

It also contributes the **Composer Plugin (Sandbox)** project template: a project whose agent builds a TypeScript Composer plugin in an EDGE sandbox, serves the build from the container, and offers the exposed URL back to load — the Dev Shell template's demo without a locally served Composer.

## Exposed ports

`exposePort` issues a URL that proxies any request to that port in the container with no `Authorization`, so a browser can fetch a manifest and import a module from it: on its own host, `https://<port>-<sandboxId>-<token><suffix>/` (`-dev.dxos.ai` on dev, `.dxos.ai` in production), or under `<edge>/sandbox/preview/<sandboxId>/<port>/<token>/` where an env has no preview hosts. The random token is the only credential, and it is checked before the container is touched. Given the `command` that serves the port, the service starts it when it is not running and again whenever the container has slept, so the URL lives as long as the sandbox.

`exec` streams the command's output from the service and returns once it exits, so a command of several minutes runs in one call; a request answered only at the end lost its connection while the command ran.

## Backends

The operations run against `SandboxService.Service`, which the plugin contributes to the process runtime as an application-affinity `LayerSpec`. Sandboxes run on EDGE's sandbox-service unless the plugin's **Backend** setting is `local`, its default in the desktop app (`DX_SANDBOX_BACKEND=local|edge` overrides it under Node or Bun). Local sandboxes are processes confined by the OS sandbox (bubblewrap on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS) via `@carderne/sandbox-runtime`:

- **Where they run**: in-process under Node or Bun. In the desktop app, whose webview cannot spawn processes, the plugin starts `dx-sandbox` (this package's `compile-sidecar` output) and the webview reaches it on a loopback port with a per-launch token passed over stdin. The launcher is annotated `environments: ['tauri']`, so only the Tauri (desktop and iOS) bundles carry it.
- **Filesystem**: each sandbox is `$DX_SANDBOX_ROOT/<id>/` (default `~/.local/state/dxos/sandboxes`). Commands write only its `workspace/` (their cwd and `$HOME`) and `tmp/`; the user's home directory and other sandboxes are unreadable. `/workspace/…` paths in file operations map onto `workspace/`.
- **Network**: only package registries, pkg.pr.new and GitHub (`DEFAULT_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`) are reachable.
- **Toolchain**: in the desktop app, commands find `bun` and `bunx` first on their `PATH`. They are the helper itself, a `bun build --compile` executable run with `BUN_BE_BUN=1`, so a sandbox installs and builds JavaScript on a machine with no node or bun of its own.
- **Limits**: per-command CPU time, writable memory (Linux only) and file size, plus the wall-clock `timeout`, which kills the command's whole process group.
- **Environment**: the host's environment is not inherited; only `PATH`, `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `LANG`, `WORKSPACE` and the operation's `env` are set, plus the helper's own `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` and `SSL_CERT_FILE` (and read access to the bundles they name), so installs work behind a TLS-inspecting proxy.

## Repositories

Sandboxes are ephemeral; a repository is durable. An EDGE repository is a type:Repo (from `@dxos/types`, the same type a GitHub repository is) carrying an `edge.dxos.network` foreign key: a git repository hosted by EDGE on [Cloudflare Artifacts](https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/), named after its space and that key's id, so the space is part of its identity and stands in as the `Repo`'s owner. The ECHO object is created locally and the repository on EDGE by the first read of it (or by attaching it), so a repository made offline, or on another device, is backed as soon as anything uses it.

- **One type, host as provenance.** A project lists GitHub and EDGE repositories side by side; what this plugin does with one (attach, read) needs the EDGE key and fails for a `Repo` without it. Spaces made before the fold hold `org.dxos.type.repository` objects, which a migration turns into `Repo`s in place, keeping the object id and carrying it over as the EDGE key.

- **Attached, not driven.** A sandbox's `repositories` are part of its configuration, like its `credentials`: set when the sandbox is created or by `attachRepository`, and held by EDGE with the sandbox. Every command the sandbox runs then has each one as a git remote named after the repository (`$DX_REPOSITORIES` lists them), so the agent moves work with plain git — `git push <remote> HEAD:main`, `git pull <remote> main`. No operation pushes or pulls for it.
- **Credentials per command.** EDGE mints a write token per attached repository for each command, passes it as the process's git config (an `http.<remote>.extraHeader` scoped to that remote's URL, never the remote URL itself), revokes it when the command ends, and scrubs it from the output. The token never reaches the client.
- **Reads** (branches, log, tree, file) come from a shallow in-memory clone EDGE keeps per repository, fetched to 200 commits per branch, so history beyond that is not browsable.
- Only EDGE sandboxes can have repositories attached; a local sandbox has no route to the service's git remote.
- The article surface browses a repository: a branch picker, a lazily listed file tree beside the selected file, and the history, where picking a commit browses the files at it.

## Types

- **type** `Sandbox`

## Operations

- **op** `createSandbox` Creates a new sandbox environment persisted as an ECHO object in the space.

- **op** `exec` Runs a shell command in the sandbox.

- **op** `exposePort` Publishes a port the sandbox listens on at a public URL loadable without credentials (EDGE only).

- **op** `uploadFile` Uploads a file from ECHO into the sandbox filesystem.

- **op** `downloadFile` Downloads a file from the sandbox filesystem into ECHO.

- **op** `publishFiles` Serves a directory of a local sandbox read-only over HTTP on this machine and returns its base URL.

Only the desktop app's helper publishes: it serves the directory at `http://localhost:<port>/files/<key>/` without the bearer token, since a module loader cannot send one, so the 128-bit key minted per call is the credential. Paths that climb out of the directory, and symlinks out of the workspace, answer 404; files are served `nosniff` under `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`, and keys are forgotten when the helper exits. Under the EDGE backend, or in-process under Node, the output carries the reason instead.

- **op** `attachRepository` Attaches a repository to a sandbox; every later command has it as a git remote.

- **op** `createRepository` Creates a git repository persisted as an ECHO object, backed by Cloudflare Artifacts on EDGE.

- **op** `listRepositoryBranches` Lists a repository's branches and the commit each points at.

- **op** `getRepositoryLog` Lists commits newest first.

- **op** `listRepositoryFiles` Lists a directory of a repository at a branch or commit.

- **op** `readRepositoryFile` Reads a file of a repository at a branch or commit; binary content is base64.

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Create a sandbox and run a command — The core sandbox round-trip — create an isolated shell environment, exec a command in it.

- **test** `QA-2` Build in a sandbox, push to a repository with git, pick it up in another sandbox — A sandbox's work outlives it — attach a repository, push with plain git, browse it, pull it into a fresh sandbox.

pages.title: ScriptPlugin
pages.summary: A scripting plugin for `DXOS` Composer that lets users write, deploy, and run custom TypeScript functions as ECHO objects inside their spaces.
pages.content:
A scripting plugin for `DXOS` Composer that lets users write, deploy, and run custom TypeScript functions as ECHO objects inside their spaces. Scripts execute on the Cloudflare Workers-based EDGE runtime and can call DXOS SDK packages, Effect-TS, and a curated set of third-party libraries. An AI assistant skill wires CRUD, deploy, invoke, and inspection operations as tools so an agent can scaffold, iterate, and test scripts entirely within a chat session.

## Types

- **type** `Script` Root ECHO object (typename from @dxos/compute Script.Script).

- **type** `Notebook` Root ECHO object for a multi-cell notebook view.

- **type** `Settings` Plugin-scoped settings atom.

- **type** `InvocationSpan` A single function invocation record from the EDGE trace feed.

- **type** `DeployedFunction` Metadata about a function already deployed to the EDGE runtime.

## Components

- **component** `ScriptArticle` Primary editor surface for a Script object.

- **component** `NotebookArticle` Multi-cell notebook surface for a Notebook object.

- **component** `TestContainer` Execute companion panel.

- **component** `DeploymentDialog` Dialog for deploying or redeploying a Script to the EDGE runtime.

- **component** `ScriptPluginSettings` Plugin settings panel; exposes editor keybinding mode selector.

## Operations

Skill operations (called by the Script assistant via its tool set).

- **op** `create` Creates a new Script ECHO object with the given name and TypeScript source, and adds it to the space.

- **op** `read` Reads the name, source code, and description of an existing Script.

- **op** `update` Applies one or more string edits (find/replace pairs) to a Script's source and optionally updates its name and description.

- **op** `delete` Permanently removes a Script and its source from the space.

- **op** `deploy` Compiles and deploys a Script to the EDGE (Cloudflare Workers) runtime.

- **op** `invoke` Calls a deployed EDGE function with an optional JSON payload.

- **op** `inspectInvocations` Queries the EDGE invocation trace feed for a function and returns recent invocation spans (id, timestamp, duration, outcome, input, error).

- **op** `queryDeployedFunctions` Lists all functions currently deployed to the EDGE runtime.

- **op** `installFunction` Installs a globally-deployed EDGE function into the current space by key.

UI-facing operation (creates Script via the navtree / "create object" flow).

- **op** `createScript` Creates a new Script ECHO object via the Composer create-object flow.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Script ECHO Object
  - `F-1.1` Script objects are registered via `addSchemaModule` and visible in space object lists.
  - `F-1.2` Script objects can be created from the navtree "+" menu.
  - `F-1.3` user creates a Script without a template → source is seeded from the default template
  - `F-1.4` user provides a GitHub Gist URL → gist content is fetched and used as initial source

- **feat** `F-2` Script Editor
  - `F-2.1` ScriptArticle renders a TypeScript-aware CodeMirror editor for the Article role.
  - `F-2.2` Editor keybinding mode (default/vim/emacs) is configurable via plugin settings.
  - `F-2.3` Changes to source are persisted to the Script ECHO object reactively.
  - `F-2.4` script object changes externally (peer edit) → editor content updates without losing cursor position if possible

- **feat** `F-3` Deploy to EDGE
  - `F-3.1` A Deploy button in the ScriptToolbar opens the DeploymentDialog.
  - `F-3.2` user confirms deployment → op:deploy is called; script compiled and sent to EDGE runtime
  - `F-3.3` compilation fails → error messages are surfaced to the user; no deployment occurs
  - `F-3.4` deployment succeeds → dialog shows the function URL (if available)

- **feat** `F-4` Execute Companion
  - `F-4.1` An "Execute" companion node is added to every Script in the app graph.
  - `F-4.2` TestContainer renders a form derived from the script's Operation input schema.
  - `F-4.3` user submits the form → op:invoke is called with the form payload; response displayed
  - `F-4.4` A "Logs" companion node shows the invocation trace via InvocationTraceContainer.

- **feat** `F-5` Script Skill
  - `F-5.1` A skill with key `org.dxos.skill.script` is contributed via `addSkillDefinitionModule`.
  - `F-5.2` Skill tool set includes: create, read, update, delete, deploy, invoke,
  - `F-5.3` System instructions describe the EDGE Operation pattern, required export format,
  - `F-5.4` Skill is agent-enabled; the assistant can activate it autonomously.

- **feat** `F-6` Notebook
  - `F-6.1` Notebook objects are registered and can be created from the navtree.
  - `F-6.2` NotebookArticle renders each linked Script as a sequential cell.
  - `F-6.3` Cells can be added and removed independently.

- **feat** `F-7` Plugin Settings
  - `F-7.1` ScriptPluginSettings is rendered via the app settings surface.
  - `F-7.2` Editor input mode is persisted in the Settings atom.
  - `F-7.3` An Authenticate button lets the user write an access credential to HALO.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-2` Create script from Gist

- **scenario** `T-3` Edit and persist source

- **scenario** `T-4` Deploy script

- **scenario** `T-6` Inspect invocations

- **scenario** `T-7` Skill tools resolve

- **scenario** `T-8` Agent creates and deploys script

- **scenario** `T-9` QueryDeployedFunctions and install

pages.title: SearchPlugin
pages.summary: A full-text search plugin for `DXOS` Composer that lets users locate objects within the active space, ranked and highlighted against the space's FTS5 index.
pages.content:
A full-text search plugin for `DXOS` Composer that lets users locate objects within the active space, ranked and highlighted against the space's FTS5 index. The same index also filters messages in the mailbox.

## Types

- **type** `SearchQuery`

- **type** `MatchField`

- **type** `SearchResult`

## Components

- **component** `SearchDialog` Modal command-palette style dialog invoked globally via the OpenSearch operation.

- **component** `SearchArticle` Inline search panel mounted in the deck companion (sidebar) and in the search-input role.

## Operations

- **op** `OpenSearch` Opens the global SearchDialog by dispatching a LayoutOperation.UpdateDialog event.
- **op** `SelectObject` Opens the same SearchDialog as an object picker: the caller decides what the object is for (add it to a chat's context, link it from a document), so picking a result returns it instead of opening it.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Local Object Search
  - `F-1.1` User can open SearchDialog from anywhere in Composer via the OpenSearch operation.
  - `F-1.2` user types into the search input → query is debounced (400 ms) then matched against all ECHO objects in the active space
  - `F-1.3` an object's field value matches the query regex → result entry shown with the object type, matched field key, and field value snippet
  - `F-1.4` query is empty or cleared → results list is empty; no search is executed

- **feat** `F-2` Global Filter Integration
  - `F-2.1` SearchContextProvider is mounted → active query is propagated to GlobalFilterProvider so all views using
  - `F-2.2` query is cleared → GlobalFilterProvider returns all objects unfiltered

- **feat** `F-3` Deck Companion Search Panel
  - `F-3.1` user opens the deck companion panel with role deck-companion--search → SearchArticle is rendered scoped to the active Space
  - `F-3.2` user types in SearchArticle → results update in real time using the same debounced filter as SearchDialog

- **feat** `F-4` Mailbox Message Search
  - `F-4.1` user types a query in the mailbox search box → messages are filtered against the same FTS5 index used by SearchDialog / SearchArticle
  - `F-4.2` a message matches the query → the matched text is highlighted in the message list

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` OpenSearch operation opens dialog

- **scenario** `T-2` Query returns matching objects

- **scenario** `T-3` Empty query shows no results

- **scenario** `T-4` GlobalFilter propagation

- **scenario** `T-5` Non-matching query shows empty state

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Open search and find an object — The core search round-trip — open the dialog, type a query, get a matching result.

pages.title: SequencerPlugin
pages.summary: A music sequencer / step-grid editor for `DXOS` Composer.
pages.content:
A music sequencer / step-grid editor for `DXOS` Composer. A `Score` owns a set of tracks and per-track `Sequence` objects whose `Note`s are edited on a 2D grid (pitch on the y-axis, time on the x-axis). Backed by the plugin's own canvas-based `CellGrid` component.

## Notes (Phase 2)

- Edit sequences
- Arrange sequences
- Sound engine

## Types

- **type** `Note` A single note in a sequence.

- **type** `Track` Track metadata.

- **type** `Sequence` An ordered collection of notes associated with a single track.

- **type** `Instrument` A physical instrument: what it can play (its tuning) and how it sounds (its calibration, recorded by striking each note).

- **type** `Score` Top-level container.

## Components

- **component** `SequenceGrid` 2D grid editor for a single Sequence.

- **component** `TrackList` Vertical list of tracks in a Score with mute/instrument controls and selection state.

- **component** `ScoreArticle` Top-level article surface for a Score.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Create Score
  - `F-1.1` User can create a new Score from the navtree.
  - `F-1.2` New Score has tempo=120, no tracks, no sequences.

- **feat** `F-2` Manage Tracks
  - `F-2.1` user adds a track → new Track appended to Score.tracks with a unique id and default name
  - `F-2.2` user removes a track → Track removed AND all Sequences referencing trackId are removed
  - `F-2.3` user mutes a track → Track.muted toggled; playback skips notes from muted tracks

- **feat** `F-3` Edit Sequence Notes
  - `F-3.1` user clicks an empty cell in SequenceGrid → new Note added at (pitch, startTime); duration = beatsPerCell
  - `F-3.2` user clicks a cell containing a note → that Note removed from the Sequence
  - `F-3.3` user drags across empty cells in the same row → Notes are added at each cell along the drag (paint mode)
  - `F-3.4` SequenceGrid is scrolled or zoomed → pitch labels (y-axis) and beat ruler (x-axis) stay frozen / visible

- **feat** `F-4` Playback
  - `F-4.1` user presses play → playhead advances at Score.tempo BPM across the active Sequence
  - `F-4.2` playhead reaches end of Sequence.length → playhead loops to 0 (v1: no score-level transport across sequences)
  - `F-4.3` user presses stop → playhead returns to null; SequenceGrid removes playhead overlay

- **feat** `F-5` Sequence Selection
  - `F-5.1` user clicks a track in TrackList → first Sequence for that track is shown in the SequenceGrid; if no
  - `F-5.2` selected track changes → SequenceGrid re-renders with the new sequence's notes

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` New Score defaults

- **scenario** `T-2` Add and remove note

- **scenario** `T-3` Remove track cascades sequences

- **scenario** `T-4` Playhead loops

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Read and write a score as lead-sheet text — The agent-facing round-trip: read a Score's lead-sheet text, write a modified version back, and read again to confirm.
- **test** `QA-2` Showcase clip — The 10s showcase clip: Fill a step grid in a new score.

pages.title: SheetPlugin
pages.summary: Spreadsheet plugin for `DXOS` Composer — a full-featured grid backed by ECHO for local-first, real-time collaborative data entry, formula evaluation, and structured data display.
pages.content:
Spreadsheet plugin for `DXOS` Composer — a full-featured grid backed by ECHO for local-first, real-time collaborative data entry, formula evaluation, and structured data display.

## Types

- **type** `CellValue`

- **type** `RowColumnMeta`

- **type** `Range`

- **type** `Axis`

- **type** `Sheet`

## Components

- **component** `SheetArticle` Primary spreadsheet view rendered inside an article or section role surface.

- **component** `RangeList` Object-properties panel listing named ranges and formatting annotations on a Sheet.

## Operations

- **op** `insertAxis` Inserts one or more rows or columns at the given index in the sheet model.

- **op** `dropAxis` Removes a row or column by axis index, returning data needed to restore it (undo).

- **op** `restoreAxis` Restores a previously dropped row or column (undo of dropAxis).

- **op** `scrollToAnchor` Programmatically scrolls and highlights a cell range in an active grid instance.

Agent-facing skill operations (not previously documented here — found in `src/types/SheetOperation.ts`):

- **op** `create` Creates a new Sheet and adds it to the space.
- **op** `getRange` Reads cell values from a sheet as a 2D array.
- **op** `setRange` Sets multiple cell values in a sheet at once, keyed by A1 address.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Sheet Object
  - `F-1.1` A Sheet is an ECHO object with typename org.dxos.type.sheet persisted in the user's space.
  - `F-1.2` Cells are stored in a sparse map keyed by internal row/column indices.
  - `F-1.3` Row and column order is maintained via ordered index arrays; insertion/deletion preserves existing cell references.
  - `F-1.4` Range-based formatting annotations are stored as a flat array on the Sheet object.

- **feat** `F-2` Formula Evaluation
  - `F-2.1` Formulas are prefixed with "=" and evaluated by the HyperFormula engine via the ComputeGraph.
  - `F-2.2` Over 400 built-in functions are available (arithmetic, statistical, text, date/time, financial, logical).
  - `F-2.3` a cell value changes → all dependent formula cells are recomputed reactively
  - `F-2.4` Cell references in stored formulas are translated to internal indices; A1-notation is converted on read/write.

- **feat** `F-3` Row and Column Management
  - `F-3.1` op:insertAxis is called → a new row or column is inserted at the specified index; existing cells shift accordingly
  - `F-3.2` op:dropAxis is called → the row or column is removed and undo data returned; op:restoreAxis reverses the operation
  - `F-3.3` Row and column sizes are persisted in rowMeta/columnMeta; absent size means default grid size.

- **feat** `F-4` Cell Formatting
  - `F-4.1` Ranges support alignment values: start | center | end.
  - `F-4.2` Ranges support comment annotations displayed as a visual overlay on the cell.
  - `F-4.3` Ranges support style values: highlight | softwrap.
  - `F-4.4` RangeList in the object-properties surface allows users to view and manage range annotations.

- **feat** `F-5` Collaborative Editing
  - `F-5.1` All cell edits are written through ECHO and replicated to peers in real time.
  - `F-5.2` a peer writes a cell value → the local grid re-renders with the updated value without full reload
  - `F-5.3` ComputeGraphRegistry manages per-space HyperFormula instances so all peers share the same formula graph.

- **feat** `F-6` Markdown Integration
  - `F-6.1` SheetPlugin contributes a CodeMirror extension to plugin-markdown via MarkdownCapabilities.ExtensionProvider.
  - `F-6.2` the extension is active in a document that belongs to a space → formula references inside Markdown fenced code blocks resolve against the space's ComputeGraph

- **feat** `F-7` Anchor Navigation
  - `F-7.1` op:scrollToAnchor is invoked with a sheet attendable ID and cursor → the corresponding SheetArticle scrolls to the target cell and applies the active-ref highlight
  - `F-7.2` AnchorSort contributes a sort comparator so sheet anchors appear in canonical order in navigation menus.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Create sheet and enter a value

- **scenario** `T-2` Formula evaluation

- **scenario** `T-3` Insert and drop row

- **scenario** `T-4` Range formatting

- **scenario** `T-5` Real-time collaboration

- **scenario** `T-6` Scroll to anchor

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Create a sheet, set values, evaluate a formula, read back — The core spreadsheet round-trip — create, set cells (including a formula), read the

- **test** `QA-2` Build a budget and watch its totals recompute — The demo path — create a sheet, type a small table, total it with SUM, and change a value.

- **test** `QA-3` Chart a sales report in the Charts companion — The charts demo — open the Bramble template's sales report and switch between its charts.
- **test** `QA-4` Showcase clip — The 10s showcase clip: Fill a sheet with values and formulas.

pages.title: SidekickPlugin
pages.summary: A personal companion agent plugin for DXOS Composer that monitors activity, maintains profiles of people and the user, keeps a daily journal, and helps manage communications.
pages.content:
A personal companion agent plugin for DXOS Composer that monitors activity, maintains profiles of people and the user, keeps a daily journal, and helps manage communications. The agent is document-aware, workflow-aware, and agent-aware. Interaction is primarily via Chat with voice input support.

## Types

Existing types used by this plugin (defined elsewhere):

| Type           | Source                    | Typename                       | Role in Sidekick                                                      |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Agent`        | `@dxos/assistant-toolkit` | `org.dxos.type.agent`          | The sidekick instance (spec, chat, queue, artifacts)                  |
| `Chat`         | `@dxos/assistant-toolkit` | `org.dxos.type.assistant.chat` | Primary interaction channel                                           |
| `Journal`      | `plugin-outliner`         | `org.dxos.type.journal`        | Daily journal (date-indexed entries)                                  |
| `JournalEntry` | `plugin-outliner`         | `org.dxos.type.journalEntry`   | Per-day entry with markdown task lists                                |
| `Feed`         | `@dxos/echo`              | `org.dxos.type.feed`           | Backing store for Chat messages                                       |
| `Person`       | `@dxos/types`             | `org.dxos.type.person`         | People the agent tracks and profiles                                  |
| `Text`         | `@dxos/echo`              | (system)                       | Profile documents, agent instructions                                 |
| `Message`      | `@dxos/echo`              | (system)                       | Chat messages including voice-transcribed input                       |
| `Tag`          | (system)                  | (system)                       | Person categorization (friend, colleague, customer, investor, family) |

New types defined by this plugin:

- **type** `Profile` Agent-managed profile linking to an underlying object (e.g., Person) with metadata.

- **type** `SidekickProperties` Per-agent configuration stored alongside AgentProperties.

## Components

- **component** `SidekickArticle` Primary dashboard for the sidekick agent.

- **component** `DayAhead` Summarizes today's journal entry and upcoming items.

- **component** `ActionItems` Aggregated task list from recent JournalEntries.

- **component** `ProfileGrid` Grid of Profile cards showing subject name, tags, and notification counts.

- **component** `ProfileSummary` Excerpt from the user's profile document showing current goals.

- **component** `Permissions` Per-profile permission toggles for agent communication behavior.

## Services

- **service** `SidekickSkill` Composes existing skills to provide the agent's full capability set.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Agent Creation and Configuration — Create and configure a Sidekick agent instance in a space.
  - `F-1.1` Plugin creates an Agent.Agent with skill org.dxos.skill.sidekick.
  - `F-1.2` Agent spec populated with instruction template including user name.
  - `F-1.3` Agent chat created and linked for companion interaction.
  - `F-1.4` Agent queue created for event processing.
  - `F-1.5` Journal created and added as agent artifact.
  - `F-1.6` Create document to track agent memories.

- **feat** `F-2` Person Profile Management — Maintain a markdown Profile document for each Person in the space.
  - `F-2.1` agent discovers a Person without a linked Profile → creates a markdown document titled "Profile: {personName}"
  - `F-2.2` profile document is created → linked to Person via relation and added as agent artifact
  - `F-2.3` agent learns new information about a Person (via email, chat, etc.) → updates the Person's profile document
  - `F-2.4` Person has no tag → agent suggests a category tag (friend, colleague, customer, investor, family)

- **feat** `F-3` User Profile — Maintain a frank profile document about the user.
  - `F-3.1` Agent creates "Profile: {userName}" document on initialization.
  - `F-3.2` Profile includes character assessment and current goals sections.
  - `F-3.3` user chats with agent → agent may ask clarifying questions to refine user model
  - `F-3.4` user's goals or priorities change → agent updates the goals section of the user profile

- **feat** `F-4` Daily Journal — Track important decisions, conversations, and actions in a Journal.
  - `F-4.1` something important happens (decision, key conversation, action item) → agent creates or updates today's JournalEntry
  - `F-4.2` JournalEntry content uses markdown task lists for action items.
  - `F-4.3` Day-ahead summary on dashboard is derived from today's JournalEntry.

- **feat** `F-5` Dashboard — Article surface providing overview of sidekick state.
  - `F-5.1` Dashboard displayed for Agent objects with sidekick skill.
  - `F-5.2` Day Ahead section shows summary from today's JournalEntry.
  - `F-5.3` Action Items section aggregates open tasks from recent entries.
  - `F-5.4` People section shows Person cards with tags and update counts.
  - `F-5.5` Your Profile section shows excerpt from user's profile document.
  - `F-5.6` Permissions section shows auto-respond and draft-only toggles per contact.

- **feat** `F-6` Chat and Voice Interaction — Primary interaction via Chat companion with voice input.
  - `F-6.1` Chat companion linked to agent's Chat object.
  - `F-6.2` Voice input via existing useVoiceInput from plugin-transcription.
  - `F-6.3` Agent tolerates transcription artifacts in voice-transcribed messages.

- **feat** `F-7` Email Integration (Phase 2) — Monitor email and manage communications for authorized contacts.
  - `F-7.1` Agent reads and classifies incoming email for tracked persons.
  - `F-7.2` Agent drafts responses for authorized contacts.
  - `F-7.3` Auto-respond only for explicitly permitted contacts.
  - `F-7.4` Draft messages shown for review unless auto-respond enabled.
  - `F-7.5` Action items extracted from incoming messages.

- **feat** `F-8` Comment Thread Responses (Phase 2) — Agent responds to comments in markdown document threads.
  - `F-8.1` Agent monitors comment threads on documents it manages.
  - `F-8.2` Agent responds with relevant context from profiles and journal.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Agent initialization

- **scenario** `T-2` Person profile creation

- **scenario** `T-3` Person tagging

- **scenario** `T-4` User profile maintenance

- **scenario** `T-5` Journal entry creation

- **scenario** `T-6` Dashboard rendering

- **scenario** `T-7` Voice input tolerance

## Phased Rollout

### Phase 1 — Core Functionality

- Plugin skeleton (meta, translations, skill registration).
- Sidekick Skill composing database, agent, markdown, inbox skills.
- Agent creation with instruction template, chat, journal, artifacts.
- Person profile creation and linking.
- User profile document.
- Journal with daily entries.
- SidekickArticle dashboard.
- Voice input via Chat companion.

### Phase 2 — Communication and Monitoring

- Email monitoring and draft generation (F-7).
- Permission system for auto-respond vs draft-only per contact (F-5.6).
- Background research on persons via research skill.
- Thread comment responses (F-8).
- Proactive suggestions based on email/calendar context.

### Phase 3 — Future Research

- Local ML transcription via plugin-transformer.
- Calendar integration for day-ahead enrichment.
- Multi-space person deduplication.
- Agent-to-agent communication.
- Data migration tooling for schema evolution.

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Create a Sidekick agent and view its dashboard — The core round-trip — create an Agent instance carrying the sidekick skill, and confirm the dashboard surface renders for it.

---

pages.title: SlackPlugin
pages.summary: SlackPlugin connects a Slack workspace to DXOS Composer via OAuth, discovers conversations (public channels, private channels), and incrementally syncs messages into ECHO as `Channel` and `Message` objects so they appear alongside everything else in a space.
pages.content:
SlackPlugin connects a Slack workspace to DXOS Composer via OAuth, discovers conversations (public channels, private channels), and incrementally syncs messages into ECHO as `Channel` and `Message` objects so they appear alongside everything else in a space. Each synced Channel is on the Slack channel backend (plugin-thread's `ChannelBackend`), so agents post to it as the connection's bot.

## Types

- **type** `ConversationKind` Slack conversation category returned by conversations.list.

- **type** `RemoteTarget` Wire-shape descriptor for a single Slack conversation as returned by op:GetSlackChannels.

- **type** `PullResult` Aggregate count returned by op:SyncSlackChannel.

- **type** `SlackCredentials` Effect Context.Tag holding the bearer token used by SlackApi calls.

- **type** `SlackChannel` Config of a Slack-backed Channel (Channel.backend.config, kind org.dxos.channel.backend.slack).

## Operations

Discovery operations — read-only, no ECHO writes.

- **op** `GetSlackChannels` Lists all Slack conversations reachable from the integration's OAuth token without creating any local ECHO objects.

Sync operations — pull messages from Slack and write to ECHO.

- **op** `SyncSlackChannel` Reconciles messages for the currently-selected Slack targets on an Integration.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` OAuth Connection
  - `F-1.1` Plugin MUST contribute an IntegrationProvider for source 'slack.com'
  - `F-1.4` A connection made before chat:write was requested keeps syncing;
  - `F-1.2` OAuth flow completes and an AccessToken is created → auth.test is called; accessToken.account is set to '<user>@<team>'
  - `F-1.3` Bearer token MUST be passed via POST body (application/x-www-form-urlencoded)

- **feat** `F-2` Channel Discovery
  - `F-2.1` op:GetSlackChannels is invoked with a valid Integration ref → all pages of conversations.list are drained and one RemoteTarget
  - `F-2.2` Discovery MUST NOT create any local Channel objects; materialization
  - `F-2.3` a conversation has no name (IM) → label is 'DM with <user-id>' (display name resolution is lazy)

- **feat** `F-3` Incremental Sync
  - `F-3.1` op:SyncSlackChannel is invoked for the first time on a target → a new Channel is created in ECHO with a foreign key
  - `F-3.2` op:SyncSlackChannel is invoked on a previously-synced target → only messages with ts > target.cursor are fetched.
  - `F-3.3` After a successful sync, target.cursor MUST be updated to the
  - `F-3.4` a target sync fails → target.lastError is set to a human-readable string; other targets
  - `F-3.5` Messages of subtype channel_join or channel_leave MUST be filtered

- **feat** `F-4` Message Mapping
  - `F-4.1` Each Slack message MUST map to a @dxos/types Message with:
  - `F-4.2` Slack rich-text blocks array is intentionally NOT mapped in v1;
  - `F-4.3` User ids referenced in messages MUST be resolved via users.info
  - `F-4.4` Bot ids MUST be resolved via bots.info with the same concurrency

- **feat** `F-5` Error Handling and Retries
  - `F-5.1` Slack API calls MUST retry on transient failures (transport
  - `F-5.2` Slack application errors ({ ok: false }) MUST NOT be retried;
  - `F-5.3` SyncSlackChannel fails at the operation level (not per-target) → a toast notification MUST be shown via LayoutOperation.AddToast
  - `F-5.4` SyncSlackChannel succeeds → a success toast MUST be shown via LayoutOperation.AddToast.

- **feat** `F-6` Slack Channel Backend
  - `F-6.1` Plugin MUST contribute a ThreadCapabilities.ChannelBackend of kind
  - `F-6.2` send MUST post with chat.postMessage into config.conversationId and
  - `F-6.3` threads.send MUST reply with thread_ts when the thread id is a Slack
  - `F-6.4` openDirect MUST read the person's identity labelled 'slack' and
  - `F-6.5` Slack refusals (missing_scope, not_in_channel, …) MUST fail with a
  - `F-6.6` readOnly is always true: the channel article never posts as the bot;
  - `F-6.7` Sync MUST skip messages whose ts the mirror feed already holds.
  - `F-6.8` Materialize and sync MUST move a feed-backed Slack channel onto the
  - `F-6.9` Real-time receiving (Events API / Socket Mode on EDGE) is deferred;

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` OAuth populates account field

- **scenario** `T-2` Discovery returns targets without ECHO writes

- **scenario** `T-3` First sync materializes Channel

- **scenario** `T-4` Second sync is incremental

- **scenario** `T-5` Per-target failure does not abort other targets

- **scenario** `T-6` System messages filtered

- **scenario** `T-7` Thread replies grouped

- **scenario** `T-8` Idempotent re-sync

- **scenario** `T-9` A posted message is not synced twice

## QA

pages.title: SpacePlugin
pages.summary: Core workspace container plugin for `DXOS` Composer — creates, manages, and shares collaborative spaces with full membership control, object lifecycle management, schema registration, and navigation.
pages.content:
Core workspace container plugin for `DXOS` Composer — creates, manages, and shares collaborative spaces with full membership control, object lifecycle management, schema registration, and navigation.

## Types

- **type** `SpaceForm`

- **type** `SpacePluginOptions`

- **type** `ObjectViewerProps`

- **type** `PluginState`

## Components

- **component** `CollectionArticle` Main article view for a Collection — renders its child objects as an ordered list, supports drag-reorder and per-item actions.

- **component** `CollectionSection` Compact list of objects belonging to a collection, used inside sidebars and companion panels.

- **component** `RecordArticle` Schema-driven form/detail view for a single ECHO object rendered in an article slot.

- **component** `RelatedArticle` Companion panel listing objects semantically related to the current subject via ECHO relations.

- **component** `ObjectFormDialog` Modal dialog that lets the user pick a target and a schema type and fill in a new ECHO object.

- **component** `CreateSpaceDialog` Modal dialog for creating a new space with name, icon, colour, and replication options.

- **component** `ImportSpaceDialog` Dialog that accepts a space archive file and imports it as a new space.

- **component** `JoinDialog` Dialog that accepts an invitation code and joins the corresponding space.

- **component** `MembersContainer` Panel showing all members of a space with their presence status and role; allows managing invitations.

- **component** `SpaceSettingsContainer` Settings panel for a single space — name, icon, colour, replication toggle, and member management.

- **component** `SchemaContainer` Browsable table of all registered ECHO schemas in the current space; allows adding new schemas.

- **component** `ViewEditor` Interactive editor for a View — reorder, add, and remove fields; configure field display settings.

- **component** `SpacePresence` Avatar cluster indicating which peers are currently attending the active object/space.

- **component** `SyncStatus` Icon/indicator reflecting the CRDT sync health of the active space.

## Operations

- **op** `SpaceOperation.Create` Creates a new space with the given display properties.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.Join` Joins an existing space by resolving and accepting an invitation code.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.Open` Navigates the layout to the given space.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.Close` Removes the space from the active navigation context.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.Share` Creates an invitation observable for sharing a space; supports single-use and multi-use codes.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.Rename` Opens a rename popover for the given space.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.AddObject` Adds an existing ECHO object to a database or collection and optionally navigates to it.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.RemoveObjects` Removes one or more objects from a collection; returns undo data.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.RestoreObjects` Restores previously removed objects to their collection (inverse of RemoveObjects).

- **op** `SpaceOperation.AddSchema` Registers a new schema type in the space database; optionally makes it visible in the type picker.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.AddRelation` Creates a typed relation between two ECHO objects.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.DeleteField` Removes a field from a View; returns undo data.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.RestoreField` Restores a deleted field to a View at its original index (inverse of DeleteField).

- **op** `SpaceOperation.ImportSpace` Imports a binary space archive as a brand-new space.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.ExportSpace` Serialises a space to an archive and triggers a browser download.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.Snapshot` Captures a point-in-time snapshot of a database or filtered query as a Blob.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.Migrate` Runs registered migrations against a space to bring it to the current schema version.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.Reset` Permanently deletes all objects and truncates feeds in a space via a new epoch.

- **op** `SpaceOperation.GetShareLink` Constructs a shareable URL for a space or specific object; optionally copies it to the clipboard.

- **op** `CollectionOperation.Create` Creates a new Collection object in the active space.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Space Lifecycle
  - `F-1.1` User can create a new space via op:SpaceOperation.Create; the space appears in the navigation graph.
  - `F-1.2` User can join a space via op:SpaceOperation.Join with an invitation code.
  - `F-1.3` User can close/open spaces; closed spaces remain listed with their cached name.
  - `F-1.4` user triggers op:SpaceOperation.Reset → all objects are deleted and a new epoch is created; the operation is unrecoverable

- **feat** `F-2` Membership and Sharing
  - `F-2.1` user triggers op:SpaceOperation.Share → an invitation observable is created; the invitation URL uses the configured shareableLinkOrigin
  - `F-2.2` MembersContainer shows all current members with their presence status.
  - `F-2.3` User can generate single-use or multi-use invitation links.
  - `F-2.4` User can get a direct shareable link to a space or object via op:SpaceOperation.GetShareLink.

- **feat** `F-3` Object Lifecycle
  - `F-3.1` user opens the create-object dialog → all registered schema types are shown for selection
  - `F-3.2` op:SpaceOperation.AddObject adds an object to a collection and fires navigation if navigable.
  - `F-3.3` op:SpaceOperation.RemoveObjects records undo data; op:SpaceOperation.RestoreObjects reverts the removal.
  - `F-3.4` op:SpaceOperation.DuplicateObject creates a shallow copy of an object in the same target.

- **feat** `F-4` Schema Registry
  - `F-4.1` a plugin registers a schema via AppPlugin.addSchemaModule → the type is available globally across all spaces
  - `F-4.2` user triggers op:SpaceOperation.AddSchema → a StoredSchema entry is persisted in the space database
  - `F-4.3` SchemaContainer lists all schemas in the active space; user can add a new user-defined schema.

- **feat** `F-5` Collections
  - `F-5.1` A Collection is an ordered list of references to ECHO objects.
  - `F-5.2` CollectionArticle renders collection contents with drag-to-reorder support.
  - `F-5.3` op:CollectionOperation.Create creates an empty Collection in the active space.
  - `F-5.4` An object's collection ancestry is its canonical location: `resolveCollectionObjectPath`
  - `F-5.5` The plugin's NavigationTargetResolver offers the collection path first, then the type-section

- **feat** `F-6` Persistence and Migrations
  - `F-6.1` client emits SetupMigration → all registered migrations run against every space
  - `F-6.2` user triggers op:SpaceOperation.Migrate → the space is migrated to the specified (or latest) version; returns true if work was done
  - `F-6.3` op:SpaceOperation.ExportSpace serialises a space as a binary archive for backup.
  - `F-6.4` op:SpaceOperation.ImportSpace restores an archive as a new space with optional tags.

- **feat** `F-7` View and Field Editing
  - `F-7.1` op:SpaceOperation.DeleteField removes a field from a View and returns full undo state.
  - `F-7.2` op:SpaceOperation.RestoreField reinstates a deleted field at its original position.
  - `F-7.3` ViewEditor provides an interactive UI for reordering and configuring View fields.

- **feat** `F-8` Presence and Sync Status
  - `F-8.1` SpacePresence tracks which peers are viewing which objects via the attention system.
  - `F-8.2` SyncStatus reflects CRDT sync health; unsynchronised changes are indicated visually.
  - `F-8.3` a peer starts or stops attending an object → viewersByObject and viewersByIdentity maps are updated in ephemeral plugin state

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Create and open a space

- **scenario** `T-2` Join space via invitation

- **scenario** `T-3` Add and remove object with undo

- **scenario** `T-4` Export and import space

- **scenario** `T-5` Schema registration

- **scenario** `T-6` View field delete and restore

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Create a space, add and remove an object — The core space round-trip — create a space, add an object to it, remove it with undo data.

- **test** `QA-2` Register a schema and add a typed relation — Schema-registry and relation round-trip — the machinery plugin-table/plugin-kanban build on.

pages.title: SpotlightPlugin
pages.summary: The Spotlight plugin drives the Tauri popover window that gives users instant keyboard access to Composer commands and navigation from anywhere on the desktop.
pages.content:
The Spotlight plugin drives the Tauri popover window that gives users instant keyboard access to Composer commands and navigation from anywhere on the desktop. It renders the commands dialog as its primary content, intercepts layout operations to forward navigation events to the main window, and dismisses the panel automatically when focus is lost or Escape is pressed.

## Types

- **type** `SpotlightState`

## Components

- **component** `SpotlightLayout` Root layout component for the Tauri spotlight window.

## Operations

- **op** `UpdateDialog` Intercepts the standard LayoutOperation.UpdateDialog.

- **op** `Open` Intercepts LayoutOperation.Open.

- **op** `SwitchWorkspace` Intercepts LayoutOperation.SwitchWorkspace.

- **op** `Close` Intercepts LayoutOperation.Close.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Commands Dialog as Primary Content
  - `F-1.1` the spotlight window opens → SpotlightLayout renders the commands dialog surface (CommandsDialogContent)
  - `F-1.2` the Tauri window gains focus → state is reset to { dialogOpen: true, dialogContent: COMMANDS_DIALOG }

- **feat** `F-2` Auto-Dismiss on Focus Loss and Escape
  - `F-2.1` the spotlight window loses focus → SpotlightDismiss capability calls hide_spotlight immediately
  - `F-2.2` user presses Escape while the spotlight window has focus → SpotlightDismiss capability calls hide_spotlight immediately

- **feat** `F-3` Debounced Dismiss on Dialog Close
  - `F-3.1` UpdateDialog({ state: false }) is received → a 100 ms debounced call to hide_spotlight is scheduled
  - `F-3.2` UpdateDialog({ subject }) arrives before the debounce fires → the pending dismiss is cancelled and dialog content is switched to the new surface

- **feat** `F-4` Navigation Forwarding to Main Window
  - `F-4.1` LayoutOperation.Open is dispatched in the spotlight context → the payload is forwarded to the main window via Tauri event emitTo
  - `F-4.2` LayoutOperation.SwitchWorkspace is dispatched → the workspace change is forwarded to the main window without hiding spotlight
  - `F-4.3` LayoutOperation.UpdateSidebar, UpdateComplementary, UpdatePopover, RevertWorkspace, → these operations are silently ignored (no-ops) in the spotlight context

- **feat** `F-5` Layout State Publication
  - `F-5.1` the spotlight plugin initialises → State capability contributes an AppCapabilities.Layout atom with

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Spotlight opens with commands dialog

- **scenario** `T-2` Escape dismisses spotlight

- **scenario** `T-3` Focus loss dismisses spotlight

- **scenario** `T-4` Debounce prevents premature dismiss

- **scenario** `T-5` Open forwards to main window and hides spotlight

pages.title: StackPlugin
pages.summary: Collections plugin for `DXOS` Composer — renders any `Collection` object as a vertically scrollable stack of collapsible sections, where each section displays an arbitrary ECHO object via the `section` surface role.
pages.content:
Collections plugin for `DXOS` Composer — renders any `Collection` object as a vertically scrollable stack of collapsible sections, where each section displays an arbitrary ECHO object via the `section` surface role. Supports adding, removing, navigating, and collapsing individual sections.

## Types

- **type** `StackSectionItem`

- **type** `AddSectionPosition`

- **type** `StackSettingsProps`

## Components

- **component** `StackArticle` Full-page article view of a Collection — renders items as a vertical stack of StackSection components with a toolbar for adding sections.

- **component** `StackSection` A single collapsible section in the stack — shows a sigil icon button with a dropdown menu and delegates content rendering to the section surface slot.

- **component** `StackSettings` Settings panel for configuring stack-level display preferences such as section separation.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Stack Rendering
  - `F-1.1` StackPlugin registers a surface for the article role filtered to Collection objects.
  - `F-1.2` StackArticle renders each item in the collection as a StackSection in document order.
  - `F-1.3` Each StackSection title is derived from the object's title property or graph node label.
  - `F-1.4` The icon displayed on the section sigil is taken from the object schema's IconAnnotation.

- **feat** `F-2` Section Management
  - `F-2.1` user clicks the Add Section button in the toolbar → SpaceOperation.OpenObjectForm dialog is invoked with the collection as target
  - `F-2.2` user selects "Add Before" or "Add After" from a section dropdown → LayoutOperation.UpdateDialog is invoked with the AddSectionDialog, position, and collection context
  - `F-2.3` user selects "Remove" from a section dropdown → SpaceOperation.RemoveObjects is invoked; section is removed from the collection
  - `F-2.4` user selects "Navigate to" from a collapsed section dropdown or the navigate button → LayoutOperation.Open is invoked with the section's id

- **feat** `F-3` Collapse / Expand
  - `F-3.1` Each section can be individually collapsed via the dropdown menu or caret trigger.
  - `F-3.2` section is expanded → full Surface:section content is visible; navigate button shown in heading
  - `F-3.3` section is collapsed → only the title is shown in StackItem.Content; expand toggle shown in heading
  - `F-3.4` Collapsed state is managed locally in StackArticle component state (not persisted).

- **feat** `F-4` Settings
  - `F-4.1` StackPlugin exposes a settings panel via the StackSettings component.
  - `F-4.2` The separation setting controls whether visual separators appear between sections.

- **feat** `F-5` Schema Registration
  - `F-5.1` StackPlugin registers StackViewType with the ECHO schema module on activation.
  - `F-5.2` StackViewType stores per-section metadata (height, custom data) keyed by object id.

pages.title: StreamDeckPlugin
pages.summary: Projects a Composer space onto Stream Deck hardware: the space's favorites on the keys, running tasks or space statistics on the dials.
pages.content:
Projects a Composer space onto Stream Deck hardware: the space's favorites on the keys, running tasks or space statistics on the dials.

The device itself is driven by a separate Elgato plugin (`@dxos/composer-stream-deck`), because Elgato's application holds the HID device exclusively while it runs. This plugin is the brain: it builds the model from ECHO, renders every key as an SVG string, and publishes frames over a loopback WebSocket. Design: `agents/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-stream-deck-design.md`.

## Types

- **type** `DeviceProfile` Physical characteristics of a Stream Deck model, reported by the device plugin.

- **type** `Shortcut` What one key shows.

- **type** `MetricSpec` What one touch-strip segment shows — a running task, or a statistic when nothing is running.

- **type** `SpaceStats`

- **type** `KeyImage` One rendered key on the wire.

- **type** `DialFeedback` One touch-strip segment on the wire, expressed semantically rather than as an Elgato layout.

- **type** `Frame` The full display state.

- **type** `BridgeStatus` Live connection state, published so surfaces can read it without opening a connection.

## Components

- **component** `VirtualStreamDeck` On-screen replica rendering the very frame the device is sent, so the two cannot drift.

- **component** `StreamDeckStatus` Rail indicator, rendered only while a device is attached.

- **component** `StreamDeckDashboard` Space-level deck companion previewing the hardware; renders the frame but does not send it.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Favorites on the keys
  - `F-1.1` A key shows an object carrying the space's `favorite` ECHO tag, with its icon and name.
  - `F-1.2` The favorite tag is resolved by label among keyless tags; a keyed provider tag labelled
  - `F-1.3` Slots are filled from a stable sort (label, then path); positions are not persisted.
  - `F-1.4` A favorite with no derivable navigation path is dropped rather than shown as a dead key.
  - `F-1.5` Pressing a key opens that object and brings the window forward.

- **feat** `F-2` Monitors and statistics on the dials

pages.title: SupportPlugin
pages.summary: Composer's user-facing assistance plugin.
pages.content:
Composer's user-facing assistance plugin. Covers two paths:

1. **Conversational support** — users open a `Ticket` from the navtree and the AI assistant collaborates on diagnosing the issue, searching documentation, and recording the resolution. Tickets are ECHO objects so a conversation is local-first, replicable to other devices, and reviewable by a human supporter later.
2. **One-shot feedback** — users send anonymous feedback (with optional debug logs) to the observability backend via the deck `--help` companion. This replaces the same surface previously owned by plugin-observability and keeps the telemetry plugin focused on instrumentation only.
3. **GitHub issue submission** — same form, optional third action: file a structured bug/feature request against the upstream repo. When the user has authenticated the GitHub integration (via plugin-connector) the issue is filed as them via the GitHub API; otherwise we open a prefilled `issues/new` URL in a new tab so the user can finish the submission in their own browser session.

A future iteration will absorb plugin-help (welcome tour, contextual hints, keyboard shortcuts) so all user education lives here.

Initial scope is a thin skeleton: a `Ticket` schema, four ticket operations wired to a skill, a `FeedbackForm` + `submitReport` operation, and two surfaces (`Ticket` article + `--help` companion). Documentation search and issue filing are stubbed — the skill exists so the assistant can be exercised end-to-end while the integrations land in later phases.

## Types

- **type** `TicketStatus`

- **type** `Ticket` A user-reported support ticket.

- **type** `IssueType`

- **type** `Severity`

- **type** `SupportRequest` Form payload submitted from the help companion.

## Components

- **component** `SupportArticle` Article surface bound to a Ticket.

## Operations

- **op** `createTicket` Creates a new Ticket in the active space.

- **op** `markInProgress` Marks a Ticket as in progress (active investigation).

- **op** `resolveTicket` Marks a Ticket as resolved with optional resolution notes.

- **op** `searchDocs` Searches Composer / DXOS documentation for the given query and returns a list of excerpts.

- **op** `submitIssue` Files a report straight to Linear through the support service's `/issue` route: no PostHog ticket, no Discord thread.
- **op** `submitReport` Files a user report through the support service (discord-service on EDGE), which creates the PostHog support ticket anchoring the report's telemetry, notes where the debug logs went, and opens the public Discord help th…

GitHub issue submission is performed inline by the FeedbackPanel — it queries the user's personal space for an `AccessToken` with source `github.com`, POSTs to the GitHub API if found, and falls back to opening a prefilled `issues/new` URL otherwise. No dedicated operation is exposed in this phase; if AI / CLI invocation is needed later, add one wrapping the same flow.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Ticket Lifecycle
  - `F-1.1` User can create a Ticket from the AI assistant or directly via the navtree.
  - `F-1.2` a Ticket is created → status === open; resolution unset.
  - `F-1.3` assistant or user calls markInProgress → status === in_progress.
  - `F-1.4` assistant or user calls resolveTicket → status === resolved; resolution recorded (if provided).
  - `F-1.5` Ticket title and body are editable in SupportArticle.
  - `F-1.6` user clicks Reopen on a resolved Ticket in SupportArticle → status === open (UI-driven; no dedicated op).

- **feat** `F-2` AI Support Assistant
  - `F-2.1` A skill is registered with key org.dxos.skill.support.
  - `F-2.2` Skill tools include createTicket, markInProgress, resolveTicket, searchDocs.
  - `F-2.3` a Ticket is the active object → the support skill is bound to the chat companion surface.
  - `F-2.4` The assistant is instructed to gather details, search docs, and only resolve when the user confirms.

- **feat** `F-3` Documentation Search
  - `F-3.1` searchDocs operation is defined with a query input.
  - `F-3.2` assistant calls searchDocs → zero or more {title,url,excerpt} results are returned.
  - `F-3.3` Initial implementation returns a small in-memory set; replaceable without changing the schema.

- **feat** `F-4` One-shot Feedback
  - `F-4.1` plugin-support contributes the deck `--help` companion surface; it renders a FeedbackForm.
  - `F-4.2` user submits the FeedbackForm → submitReport files the PostHog ticket, then the ticket id anchors the public Discord thread.
  - `F-4.3` feedback succeeds → a confirmation toast is shown and the companion collapses.
  - `F-4.4` When the LogDownloader capability is contributed, a "Download logs" action is offered alongside the form.
  - `F-4.5` the Observability capability reports feedback is unavailable → the submit button is disabled.

- **feat** `F-5` GitHub Issue Submission
  - `F-5.1` FeedbackForm exposes type (bug/feature), severity, title, body, and area (optional plugin) alongside the existing submit + Discord actions.
  - `F-5.2` The form auto-populates and submits a hidden `version` field (app build) without rendering it as an input.
  - `F-5.3` The area select is populated from the runtime plugin list (plugin id + name); empty selection is allowed.
  - `F-5.4` user clicks "Create GitHub issue" → submitGitHubIssue is invoked with the form values.
  - `F-5.5` an AccessToken with source `github.com` is present in the active space → the issue is POSTed to the GitHub API; the response URL is opened in a new tab and a success toast is shown.
  - `F-5.6` no GitHub AccessToken is present → a prefilled `issues/new` URL is opened in a new tab; the user finishes the submission manually.
  - `F-5.7` type maps to GitHub's Issue Type field via `?type=Bug` / `?type=Feature`; severity is emitted as a label whose name matches the literal (e.g.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Create a ticket

- **scenario** `T-2` Resolve a ticket

- **scenario** `T-3` SupportArticle renders ticket

- **scenario** `T-4` Resolve button updates status

- **scenario** `T-5` Mark in progress

- **scenario** `T-6` Reopen a resolved ticket

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Create a support ticket and resolve it — The core ticket lifecycle round-trip — create, mark in progress, resolve, read back.

- **test** `QA-2` Send one-shot feedback via the help companion — The `--help` companion's PostHog feedback path — no ECHO object is created.

pages.title: TerraPlugin
pages.summary: A deterministic 3D planet plugin for `DXOS` Composer, rendering seed-driven stylized worlds with `Babylon.js`.
pages.content:
A deterministic 3D planet plugin for `DXOS` Composer, rendering seed-driven stylized worlds with `Babylon.js`. The same seed and configuration always produce the same land, water, and biome layout, so planets are fully reproducible and shareable by seed plus configuration.

Terrain is generated procedurally — elevation and biome placement derive from layered simplex noise seeded via `seedrandom` — and rendered as a stylized low-poly sphere with distinct land, water, and biome coloring.

Live parameters (seed, water level, elevation and mountain scale, tree density, resolution) let users reshape the planet in real-time from a config panel without leaving Composer. Biomes are assigned from elevation and latitude, and trees/rocks are scattered across land using thin instances for cheap rendering at scale.

## QA

pages.content:
A collaborative whiteboard plugin for `DXOS` Composer — powered by tldraw, persisted in ECHO, and available as a first-class workspace object.

## Types

- **type** `Canvas` Low-level drawing document backed by a tldraw store.

- **type** `Sketch` User-facing whiteboard object that wraps a Canvas.

- **type** `SketchGrid`

- **type** `Settings`

- **type** `Scene` Backend-neutral scene DSL (src/model).

- **type** `WorldObject`

- **type** `Command` Scene edit commands (D2-Oracle-style, addressed by id).

## Components

- **component** `SketchArticle` Full-screen whiteboard surface for a Sketch object.

- **component** `SketchSettings` Settings panel for the Sketch plugin — controls grid visibility and type.

## Operations

> **Architecture has moved since this section was written.** `plugin-tldraw` no longer owns a
> `Sketch`/`Canvas` type or a `createSketch`/`readSketch`/`editSketch` operation — there is no
> `operations/` directory and no `Sketch` class in `src/` at all. Tldraw is now a **render/create
> variant** contributed to `plugin-illustrator`'s `Drawing` type
> (`src/capabilities/drawing-variant.ts`, `IllustratorCapabilities.VariantProvider`, id
> `tldraw.com/2`) — `TldrawArticle`/`TldrawCard` render a `Drawing.Canvas` whose `schema` is
> `tldraw.com/2`, and the Scene DSL create/read/edit operations documented below actually live in
> `@dxos/plugin-illustrator` (`org.dxos.operation.illustrator.{create,read,edit}`), invoked with
> `variant: 'tldraw.com/2'` to select this plugin's renderer. The type/component sections above
> (`Canvas`, `Sketch`, `Scene`, `WorldObject`, `Command`) and F-7/F-8 below describe the DSL
> correctly in spirit but attribute it to the wrong plugin; QA-1/QA-2 below invoke the real keys.

- **op** `createSketch` Owned by plugin-illustrator, not this plugin (see note above).

- **op** `readSketch` Owned by plugin-illustrator (see note above).

- **op** `editSketch` Owned by plugin-illustrator (see note above).

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Whiteboard Canvas
  - `F-1.1` Each Sketch owns exactly one Canvas; the Canvas holds the full tldraw store snapshot.
  - `F-1.2` Canvas content is stored as a plain record in ECHO — no binary blobs.
  - `F-1.3` All tldraw shape types (freehand, geometric, text, arrow, image) are supported.

- **feat** `F-2` ECHO Persistence
  - `F-2.1` user makes any edit in the whiteboard → Canvas.content is updated in ECHO within the debounce window
  - `F-2.2` Sketch is opened after a page reload → tldraw store is hydrated from Canvas.content; no drawing is lost
  - `F-2.3` Canvas is a separate ECHO object from Sketch so it can be replicated independently.

- **feat** `F-3` Real-time Collaboration
  - `F-3.1` two or more peers open the same Sketch → edits by each peer appear on the other's canvas via ECHO replication
  - `F-3.2` a peer is offline and makes edits → changes merge with remote state on reconnection using ECHO CRDT semantics

- **feat** `F-4` Roles and Presentation
  - `F-4.1` role is article → full tldraw toolbar shown when the sketch has attention; hidden otherwise
  - `F-4.2` role is slide → canvas is read-only; zoom capped at 1.5×
  - `F-4.3` role is section → canvas auto-zooms to fit content; no toolbar shown

- **feat** `F-5` Comment Threads
  - `F-5.1` user activates the thread tool in the toolbar → a new comment thread is created anchored to the current selection
  - `F-5.2` Thread anchor positions are stored alongside the drawing so they survive reloads.

- **feat** `F-6` Grid Settings
  - `F-6.1` Settings.showGrid is true → a background grid rendered beneath drawing content
  - `F-6.2` Settings.gridType is mesh → a square-mesh grid is shown
  - `F-6.3` Settings.gridType is dotted → a dotted grid is shown

  - `F-7.1` Plugin contributes op:createSketch to the operation registry.
  - `F-7.2` op:createSketch is invoked → a Sketch + Canvas pair is created and returned; the Sketch is added to the target collection

- **feat** `F-8` Scene DSL and Agent Skill
  - `F-8.1` The scene model (src/model) is backend-neutral — no tldraw imports in scene.ts;
  - `F-8.2` Every DSL-generated tldraw record carries meta { object, element, kind, scale, dialect };
  - `F-8.3` op:editSketch upserts elements of an existing object → only records with matching element ids are replaced; sibling elements are untouched
  - `F-8.4` a shape bound by an arrow is removed → its bindings are removed too; no dangling binding records remain
  - `F-8.5` op:readSketch runs after a user drags shapes in the UI → the derived scene reflects the moved geometry (origin = bbox top-left)
  - `F-8.6` Plugin contributes the org.dxos.skill.sketch skill (create/read/edit tools +
  - `F-8.7` A dialect registry (scene only for now) reserves the extension point for

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-3` Collaborative edit
