Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number. Tldraw is enabled by default in every environment (`plugin-defs.tsx` `getDefaults`).

- **test** `QA-1` Create a tldraw sketch and draw on it — The core whiteboard round-trip — create a Drawing bound to the tldraw variant, draw, reload.

- **test** `QA-2` Scene DSL round-trip — draw a face, then add a hat without redrawing it — The agent-facing DSL path (F-8 / T-7): create, read, and edit a scene addressed by semantic object ids, verifying an edit to one world object leaves siblings untouched.
- **test** `QA-3` Showcase clip — The 10s showcase clip: Draw a few shapes in tldraw.

pages.title: TranscriptionPlugin
pages.summary: A real-time voice-to-text transcription plugin for DXOS Composer.
pages.content:
A real-time voice-to-text transcription plugin for DXOS Composer. Captures spoken audio from a microphone, converts it to timestamped text segments via the Whisper speech-recognition service, and stores the results in an ECHO `Transcript` object backed by a `Feed`. The plugin also exposes skill-compatible operations that let AI assistants open and summarize transcripts inside agent workflows.

## Types

- **type** `TranscriptSegment`

- **type** `Message`

- **type** `Transcript`

- **type** `WhisperWord`

- **type** `WhisperSegment`

- **type** `Settings`

## Components

- **component** `Transcription` Read-only CodeMirror editor that renders transcript messages as Markdown with byline headings.

- **component** `Oracle` Ambient display surface with an SVG graph canvas and a centered text overlay.

- **component** `TranscriptionArticle` Full-page article panel combining the Transcription editor with a start/stop recording toolbar action.

## Operations

Pure operations — no side-effects.

- **op** `openTranscript` Loads a Transcript from ECHO, reads all Messages from its Feed, and returns the full text content rendered with speaker bylines.

Effectful operations — produce output via AI or mutate persistent state.

- **op** `createTranscript` Creates a new Feed and a Transcript object linked to it, then writes both into the current ECHO space.

- **op** `summarizeTranscript` Sends a transcript string and optional participant notes to an LLM and returns a Markdown summary with key points, verbatim quotes, and actionable tasks extracted from the conversation.

- **op** `enrichMessage` Extracts proper nouns from each transcript block of a Message using a small LLM, full-text-searches the space for matching objects, and rewrites the text with inline `[noun](https://github.com/dxos/dxos/blob/main/packages/plugins/plugin-transcription/dxn)` reference links.

- **op** `normalizeSentences` Post-processes an array of raw transcript messages, merging word-level tokens into grammatically complete sentences.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Recording Lifecycle
  - `F-1.1` User can start microphone capture from TranscriptionArticle toolbar.
  - `F-1.2` User can stop microphone capture; final buffered chunks are flushed and transcribed.
  - `F-1.3` TranscriptionManager restarts the Transcriber automatically when the audio track changes.

- **feat** `F-2` Audio Chunking and Transcription
  - `F-2.1` user is speaking and chunk count reaches transcribeAfterChunksAmount → Transcriber schedules a deferred transcription task
  - `F-2.2` transcription task runs → buffered PCM chunks are merged into a WAV file and POSTed to the Whisper endpoint
  - `F-2.3` Whisper response is received → segments are filtered by no_speech_prob and aligned to absolute wall-clock timestamps
  - `F-2.4` user is not speaking → only prefixBufferChunksAmount most-recent chunks are retained; older chunks discarded

- **feat** `F-3` Transcript Persistence
  - `F-3.1` aligned segments are produced → a Message object with the segments is appended to the Transcript's ECHO Feed
  - `F-3.2` a messageEnricher is configured → Message is passed through the enricher before being written to the Feed
  - `F-3.3` a peer's ECHO space receives the Feed update → TranscriptionArticle re-renders with the new messages

- **feat** `F-4` Transcript Display
  - `F-4.1` a Transcript object is opened → all Messages are rendered in the Transcription editor with speaker bylines and timestamps
  - `F-4.2` new messages arrive during live recording → the TranscriptModel is updated and the editor scrolls to show the latest content

- **feat** `F-5` AI Summary
  - `F-5.1` op:summarizeTranscript is invoked → LLM returns a structured Markdown document with key points, quotes, and tasks
  - `F-5.2` participant notes are provided → notes are correlated with transcript content in the summary
  - `F-5.3` no actionable tasks are found → the tasks section is omitted from the summary

- **feat** `F-6` Skill Integration
  - `F-6.1` Skill exposes op:openTranscript and op:summarizeTranscript as AI tools.
  - `F-6.2` An AI assistant can open a transcript by Ref and return formatted text to the user.
  - `F-6.3` An AI assistant can invoke the summary operation and present the result as a message.

- **feat** `F-7` On-device Streaming Transcription (Whistle story)
  - `F-7.1` the user presses Record, or holds Space outside a text field → the microphone streams into Whistle in a worker as one stream, re-decoded after every pass interval of new audio; nothing leaves the tab
  - `F-7.2` two consecutive passes agree on a word → the word is committed; the unconfirmed tail is shown in italics after the last paragraph
  - `F-7.3` The pass interval is 1 s, as in Cactus's demo; Low latency makes it 200 ms, which commits sooner but agrees on half-heard words more often.
  - `F-7.4` the audio holds 1.5 s of silence or more between two committed words, or the stream stops → a new paragraph starts; silence is measured in the audio against the noise floor, not between the model's word times
  - `F-7.5` Without a pause, a paragraph closes at the first sentence end after 30 words.
  - `F-7.6` Keywords bias recognition from the next pass; the list is prefilled with DXOS terms.
  - `F-7.7` The whole recording stays in the tab; each paragraph can be played back or saved as WAV, and so can the whole recording.
  - `F-7.8` The engine and model download on first use only and are kept in Cache Storage; mounting the story downloads nothing.
  - `F-7.9` After first use the microphone stays open, so push-to-talk does not clip the first word.
  - `F-7.10` the audio holds no sound louder than -35 dBFS for 0.15 s → no stream is opened and nothing is decoded, so Whistle cannot invent words in silence or room tone; the last 0.5 s before sound is kept so the first word is hea…

- **feat** `F-8` On-device Voice Home Assistant (Home story)
  - `F-8.1` the user holds Space, or toggles Talk, and says a request such as "turn on the kitchen lights" → Whistle transcribes it as it is spoken, and Needle 3, loaded into the same engine and worker, answers it against five home…
  - `F-8.2` The tools are set_lights, set_thermostat, operate_door, set_blinds and play_music; each call changes a mock home drawn as a floor plan, and the rooms it touched are highlighted.
  - `F-8.3` a request ends → it is answered from the stream's committed words and its latest unconfirmed tail, before the stream's closing pass; audio after a pass that already heard 0.15 s of silence is not decoded again
  - `F-8.4` Low latency (on by default) caps the answer at 32 tokens, which skips the model's reasoning line; a request that joins actions with "and", "then" or "also" keeps the 128-token budget so every call survives.
  - `F-8.5` Hands-free is on and the microphone is open → a request ends after 0.7 s of silence following speech (0.5 s in Low latency), found in the audio as it reaches the worker, and capture continues into the next request
  - `F-8.10` Silence is handled in the worker, in audio time: passes pause once the stream has heard 0.15 s of silence, and a stream that hears nothing for 1 s is ended at the next silence, so each request's stream holds little more…
  - `F-8.6` the model withholds a call (suppressed_calls) → it is offered as "Did you mean …?" and runs only when the user confirms it
  - `F-8.7` no tool serves the request → the log says so and nothing changes
  - `F-8.8` Each command in the log shows its transcript, what changed, the calls, the time from the end of the request to the answer, and the model's time and confidence.
  - `F-8.9` Call arguments are checked against the home before they apply; an argument outside the schema is an error in the log, never a change.

- **feat** `F-9` Audio Tooling and Evals
  - `F-9.1` The audio-view skill describes a recording's levels and speech/silence timeline as text, draws a labelled spectrogram, and replays it through the pinned Whistle engine in Node exactly as the story streams it.
  - `F-9.2` Recordings with real voices are private fixtures in the encrypted test-fixtures bucket, never in git; the agents scope holds whistle-silence, whistle-one-two-three, whistle-echo-query-a and whistle-echo-query-b.
  - `F-9.3` the manual Whistle evals run and a fixture is present → each recording is replayed through the story's silence gate and its word error rate against the expected transcript, the words committed during silence and keyword…
  - `F-9.4` A compare script runs one recording through larger hosted models (OpenAI whisper-1 and gpt-4o-transcribe, Cloudflare Workers AI whisper-large-v3-turbo), skips a provider without credentials, and prints the transcripts s…

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Create transcript

- **scenario** `T-2` Record and persist segment

- **scenario** `T-3` Deduplicate segments across chunk boundaries

- **scenario** `T-4` Open transcript

- **scenario** `T-5` Summarize transcript

- **scenario** `T-6` Sentence normalization is pure

- **scenario** `T-7` Toggle recording in UI

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number. Transcription is enabled by default in every environment (`plugin-defs.tsx` `getDefaults`).

- **test** `QA-1` Create a transcript and read it back — The ECHO round-trip that does not require a live microphone or Whisper endpoint — create a Transcript, and read its (empty) content back via op:openTranscript.

- **test** `QA-2` Record, transcribe, and summarize a meeting — The full audio round-trip — start recording, speak, stop, and summarize what was said.

pages.title: TransformerPlugin
pages.summary: A browser-based machine learning plugin for DXOS Composer that runs Hugging Face Transformers.js models entirely in-browser via WebAssembly and WebGPU.
pages.content:
A browser-based machine learning plugin for DXOS Composer that runs Hugging Face Transformers.js models entirely in-browser via WebAssembly and WebGPU. It provides automatic speech recognition (Whisper) through a React hook and component layer, enabling real-time voice transcription without any server-side inference infrastructure.

## Types

- **type** `PipelineConfig`

- **type** `PipelineState`

- **type** `AudioStreamConfig`

- **type** `AudioStreamState`

- **type** `TranscriptionOptions`

- **type** `EmbeddingOutput`

## Components

- **component** `Voice` Composite component that wires usePipeline and useAudioStream together to provide live Whisper transcription from the microphone.

## Operations

- **op** `LoadModel` Loads a Transformers.js automatic-speech-recognition pipeline for the given model id.

- **op** `Transcribe` Runs the loaded ASR pipeline against a Float32Array of 16 kHz mono audio.

- **op** `CaptureAudio` Requests microphone permission via getUserMedia and wires an AudioWorklet that accumulates 2-second chunks (32000 samples at 16 kHz) before forwarding them to the onAudioData callback.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` In-Browser ASR Pipeline
  - `F-1.1` Voice component mounts with active = true → usePipeline loads the Whisper model via Transformers.js; isLoading is true until complete
  - `F-1.2` WebGPU is available in the browser → the ONNX backend is configured for WebGPU execution and gpuInfo reflects the adapter
  - `F-1.3` WebGPU is not available → the pipeline falls back to WASM/CPU and gpuInfo is set to a 'not supported' message
  - `F-1.4` model loading fails → PipelineState.error contains a human-readable message; isLoading is false

- **feat** `F-2` Microphone Capture
  - `F-2.1` useAudioStream is activated → getUserMedia is called with mono 16 kHz audio and echo/noise cancellation enabled
  - `F-2.2` audio is captured → an AudioWorklet accumulates samples and emits 2-second chunks via the onAudioData callback
  - `F-2.3` active is set to false or the component unmounts → all MediaStream tracks are stopped, AudioContext is closed, and AnimationFrame is cancelled
  - `F-2.4` getUserMedia is denied → AudioStreamState.error is set with the underlying error message

- **feat** `F-3` Live Transcription
  - `F-3.1` a 2-second audio chunk arrives and the model is loaded → usePipeline.transcribe is called with 16 kHz mono options and the result appended to the transcript
  - `F-3.2` transcription is already in progress (isTranscribing = true) → the incoming audio chunk is dropped to avoid concurrent inference
  - `F-3.3` transcription returns an empty or whitespace-only string → the transcript state is not updated

- **feat** `F-4` RAG Embedding Pipeline (Testing)
  - `F-4.1` RagPipeline.generateCompletions is called with an input and a knowledge base → embeddings are generated for both the input and each knowledge-base entry
  - `F-4.2` embeddings are available → cosine similarity is computed and the top-3 most similar contexts are selected

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Model loads and transitions isLoaded

- **scenario** `T-2` Model load failure sets error state

- **scenario** `T-3` Microphone capture populates stream state

- **scenario** `T-4` Audio chunk triggers transcription

- **scenario** `T-5` Concurrent transcription calls are dropped

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Load the Whisper model and transcribe from the microphone — plugin-transformer has no user-visible surface at all: it is not wired into `plugin-defs.tsx` (searched — no import, no `.make()` call anywhere under `packages/apps/composer-app/src`), it contributes no ECHO type and no…

---

pages.title: TrelloPlugin
pages.summary: Integrates Trello into DXOS Composer, mirroring boards and cards as local-first Kanban objects that stay available alongside everything else in the workspace.
pages.content:
Integrates Trello into DXOS Composer, mirroring boards and cards as local-first Kanban objects that stay available alongside everything else in the workspace.

The plugin bridges the Trello REST API with ECHO's object graph using a snapshot-driven three-way merge: remote edits to untouched fields flow in, local edits to untouched fields flow out, and when both sides change a field the remote wins. Every board the user selects is materialized as a `Kanban` object keyed by its Trello board id; individual cards become `Expando` objects inside the Kanban's `items` array.

Credentials are stored as a colon-separated `apiKey:userToken` string in an `AccessToken` object inside the user's `Integration`. The OAuth callback in the companion `kms-service` writes this format so the plugin stays self-contained and no runtime environment variable is required.

Sync is bidirectional (pull then push) per board. Newly-created local cards without a Trello foreign key are pushed with `POST /cards`. Locally-edited fields that diverge from the last-pull snapshot are pushed with `PUT /cards/{id}`. Board creation and board-rename push are not yet implemented in v1.

## Types

- **type** `TrelloMember`

- **type** `TrelloBoard`

- **type** `TrelloList`

- **type** `TrelloCard` string

- **type** `SyncTarget`

- **type** `PullResult`

- **type** `PushResult`

## Operations

- **op** `GetTrelloBoards` Discovery only — list Trello boards reachable from the integration's token.

- **op** `SyncTrelloBoard` Bidirectional reconcile of currently-selected Trello targets in an Integration.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Discover Boards
  - `F-1.1` user opens the integration target picker → op:GetTrelloBoards lists every open board on the token; no local object is created

- **feat** `F-2` Materialize Board
  - `F-2.1` SyncTrelloBoard runs for the first time against a selected target → a Kanban is created in ECHO keyed by the remote board id;

- **feat** `F-3` Pull Cards
  - `F-3.1` a card exists on Trello but not locally → an Expando is created with the Trello foreign key; name, desc, listName seeded from remote
  - `F-3.2` a card exists both locally and on Trello → three-way merge applied per field (name, desc, listName);
  - `F-3.3` a card is closed on Trello or absent from the response → the local Expando is soft-deleted; its ref in kanban.spec.items is preserved
  - `F-3.4` pull completes → kanban.arrangement.order reflects Trello list order sorted by pos

- **feat** `F-4` Push Cards
  - `F-4.1` a local Expando has no Trello foreign key and belongs to a named list → POST /cards creates the card on Trello; foreign key written back; snapshot seeded
  - `F-4.2` a local Expando with a foreign key has fields diverged from snapshot → PUT /cards/{id} sends only the diverged fields (name, desc, idList)
  - `F-4.3` a locally soft-deleted card is encountered during push → card is skipped; no Trello API call is made

- **feat** `F-5` Authentication
  - `F-5.1` plugin initializes an API call → TrelloCredentials service is resolved from the Integration's AccessToken;

- **feat** `F-6` Resilience
  - `F-6.1` an HTTP request fails with a 429 or 5xx status → exponential back-off retry with jitter, up to 3 attempts
  - `F-6.2` a request fails with a 4xx status (excluding 429) → no retry; error propagated immediately
  - `F-6.3` a sync target fails → lastError recorded on that target; remaining targets continue

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Discover boards — no local side effects

- **scenario** `T-2` First sync materializes Kanban

- **scenario** `T-3` Pull creates new card

- **scenario** `T-4` Pull applies three-way merge

- **scenario** `T-5` Pull soft-deletes removed card

- **scenario** `T-6` Push creates locally-created card

- **scenario** `T-7` Push updates diverged fields

- **scenario** `T-8` Invalid token fails fast

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Connect Trello, materialize a board, and sync it — The core Trello round-trip — discover boards, materialize one as a local Kanban, then reconcile cards.

---

pages.title: TripPlugin
pages.summary: A Composer plugin for managing travel itineraries.
pages.content:
A Composer plugin for managing travel itineraries. A `Trip` is an ordered list of typed `Segment`s (Flight, Train, Boat, Road, Lodging, Activity), each of which may be associated with a `Booking` (the actual ticket / reservation). Trips can be browsed individually or in aggregate via existing Table and Map views, presented as Articles, or embedded as surfaces inside Markdown documents.

Phase 1 shipped the data model, `TripArticle` surface (with a calendar mini-view and `SegmentStack`), `SegmentArticle` companion surface, and plugin wiring.

Phase 2 (this milestone) adds inbox integration: a generic `MessageExtractor` contract in plugin-inbox plus a `TravelMessageExtractor` impl in plugin-trip that converts confirmation emails into `Booking`s + `Segment`s and attaches them to a Trip.

Planned cross-plugin integrations (follow-up phases):

- A `TripCalendarSource` that plugs into plugin-inbox's `CalendarEventSource` contract to project `Segment`s as calendar events, so trips render directly on the calendar without a dual write to materialised events.

Future work (deferred from v1):

- `SegmentRequest` — a "desired multi-leg travel" shape that feeds a search provider and produces candidate `Segment`s + `Booking`s.
- A `BookingFor` ECHO relation linking `Booking` → `Trip` (queries currently reach bookings via `Trip.segments[].booking`).

## Cross-package additions

Some types and contracts referenced here are added outside `plugin-trip` because they are generally useful:

| Symbol                | Package                | Notes                                                                                              |
| --------------------- | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Provider`            | `@dxos/types`          | New plain `Schema.Struct`. Parallel to `Actor`. Used wherever a third-party service is referenced. |
| `Account`             | `@dxos/types`          | New ECHO object (`org.dxos.type.account`). Loyalty / membership accounts at providers.             |
| `MessageExtractor`    | `plugin-inbox`         | New generic contract. plugin-trip registers `TravelMessageExtractor`.                              |
| `ExtractedFrom`       | `plugin-inbox`         | New ECHO relation. Source = extracted object, target = source `Message`.                           |
| `CalendarEventSource` | `plugin-inbox`         | New generic contract. plugin-trip registers `TripCalendarSource`.                                  |
| `CalendarEventLike`   | `plugin-inbox`         | Uniform projection shape returned by `CalendarEventSource` impls.                                  |

## Types

### Existing types used by this plugin

| Type           | Source                  | Typename                       | Role                                                  |
| -------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `Organization` | `@dxos/types`           | `org.dxos.type.organization`   | Optional rich link target for `Provider.ref`.         |
| `Person`       | `@dxos/types`           | `org.dxos.type.person`         | Optional link for passengers on a `Booking`.          |
| `File`         | `@dxos/types`           | `org.dxos.type.file`           | Attachment target for booking PDFs / e-tickets.       |
| `GeoPoint`     | `@dxos/echo` (`Format`) | (system)                       | Optional geometry on `Place`.                         |
| `DateTime`     | `@dxos/echo` (`Format`) | (system)                       | Used for `departAt`, `arriveAt`, `checkIn`, etc.      |
| `Hostname`     | `@dxos/echo` (`Format`) | (system)                       | Used for `Provider.domain`.                           |

### New shared types (added to `@dxos/types`)

- **type** `Provider` Reference to an external service or company — airline, hotel chain, rail operator, ticketing platform, etc.

- **type** `Account` A user's account / membership with an external service.

### New plugin-trip types

- **type** `Place` Generic location shape used as origin / destination on every Segment.

- **type** `SegmentCore` Shared fields present on every Segment variant.

- **type** `FlightSegment` Air travel leg.

- **type** `TrainSegment` Rail travel leg.

- **type** `BoatSegment` Water travel leg.

- **type** `RoadSegment` Road travel leg.

- **type** `LodgingSegment` Accommodation — a "stationary" segment.

- **type** `ActivitySegment` Tour, dinner reservation, ticketed event, etc.

- **type** `Segment` Tagged union of all segment variants.

- **type** `Trip` Itinerary container.

- **type** `Booking` A purchased ticket / reservation.

## Contracts consumed (new in plugin-inbox)

These are generic — defined in plugin-inbox so any plugin can implement them. plugin-trip provides one impl of each. The `MessageExtractor` contract and `ExtractedFrom` relation ship as part of Phase 2 alongside `TravelMessageExtractor`; `CalendarEventSource` is described here for context but is a follow-up phase.

- **type** `MessageExtractor` Pluggable handler invoked by plugin-inbox on Messages.

- **type** `MatchResult`
- **type** `ExtractCtx`
- **type** `ExtractResult`

- **type** `ExtractedFrom` ECHO relation.

- **type** `MailboxExtractorConfig` Optional Mailbox-level config for the auto-on-arrival dispatch mode.

- **type** `CalendarEventSource` Pluggable contract used by calendar views.

- **type** `CalendarEventLike` Uniform shape returned by CalendarEventSource implementations.

### Inbox dispatch modes

plugin-inbox supports three dispatch modes for `MessageExtractor`s. All three ship in Phase 2.

- **manual** — user picks an extractor from a message action menu on an opened message. Always available; the menu lists every registered extractor whose `match()` returned `matched: true` for the message. Implemented as a `MessageActions` surface in plugin-inbox that queries the `MessageExtractor` capability registry.
- **agent-assisted** — the `ExtractMessage` operation is exposed as a tool via the inbox skill's `toolDefinitions`. The agent invokes it with `{ message, extractorId?, target? }`; when `extractorId` is omitted, the operation picks the highest-confidence match.
- **auto-on-arrival** — gated by `Mailbox.extractors`. After each message append in `GoogleMailSync` (and any other future ingestion paths), the inbox iterates every enabled extractor's `match()` and dispatches the top match if `confidence >= threshold`. Off by default; opt-in per Mailbox.

All three modes funnel through the single `ExtractMessage` operation, so the only differences are how the operation is invoked and whether a user-facing toast is shown.

- **op** `ExtractMessage` Dispatches a Message to a registered MessageExtractor and persists the result.

## Implementations contributed by this plugin

- **feat** `TravelMessageExtractor` plugin-trip's MessageExtractor impl.

### Phase 2 file layout

```text
packages/plugins/plugin-inbox/src/
  types/
    ExtractedFrom.ts            # ECHO relation (new)
    Mailbox.ts                  # add optional `extractors` config (edit)
  capabilities/
    MessageExtractor.ts         # capability + MatchResult/ExtractResult types (new)
  operations/
    extract-message.ts          # operation handler used by all three modes (new)
    google/gmail/sync.ts        # auto-on-arrival dispatch hook (edit)
  skills/
    inbox.ts                    # append ExtractMessage to toolDefinitions (edit)
  components/
    MessageActions.tsx          # menu surface; queries MessageExtractor registry (new)

packages/plugins/plugin-trip/src/
  extractors/
    TravelMessageExtractor.ts   # the MessageExtractor impl (new)
    parseUnitedFlight.ts        # pure parser for @united.com (new)
    parseBookingComHotel.ts     # pure parser for @booking.com (new)
    providers.ts                # known-domain → Provider lookup (new)
    __fixtures__/               # raw email bodies used in tests
  capabilities/
    index.ts                    # register TravelMessageExtractor (edit)
```

### Tests

- **scenario** `parseUnitedFlight` Parser unit tests against fixture emails (canonical + edge cases).
- **scenario** `parseBookingComHotel` Parser unit tests against fixture emails.
- **scenario** `TravelMessageExtractor` Dispatch, Trip resolution, and Account dedup.

- **feat** `TripCalendarSource` plugin-trip's CalendarEventSource impl.

- **feat** `TripMapMarkers` plugin-trip contributes a MapCapabilities.MarkerProvider (from @dxos/plugin-map) that plots a Trip's segments: one marker per segment (keyed by segment id) plus origin→destination arcs for transport segments, with IATA-…

## Out of scope for Phase 1

- View definitions for Table / Map. The existing Table and Map view configurations are sufficient — Segments and Trips become queryable data sources for those views without new type contributions here.
- Markdown embedding surfaces. Trips and Segments use the generic article / embedded-surface mechanisms; no plugin-specific surface types are added.
- Currency conversion and price roll-ups. These are derived and live in view-side logic.
- `SegmentRequest` — multi-leg "desired travel" search input. Added when a real search provider is wired.
- `BookingFor` relation linking `Booking` → `Trip`. Added when a query needs Bookings without walking Segments.
- Splitting `BoatSegment` into ferry vs. cruise, and `RoadSegment` into per-mode variants. Revisit when usage demands richer per-mode typing.

## Out of scope for Phase 2

- Agent-backed extractor variants. The contract supports them (`extract` returns an `Effect`); a concrete impl is a follow-up.
- Additional carrier parsers (BA, Lufthansa, Eurostar, Avis, …). The v1 parser registry is intentionally narrow (UA + Booking.com); new carriers are additive parser modules and unit tests.
- A UI for editing `Mailbox.extractors`. Developer-set in v1; UI lands when the auto-on-arrival mode gets validated in real mailboxes.
- A Trip picker in the manual extraction flow. v1 always resolves to most-recently-updated-or-new; a picker is a follow-up.
- `TripCalendarSource` (described above) — separate slice.

## Open follow-ups

- Confirm whether `Provider` should also replace `AccessToken.source` (currently `Hostname`); out of scope here but worth a follow-up to keep the model uniform.
- Smarter Trip resolution (date-range overlap, traveller match) for auto-on-arrival ingestion; v1 uses last-updated as a stand-in.

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Create a trip and add a segment — The core trip round-trip — create a trip, add a travel segment, read it back.

---

pages.title: TypefullyPlugin
pages.summary: Implements `plugin-blogger`'s provider-agnostic `Publisher.PublisherService` capability against the Typefully v1 REST API (`https://api.typefully.com`), authenticating via a `plugin-connector` `Connection` built from a user-submitted API key (Typefully has no OAuth flow).
pages.content:
Implements `plugin-blogger`'s provider-agnostic `Publisher.PublisherService` capability against the Typefully v1 REST API (`https://api.typefully.com`), authenticating via a `plugin-connector` `Connection` built from a user-submitted API key (Typefully has no OAuth flow).

**As-built limitation, stated up front:** the Typefully v1 API supports only creating a draft and listing recently-published drafts. It has no get-by-id, update, or delete endpoint. `getDraft`, `updateDraft`, and `deleteDraft` are implemented to reject unconditionally with `Publisher.PublisherError` rather than fabricate an endpoint — see Features F-3 through F-5 and the composition impact called out in F-6.

## Types

- **type** `TypefullyDraftResponse` Permissive view of a Typefully v1 draft response.

## Operations

- **op** `SubmitTypefullyCredentials` credentialForm.onSubmit for the Typefully ConnectorEntry (id "typefully", source "typefully.com"), contributed on AppActivationEvents.SetupConnectors.

## Services

- **service** `TypefullyPublisherService` Implements Publisher.PublisherService against the Typefully v1 REST API.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Credential Entry
  - `F-1.1` The Typefully ConnectorEntry (id "typefully", source "typefully.com", label "Typefully") is contributed on AppActivationEvents.SetupConnectors.
  - `F-1.2` Submitting a non-blank API key via op:SubmitTypefullyCredentials builds an AccessToken (source "typefully.com") and a Connection linked to the "typefully" connector, returned as { kind: 'complete' }.
  - `F-1.3` Submitting a blank (or whitespace-only) API key rejects before any AccessToken or Connection is built.

- **feat** `F-2` Publisher Service Registration
  - `F-2.1` service:TypefullyPublisherService is contributed under plugin-blogger's BloggerCapabilities.PublisherService.
  - `F-2.2` Every request authenticates via TypefullyCredentials.fromConnection: loads the Connection then its linked AccessToken, and sends X-API-KEY: Bearer <token>.

- **feat** `F-3` Create Draft (real)
  - `F-3.1` createDraft is called with { text, scheduledAt?

- **feat** `F-4` List Drafts (real, limited)
  - `F-4.1` listDrafts is called → GETs /v1/drafts/recently-published/ — the v1 API's closest analogue to a general list-all-drafts endpoint — and normalises each entry to a PublisherDraft.

- **feat** `F-5` Unsupported CRUD Verbs (honest limitation)
  - `F-5.1` getDraft always rejects with PublisherError("getDraft is not supported by the Typefully v1 API.") without issuing any HTTP request.
  - `F-5.2` updateDraft always rejects with PublisherError("updateDraft is not supported by the Typefully v1 API.") without issuing any HTTP request.
  - `F-5.3` deleteDraft always rejects with PublisherError("deleteDraft is not supported by the Typefully v1 API.") without issuing any HTTP request.

- **feat** `F-6` Composition Impact on plugin-blogger Sync Operations — Derived from reading both packages together (op:PublishDraft / op:ImportDrafts / op:UnpublishDraft in plugin-blogger call getDraft / updateDraft / deleteDraft on the resolved PublisherService).
  - `F-6.1` A Draft's FIRST op:PublishDraft against a Typefully Connection succeeds (createDraft, unlinked → linked).
  - `F-6.2` Any SUBSEQUENT op:PublishDraft on the same (now-linked) Draft calls updateDraft and fails with PublisherError — Typefully re-publish/update is NOT supported.
  - `F-6.3` op:ImportDrafts against a Typefully Connection fails with PublisherError as soon as listDrafts returns any remote draft not yet linked to a local Draft, because the handler then calls getDraft for its body.
  - `F-6.4` op:UnpublishDraft against a Typefully Connection fails with PublisherError whenever the Draft is linked (deleteDraft always rejects); it remains a no-op only when the Draft was never linked.

- **feat** `F-7` Resilience
  - `F-7.1` an HTTP request fails with 429 or 5xx, or times out (15s) → exponential back-off retry with jitter, up to 3 attempts
  - `F-7.2` response decoding fails (Schema.decodeUnknown) → no retry; the ParseError propagates immediately

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Connector entry maps apiKey to AccessToken.token

- **scenario** `T-2` Connector entry rejects a blank API key

- **scenario** `T-3` createDraft POSTs with X-API-KEY Bearer auth

- **scenario** `T-4` createDraft forwards scheduledAt as schedule-date

- **scenario** `T-5` listDrafts GETs recently-published

- **scenario** `T-6` getDraft, updateDraft, deleteDraft reject without any network call

- **scenario** `T-7` PublishDraft against Typefully — create-once, no re-publish

- **scenario** `T-8` ImportDrafts against Typefully fails on any unlinked remote draft

- **scenario** `T-9` UnpublishDraft against Typefully fails once linked

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Connect Typefully, publish once, and confirm the no-republish limitation — plugin-typefully has no ECHO object type or navtree surface of its own — it is a Publisher.PublisherService implementation consumed through plugin-blogger's Publication/Post UI.

---

pages.title: TypeSafePlugin
pages.summary: Connects TypeSafe System One (`jev`) to a space and serves its decision model through AiService to every operation running there.
pages.content:
Connects TypeSafe System One (`jev`) to a space and serves its decision model through AiService to every operation running there. Headless: a connector and a model resolver, no surfaces.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Bring your own key
  - `F-1.1` A connector for source `typesafe.ai` takes an API key pasted by the user.
  - `F-1.2` The key is stored as an AccessToken plus a Connection, resolvable by CredentialsService.
  - `F-1.3` A blank or whitespace-only key fails inline, leaving the dialog open with the reason.
- **feat** `F-2` Decision model in the space
  - `F-2.1` An AiModelResolver serves `ai.typesafe.model.jev.latest` via AiService.decisionModel in every space.
  - `F-2.2` The key is read per call, so connecting or disconnecting takes effect on the next question.
  - `F-2.3` With the endpoint override set and no key connected, the decision fails with an AiError (AuthenticationError, MissingKey), never a defect.
  - `F-2.4` Unless overridden, calls go through EDGE `/ai/generate/typesafe`: with no key connected EDGE answers on the platform key, and a connected key rides as `X-BYOK`.
  - `F-2.5` `Model.defaultDecisionModel` resolves to the **Default decision model** setting, and to Cloudflare's Clef on Workers AI (through EDGE `/ai/generate/workers-ai/typesafe`) when the setting is unset.

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` A pasted key reaches the model
- **scenario** `T-2` No key answers through EDGE on the platform key
- **scenario** `T-3` A direct endpoint with no key is a failed decision, not a crash

## QA

- **test** `QA-1` Connect TypeSafe and label a mailbox — The only user-visible journey this plugin has — connect the key, then watch a consumer use it.

pages.title: VoxelPlugin
pages.summary: A 3D voxel editor plugin for `DXOS` Composer.
pages.content:
A 3D voxel editor plugin for `DXOS` Composer. Users create, paint, and sculpt block-based 3D worlds that are persisted as `World` objects in ECHO and replicated across peers in real-time. The editor runs entirely in the browser via `@react-three/fiber` (Three.js), requires no server-side rendering, and is designed to work offline-first.

Worlds are represented as a sparse `VoxelMap` — a coordinate-keyed record of voxel properties — so only occupied cells are stored. Grid dimensions and block size are configurable per-world, defaulting to a 32×32 ground plane with unit-sized blocks.

The plugin also exposes a Conway's Game of Life simulation that runs on the ground plane (z=0), letting users seed well-known patterns (glider, LWSS, Gosper glider gun, pulsar, etc.) and step them forward in real-time. Life ticks apply standard Conway rules (survive on 2–3 neighbours; born on exactly 3) using the existing voxel data as the cell state.

Four agent-callable operations — `QueryWorld`, `AddVoxels`, `RemoveVoxels`, and `GenerateShape` — give AI assistants first-class access to read and modify the world. `GenerateShape` supports five geometric primitives (cube, wall, sphere, cylinder, tower) placed at an arbitrary origin with a caller-supplied hue.

## Types

- **type** `VoxelProps`

- **type** `VoxelData`

- **type** `VoxelMap` Sparse map of occupied voxels.

- **type** `World` ECHO object (typename: org.dxos.type.voxel) representing a voxel world.

- **type** `ToolMode`

- **type** `ModelType`

- **type** `Origin`

## Components

- **component** `VoxelEditor` Interactive Three.js Canvas rendering the voxel world.

- **component** `VoxelToolbar` Composable toolbar providing tool-mode toggle, hue picker, and optional action buttons.

- **component** `VoxelArticle` Full editor surface (article role).

- **component** `VoxelCard` Read-only card surface (card role).

## Operations

Pure read operations — no side effects.

- **op** `queryWorld` Returns the current state of the voxel world including all voxels, grid dimensions, and block size.

Effectful operations — mutate persistent ECHO state.

- **op** `addVoxels` Adds one or more voxels to the world at specified coordinates with a given hue.

- **op** `removeVoxels` Removes voxels at specified coordinates from the world.

- **op** `generateShape` Generates a 3D geometric shape (cube, wall, sphere, cylinder, or tower) and places it at the given origin.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Place Voxel
  - `F-1.1` tool mode is add and user clicks the ground plane → a new voxel is placed at the clicked grid cell at z=0
  - `F-1.2` tool mode is add and user clicks the face of an existing voxel → a new voxel is placed adjacent to the clicked face
  - `F-1.3` tool mode is add and cursor is over a valid placement target → a semi-transparent ghost cursor shows the pending voxel position
  - `F-1.4` the target cell is outside the grid bounds → placement is rejected; no voxel is created

- **feat** `F-2` Remove Voxel
  - `F-2.1` tool mode is remove and user clicks an existing voxel → the voxel is deleted from the world
  - `F-2.2` tool mode is remove and cursor hovers over a voxel → a red ghost cursor indicates the voxel will be removed

- **feat** `F-3` Hue Selection
  - `F-3.1` user selects a hue via the HuePicker in the toolbar → newly placed voxels use the selected hue
  - `F-3.2` hue is changed → existing voxels are not recolored

- **feat** `F-4` Generate Shape
  - `F-4.1` user clicks the "Generate shape" toolbar button → a random ModelType is chosen and placed at selectedPosition (or origin)
  - `F-4.2` op:generateShape is invoked by an agent → the specified shape is placed at the given origin with the given hue
  - `F-4.3` All five ModelTypes (cube, wall, sphere, cylinder, tower) are supported.

- **feat** `F-5` Game of Life Simulation
  - `F-5.1` user clicks "Seed" in the toolbar → a random well-known pattern is applied to the ground plane (z=0)
  - `F-5.2` user clicks "Play" → the simulation ticks every 500 ms using standard Conway rules
  - `F-5.3` user clicks "Pause" → ticking stops; current voxel state is preserved
  - `F-5.4` a tick completes → updated world is written to ECHO and replicated to peers
  - `F-5.5` Non-ground voxels (z>0) are unaffected by the simulation.

- **feat** `F-6` World Persistence
  - `F-6.1` a voxel is added or removed interactively → the World object is updated in ECHO via useObject
  - `F-6.2` an ECHO update arrives from a peer → VoxelArticle re-renders with the new voxel state
  - `F-6.3` a World object is created → it is stored with typename org.dxos.type.voxel and appears in the space

- **feat** `F-7` Camera and Navigation
  - `F-7.1` editor opens → camera is positioned to show the full grid with perspective view
  - `F-7.2` user middle-clicks and drags → camera orbits around the grid center
  - `F-7.3` user Shift+middle-clicks and drags → camera pans
  - `F-7.4` user scrolls → camera zooms
  - `F-7.5` VoxelCard renders in readOnly mode → camera auto-fits all voxels; pan/zoom/orbit are disabled

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Place voxel on ground

- **scenario** `T-2` Place voxel on face

- **scenario** `T-3` Remove voxel

- **scenario** `T-4` Out-of-bounds placement rejected

- **scenario** `T-5` Generate shape via toolbar

- **scenario** `T-6` op:generateShape — sphere

- **scenario** `T-7` Life simulation tick

- **scenario** `T-8` Collaborative sync

- **scenario** `T-9` op:queryWorld

- **scenario** `T-10` Card read-only mode

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Build and query a shape agent-only — The core voxel round-trip through the four agent-callable operations — query an empty world, generate a shape, remove part of it, and query again to confirm the mutation.
- **test** `QA-2` Showcase clip — The 10s showcase clip: Orbit a voxel world.

---

pages.title: WnfsPlugin
pages.summary: A decentralized file storage plugin for `DXOS` Composer built on the Web Native File System (WNFS) protocol.
pages.content:
A decentralized file storage plugin for `DXOS` Composer built on the Web Native File System (WNFS) protocol.

WNFS provides a content-addressed, end-to-end encrypted private file system using a cryptographic "dark forest" structure. Files are stored as IPLD blocks referenced by CID, replicated to a DXOS edge blob service, and cached locally in IndexedDB. The plugin registers a `BlobBackend` (schemes: `['wnfs']`) on the ECHO Hypergraph via `client.graph.registerBlobBackend`, and contributes a matching `FileCapabilities.Backend` descriptor (`{ storage: 'wnfs' }`) so `plugin-file` — and any plugin built on it, e.g. `plugin-gallery` — can upload files and resolve `wnfs://` URIs uniformly via the core `Blob.fromBytes`/`Blob.url`/`Blob.read` API, without knowing the underlying storage layer. Uploads are scoped to a DXOS Space; the private forest root CID is persisted on the space's ECHO properties and updated atomically on every write.

## Types

- **type** `Cid` A content-addressed identifier encoded as a base-32 multibase string (CIDv1, sha2-256).

- **type** `WnfsPath` A WNFS path encoded as a wnfs:// URL; segments are percent-encoded.

- **type** `FileInfo` Internal return value of the `upload` helper.

- **type** `BlockstoreState` Runtime state of the MixedBlockstore.

- **type** `WnfsInstances` In-memory cache mapping forest CID → loaded PrivateDirectory/PrivateForest pair.

- **type** `WnfsInstance` A loaded WNFS private file system rooted at a specific forest CID.

## Operations

Pure operations — no external effects.

- **op** `wnfsUrl` Encodes a WNFS path array into a wnfs:// URL with percent-encoded segments.

- **op** `getPathFromUrl` Decodes a wnfs:// URL back into a path segment array.

BlobBackend implementation — registered on the ECHO Hypergraph, dispatched to by core `Blob.fromBytes` / `Blob.read` / `Blob.exists` / `Blob.url` whenever a Blob's storage or URI scheme resolves to `wnfs`.

- **op** `wnfsBlobPut` Implements BlobBackend.put.

- **op** `wnfsBlobGet` Implements BlobBackend.get.

- **op** `wnfsBlobHas` Implements BlobBackend.has by delegating to the same read path as wnfsBlobGet and checking for a defined result.

- **op** `wnfsBlobGetUrl` Implements BlobBackend.getUrl.

Effectful operations underlying the BlobBackend implementation above.

- **op** `uploadFile` Reads a File, writes its bytes into the WNFS private directory at a CID-derived path, persists the updated forest pointer to the space's ECHO properties, and returns FileInfo.

- **op** `flushBlockQueue` Drains the pending-upload queue by assembling a CAR archive and POSTing it to the edge blob service.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Upload File
  - `F-1.1` core Blob.fromBytes routes to the 'wnfs' storage (i.e.
  - `F-1.2` the write succeeds → the space's ECHO properties are updated with the new privateForestCid
  - `F-1.3` the upload completes → the returned uri is a wnfs:// URL, embedded by core Blob.ts as the Blob object's

- **feat** `F-2` Resolve wnfs:// blobs
  - `F-2.1` a Blob's URI scheme is 'wnfs' (i.e.
  - `F-2.2` BlobBackend.get or .has is called with a wnfs:// uri → loads or reuses a cached WnfsInstance for the space and reads the file bytes
  - `F-2.3` BlobBackend.getUrl is called with a wnfs:// uri → bytes are read and wrapped in a blob: object URL for in-browser display
  - `F-2.4` the space is not open, or reading/writing fails → get/has/getUrl resolve to undefined/false rather than throwing; put rejects

- **feat** `F-3` Blockstore Sync
  - `F-3.1` a block is written via blockstore.put → the block is saved to IndexedDB and added to the upload queue
  - `F-3.2` the browser is online and the queue is non-empty → blocks are batched into a CAR archive and flushed to the edge service
  - `F-3.3` the browser goes offline → the queue is persisted to IndexedDB; no upload is attempted
  - `F-3.4` the browser comes back online → the flush is triggered automatically
  - `F-3.5` a block is requested via blockstore.get and is present in IndexedDB → the block is returned from the local cache without a network request
  - `F-3.6` a block is not in IndexedDB and the browser is online → the block is fetched from the edge service and cached locally

- **feat** `F-4` Space-Scoped Private File System
  - `F-4.1` a space has no existing WNFS properties → a new PrivateForest and PrivateDirectory are created and stored
  - `F-4.2` a space already has a privateForestCid → the existing forest and directory are loaded from the blockstore
  - `F-4.3` a WnfsInstance is already cached for the current forest CID → the cached instance is reused without reloading from the blockstore
  - `F-4.4` legacy snake_case WNFS properties are found on a space → they are deleted and replaced with the current camelCase schema

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Upload creates a wnfs:// blob

- **scenario** `T-2` Resolve uploaded blob via getUrl

- **scenario** `T-3` get/has/getUrl return undefined/false when the space is not open

- **scenario** `T-4` Blockstore offline queuing

- **scenario** `T-5` Blockstore queue flushes on reconnect

- **scenario** `T-6` New space initializes WNFS directory

- **scenario** `T-7` WnfsInstance cache hit

---

## QA

Executable tests. Each step carries a human instruction (`do`) and, where the step maps to an invocable operation, an agent binding (`invoke`). Report failures by test and step number.

- **test** `QA-1` Upload a file and resolve it back through the wnfs:// scheme — plugin-wnfs has no ECHO type or navtree surface of its own — it is a `BlobBackend` (`schemes: ['wnfs']`) that `plugin-file` dispatches to transparently through `Blob.fromBytes`/`Blob.read`/`Blob.url`.

---

pages.title: ZenPlugin
pages.summary: ZenPlugin is an ambient sound and meditation plugin for DXOS Composer.

features.title: Timed Dreams fade out instead of stopping

ZenPlugin is an ambient sound and meditation plugin for DXOS Composer. Users create and edit `Dream` objects — named, duration-bound soundscapes composed of layered audio `Sequence` tracks. - **type** `Source` Discriminated union of audio sources.

- **type** `Sequence` A single audio layer in a Dream.

- **type** `Dream` ECHO object (typename dxos.org.type.Dream).

pages.title: SceneEnginePostM4
pages.summary: The fixes made after migration milestone M4 landed, as executable checks.
pages.content:
The fixes made after migration milestone M4 landed, as executable checks. They are separated from `SPEC.mdl` — which states what the engine IS — because this file states what was WRONG and how to see that it no longer is: every flow here began as a report against a build, and several of the first attempts at a fix were wrong in ways only a measurement showed.

The through-line is one mistake made three times: **a quantity fixed in scene units, compared against something measured on screen**. The grid drew levels filtered by their on-screen size while snapping used a constant; node defaults were constant while the camera that displays them was not; text was constant while the level it sat in was not. Each flow below pins one of those to the quantity it has to track.

Run `moon run react-ui-canvas:e2e` for the automated subset (`src/playwright/create.spec.ts` and `scene.spec.ts`), or the storybook at 9006 / 9009 for the human ones.

## QA

- **test** `PM4-1` A create covers the same screen area at any zoom — The palette drop and the toolbar's create menu had the type's default size in scene units, so what they produced grew and shrank with the camera: at a nested level, where the camera arrives at a fraction of the parent's…

- **test** `PM4-2` A drawn box is what the pointer swept, and an empty gesture creates nothing — A press that moved less than a cell used to fall back to the type's default size, so a stray click with a shape tool planted a node, and a small deliberate box silently became a large default one.

- **test** `PM4-3` Snapping lands on the lines that are drawn — The snap unit was fixed in scene units while `Grid` keeps a level only while its cells are legible on screen, so the two parted company with the zoom.

- **test** `PM4-4` The zoom readout is against the level's own 1:1 — Entering a portal divides the camera by the frame's factor, so the raw number dropped fourfold on a drill-in that changed nothing the user could see (70% became 23%).

- **test** `PM4-5` Links join shapes, not just ports — A link could only start at a port, so joining two shapes meant aiming at a 5px dot; and with a link tool every node drew its ports at once, a field of dots over the diagram being drawn.

- **test** `PM4-6` A smart link is routed, not drawn — First cut: a stub out of each port along its side's normal by half a major cell, one segment joining them, corners rounded by the same builder a spline uses.

- **test** `PM4-7` Text reads at the level it was drawn in — `style.fontSize` in the node's own scene units.

pages.title: SceneEngine
pages.summary: The scene engine: an infinite, multi-depth diagram surface.
pages.content:
The scene engine: an infinite, multi-depth diagram surface. A scene is typed nodes and typed links in one flat coordinate space; a node of type `scene` is a portal into another scene, which is what depth means. The engine lives here rather than in a plugin because it is UI with no ECHO dependency — `plugin-canvas` and `plugin-conductor` are thin variant hosts that supply a store, a registry and a projection. `docs/DESIGN.md` carries the reasoning and the numbered decisions this document cites; `docs/MIGRATION.md` the plan that brought canvas-editor and canvas-compute onto it.

The seam that makes one surface serve every host is the **projection** (decision 11): the surface reads a positioned `Scene` and emits `Intent`s, and never writes a coordinate itself. A projection may apply, rewrite or reject each intent and then re-emits the scene. Freehand is the identity projection; constrained, dynamic and compute projections own a model of their own and position the scene from it.

Status 2026-09-22: **implemented** through migration milestone M3. Node types are open (`NodeBase` plus what a type adds), the editor surface is a superset of the retired canvas editor minus auto layout, and `react-ui-canvas-compute` runs its shapes as node definitions over this engine. M4 (ECHO persistence, the `layout` intent and the plugin switch) is in flight; what M4 adds is marked below.

## Types

Effect `Schema` structures in `src/model/types.ts`; plain schemas, so a host wraps them into an ECHO type without changing a field (decision 3).

- **type** `Scene` One diagram: nodes and links keyed by id in a single flat coordinate space (decision 4).

- **type** `NodeBase` What every node is, whatever its type adds (decision 1).

- **type** `BuiltinNode` The engine's own five, each `NodeBase` plus its own fields; `isRectNode`-style guards narrow to them, sound because the registry maps one type name to one schema.

- **type** `NodeStyle` Presentation a node carries; every field optional, the frame supplying the default look.

- **type** `Link` A typed edge: `line` (straight), `curve` (cubic Bézier leaving each port along its side's normal), `spline` (the polyline through its control `points`, each interior point rounded by a quadratic that takes the point as…

- **type** `Endpoint` Either end of a link, and the reason a link can exist before both its ends do: `{node, port?}` with no port pairs automatically (the closest appropriate pair, recomputed on every projection, so a moved node re-routes),…

- **type** `Port` An attachment point on a node's frame.

- **type** `Camera` The view's position over one scene: screen = (scene + {x, y}) * zoom.

- **type** `NodeDef` A node type's definition: its schema, what it renders, where its ports are, how it may be manipulated, and how the palette presents it.

- **type** `ViewStore` Scenes by id behind atoms, so a view subscribes to exactly the scene it shows.

- **type** `Projection` The only thing the surface knows about the model (decision 11).

- **type** `Tool` The active tool; a node type draws that node, a link type is what a port drag creates.

## Components

One folder per component under `src/components`, stories beside it, all behind the `src/index.ts` barrel. Rendering is DOM with the camera as one CSS transform, SVG for the link and control layers (decision 7); no third-party canvas engine, and d3 only as pure functions (decision 8).

- **component** `Canvas` The surface: one scene under a camera, with the palette, toolbar, breadcrumbs and control frame around it.

- **component** `SceneLayer` The nodes and links of one scene, and — for a portal node — the child scene rendered live inside it at the portal's scale, which is what makes depth continuous rather than a page change.

- **component** `ControlFrame` Everything drawn about the selection rather than in the scene: the selection outline, eight resize handles, the hover border, ports, the rubber band of a link drag, the marquee, a spline's control points and the midpoin…

- **component** `Palette` Node and link types from the registry, grouped, each with its shortcut; entries are pdnd drag sources.

- **component** `Toolbar` Optional chrome (decision 5): up and breadcrumbs, fit, zoom, snap, undo/redo, cut/copy/paste/delete, a create menu, auto layout, debug, and a readout of zoom, pointer and depth.

- **component** `Properties` The schema-driven `Form` over the selected node or link's OWN schema — the registry already carries it, so a host type gets a properties panel with no extra work.

- **component** `GeometryField` A node's `center` or `size` as one row of two labelled number cells (X / Y, W / H) rather than a collapsible fieldset.

- **component** `Breadcrumbs` The path from the root to the scene being edited; a click drills out to that level.

- **component** `Grid` Multi-resolution grid in screen space, fed the camera.

- **component** `PartEditor` In-place text editing: a `react-ui-editor` over one `TextPart` of a node (a rect or ellipse label, a text body, a class's name, attributes or methods).

## Operations

The projection seam IS the operation surface: these are the only ways the model changes, and every one of them is a value the view hands to `projection.apply`. `reduceIntent` is freehand's semantics as a pure reducer, which is what makes them testable without a DOM.

- **op** `move` Translate every unlocked node in `ids` by `delta`.

- **op** `resize` Set one unlocked node's frame.

- **op** `link` Add a link.

- **op** `create` Add a node, built by its type's `NodeDef.create`.

- **op** `delete` Remove nodes and links by id.

- **op** `reorder` Set one element's fractional `z`; nodes and links share the namespace and the key space.

- **op** `update` Property edits — a label, a text body, geometry, a spline's control points, a style.

- **op** `batch` Several intents as ONE model change, so a paste or a drill-in fix-up is one undo step.

- **op** `layout` Arrange the scene into ranked rows along its links, through `@dxos/diagram`'s ranking — the engine the dynamic projection already lays its graph out with, rather than a second one.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Depth and navigation
  - `F-1.1` Double-clicking a portal drills in; Escape drills out; the breadcrumbs drill to any level.
  - `F-1.2` Drill-in stops where the child would pass 1:1, so its text lands at natural size rather
  - `F-1.3` Zooming past a portal drills in on its own; zooming out below the arrival coverage drills
  - `F-1.4` A portal's frame is the portal box times a power of the grid ratio, never once, placed on
  - `F-1.5` A scene entered through a portal keeps the frame it arrived with for the visit and exits
  - `F-1.6` At most `liveDepth` levels mount live; deeper portals draw as previews (decision 10).
  - `F-1.7` Alt+Left / Alt+Right walk the view's own camera history.

- **feat** `F-2` Grid and snapping
  - `F-2.1` The grid is drawn only while snapping is on (G toggles both): its lines are what a gesture
  - `F-2.2` Gestures snap to the FINEST LEVEL THE GRID ACTUALLY DRAWS, read back through the same rule
  - `F-2.3` A node drawn on the canvas, moved or resized lands on the major level, so its edges and ports
  - `F-2.4` An arrow nudges by the minor grid, Shift+arrow by a major cell.
  - `F-2.5` A link band follows the pointer exactly and snaps once, as it lands.
  - `F-2.6` Snapping off means every gesture is free and the grid is hidden; nothing else changes.

- **feat** `F-3` Selection and editing
  - `F-3.1` Nodes and links are selected together in one set; Delete removes either.
  - `F-3.2` A marquee replaces the selection, Shift adds, Alt subtracts.
  - `F-3.3` A port drag creates a link; dropping on empty canvas leaves a free end; dragging an end
  - `F-3.4` A selected spline offers the midpoint of every span; pressing one inserts a control point
  - `F-3.5` A create drag previews the bounds the node will land in; a palette drop shows that frame
  - `F-3.6` A box drawn on the canvas is exactly what the pointer swept — no minimum and no fallback to
  - `F-3.7` A create with NO drawn box (a palette drop, the toolbar's create menu) takes the type's
  - `F-3.8` Picking a shape or link tool clears the selection; the node the gesture makes becomes it.
  - `F-3.9` Double-click edits a node's text part in place; Enter commits, Escape rejects.
  - `F-3.10` The properties panel edits the selected element's own schema through `update` intents,
  - `F-3.11` A scene shape's Scene picks any scene of the store for it to open, so several shapes may
  - `F-3.12` Style classes are named looks kept beside the scenes (`ViewStore.styles`): an element
  - `F-3.14` Nodes and links share one `style` object: its common base (`lineStyleFields`: colour and line
  - `F-3.15` A scene has ordered layers (`Scene.layers`, one implicit when it names none) and every node and link
  - `F-3.13` Group (⌘G) moves the selected nodes, and the links between them, into an anonymous Object

- **feat** `F-4` Undo and clipboard
  - `F-4.1` Undo is a snapshot log over the projection seam, so it works for any projection without
  - `F-4.2` A restored snapshot reconciles the projection's own model (the compute projection takes
  - `F-4.3` Cut / copy / paste use a per-view clipboard: fresh ids, links rewired between the pasted

- **feat** `F-5` Read-only
  - `F-5.1` `readonly` lets the view select, pan, zoom and drill, and nothing else.
  - `F-5.2` No handle, port, tool or toolbar edit is drawn or reachable, whatever the projection's

- **feat** `F-6` Open registry
  - `F-6.1` The engine operates on `NodeBase`; a host's type is not a special case.
  - `F-6.2` A host composes its registry from the built-ins and its own defs, and its scene schema with
  - `F-6.3` An unknown type still renders rather than throwing, as the core base (`BaseNode`): a node as
  - `F-6.4` Ports come from the definition; a node may still carry its own.

- **feat** `F-7` Persistence (M4)
  - `F-7.1` `createEchoStore(board)` maps nodes to `CanvasBoard.layout.nodes` and links to
  - `F-7.2` The store is the only seam that changes: `Canvas` takes the ECHO store exactly as it
  - `F-7.3` `plugin-conductor`'s `CanvasArticle` renders `Canvas` with the compute projection over

- **feat** `F-8` Links between shapes
  - `F-8.1` With a link tool a node's BODY is a source like a port is, so two shapes can be joined
  - `F-8.2` A drop resolves the same way: a port claims it only while the pointer is within reach,
  - `F-8.3` Ports are drawn for the node under the pointer alone (and a drop target mid-drag, which
  - `F-8.4` A `smart` link is routed, not drawn: a stub leaves each port along its side's normal by

## Rules

Conventions this engine's code must hold that a linter cannot express; each block is discovered by the agentic-review harness.

- **rule** `intents-not-coordinates` The surface emits intents; only a projection writes coordinates

- **rule** `key-chords-live-in-the-table` Every chord is a KEY_BINDINGS entry, matched and labelled from it

- **rule** `named-react-imports` Import React members by name, never through a `React.` namespace

- **rule** `scene-bounds-are-derived` Never store a scene's bounds

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Drill in and back out

- **scenario** `T-2` A link survives its node moving

- **scenario** `T-3` A free-ended link

- **scenario** `T-4` Read-only

- **scenario** `T-5` Undo across a projection

- **scenario** `T-6` An existing board opens unchanged (M4)

## QA

Executable tests over the **storybook**, not the app: the engine ships no plugin of its own, and the stories are the surface a host composes. Run `moon run storybook-react:serve` (9009) or the e2e storybook (9006); `moon run react-ui-canvas:e2e` runs the automated subset.

- **test** `QA-1` The editor surface end to end — The gestures a host inherits by rendering `Canvas`.

- **test** `QA-2` Persistence round trip (M4) — The one thing stories cannot cover, because it needs a space: that a board written by the old editor opens unchanged on the engine, and that an edit made on the engine survives a reload.

pages.title: FeedSpec
pages.summary: Consolidation spec for the feed spike.
pages.content:
Consolidation spec for the feed spike. The spike answered "can one anchor-placed window scroll smoothly with a CodeMirror editor per row" (yes — `DESIGN.md` has the principles, `TESTING.md` the manual evidence). This document specifies the four parts to consolidate — **virtualizer**, **list**, **outliner**, **minimap** — the seams between them, and what is an aspect (a policy the host may swap, exposed as a reusable hook per the `react-ui-list` pattern) versus an internal (an invariant the engine must hold, never exposed).

Status 2026-08-18: **implemented** — the virtualizer and debug entry points exist, the model and the five aspects are in, the rails moved, and the flagship `assistant/Assistant` story exercises the whole loop. Additions found by building: `ListModel.patch` (streaming for frozen items — an identity-preserving replacement announced as `updated`), and the follow's speeds raised for streaming (8 rows/s; the class defaults were tuned for a single arrival).

Decisions taken:

- The virtualizer shipped as an entry point of this package first, then graduated to `@dxos/react-ui-virtual` (placement, `useWindow`/`Window`, the follow, and `ListModel`); this package depends on it and keeps the message-native layer.
- The list consumes a **model**, not an array: a low-level `ListModel` (reactive via `@effect/atom`) the virtualizer binds to, and `FeedModel` as the native case — not an add-on. `fromMessages()` keeps the array form as an adapter.
- The follow glide (`ScrollFollower`) is wired and on by default; instant is the fallback.
- Search is **not** the list's concern. Cross-cutting per-item data — search highlights, selection — reaches items through provider + hook (the decoration pattern, §Aspects); the list neither knows nor routes it.
- The rails live in **this package**: `Minimap` is promoted here, and `Outline` moves here from `react-ui-components` — call sites updated, no compatibility re-export.
- The horizontal axis is in scope for the **virtualizer** (axis-neutral arithmetic, an inline acceptance story against real content) and out of scope for the **feed list** (vertical only; rails stay vertical until a horizontal consumer exists).

## Types

- **type** `Extents` The host's answer about row sizes, in scalars along one axis — never height or width, so the axis stays the DOM binding's business.

- **type** `Layout` The mounted range and where its parent goes.

- **type** `WindowState` Published state for chrome that lives outside the scroller — toolbar, statusbar, rails.

- **type** `ListModel` The low-level contract the virtualizer binds to — what the engine already consumed as separate props (count, getId, extents), made one reactive object.

- **type** `FeedModel` The native case, not an add-on: a ListModel of messages with the feed's own semantics.

- **type** `Decoration` A range of one item's rendered text that some producer wants painted — search is ONE producer; linting, mentions, and diff spans are others.

- **type** `Stop` One position navigation can land on.

- **type** `Marker` An outliner tick's model.

- **type** `EdgeDrift` What reaching an edge revealed about the estimates.

## Components

- **component** `Virtualizer` The reusable placement engine: Placement (pure arithmetic, no DOM/React) + useWindow (binding to an element the HOST owns) + Window (the trivial own-scroller binding for stories and simple hosts).

- **component** `MessageList` The chat feed built on the Virtualizer.

- **component** `Outline` Index-space rail: one tick per stop, thinned to a fixed pitch, each tick standing for the span to the next.

- **component** `Minimap` Content-space rail: the document in miniature, drawn from WindowState.geometry only.

## Aspects

The `react-ui-list` pattern: standalone, tested hooks that components compose. The dividing rule — **a policy the host may swap is an aspect; an invariant the engine must hold is an internal.** Internals (the anchor, prepend detection, the id-keyed measurement pass, the single writer of the scroll) are never exposed: a hook over an invariant invites a second party into exactly the seams the design keeps single-owner.

- **aspect** `useWindow` The virtualizer itself, bound to a scroller the host owns.

- **aspect** `useStops` Navigation stops as an atom over the model (FeedModel.stops): per message, per prompt (user turns), per block, per day divider.

- **aspect** `useDecorations` THE PATTERN for cross-cutting per-item data, retrofitted everywhere rather than invented per surface: a provider at the host carries producers (search, mentions, lint, diff); an item asks useDecorations(id) for its own…

- **aspect** `useItemSelection` The item-side hook of the same pattern: an item asks for its own { selected, toggle, rowProps } by id instead of the list threading selectedIds through props.

- **aspect** `useFeedNavigation` Step/jump intents over a WindowController plus stops — the ONE seam every driver calls (toolbar buttons, arrow keys, outliner, minimap).

- **aspect** `useFollow` The sticky tail as an intent — withdrawn only by a backwards scroll, never re-derived from proximity (corrections grow the document under a stationary reader).

- **aspect** `useListSelection` ADOPTED from react-ui-list, not rebuilt — single and multi modes exist there with ARIA semantics (aria-selected, dx-selected).

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Virtualizer invariants
  - `F-1.1` Prepending moves nothing at or after the anchor.
  - `F-1.2` Measuring a row after the anchor never moves the anchor; measurements are keyed by id.
  - `F-1.3` Corrections move the window's transform, never the scroll offset.
  - `F-1.4` A scroll moves content by exactly what was scrolled — including upward from the tail,
  - `F-1.5` Reserve is a sizer term; the last row rests at the content's end, not the document's.
  - `F-1.6` Edge drift is reported (onEdge), never silently applied.
  - `F-1.7` Axis-neutral: block and inline are the same arithmetic; only the binding differs.

- **feat** `F-2` Rendering
  - `F-2.1` Block renderers are pluggable by kind — markdown (CodeMirror, cached shared extension
  - `F-2.2` Chrome is a host render-prop and must not affect measurement beyond being inside the
  - `F-2.3` Widgets (XML tag -> React via registry) may expand after mount; expansion is not a
  - `F-2.4` Widget state lives in a Root-owned store and survives its row unmounting.
  - `F-2.5` The streaming item (FeedModel.streamingId) reconciles by delta rather than remounting.

- **feat** `F-3` Navigation
  - `F-3.1` Stops are a model policy (FeedModel.stops via useStops); default is every message;
  - `F-3.2` All drivers — toolbar, arrows, outliner, minimap — call useFeedNavigation; no parallel
  - `F-3.3` The cursor is the row containing the scroll offset; every press travels.
  - `F-3.4` Steps within the mounted window glide; far jumps are instant.
  - `F-3.5` Cmd/Ctrl+Arrow jumps to first/last.

- **feat** `F-4` Selection
  - `F-4.1` Selection modes single, multi, range are interchangeable policies (useListSelection).
  - `F-4.2` Selection is model-space (ids) and survives virtualization; items read their own
  - `F-4.3` One SelectionGroup spans every editor for text selection.

- **feat** `F-5` Follow
  - `F-5.1` Following is an intent; only a backwards scroll withdraws it, returning to the tail
  - `F-5.2` An answer arriving while the reader is at the tail keeps the tail at rest on the
  - `F-5.3` An answer arriving while the reader is elsewhere moves nothing.

- **feat** `F-6` Rails
  - `F-6.1` Outline ticks and card: pointer wins while pointing, keyboard while navigating,
  - `F-6.2` Minimap draws only from WindowState.geometry; viewport band stays inside the mounted
  - `F-6.3` Both rails are 2rem wide by default; asserted equal.
  - `F-6.4` Both rails live in react-ui-feed; Outline moves from react-ui-components with its

- **feat** `F-7` Model
  - `F-7.1` The virtualizer binds to ListModel; a prepend is told, never inferred by identity scan.
  - `F-7.2` FeedModel is the native case: stops, streamingId, and iteration (loadBefore/loadAfter
  - `F-7.3` fromMessages(array) adapts the plain case; ECHO/queue bindings adapt outside this
  - `F-7.4` Reactivity is @effect/atom; derivations (stops, decorations, readouts) are atoms over

- **feat** `F-8` Retrofit
  - `F-8.1` DONE — the virtualizer (placement + useWindow + Window + follow + ListModel + tests)
  - `F-8.2` react-ui-mosaic VirtualStack (still on tanstack react-virtual) rebinds onto useWindow
  - `F-8.3` react-ui-list conventions adopted, not duplicated: useListSelection extended with

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-1` Tail at rest with reserve

- **scenario** `T-2` Upward scroll holds still

- **scenario** `T-3` Prepend moves nothing

- **scenario** `T-4` Follow

- **scenario** `T-5` One navigation seam

pages.title: Outliner
pages.summary: The outliner is a CodeMirror extension (`outliner()`) that turns a plain markdown task/bullet list into a structured, hierarchical outline editor.
pages.content:
The outliner is a CodeMirror extension (`outliner()`) that turns a plain markdown task/bullet list into a structured, hierarchical outline editor. The document is always valid markdown — nesting is leading-whitespace indentation, items are `- [ ] ` tasks or `- ` bullets — so the same text round-trips through any markdown tool and syncs as ordinary text.

It is built **on top of `../blocks`**, which owns whole-block selection, the gutter drag grip, the selection highlight, and the clipboard. The outliner contributes only what is hierarchy/markdown-specific: tree parsing, edit constraints, structural commands, the drag re-indent rule, and the item menu. See `DESIGN.md` for the rebuild rationale and the drag-reindent derivation; this spec is the normative behavior.

## Modules

`outliner()` composes these modules (source files under `src/extensions/structure/outliner/`); selection, drag, highlight, and clipboard come from `../blocks`.

- **module** `tree` Parses the markdown list into an item Tree, recomputed as a facet on doc change.

- **module** `editor` A transactionFilter constraining edits to a valid outline: snaps the caret out of the marker into the content range, allows whole-line deletes, and guards marker/continuation edits.

- **module** `commands` Keymap + exported structural commands.

- **module** `dnd` Adapts `../blocks` drag/selection to the outline: per-item grips, subtree extent, subtree move with re-indent, and the drop-level rule.

- **module** `menu` A floating per-item trigger (⋮) pinned in the right margin, hidden while dragging.

## Features

- **feat** `F-1` Document model
  - `F-1.1` text is a markdown list of `- [ ] ` tasks and `- ` bullets, nested by 2-space indentation → it parses to a Tree of items, each with a level, type, own line range, and subtree
  - `F-1.2` the document changes → the Tree is recomputed and exposed via treeFacet; the document stays valid markdown text
  - `F-1.3` the document is empty → a first item (`- [ ] `) is seeded and the caret placed in its content

- **feat** `F-2` Editing constraints
  - `F-2.1` the caret is moved into an item's marker (before its content start) → it snaps to a valid position — content start when moving down/into, content end when moving
  - `F-2.2` a whole item line is deleted → the edit is allowed; marker-internal edits that would break the item are constrained
  - `F-2.3` task-marker atomicity is required (backspace removing a whole marker, continuation indent) → it is enforced by the markdown keymap that shapes the change, not by raw edits
  - `F-2.4` the document holds prose or headings before, between, or after lists → each top-level list is its own island in the tree, the prose belongs to no item, the caret
  - `F-2.5` Enter is pressed on an empty, childless item → the marker is removed and a blank line separates the list from the caret's line, so what is
  - `F-2.6` the focused caret is on an empty item, or on a blank line outside any item → the empty item shows an "Enter task" placeholder in its content; the blank line shows an

- **feat** `F-3` Selection (single model, subtree unit)
  - `F-3.1` an item is selected via grip click / shift-click / keyboard → the sole selection state is blockSelectionField (anchors); there is no second model
  - `F-3.2` an item is selected or dragged → its visual/operational extent is its whole subtree (getExtent = getRange), so a parent
  - `F-3.3` the caret sits in an item and nothing is selected → a subtle current-item border marks that item's subtree, distinct from the selection accent

- **feat** `F-4` Structural commands
  - `F-4.1` Tab / Shift-Tab is pressed on an item → the item AND all its descendants re-indent together (the subtree moves with its parent); Tab
  - `F-4.2` an item is moved up/down → it swaps with the adjacent sibling as whole subtrees
  - `F-4.3` toggleTask runs → every item in the action scope flips uniformly between task and bullet, preserving indent

- **feat** `F-5` Drag and drop re-indent
  - `F-5.1` an item is dragged → its whole subtree lifts (collapsed out) and a floating preview follows the pointer; the
  - `F-5.2` the pointer hovers a drop slot (before target T, with A the item above the slot) → the target level defaults to the dragged item's own level, clamped to
  - `F-5.3` the slot is a branch boundary (T shallower than the default) AND the pointer is over T's row → the level drops to a sibling of T — it outdents to leave the branch (ii)
  - `F-5.4` the target level differs from the source level → the preview shifts horizontally to preview it, and on drop the subtree re-roots to exactly

- **feat** `F-6` Menu / action scope
  - `F-6.1` a menu command runs with a block selection → it acts over every selected item's whole subtree (the action scope)
  - `F-6.2` a menu command runs with no selection → it acts over the caret item's subtree
  - `F-6.3` delete runs → each scope subtree (with its trailing separator) is removed, overlapping ranges merged, and

## Acceptance

- **scenario** `T-indent-subtree`

- **scenario** `T-drop-stays-in-branch`

- **scenario** `T-drop-outdents-over-target`

- **scenario** `T-delete-subtree`
